Chen Yi, sitting on the Frozen Throne, somewhat speechlessly massaged his forehead and sighed, “Let’s be humans here, all these useless props are clearly the milu deer’s private toys. What use is there in digging them out?”
“Just put them back for them.”
“I’m really begging you to be a human.”
Just then—
A gigantic Crescent Blade appeared on the grass beside them.
The Crescent Blade, nearly thirty meters long, appeared incredibly sharp, giving people a feeling of sheer sharpness and killing intent just by glancing at it!
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit looked at his right hand in shock, then at the thirty-meter-long Crescent Blade beside him, and incredulously turned to the milu deer, which didn’t resist at all and was turned away from him, and exclaimed in shock.
“This thing, you’re telling me I pulled it out from inside you?”
“You’ve got quite the storage capacity there!”
“I finally understand where Santa Claus stores all the Christmas gifts when he’s delivering them around the world. I always wondered how a single sleigh could carry so many gifts.”
“Prop Name”: Spare Left Blade of Santa Claus’s Sleigh.
“Prop Level”: None.
“Prop Effect”: Can be used to replace the left blade of Santa Claus’s sleigh in the event of a malfunction.
“Prop Introduction”: “Better to be safe than sorry, safety first.”
This thing looked exactly like the blade under Chen Yi’s sleigh on the left side, but it was more than ten times bigger than his.
If just one sleigh blade is this massive.
One can only imagine how big Santa Claus’s sleigh must be.
As Tuberculosis Rabbit was still marveling at how such a massive thing could fit inside, that there’s really no limit to what the world can hold, Chen Yi’s eyes flashed with a hint of brilliance.
“Wait a minute!”
“If we install this blade on the front of the sleigh, given the speed of our sleigh, we could plow straight ahead like a bulldozer, couldn’t we?”
“I’m afraid that’s not going to work.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit stretched out his hand and removed his gloves before hesitatingly saying, “It’s too fast. With so many obstacles, the milu deer is likely to run into trouble.”
“We can use the Mechanical Milu Deer.”
“But the Mechanical Milu Deer can only be a decoration; it can’t control direction.”
“Why do we need to control direction?”
Chen Yi looked up toward the forest that stretched as far as the eye could see and said, “We just need to install the blade on the front of the sleigh, then step on the gas and charge forward in a straight line.”
“Just like harvesting wheat at harvest time.”
“Since we’re building a house, we might as well build a big one.”
“We should have enough time in ten days to cut the entire forest down and build a house that covers this world, right?”
“…”
After silently pondering for a while, Tuberculosis Rabbit suddenly lit a cigarette, took a slow drag, and murmured with anticipation, “Yi, you’ve gotten me interested.”
“I’ve always wanted to build a big enough house.”
“So, shall we start?”
“What else are we waiting for?”
…
One hour later.
The Mechanical Moose Christmas Sleigh had been completely transformed, with the thirty-meter-long, gigantic blade firmly attached to the front of the sleigh.
They spent several thousand Points to add a slot in the front part of the sleigh, then wedged the blade into it. It didn’t quite match, fitting somewhat loosely.
But after taking some logs out of the bag, splitting them into firewood, and stuffing the wood into the gaps, it became somewhat secure.
As long as the sleigh started moving.
Read new chapters at empire
Under the massive thrust of the nitrogen, the huge blade would constantly be pushed forward, with no chance to fall off. And even if it did, they’d just stop and mount it back on.
After all, it wasn’t the original part, and it couldn’t be made to fit perfectly.
Although it looked a bit crude, it would suffice.
That would do.
The Mechanical Elk was suspended at the rear of the sleigh; although it was useless, without a milu deer hanging on the sleigh, it would be deemed not roadworthy, so they still had to hang this thing.
Since the Five-Spice Milu Deer had been unloaded from the sleigh and couldn’t be put into the bag, and they weren’t comfortable leaving it behind, it had to be accommodated inside the sleigh cabin with them.
Once everything was ready.
Chen Yi sat in the sleigh, lowered the glass protective shield, and after exchanging a glance with Tuberculosis Rabbit, took a deep breath, stepped down on the gas pedal to the max, and shouted.
“Let’s go!”
The next second—
This sleigh, which had been modified into an odd shape, with fifteen nitrogen cylinders at the rear, suddenly spouted dazzling red and blue flames, and the powerful thrust pushed the sleigh directly toward the forest in a sprint!
The massive Crescent Blade embedded at the very front of the sleigh!
Instantly cut down all the pine trees in its path at the roots, and as those cut trees fell and turned into logs, they became streaks of light, chasing after the now distant sleigh!
A grand and ambitious lumberjacking journey had officially begun!
…
ps: Thank you to the boss “Ten Thousand Eight Hundred Thoughts” for the reward of 6500 Starting Points, thank you to the boss “Floating Clouds, Formless and Intentional” for the reward of 5000 Starting Points, thank you to the boss “Miyu’s Big Brother” for the reward of 4500 Starting Points, thank you to the boss “Heisaki Huyi” for the reward of 10000 Starting Points!!!
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 95 - 95 - 94: "Is this... the World Barrier?
chapters.content:
Chapter 95 – 94: “Is this… the World Barrier?
The wind rose, clouds surged.
Rather than calling it a tool, the log-cutting sled machine was more fittingly described as a toy, a spectacular plaything for adults.
Under tremendous thrust, the thirty-meter-long, incredibly sharp skids sliced seamlessly through the pine trees at their roots without any impediment.
It was as smooth as cutting butter with a red-hot knife.
Inside the vehicle, one could hardly feel any severe jolts.
Extremely fluid.
And those logs turned into light points were desperately trying to catch up with the log-cutting sled machine sprinting ahead, their mission being to transform into tiny dots and drill into that player’s backpack in front.
But they probably never anticipated a day when they couldn’t keep up.
The sled’s speed was too fast, so much so that it seemed to be outpacing the light points.
The sled had to stop from time to time to ensure those light points could catch up with Chen Yi inside it.
Just over ten minutes.
They were unclear on how many pine trees they had harvested, only aware that the number of logs in their backpacks had far exceeded six figures, which was enough to build an extremely sturdy and safe house.
But that wasn’t enough.
Not nearly enough.
As the system announcement indicated, the map was vast enough that even after driving almost at full speed in one direction for over ten minutes, they still hadn’t reached the end.
It’s worth noting.
Their sled’s speed had hit the terrifying mark of a thousand kilometers per hour.
Under such circumstances, even ten minutes represented a considerable distance.
Such an expanse of pine forest, if left to a normal player to harvest, would likely take years of effort, and not even Bald Qiang could finish it before retirement.
Chen Yi, operating the sled, glanced at the map where the edge was starting to appear, and that green dot symbolizing their location was dashing towards the boundary. His eyelids flicked slightly as he slowly released the accelerator and pressed the brake.
The speed of the sled gradually reduced.
Until it smashed into a wall of air that felt like glue, embedding the front of the vehicle into it.
“Hm?”
Chen Yi jumped off the sled, approached the head of the vehicle, and looked up at this glue-like wall of air in front of him.
The edge of the forest held a towering wall of air that stretched high into the clouds, with no end in sight on either side.
On one side of the wall was an endless, dense forest, while on the other was a murky pale yellow viscous substance mixed with white particles.
The scene was bizarre, to say the least, something that simply could not exist in real life. Explore more stories at empire
He picked up a branch from the ground and tried stabbing it into the wall of air.
Without much effort.
The branch easily pierced in, but was quickly enveloped by the viscous matter on the other side of the wall. He tried to pull the branch out and found it required a good deal of strength.
Under the influence of the D-level Skill Calm and Composed, his physical condition maintained a constant doubling of strength.
His strength far exceeded that of ordinary people.
In this situation, the fact that it was so difficult to pull out the branch illustrated the substantial adhesive force of the viscous liquid on the other side of the wall.
It took all his power to yank the branch back out!
Immaculately clean.
The branch that came out was completely clean, without a single drop of the viscous liquid on it, and the wall of air in front of him remained intact, suggesting it had rapidly “healed” the hole pierced by the branch would be an understatement.
To describe it accurately, it was as if the wall of air had never been pierced at all.
It seemed that the wall was composed of individual molecules that shifted aside when the branch was inserted, and recombined when the branch was removed.
There was no concept of a hole or a wound to begin with.
“Is this… the world barrier?”
Tuberculosis Rabbit looked up at the towering wall of air, with the pale yellow viscous substance piling up on the other side of the wall stretching into the sky. Should that stuff fall, not a single player in the forest would make it out alive.
Even with infinite resurrection, one would perish and resurrect endlessly within the endless viscous liquid.
They’d all drown or suffocate in the cycle.
Better to just die outright, clean and swift.
“There’s a group of people on Blue Star who firmly believe that Blue Star is a continent, not spherical, and at the edge of Blue Star exists a world barrier. Crossing it poses the risk of falling into the cosmic void.”
“What we see before us resembles the world barrier as described by those people.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit’s eyes held a trace of shock, finding it difficult to calm his heart for a moment.
Both of them more or less guessed what this pale yellow viscous liquid was.
This pale yellow viscous liquid, if expectations were correct, should be the substance used for creating maps.
And this map… probably was crafted using this type of liquid.
The Snow Sea Project Team, they wielded almost creator-like abilities, able to use this viscous liquid to fabricate a forest out of nothingness, endowing it with all sorts of magical rules.
For example, in this forest, one could infinitely resurrect.
Or in this forest, cutting down a pine tree meant the tree would turn into a log and fly into the player’s backpack.
Or even generate savages to attack the players.
Creators?
No, perhaps even creators lack such capabilities.
“…”
Chen Yi remained silent, not speaking a word, glanced at the skid blade that had lodged into the wall, boarded the sled, revved up the engine to its maximum, and began to reverse.
The resistance wasn’t that great either.
After a few seconds of strain, the skid blade that had embedded into the wall began to pull out, dragged by the sled.
“`
“Let’s go.”
Chen Yi looked at the Tuberculosis Rabbit still standing in front of the air wall, “With our current strength, all we can do is watch. Whatever the purpose of the Snow Sea Project Team is, there will come a day when the truth will be revealed.”
“And what we need to do is to stay alive, and to make ourselves stronger.”
The Snow Sea Project Team is human.
This much everyone knows.
To describe them as human may not be entirely accurate; it should be said they are intelligent life forms. The very name of the team makes this quite clear, not to mention that the Snow Sea Project Team actually recruits customer service representatives.
That made it even more obvious.
He had actually vaguely guessed what the aim of the Snow Sea Project Team might be, but he had never said it out loud; after all, it was just a guess and he wasn’t sure. Moreover, even if he guessed correctly, it wouldn’t really mean much.
Simply by following the rules of the past three months, and the tenth rule of the June regulations, it isn’t hard to guess.
…
Nearly twenty minutes later, Chen Yi and his companion had made a clearing by driving the snowmobile back and forth in the direction they had come from.
The cleared space behind them looked extremely neat.
No fallen trees, no branches or leaves. Any tree cut down by a player would turn into a log, transform into a stream of light, and fly into the player’s backpack, leaving no trace on the ground; in fact, it looked quite clean.
The group didn’t stop.
They just kept going in this continuous loop.
Since they had already entered this map, the current focus should be on the map task, that is, building a house. To build a house, naturally, they needed to gather wood.
…
“I’m a happy lumberjack.”
Li Yide hummed a lively tune, casually pulling up a few mushrooms from under a tree root, wiping them on his sleeve, and tossing them into his mouth to refuel himself for the work ahead.
This map’s mission wasn’t bad at all.
He liked it.
Especially the fact that you could resurrect infinitely, which was really strange, though limited to this map, but that feeling of being able to revive was still very odd.
You should know, the word ’death’ has always been taboo for humans.
Once you cross that line, it means many rules can be broken.
Before long.
After refueling, Li Yide patted his belly, took a deep satisfying breath, reveling in the sensation of his vehicle’s fuel increasing, then burst into laughter and took off with his chainsaw towards the distance.
But just then—
He suddenly heard a piercing sonic boom ahead of him, and before he could react, he saw a white light rapidly filling his pupils until it magnified!
’You have been killed by another player, and will revive in the same spot after an hour.’
Consciousness had already slipped into darkness.
And in that darkness, a prompt sounded by his ear.
“Is this what death feels like?”
Li Yide looked around, seeing only pitch black where he couldn’t even see his hand in front of his face, and without the solid feeling of standing on the ground, he felt as if he was floating in the air.
He reached out to touch his body, there was a clear sense of touch.
But everything around him was empty.
He could speak and there was sound, but there was no echo, nor any response.
He floated like a willow fluff in the deepest darkness of the universe. His personal panel was not displayed, the title above his head was gone too, there was nothing.
Isolation, desolation.
Here, it was perfectly embodied.
He couldn’t feel the passage of time, even the thoughts in his mind were unconsciously slowing down.
Here, it was as if everything had stopped.
He didn’t know how much time had passed.
Li Yide suddenly found the darkness he had become accustomed to gradually fading, till light filled the space around him. He closed his eyes tightly and held his hand in front of him to avoid being invaded by the blinding sunlight.
After a while, he came around, supporting himself on a tree root, standing on the spot, feeling slightly week in the knees as he felt his body up and down.
Completely unharmed without any injury.
Props undamaged.
The logs that had dropped out of his backpack were neatly arranged to one side, unclaimed by anyone.
The feeling of standing on solid ground had come back to him.
He had truly been revived.
Li Yide, who stood still for a few minutes after revival, then had a flicker of fear in his eyes and shot off in the direction he had come from.
Players could revive, that was true.
But the feeling of death was not pleasant.
No pain.
But in that hour of darkness, he even felt like he had forgotten the existence of his own body. At the beginning, he wondered if his props would be damaged, whether the resources he had worked hard to obtain would be taken away.
He pondered many problems.
But as time went by, he found his thoughts gradually stagnating.
He forgot the existence of his body, forgot to think, and even forgot his own existence.
When he revived again.
It even felt like a lifetime had passed.
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 96 - 96 - 95: At the moment of detonation, art reached its peak.
chapters.content:
Chapter 96 – 95: At the moment of detonation, art reached its peak.
After coming back to life again, Li Yide was set to compete with Chen Yi for the leaderboard rankings, ready to gather many logs to build a sufficiently large house; he cast all other concerns to the back of his mind.
He just wanted to find a safe place, to build a shelter with his own gathered resources that could protect him.
Avoiding the savages would be enough.
Read new chapters at empire
He wanted to get through these ten days smoothly; the sensation of death was something he had experienced once already, and he did not want to experience it again.
The vast clearing under his feet seemed to tell him that Chen Yi had recently swept through here with a sleigh.
And he was naturally clear about whose handiwork this was.
His goal was also clear: follow this clearing to find a suitable place, then build his house.
Since Chen Yi had already logged all these trees, naturally, he wouldn’t log them again.
…
Nine hours had passed.
Chen Yi stood on the floating sleigh, leaning over to look at their achievements over the past few hours.
The entire forest had turned into a massive wasteland by now.
Empty and void.
The previously dense and towering forest had now become a wasteland.
“Yi, stay here, I’ll handle building the house.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, with a cigarette in his mouth, excitedly jumped into the sleigh and, without looking back, shot off toward the edge of the forest.
Chen Yi did not reply.
Lying on the folding bed, he placed his hands behind his head and closed his eyes, feigning sleep, letting Tuberculosis Rabbit do as he pleased.
His brow was slightly furrowed.
One could not tell what he was thinking.
…
Before long.
Tuberculosis Rabbit, with a backpack filled with log resources, came to the edge of the map, gleefully steering the sleigh, and looked toward the edge of the map.
The next second—
A log obediently lay there, serving as the foundation.
Building a house was simple.
One only needed to direct their gaze to a specific spot on the ground, and then mentally select the construction option they wanted.
Just like now.
Soon, close to a hundred logs were neatly placed on the ground, interconnected with one another, leaving no gaps, and the log serving as the foundation no longer kept its original log shape.
It became a flat plane.
As if the log had been cut open through the middle.
The entire foundation was extremely flat upon a glance.
Tuberculosis Rabbit did not linger; he just drove the sleigh straight on to the other side of the map.
Below.
One could see logs continuously emerging peculiarly, forming the foundation; the scene looked rather spectacular indeed.
He did not activate the sleigh at its maximum speed.
Too fast, and it would be hard to keep up visually.
After well over an hour.
Tuberculosis Rabbit finally arrived at the other side of the map with the sleigh. On his way there, the map had been completely covered with logs, and a row of foundation on the map had been successfully constructed.
He rubbed his slightly sore eyes, lifted his head, and looked toward an even larger area of open land.
His heart was full of drive.
He glanced at the time; luckily, the June rules in this map would not take effect; otherwise, it would have been truly torturous, as the sky was already turning dark.
He didn’t linger any longer, operating the sleigh to continue along the other side, repeating the operation.
He had played a game before, a pixelated, crafting game composed of blocks.
In it, players could build houses or defeat monsters.
And he had achieved a feat in that game.
He filled the entire map with TNT dynamite: ravines, underground, skies.
The earth’s soil, the forests on the ground, he replaced them all with TNT dynamite.
The entire map had only one type of block, which was the TNT block.
It was a form of art.
An art form that couldn’t captivate the masses but was destined for a niche audience.
But art is art precisely because it’s niche; if it’s mainstream, then it’s not considered art.
And after admiring it for three days, he chose to detonate it.
At the moment of detonation, the art reached its peak; his graphics card seemed to catch fire, beginning to smoke as if the game was invading reality.
He had a very peculiar passion.
He enjoyed doing repetitive things, doing the same thing countless times, then slowly admiring his grand creation.
Like when he filled the entire map with TNT, that was truly satisfying.
The same goes for now.
The houses built this way lacked any aesthetic value, but he liked them; he liked the feeling of filling the entire map, the repetition of doing one thing over and over.
This sense of completeness was very enjoyable.
…
“…”
Li Yide, with a slack expression, watched his newly built house get demolished by the free-roaming sleigh; his heart was filled with despair. His mouth slowly gaped open, and he wanted to curse.
He knew Chen Yi was formidable.
Wanting to build a very large house and top the building rating leaderboard, he could understand that.
It’s quite normal, human nature; everybody wants to be number one.
But he never imagined Chen Yi would construct a house that would cover the entire map.
Are you insane?!
Have you had enough?!
This huge map, over a hundred people come in, and it’s all about watching you play?
As soon as his house was finished, he saw the sleigh fly over his head, then his house was smashed to pieces. The man who often stayed by Chen Yi’s side jumped down from the sleigh.
He said, with a serious face, not to build a house within his house.
He hated any anomaly within his own house, as it would make him very uncomfortable, and once he felt uncomfortable, there was no telling what he might do.
“`
And then it flew away.
At that moment, his original house had already been demolished, replaced with a foundation of logs that stretched as far as the eye could see.
Yes, this place was the foundation for Chen Yi’s new house.
He did try to find a spot that Chen Yi hadn’t touched, but just as he prepared to fly toward the open space far off to the side, that person reminded him that it was also included.
The entire map was.
He gave up.
Completely gave up.
Building a house? No need, he would just live in Chen Yi’s house.
Since you won’t let me build a house in your house, then staying in your house should be fine, right? Anyway, by the looks of it, those savages probably couldn’t attack him now.
At least he hadn’t seen any savages now.
…
Soon it grew dark.
Savages began to slowly emerge from the wall of air at the edge of the forest. They hadn’t taken a step before they saw signs of construction and paused, but all the same, they started to dismantle the foundations.
Their mission was precisely to destroy houses built by players and to hunt down players.
“Hm?”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, who was enjoying dinner with Chen Yi by the campfire, suddenly heard a notification telling him his house was under attack by savages. He quickly glanced at the thumbnail of his house’s blueprint.
As he saw the foundations at the edge of the map being destroyed by savages,
Tuberculosis Rabbit, who hadn’t finished his meal, became instantly furious, hopped onto his sled, and rushed toward the edge of the map. Someone daring to demolish his house was practically asking for trouble.
Did they not realize how much effort he had put into laying those foundations?
You can kill people, but you can’t tear down their houses!
…
At the edge of the map.
Tuberculosis Rabbit controlled his sled and slaughtered savages all night long, his eyes bloodshot, painting the foundations at the map’s edge red.
Countless chunks of savage corpses piled up at the edge of the map, stinking to high heaven!
Finally, daylight came.
When no more savages emerged from the air wall, Tuberculosis Rabbit, with bloodshot eyes, finally regained a moment of clarity. Exhaustion began to flow over him, but observing the number of damaged foundations, he dared not pause.
Instead, he first repaired all the damaged foundations,
before beginning to reinforce the already laid foundations!
A single log could make a stretch of foundation.
And a single log could turn a foundation into an Enhanced Foundation, making it harder for savages to destroy.
On top of that, adding another log could turn the Enhanced Foundation into an Ultimate Foundation, extremely difficult for savages to destroy.
Different levels of foundations had different shapes; an Ultimate Foundation was topped with a thick steel plate, giving it an extremely robust appearance.
Although it was unclear how wood could be enhanced into steel plates, it was obviously the rule.
In this way, it wouldn’t be easily destroyed by savages.
Upon seeing that the foundations damaged last night had been repaired, he didn’t go on to build new ones.
He had only laid six rows of foundations the day before, probably a thirtieth of the entire map.
But now he didn’t plan to lay anymore but intended to reinforce the six rows of foundations from yesterday to Ultimate Foundations, so they wouldn’t be destroyed by savages.
No hesitation.
He immediately flew back along the foundations he had laid the day before.
…
“Yawn.”
A player sleeping in a hole stretched leisurely in the spacious cavern and let out a satisfied yawn, reluctantly lying on the soft grass bed.
He rubbed his bleary eyes, turned over, and settled into a comfortable position.
He had slept very well last night.
No savages had come looking for him, not even a whisper of noise—although he had faintly heard the roars of savages, sounding somewhat like sonic booms, they ultimately didn’t find him.
It seemed that his decision to dig a deep pit underground and then sleep there was wise, at least it was sufficiently concealed.
A night passed safely.
After lying there for about fifteen minutes, his sleepiness had pretty much dissipated. He stood up, removed the sod covering the hole overhead, and was ready to climb back to the surface by supporting himself against the cavern walls when.
He suddenly froze in place.
“Huh?”
Why had a chunk of… wood suddenly appeared above the hole?
He tentatively touched it with his hand and confirmed it, it was wood.
Then a notification popped up before his eyes.
“This structure is under construction by player ’Tuberculosis Rabbit.’ You can choose to destroy it or leave it.”
“Heh.”
He couldn’t help but let out a snarl tinged with bitter laughter as he pulled out his Logging Axe from his chest. Was someone building their house right above his head? This was outrageous!
You started the discourtesy; don’t blame him for being ruthless in return!
He didn’t say another word and began fiercely chopping at the foundation above his head with his Logging Axe!
“Ultimate Foundation: 1/999.”
“…”
The man stood expressionless and silent on the spot, hesitantly lifted his Logging Axe, and struck again.
“2/999.”
Clear and simple, just as he expected.
He would need to chop 999 times to destroy that damn foundation.
999 times?
That would exhaust him to death!
He stood there, looking up at the foundation that nearly obscured all vision overhead, and fell silent, not sure what to do. Surely he couldn’t just stay there for ten days, could he?
Without food, without water, he would die.
Although he could revive.
But nobody would willingly repeat the cycle of death and revival over ten days, right?
After a long silence, the man rolled up his sleeves, took a deep breath, and his eyes slowly hardened with determination as he continued chopping down.
Even a dripping tap could penetrate stone.
Besides, he just had to chop 999 times to leave.
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 97 - 97 - 96: "Key Evaluation: Harmful to others and not beneficial to oneself.
chapters.content:
Chapter 97 – 96: “Key Evaluation: Harmful to others and not beneficial to oneself.
“Hmm?”
Having pulled an all-nighter and continuing to fight off drowsiness while working overtime, Tuberculosis Rabbit stopped upon hearing the notification sound by his ear.
“Your house is being destroyed by a player.”
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, expressionless, immediately controlled his sled and rushed towards the continuously blinking red dot on the map. There was an urgent need of time, as it would take at least 7 days to cover the entire foundation across the map.
This was the scenario where he didn’t sleep and worked continuously.
Factoring in rest, it would take at least eight and a half days.
And the duration of the map was only 10 days.
He was already exhausted from racing against time, and now players were constantly tearing down his house, which was truly deserving of a thousand deaths!
Tuberculosis Rabbit steered his sled to that blinking red dot.
Without saying a word, he quickly built a small house around the foundation.
A perfectly square little house.
Each house had 10 walls, and the ceiling was also ten layers thick, with walls equally covering the outer edges where the ceiling and the walls met.
Every wall was an enhanced ultimate wall, and after throwing in some water resources and food, he left again.
The player couldn’t be killed.
Nor could he be driven away.
He simply built a house to keep the player inside, as long as they didn’t come out to cause havoc. In the future, he could do the same with other players, confining them as well.
After doing all this, he departed once again to continue laying the foundation!
A stretch of foundation was over a hundred meters wide.
When he was hovering in the sky, he could only lay a foundation of that many meters wide at once, which he called a row, the limit his eyes could take in and focus on.
The entire map required laying about 180 rows, which is 18,000 meters wide.
It was a rectangular map.
Very long, but not very wide.
The width was less than 20,000 meters.
Struggle and strive.
Tuberculosis Rabbit, after gulping down a big bucket of coffee, began to maneuver the sled and work diligently like a busy little bee.
…
It was hard to tell how much time had passed.
“993/999.”
“994/999.”
The man in the underground cave, looking above at the numbers gradually closing in, showed exhausted eyes filled with anticipation and joy, and licked his somewhat dry lips.
He slowly lifted his arm, heavy as if filled with lead, and swung the Logging Axe overhead, striking down fiercely at the foundation!
Finally—
999!
When the number reached 999, the foundation above shattered and the man, whose eyes had lost their luster, were once again filled with hopeful excitement as he struggled to climb out of the pit.
However, before he could rejoice for long, after climbing out of the hole, he noticed that he seemed to be trapped inside a house.
The dusk light spilled through the crevices into the house.
Falling on his face, it made his expression of utter despair all the more piercing.
The man, frozen in despair, let two hot streams of tears slide down his face. He didn’t know whom he had angered; he had simply dug a hole underground to take a nap, but how had it turned into this situation?
Why?
How had things developed to this point?
But soon, he saw the water and food laid out on the floor.
After a moment of stun, he grabbed a bottle of mineral water and tasted it in small sips, finding it sweet, but not daring to finish it.
The steamed bun was also delicious.
It gave his empty stomach a sense of fullness.
The man who had eaten his fill and satisfied his thirst sat on the ground, unexpectedly moved to tears. Although he didn’t understand why Tuberculosis Rabbit had locked him up, the provision of food and water was still very humane.
He had already tried it.
He had chopped at all four walls.
They were uniformly 999.
But he truly had no more strength left. Continue your saga on empire
After resting for a moment, he gritted his teeth and stood up once again, swinging his Logging Axe vigorously, chopping away. A little hardship wouldn’t stop him.
…
And amidst this bustling work.
Only 2 days remained until the time to leave the map.
On the building score leaderboard, not a single name was listed. No one had made it onto the board.
The houses of other players hadn’t made it onto the leaderboard because they were all torn down.
Chen Yi’s name wasn’t listed because Chen Yi simply didn’t build anything.
Tuberculosis Rabbit’s name wasn’t listed because Tuberculosis Rabbit hadn’t finished building yet.
So it was that the leaderboard, which the map designer might have thought would incite player competition, bizarrely showed no entries after 8 days of activity on the map.
During these eight days.
Tuberculosis Rabbit had laid all the foundations.
All foundations were enhanced to the highest level, the ultimate edition of foundations.
On top of that were many little houses, each containing a captured player—about twenty or thirty, mostly those who liked to cause destruction were confined within.
For the rest, the more well-behaved ones, Tuberculosis Rabbit didn’t bother, letting them move about freely.
As long as they didn’t tear down his houses and didn’t build within his residences, it was fine.
Then, Tuberculosis Rabbit drove his sled to the edge of the map, preparing to build the wall overtime. There wasn’t enough time; he had to build it fast.
The feeling that 10 days were completely insufficient to build the house he envisioned was daunting, not knowing if he could continue building the next time he entered.
First, he erected a wall about two meters high along the edge of the map.
Then, behind the wall, he built rows of towers taller than the first one which effectively defended against the attacks of wild people.
Next, behind this row of arrow towers, a higher wall was constructed.
Then, behind this wall, another row of even taller arrow towers was erected, with the wall serving as their foundation.
This process was repeated.
By the time the 10th day arrived,
The Tuberculosis Rabbit had finished building all the walls of the house.
A total of 10 walls!
Each one taller than the last, with the highest reaching over 20 meters!
A total of 8 rows of arrow towers!
All were protected within the sandwich of the walls.
All the walls had been enhanced to their ultimate versions, and all the arrow towers too had been enhanced to their ultimate versions, with both their firing speed and power greatly improved.
In total, 18 lines of defense firmly safeguarded his house.
Even if an enemy breached the first wall and destroyed the incredibly fragile first row of arrow towers, it would be in vain, as there were still the second, third, and up to the tenth wall!
Impenetrable as if fortified with metal and stone!
And now, there were only 4 hours left until the departure from the map.
Chen Yi lay on a folding chair, glancing at the Tuberculosis Rabbit fast asleep in the sled nearby, worn out from exhaustion, and couldn’t help but shake his head with a wry smile.
This little guy truly had remarkable perseverance.
Not to mention anything else, if he were to do this kind of repetitive work for ten days straight, he would find it somewhat hard to keep going.
But the Tuberculosis Rabbit seemed not only completely unbothered by any impatience, but actually relished the work, becoming more vigorous the more he did it.
And when the walls were erected,
The structure beneath their feet was finally recognized by the system as a building.
Their names had at last appeared on the building’s score ranking board.
“Building’s Score Ranking Board.”
“First place: Tuberculosis Rabbit, score 1,320,000,”
“Second place: None.”
“Third place: None.”
The sheer 1,320,000 points could only be described as terrifying. If he remembered correctly, the scores for the buildings that appeared on the first day of the ranking board were just in the tens, right?
The highest one had only been a little over 300.
Of course, those other buildings had all disappeared, having been dismantled by the Tuberculosis Rabbit.
A score of 1,320,000 points might be close to the limit for the highest score a building could receive on the map.
Over the days, they had discovered a bug with this map.
It was that even if all the log resources on the map were harvested, there would not be enough to cover the entire map with a house.
For instance, more than half the log resources in the Tuberculosis Rabbit’s backpack had already been used.
The foundation and walls were a bit too wasteful of the logs.
To fill the inside of the walls with houses, there would simply not be enough log resources, but as the pine trees had all been harvested, they had no way to acquire new log resources.
But it was about enough.
Soon, even the remaining few hours passed, and it was time to leave the map.
Suddenly, a flash of white light appeared.
Then, Chen Yi found himself in a white space.
The walls were white all around him, the ceiling above was white, and the floor tiles beneath were white.
A prompt sounded leisurely by their ears.
“Ding, the map is now being settled and evaluated.”
“Map Evaluation”: “You harvested 99% of the pine trees within the wilderness map, turning the wilderness into a true wasteland. Congratulations on acquiring the hidden title—The Real Wilderness.”
“You did not choose to build a house, but instead survived the barbarian crisis by adapting to the unchanging environment.”
“Therefore, your comprehensive evaluation is B+.”
“Evaluation Keywords: Lazy and Gluttonous.”
“Map Settlement”: Although you have not built a house, you have earned 84,000 Points from cutting down a large number of pine trees, as well as acquiring a complete random C-level Skill and a random D-level treasure chest.
“The Real Wilderness?”
Chen Yi looked at his Title Effect, nodded thoughtfully without speaking—after all, he wasn’t the one who built the house, the Tuberculosis Rabbit did, so naturally the rewards for building it wouldn’t fall to him.
…
“Finally out?”
A player with a dazed spirit swept his gaze around, and feeling as if he had been in a different world, when he saw that he still appeared inside a house, he somewhat lost his composure, and his body went limp, collapsing straight to the ground.
Did anyone know what he had been through these ten days?
He’d been hammering away for a whole nine days!
In fact, after the first day of hammering, when he hadn’t left, he had already thought of giving up. But by the second day, he reconsidered, thinking if he gave up, wouldn’t his efforts on the first day have been in vain?
Still unable to leave on the second day, on the third day, just when he thought about giving up, it suddenly felt as if he was abandoning the previous two days.
Thus, driven by the sunk cost fallacy, he hammered away for nine long days.
Becoming more skilled over time, he felt as if he had turned into a logger.
He had completely forgotten how many walls he had smashed—10? 20?
Too many to remember.
And then, his own evaluation panel popped up before his eyes.
“Ding, the map is now being settled and evaluated.”
“Map Evaluation”: “Because you spent 9 continuous days attacking other players’ houses, you have obtained the hidden title—Agitated Husky.”
“After successfully surviving the barbarian crisis on the first day by digging a burrow, you spent the remaining nine days doing the same action: destroying other players’ houses.”
“You didn’t cut down trees, nor did you build a house of your own, you were just destroying other players’ houses.”
“It is evident that you have a strong desire to attack, you are a player who really enjoys destruction.”
“Therefore, your comprehensive evaluation is C+.”
“Evaluation Keywords: Harmful to Others, Not Beneficial to Oneself.”
“Map Settlement”: Although you have not built a house or cut down any trees, you have earned 3,920 Points for your relentless destruction of other players’ houses, along with a complete random D-level Skill.

chapters.title: Chapter 98 - 98 - 97: "Prop Name": Life Cinema Invitation.
chapters.content:
Chapter 98 – 97: “Prop Name”: Life Cinema Invitation.
“Uh…”
The man who had been sitting on the ground, exhausted and in despair, stared blankly as he saw the system’s evaluation of himself, and then suddenly sat up from the ground.
As if his back pain and leg soreness had vanished in an instant, a glimmer of light flashed in his eyes.
The reward is so high?
Nearly 4,000 Points and a random D-level Skill?
That was way faster than the money he made from killing that Minotaur outside the city; he didn’t make 400 Points in a whole day of hunting them. Suddenly, those 10 days didn’t seem so torturous.
They were a bit tough, though.
But the return was quite generous, wasn’t it?
The man, who previously had only resentment in his eyes, now looked at the Tuberculosis Rabbit beside him with a hint of gratitude.
If it weren’t for the player who had locked him up for 10 days, he probably wouldn’t have received such a high reward for simply digging holes and trying to survive, right?
Indeed.
Sometimes, one needs a benefactor to push them; otherwise, one never knows their own strength.
Without this benefactor, he couldn’t even imagine himself swinging a hammer for 10 days straight; he had never thought he possessed such perseverance and strength.
…
“…”
The Tuberculosis Rabbit looked at the man not far away with a weird expression. For a moment, it felt a bit spooky; what was with the gratitude in this man’s eyes?
He had locked him up for 10 days, and still, the man was full of gratitude?
Is he crazy?
Could it be that he actually developed Stockholm syndrome?
He remembered this man, with tremendous physical strength, tearing down the wall while he repaired it, relentless even if it meant tearing down every day, wasting a lot of his time.
He had to repair the wall for this player now and then.
Other players locked up would give up in a few days and stay motionless in the house, but this one had been smashing for 10 full days. Whether it was his perseverance or his indomitable spirit, he was number one among the players.
And at this time—
His instance evaluation also popped up.
’Ding, map beginning settlement and evaluation.’
’Map Evaluation’: “Because you topped the building rating leaderboard in the wilderness map, you have earned the exclusive title—Master Builder”
“You spread the foundation of the house across the entire map.”
“And you built a perimeter wall along the edges of the map.”
“In just 10 days, you managed to build a house that covered the entire map,”
“And you also built houses for other players and defended them against attacks from savages, perfectly embodying what it means to be selflessly loving.”
“Therefore, your overall evaluation is S+.”
“Evaluation Keywords: Concern for the World.”
“And you have obtained the hidden title—’Concern for the World’!”
’Map Settlement’: You have earned 112,000 Points for building a sufficiently large house, obtained a complete random B-level Skill, and a random C-tier Prop Chest.
“Darn!”
The Tuberculosis Rabbit couldn’t help but exclaim in surprise, a trace of shock appearing in his eyes.
The reward is that high?
More than 100,000 Points, a complete B-level Skill, and a random C-tier Prop Chest?
Is this what he gained over the past 10 days?
He had never anticipated that just building houses could yield such a high reward!
Could it be that the map’s rewards are too high?
But he quickly figured it out.
If it hadn’t been for Yi’s Christmas sleigh possessing a thousand kilometers per hour speed, he couldn’t have possibly achieved such a feat, let alone build such a big house.
In these 10 days, he couldn’t even have finished exploring the map.
He couldn’t have found the freshwater rivers and wild game so easily as he did on the map, without a hint of struggle for survival.
Lacking for nothing in terms of resources.
The only thing missing was time; if only he had a little more time.
Just as he was preparing to take a closer look at his gains this time.
A sudden flash of white light appeared before his eyes.
By the time he reacted again, he had already returned to the rental apartment in Yancheng Garden District.
Back where he was before entering the map.
…
“Finally, I’m back.”
The Tuberculosis Rabbit walked to the window, drew the curtains, and inhaled the hot air hitting his face. With a content expression, he spread his arms wide and said reflectively, “In the blink of an eye, 10 days have passed. I wonder if there will be a save feature next time I enter the wilderness map.”
When he left the map, all the log resources in his backpack that he hadn’t used were cleared.
Yi’s wilderness map access pass could enter the wilderness three times, meaning they still had two opportunities to enter this map.
It was just uncertain whether they could continue to improve his house the next time they entered the map. There were many designs in his heart that were unfinished, waiting to be perfected the next time.
Meanwhile, Chen Yi was sitting in a chair nearby, calmly looking at a small card in his hand, not speaking.
The card in his hand resembled a bank card.
A silver-plated skull was emblazoned on the black card, which looked quite high-quality.
This item came from the random D-tier Prop Chest he got after clearing the wilderness.
A minor Prop.
’Prop Name’: Life Cinema Invitation.
’Prop Grade’: D-tier.
“Prop Effect”: After activating this card, you can enter a special cinema and watch future scenes of yourself and the people around you.
“Prop Restrictions”: Can only be used once, and is not tradable, not transferable, not discardable, not droppable, and not destructible.
“Prop Introduction”: “The scenes that appear in the movie are not the conclusion of your life, but merely a branch. You may choose to treat it as just a movie.”
It wasn’t a prop that enhances one’s strength, but an invitation to the Life Cinema.
An invitation to a cinema.
And the film being shown isn’t just any movie, it’s a movie with oneself as the protagonist?
Through this thing, you could see visions of your future?
There isn’t anyone who wouldn’t be curious about their future self, yet within that curiosity, there’s a tinge of resistance.
Chen Yi fiddled with the card in his hands, his eyes narrowed without speaking, thinking that this prop could barely be classified as an entertainment prop.
In the cinema, you could watch your own future?
As long as he activated this card, he could see his future self.
There must be many people who would want to cross the timeline to see what they would be like in the future.
And now he had that opportunity.
After pondering for a moment, Chen Yi chose to activate the prop, to be honest, he was quite curious about what kind of scene his future self would be in.
Just as the prop was activated, the silver-plated black card in his hand suddenly flashed with a thin blue light, his body stiffened slightly, the light in his eyes immediately faded, he leaned back into the chair, and stopped moving as if he had fallen into a deep sleep.
“Hmm?”
Noticing the commotion behind him, Tuberculosis Rabbit turned around to see this scene, his eyes flashed with panic as he stepped forward hurriedly, placing his finger under Yi’s nostrils to check, confirming his breathing was stable.
He then let out a sigh of relief.
It seemed that Yi must be tired from this map adventure.
But he still hesitated, even if tired, one shouldn’t just fall asleep like that.
Yet if it were fainting, the breathing was very stable.
For safety’s sake, it was still best to find a doctor to take a look.
…
“Where is this?”
As soon as Chen Yi opened his eyes, he heard a serious question next to his ear.
He didn’t speak but immediately looked around.
Inside a pure white house.
No more than fifty square meters or so, quite small.
Ten chairs were neatly arranged in the room, with him sitting in the middle one, and the other nine also occupied by people—the one who had asked the question was now sitting in the chair farthest to the right.
Ten chairs lined up in a row.
Chen Yi glanced around and saw that everyone’s bodies were pixilated as if covered in mosaic, not just obscuring faces, but making it difficult to discern even gender.
He then looked up at his own head.
His title had vanished as well.
He could clearly see his own body, however.
Having his answer, Chen Yi didn’t speak; instead, he sat with a complex expression on his face, staring straight ahead.
He hadn’t expected that a D-grade prop would give him the chance to see his own future.
The ten people here were likely all pulled in by that silver-plated black card.
Apart from the player who sat on the far right starting with a question, no one else spoke; one could only faintly sense other players continuously scrutinizing the surrounding people.
As for facial expressions, those were completely invisible.
It was as if everyone was heavily pixelated.
Besides the ten of them, there was nothing else in the room.
Not even a speck of dust in the corners, it was so clean that it didn’t look like a real house.
And then—
A line of red characters suddenly appeared on the wall in front. Find exclusive stories on empire
“Welcome to Life Cinema.”
“As you have seen on the silver card, here you can watch your future.”
“This prop is limited to 100 pieces worldwide, and we hope all players have a pleasant viewing journey.”
Chen Yi’s eyelids drooped slightly as he scanned the red text on the wall and did not speak, instead, he began to wait patiently.
It seemed it wouldn’t just show scenes of his future—the visions of the other players in the room would also be shown on the big screen.
And then—
A player sitting in a chair asked a question.
“Does this mean that other players present will also see my future visions?”
“Has privacy been considered?”
It was a woman’s voice.
Sounding around 35 years old, probably unmarried, possibly a senior executive of a listed company, her voice carried an air of decisiveness.
How one could discern marital status from a voice was completely an intuitive guess.
After all, these career-dominant women often stay single, rarely finding a man who meets their standards.
Chen Yi made a quick mental estimate in his mind.
Following that,
New red text once again emerged on the wall.
“The film will now begin.”
Completely ignoring the woman’s question, it was unclear whether the lack of response was due to an absence of intelligence or simply reluctance to reply.

chapters.title: Chapter 99 - 99 - 98: "This presumptuous world is somewhat unwelcome.
chapters.content:
Chapter 99 – 98: “This presumptuous world is somewhat unwelcome.
As the line of red characters on the wall disappeared,
a scene gradually emerged from the wall.
The perspective seemed to be from the sky, as if a camera had been mounted high above. Experience more on empire
Passing through the clouds, the buildings on the ground started to become distinct and visible, standing on the land like miniatures of a city.
With the viewpoint swiftly advancing, a man standing on the ground also became increasingly clear.
“Charge, for fuck’s sake!!!”
A piercing roar suddenly rang out in the scene, where a man with his upper body bare, covered in blood, was seen holding a large knife, standing amidst a sea of corpses, launching a final attack on the enemies surrounding him!
Under his feet lay countless human corpses.
And surrounding him were an innumerable amount of monsters, resembling praying mantises over two meters tall, their sharp arm blades casually swinging through the air, producing ear-piercing sounds as they sliced through it.
There were easily a few hundred monsters encircling this man, and the corpses beneath his feet testified to the many people who once stood here, yet now, he stood alone, the last one standing!
As that roar filled with despair and unwillingness to give in echoed, the man charged toward the closest monster for one last attack!
“Sizzle!”
Almost as soon as he had lifted his front foot, his body was instantly pierced by numerous arm blades, blood continuously streaming from his mouth, the glint in his eyes gradually fading, and the arm that held his knife aloft slowly fell.
Dead.
He died just like that.
“I… died in the future?”
A man inside the room looked at this scene, his eyes showing a trace of bewilderment, mumbling to himself dazedly, “Though in this shitty world, it’s not unusual to die.”
“It’s just that watching oneself die is still kind of strange.”
“I’ve never seen these kinds of monsters before, are they something that will appear in the future?”
The other players in the room heard the man’s voice, their expressions complex as they looked toward him, seemingly recognizing the man in the scene.
This feeling, like watching one’s future self in a cinema, was indeed odd.
–
The scene shifted once more.
“Hide the women and children, the rest of you, follow me!!”
A group of soldiers dressed in uniform, carrying firearms and looking anxious, crowded inside a supermarket, and a middle-aged man at the forefront was loudly giving commands while outside, it seemed like there were many monsters, with continuous firing and gunshot sounds.
Everywhere around were roars and the terrifying screams of monsters.
The people in the scene were hurriedly hiding women and children in the supermarket’s fruit cooling storage, turning off the air conditioning, and securing the anti-theft steel doors.
After a hasty headcount of those remaining, they exchanged glances, and together they roared as they rushed towards the outside of the supermarket!
These people were clearly trapped by the monsters inside this supermarket, perhaps thinking of temporarily hiding the women and children here, then going out to find reinforcements before coming back for them.
Or maybe they thought of going out to attract the attention of the monsters so that the women and children could survive.
From the few short sentences, it was impossible to discern any specific information.
All one knew was that not long after those people rushed out, there was no more sound from them, followed by countless mantis-like monsters breaking into the supermarket doors and windows, swarming in.
In the end, they gathered around the fruit cooling storage door where the women had been hidden.
Supermarkets typically have cooling storages made of solid steel, considered one of the more durable places of refuge within them.
However…
Under the sharp arm blades of those monsters, it was easily breached, followed by the desperate cries of the women and the sounds of monsters feasting.
“That man in the front, that’s me.”
The man sitting on the far left spoke solemnly, “When does this future take place? At the very least, I should know the time of my death, right?”
No one responded.
The wall remained silent, with no blood-red lettering emerging.
–
The scene shifted once again.
“I’ll do it.”
At the edge of a city wall littered with monster corpses in one corner, a young man in a floral shirt and beach shorts, covered in blood, searched through his pockets for a while, then grinned at the middle-aged man beside him.
“What’s with that look on your face?”
“It’s nothing, without Yi, living doesn’t hold much meaning for me.”
“I’ve wanted to die for a long time, if it weren’t for worrying that my death would reduce our fighting power and make everyone’s situation even more critical, I’d have gone down to join Yi long ago.”
“You don’t understand, Yi would be very lonely without me.”
“I’m out of cigarettes, give me one to smoke first. My biggest obsession in life has been making sure I have a cigarette before I die. For this, I deliberately practiced hard for a long time, so that my entire smoking process, from lighting up to taking a drag, takes only 0.7 seconds.”
“Thanks.”
Afterwards, the young man was seen taking a cigarette from the middle-aged man’s hand, lighting it up in his mouth, and after taking a deep breath, looked into the horizon through the haze of the light blue smoke with a bloodied, distant expression.
After pausing for a while, he looked down and began to laugh.
“This presumptuous world, it’s not quite likable.”
The next second—
The young man in the scene suddenly burst into intense light, without a hint of hesitation, he leaped straight down from the city wall, aiming directly at the group of monsters gathered in the corner!
“Heavenly Split!”
Immediately following, the scene changed once again, presenting a new image.
Chen Yi, seated in the chair, had his pupils abruptly contract, his back rigid, a cold light continuously flashing in his eyes as he forcibly suppressed the shock in his heart.
The young man in the image, calling out for Yi, was none other than Tuberculosis Rabbit!
That floral shirt and beach shorts, he still remembered; it was a beach holiday set that Tuberculosis Rabbit had bought not long ago, and he was still wearing that outfit!
Only, Tuberculosis Rabbit in the image looked much older, his body covered in blood and scars, his figure emanating a sense of world-weariness and exhaustion.
Was Tuberculosis Rabbit destined to die in the future?
And what did that phrase in the image mean, mentioning something after Yi’s death?
What did this mean? Was he destined to die in battle, to die before Tuberculosis Rabbit?
Chen Yi, his expression slightly ugly, sat in the chair without speaking.
In the image, Tuberculosis Rabbit had no title above his head; it seemed the titles above the characters’ heads in the image were hidden, but the Claw Knife that Tuberculosis Rabbit was carrying before he jumped was all too familiar!
Just then—
A familiar voice from within the image snapped Chen Yi back from his drifting thoughts, prompting him to look up at the scene unfolding on the wall in front of him once more.
“Without me, Sword Without End, the path of the sword would endure an eternal night.”
“That saying, it’s really cool.”
In the scene was a middle-aged man in green standing on some Wasteland, his head bowed in abstraction as he tenderly stroked the Three-Foot Qingfeng in his hand, with the gentleness of a bridegroom on a wedding night caressing his beloved bride.
The ground at his feet was a glaring, blood-red.
Around him were scattered corpses, carelessly strewn about, neglected by all.
Behind him, a large number of humans cried and screamed in fear as they ran backward, while in front of him loomed the over-two-meters-tall creatures of the Insect Race, their bodies covering the sky like mantises, carrying an overwhelming stench of blood.
A single glance.
They were as dense as the sea, matching the expanse of the Heavenly Water in their uniformity.
These pitch-black creatures seemed to blend into the night itself, rushing forward with a suffocating sense of terror.
“That’s right.”
“This is it, exactly.”
As if suddenly awakened, a glint of clarity flashed in the eyes of the middle-aged man. He looked up, shifting his gaze from the Three-Foot Qingfeng to the swarm of creatures charging at him like a tide, and he chuckled lightly.
“This sword will be remembered by the world.”
The next second—
The man’s head was suddenly encircled by a mass of dark clouds, making the entire scene even more gloomy. Accompanying the middle-aged man’s gesture of pointing the Green Peak toward the sky, countless Thunder Dragons surged madly within the dark clouds.
“Sword, come forth!”
As soon as the words were spoken—
The Thunder Dragons from within the dark clouds began converging into the Green Peak in the man’s hand, with a torrent of lightning striking the sword like a downpour!
Immediately after—
A swath of Sword Qi, infused with thunder and lightning and extending tens of thousands of miles, shot rapidly into the crowd of creatures ahead!
The creatures that had been surging like a tide were now chopped into chunks of corpse, littering the ground, each severed at the waist; the countless blood painted the Wasteland beneath an even more vivid scarlet.
In one strike, the field was cleared!
But in just a matter of seconds, the horizon filled once again with an overwhelming number of creatures, charging towards the middle-aged man with frenzied speed atop the bodies of their kind.
“Hmm, not bad.”
The man gazed at his handiwork with satisfaction, swayed unsteadily as if weakened, disregarding the onslaught of creatures rushing towards him. Instead, he turned to look at the crowd that had already run far away.
He propped himself up with one hand on the hilt of the Green Peak, planted in the ground, preventing his body from falling.
Taking out a cigarette from his bosom, he lit it and put it to his lips; after taking a deep drag, he exhaled a puff of smoke, then suddenly started laughing as if something came to mind.
“Come to think of it, some kid once said to me, something about having a cigarette before dying,”
“That it would make life perfect, like a complete ending.”
“Makes some sense when you think about it.”
“Really cool, it’s a shame the kid didn’t see this scene, kind of a waste.”
The man flicked the cigarette butt away.
Before the glowing, blood-red ember of the cigarette butt could touch the ground, the emerging tide of creatures engulfed it.
–
“…”
Chen Yi stared emotionlessly at the scene on the wall without speaking. He knew the person in the image; it was Sword Without End!
The kid Sword Without End was referring to must have been Tuberculosis Rabbit, who had a fixation on smoking a cigarette before dying.
Though Tuberculosis Rabbit talked a lot, he wasn’t the kind who couldn’t keep his mouth shut about everything; not many people knew of this particular obsession, and it seemed that barring himself, no one else knew either.
That Sword Without End knew this detail meant—
Did it mean they would have more interactions with Sword Without End in the future, and that their relationship seemed quite good?
After all, if they weren’t that close, Sword Without End likely wouldn’t know about Tuberculosis Rabbit’s little obsession.
But… had this person also died in the future?
So far, it appeared the scenes on the wall all ended in death.
–

chapters.title: Chapter 100 - 100 - 99: "These symptoms are exactly the same as those of the people I’ve knocked out before!
chapters.content:
Chapter 100 – 99: “These symptoms are exactly the same as those of the people I’ve knocked out before!
The scene abruptly changed again.
“Hehe.”
In the bloodstained frame, a burly man took the petite, unconscious girl off his shoulder and placed her in front of the young man lying gravely injured on the ground: “Yi, I leave her to you.”
“And there’s this.”
With somewhat slurred speech, the strong man pulled a cigarette case from his shirt pocket and, scratching his head with a hint of embarrassment, said, “When I get a tomb of my own, bury this with me.”
“I’m heading off first.”
Having said that, the brawny man walked toward the cave exit, and the scene seemed to be set within a gloomy cave.
About several minutes later, it went silent outside.
The young man, who was injured and leaning against the cave wall, stayed quiet for a while before struggling to his feet with the wall’s support, looking back at the few people behind him: “I’ll go have a look. You take her and go.”
At that moment, the girl seemed to awaken, her eyes barely open and her voice weak.
“I’ll go with you.”
Explore stories at empire
“You follow them to find Tuberculosis Rabbit.”
“No.”
The scene flashed away once more, and a new scene emerged.
…
Meanwhile, Chen Yi sat in his chair, eyes filled with shock, utterly unable to calm his mind as he stared intently at the screen on the wall—even though a new scene had already appeared, he didn’t look away.
What he had just seen replayed continuously in his mind.
Tie Chui, Jiaye… and himself!
The man lying injured on the ground was none other than him.
The face was identical to his own, with only the clothes being unfamiliar to him.
To witness himself undergoing a sequence of events he had no memory of gave him a strong sense of unreality and absurdity.
He was desperate to know how that scene would continue!
But just after Jiaye’s words, that scene abruptly ended.
Tuberculosis Rabbit said he died.
Did he die there?
Die alongside Jiaye?
Was he already with Jiaye in that scene?
He had a vague idea that Jiaye seemed to have feelings for him, but he had absolutely no interest in Jiaye.
It wasn’t that Jiaye didn’t fit his aesthetic.
Rather, he just hadn’t thought about starting a relationship at all; he couldn’t imagine what life would be like with a lover, accustomed as he was to having Tuberculosis Rabbit with him all the time.
Suddenly introducing someone new.
It would leave him feeling at a loss, unsure how to deal with it.
Furthermore, they had only met a few times; nothing substantial had even happened between them. He couldn’t fathom where Jiaye’s thoughts were coming from.
Was he separated from Tuberculosis Rabbit in that scene?
Impossible!
Ever since meeting Tuberculosis Rabbit, they had never been apart, rarely acting alone. They had grown accustomed to each other’s presence, and he even felt uncomfortable eating alone.
How could he possibly separate from Tuberculosis Rabbit under such dangerous circumstances and instead be with Tie Chui and Jiaye, along with several strangers he didn’t recognize?
And the cigarette case in Tie Chui’s hand in that scene looked oddly familiar.
He had heard Jiaye mention that Tie Chui would put the cigarettes he gave him into a case and keep it in his shirt pocket—he had seen it a few times.
The future he saw induced a subconscious resistance within him; he found it hard to accept that Tuberculosis Rabbit could die so easily.
He somewhat struggled to accept that the acquaintances he had made these days would all die one after another before him.
At that moment, a discussion suddenly started inside the room.
“The man in that video just now… he looked like Chen Yi. I’ve seen his face when he appeared globally last time.”
“It must be him. That strong man also called him Yi. But who would have thought that even Chen Yi could die in the future?”
“Is Yi also in this room with us?”
“If even Chen Yi might die in the future, how are we supposed to survive?”
The scenes kept changing on the wall.
Although the ten players within the room looked distressed as they watched the continuously shifting scenes, up until now, it seemed their fates in the movie were all death.
Finally.
Who knows how much time passed.
The scenes slowly came to a halt.
Red text once again emerged on the wall.
“This screening has come to an end, players will return to the real world in 10 seconds.”
“The outcomes depicted are not necessarily the players’ fate. Players need not worry too much, as there are many ways to die in this world. The movie merely displayed one possible death you might encounter.”
“The screening is over, farewell to all.”
And then——
A flash of white suddenly crossed Chen Yi’s vision, and when he awoke, the surroundings were once again familiar. It was his rented room, the same messy bed.
And there he was, lying on the bed, with Tuberculosis Rabbit’s voice sounding slightly anxious and angry nearby.
“You’re telling me you fell asleep?”
“Do you freaking believe I can twist your head off and kick it around like a soccer ball? How the hell couldn’t I wake you up when I shouted, and you’re telling me you were asleep? Show me how you sleep like that.”
“You clearly looked just like those people I’ve knocked out before!”
“Big Brother…”
Immediately after, a middle-aged man’s voice, tinged with a cry, rang out, “He’s really just asleep, his breathing is steady, heart rate is normal, and pulse is fine; it has nothing to do with shock or fainting.”
“Okay.”
Chen Yi sat up from the bed, scanned the room, and looked towards Tuberculosis Rabbit and a middle-aged man who had appeared at some point, somewhat absent-mindedly waving his hand.
“I’m fine, Tuberculosis Rabbit. See the guests out.”
“Yi, you’re awake!”
A glint of surprise flashed in Tuberculosis Rabbit’s eyes, then he gave the middle-aged man beside him a kick out of the doorway and scurried to take out two dishes from the microwave and place them on the table.
“It’s good that you’re okay; you really were just asleep. It seems like the map this time was indeed exhausting.”
“Our upstairs neighbor just brought down two dishes, said they made it themselves, for us to eat.”
“I let them taste it first, no poison.”
“I’ve been keeping it warm in the microwave, Yi, you should come down and try it soon, one dish of stir-fried pork with chili and one of shredded potatoes, tsk tsk, truly luxurious.”
“I haven’t had such hot dishes in a long time.”
“I also steamed a pot of rice, Yi, get up, I’ll go serve some.”
“Hmm.”
Chen Yi nodded, climbed out of bed, looked towards the blazing sun hanging mid-air outside the window, rubbed his slightly sore neck, shook his head, and spoke, “How long have I slept?”
“Over four hours, I think.”
That long?
He silently recited to himself, stood up, stretched without saying anything by the window, and felt that he had spent less than an hour in the Life Cinema, yet four hours had passed outside.
And it was different from entering the map.
He wasn’t physically present there.
Was it consciousness viewing?
He glanced down at the personal panel chat channel where Jiaye had sent a message.
“Jiaye”: “Yi, haven’t you come out from the map yet? My brother has already finished the competition. My brother took first place and earned the title of King Malphite, isn’t that great?”
“Jiaye”: “The Children’s Day limited event is about to end, Yi, haven’t you come out yet?”
“Jiaye”: “That old man who came to buy costumes from you last time, he came to Yancheng yesterday looking for you, said there was a map with high difficulty, wanted to invite you to join, but he didn’t find you so he came looking for me, I was worried he might have ill intentions towards you, so I just said I didn’t know where you were.”
“Jiaye”: “It’s been 10 days, Yi, you haven’t had an accident, have you?”
“Jiaye”: “…”
Chen Yi looked at the messages Jiaye had sent in the chat box with a complicated expression, silent without speaking. Originally, he had no particular feelings about Jiaye, but the scenes he saw about Jiaye in the Life Cinema.
There was suddenly a strange feeling inside.
Someone who could die alongside him was, at the very least, not malicious towards him.
But then again.
Why would he die there?
He had a Christmas sleigh, after all; with just one activation, he could go anywhere under the sky, so how could he be trapped in a cave?
And Jiaye and Tie Chui, don’t they have a combo move?
With their combo move, how could they be trapped in a cave with him? It made no sense.
Unless… there was some rule in that cave?
A rule that restricted their moves?
Or had they fallen into some trap, a curse that rendered their vehicles unusable?
Chen Yi shook his head without understanding, but he silently noted this event, planning to avoid caves in the future as much as possible.
“Dinner is served, Yi.”
Just then—
Tuberculosis Rabbit’s voice pulled Chen Yi back from his thoughts.
“Yi, why do you seem a little distracted since you woke up?”
“It’s nothing.”
Chen Yi shook his head, walked over to the dining table, pulled out a chair to sit down, and then reached out with chopsticks to pick up a shred of potato and put it into his mouth.
“This doesn’t taste bad at all. Why did the family upstairs suddenly think to send us dishes?”
“They were just the first.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit helplessly pointed to the pile of gifts at the doorway: “Maybe because they knew I accepted the two dishes from the upstairs neighbor, after that, almost every family one after another came to bring us gifts.”
“Just for cigarettes, we received over twenty packs, and it’ll last us a really long time now. They’re all nice cigarettes that we couldn’t afford before.”
“If I hadn’t put up a notice at the door saying that we are not accepting gifts, I reckon people would still be coming to give more.”
“Hmm, let’s eat first, and then come out with me after we finish.”
“Alright.”
Chen Yi picked up another piece with his chopsticks and into his mouth, then started to check the system messages he hadn’t received while inside the map.
The June 1st Children’s Day event lasted only for three days and had already ended.
There were quite a few rewards quietly lying in his system notification bar, waiting for him to check them out.
…
PS: Thanks to the boss ’Riddle_’ for rewarding another Silver Alliance leadership, thank you, boss, so magnificent! These two days there will be an extra update for the boss!
Don’t dare to reward the Silver Alliance, not at all, I’m already content with two leaders, boss, please don’t be impulsive!
By the way, just reporting performance, this book passed ten thousand average orders a few days ago, forgot to mention, it’s also kind of a milestone, thank everyone for the support.

chapters.title: Chapter 101 - 101 - 100: "Murder? That’s too easy.
chapters.content:
Chapter 101 – 100: “Murder? That’s too easy.
“Ding, you’ve topped the list in the June Children’s Day special event, earning the globally unique event-limited title—Godly Rich Gentleman.”
“Godly Rich Gentleman?”
Chen Yi nodded thoughtfully after seeing this title and then turned his attention to the title he had obtained in the wilderness map.
「Title Name」: The True Wilderness.
「Title Level」: Blue.
「Title Effect」: When you stab a dagger into a tree, fresh Sour Plum Soup will flow out of it, entering a 24-hour cooldown period after use.
「Obtaining Method」: Fell over 90% of the pine trees on the wilderness map.
This title might seem somewhat useless, but actually, it does have a certain use.
At the very least, should they one day urgently need water, this title could save their lives.
Of course, that’s assuming there are trees available.
Only then did he turn his attention to this newly acquired title.
「Title Name」: Godly Rich Gentleman.
「Title Level」: Red.
「Title Effect」: All your expenses will receive a 10% discount.
「Obtaining Method」: Secure the top spot in the Son of a Noble ranking during the June 1st Children’s Day limited event.
The effect of this title is quite nice.
All future expenses would be discounted by 10%. It might not seem useful in the short term, but in the long run, the benefits are definitely significant.
Chen Yi picked up a mouthful of spicy pork with his chopsticks and swiftly went through all the unread system notifications.
Then he lifted his head to look at Tuberculosis Rabbit.
“I’m full. Hurry up and eat; we need to go out after you’re done.”
“Oh.”
After gobbling up a quick bite of rice, Tuberculosis Rabbit looked up at Chen Yi with a puzzled expression and mumbled unclearly, “By the way, Yi, do you know what just happened to you?”
“Why did you sleep so long?”
“It’s nothing,”
Chen Yi shook his head calmly and said, “Just eat your meal.”
Then he stopped talking.
Discussing it seemed meaningless, after all, the Theater of Life was merely like watching a play.
If the scenes depicted inside the theater represented his destined ending, then this prop wouldn’t just be a simple D-rank prop.
What puzzled him was this.
There were nine other players in the room, and the movie showed each of these nine players, but why mosaic the players sitting in the room and not the ones on screen?
What’s the point of putting a mosaic there?
He didn’t understand.
But if you don’t consider any conspiracy theories and just look at it from an entertainment perspective, this D-rank prop is still very worthwhile because the sensation of seeing oneself as the protagonist in a movie is quite unique.
Especially when he had no memory of it, probably very few people in the world could have such an experience.
However, at that moment—
A notification suddenly sounded in his ear.
「Ding, player Zhou Ping has forcefully invited you to join the D-rank map ’Insect Tide Attack’. Please prepare yourself, as you will be forcibly teleported in ten minutes.’
Upon seeing this notification,
Chen Yi was slightly startled, frowning without saying a word, remembering this Zhou Ping.
He was the one who suddenly rose on the Global Vehicle Leaderboard, said he wanted to commemorate his 30-day anniversary with his girlfriend, and then asked Chen Yi to relinquish first place.
Chen Yi had ignored him.
There was no further action from that person afterward, but he didn’t expect him to suddenly show up now.
“What a nuisance,”
Chen Yi looked at the pop-up notification with slight dissatisfaction. He had just come out of the wilderness map, and now he wasn’t even given a day to rest?
Is it even possible to forcefully invite somebody into a map?
He wondered if it was due to some prop or another.
If everyone could force him into a map, he would end up staying there all day, without any time to sleep.
Read new chapters at empire
“I’ve got to step out for a bit.”
Chen Yi looked up at Tuberculosis Rabbit, “Someone’s pulling me into a map by force. I’m not sure how long I’ll be gone, so just to be safe, you go find Jiaye and the others until I’m back.”
“If anything unexpected happens, Jiaye and Tie Chui’s abilities should help you flee quickly.”
“Um…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit swallowed his mouthful of rice with a slightly strange expression, “Was it Zhou Ping who forcibly invited you into this ’Insect Tide Attack’ map?”
“You got dragged in too?”
“Yes…”
“Heh.”
A flicker of cold light passed through Chen Yi’s eyes, “So they think they can corner us and wipe us out in one fell swoop, huh?”
“Very well.”
The ten minutes passed by quickly.
With the sound of the system notification, Chen Yi and his companion disappeared from their room, and when they opened their eyes again, they were atop a city wall.
The wall, around seven to eight meters tall, seemed to be made of mud bricks and didn’t look particularly strong.
The edges of the city wall were pockmarked with bloodstains, evidencing numerous brutal battles.
The sky was dark.
Massive clouds loomed overhead, adding a sense of oppression, the wind howled past their ears, and their clothes flapped harshly.
The air also had a hard-to-stand, fishy stench.
Standing on the edge of the wall, Chen Yi looked at the scene before him, his pupils shrinking sharply. This scene… he had just seen it in the Theater of Life. In the movie, Tuberculosis Rabbit died right here.
The sky was the same, the wall was the same, and the name of the map, Insect Tide, was right on point.
Did that mean that Tuberculosis Rabbit would die on this map?
Impossible!
But he quickly let out a sigh of relief. It only looked broadly similar at first glance—on closer inspection, there were many differences.
For example, the walls in the movie weren’t made of mud bricks, and they weren’t this short either; they were much taller.
And the scene in the movie didn’t look like it was set on any kind of map, it looked more like it took place on Blue Star.
Before he could observe any further,
there was a prompt in his ear.
“Ding, welcome players to the Insect Race Invasion map. Please listen carefully to the map rules.”
“This map is a tower defense map.”
“Players need to hold the wall at their feet and prevent the creatures of the Insect Race from climbing over the wall and destroying the Activation Point behind it.”
“If the Activation Point is destroyed, then all players die.”
“There are ten waves of monsters from the Insect Race. Please work together, players.”
“After successfully clearing the map, rewards will be given based on the number of monsters killed by the players.”
“Within this map, players cannot attack each other.”
