“The first wave of monsters from the Insect Race will arrive in 5 minutes.”
The rules were simple.
No, to be precise, they were too simple—so simple that they could be read in a few seconds, with nothing that needed special attention.
Chen Yi furrowed his brows, staring at the rules without saying a word.
He had originally thought Zhou Ping forcefully pulled him into this map because he held a grudge and was preparing to make a move against him, but the map rules clearly stated that players couldn’t attack each other.
So what was the point of Zhou Ping pulling him in?
Just to clear the map together with him?
Just then—
A voice full of mockery and provocation rang out beside Chen Yi’s ear.
“Tsk tsk tsk, let’s see who we have here. Isn’t this our very own Chen Yi, the big brother who spends his wealth so lavishly for the smile of a beautiful lady?”
“Why the frown? Do you think the map is challenging?”
“Or do you have some other thoughts?”
Chen Yi turned around expressionlessly and looked behind him, where he saw a pot-bellied middle-aged man with an arm around a woman and his other hand in his pocket, wearing a leather jacket.
At the moment, this middle-aged man was staring at him with a full face of provocation.
The woman huddled in the man’s arms, on the other hand, looked confidently amused as she watched him.
Behind the man,
there were three men with their arms folded, smirking in the same teasing manner, like a group of lackeys.
“Are you tired of living?”
Tuberculosis Rabbit turned and looked at the middle-aged man who had spoken, paused for a moment, and then suddenly laughed, “You’re not getting cocky just because players can’t attack each other in this map, are you?”
“What else?”
The middle-aged man shrugged provocatively with one hand still in his pocket and looked at Chen Yi with a sneer, “No need to look further. I’m not planning to kill you. Someone who can casually spend 300,000 Points, you definitely have more strength than me.”
“I surely can’t kill you.”
“But back then, I had called you big brother in front of all the global players, hoping you would let me have the top spot on the leaderboard, yet you didn’t give me any face.”
“You could’ve said something like, ’Little bro, I need the top spot, can you give me some compensation or something?’
“That way, you could have let me save face, right?”
“But you didn’t.”
“So many players around the world saw my embarrassment—it was very humiliating, you know?”
“I may not be able to kill you, but I can surely annoy you.”
“Today I’m going to make you experience what it feels like to be a dog.”
“See that Activation Point?”
The middle-aged man pointed towards a red hexagonal gemstone about one meter high, standing behind the wall. He smiled somewhat proudly, and his pudgy belly trembled.
“In a few minutes, the monsters will spawn, and they will charge at the wall.”
“And you will have to stop all these monsters, otherwise they will destroy the Activation Point, and then we both will die.”
“During this time, we won’t lift a finger; we’ll just enjoy the show.”
“How about it?”
“Imagine clearing the map while carrying the most annoying people with you—doesn’t that feel irritating?”
“Although you want to tear us to pieces, you still have to get through the map with us to survive. How does that feel?”
“Hahahaha!!!”
The man couldn’t help but laugh arrogantly and excitedly, but his expression quickly turned cold, “Of course, if you refuse to be treated like a dog, just let the monsters destroy the Activation Point.”
“We’ll die together.”
“Just one thing—”
“Do you dare?”
Then he turned his head to the woman in his arms and fondly stroked her nose, “See? This is what you call a direct strategy.”
“Killing someone? That’s too easy.”
“This kind of overt, unavoidable scheme, this is the wisdom passed down by our ancestors.”

chapters.title: Chapter 102 - 102 - 101: "Looking at the situation, is the map difficulty not small?
chapters.content:
Chapter 102 – 101: “Looking at the situation, is the map difficulty not small?
And at this moment—
In the distance, one could already see the swarm of Insect Race monsters pouring in like a tide, carrying with them a pungent stench that drifted toward the group.
Sand and dust filled the sky, spreading into the air.
Outside the city wall was the Wasteland, with cracked ground and brown, dried bloodstains everywhere.
The city wall they were facing measured about 10 meters in length.
The other three walls were of the same size, but they were unguarded, with no Insect Race monsters charging at them.
It seemed that this map didn’t require players to defend the three walls, only the one beneath their feet.
The map rules were simple.
But not without things that could give one a headache.
There were a total of 7 players in this map.
Aside from them, there was Zhou Ping and his group.
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit glanced strangely at the middle-aged man next to her and spoke in a low voice, “Yi, are they not right in the head? Isn’t the reward on this map based on the number of monsters players kill?”
“Aren’t they just handing us rewards by doing this?”
“Why are they so happy?”
“Is there something wrong with their brains?”
“Let’s not worry about them for now.”
Chen Yi glanced at Zhou Ping and his group, then stopped talking and turned his gaze to the beast swarm charging toward them in the distance. The urgent matter at hand was to deal with these monsters.
As for Zhou Ping, let him jump around for a while.
Since the map didn’t allow players to attack each other, there wasn’t much he could do.
However, there might be some rule loopholes he could exploit, like throwing Zhou Ping into the swarm of monsters and letting the creatures attack him. He wondered whether that would count as player-on-player violence.
But he still didn’t plan to try it, in case there were any unknown penalties, which would be very unfortunate.
Moreover, he had a better plan in mind.
If he couldn’t attack on the map, then simply don’t attack. He could always attack on Blue Star, right?
What does the concept of a sleigh at a speed of a thousand kilometers per hour imply?
If he wished, he could arrive at any location on Blue Star in no time at all.
That was the idea.
After he got out, he would just find the person and take care of him then.
People who jumped around like this might cause trouble in the future, so it was better to deal with them sooner rather than later. Unbeknownst to Zhou Ping at the moment, Chen Yi had already begun to silently start a countdown on his life.
For now, it was okay to let the other side have a little advantage in talk.
After all, the words of the dying are always kind.
There was no time for further delay.
By this time, the Insect Race monsters were already less than a few hundred meters from the city walls.
The crimson Frozen Throne rose, and armored soldiers lined the walls like guards, swiftly filling it.
Meanwhile, not far away, Zhou Ping and his companions exchanged glances, sneered, then jumped behind the wall, sitting near the Activation Point, ready to enjoy the show.
Luxuriating in others’ work was simply too enjoyable not to do.
The monsters quickly charged up the wall, but were all chopped down one by one by the armored soldiers.
Without emotion, without fear, with strict military discipline.
If these armored soldiers were in the era of cold weapons, they would have been the most perfect defense force, second to none.
And these monsters were not like the two-meter tall mantis-like creatures seen in movies; instead, they resembled grasshoppers, not very tall at just a few centimeters, but long in shape.
They could easily leap onto the wall by stepping on their comrades’ heads, due to their good jumping ability.
Their bellies were snow white.
A single cut would spill cheesy, sticky, milky fat into the air, even stretching into threads.
The black armor of the armored soldiers was getting stained white.
There was no pressure at all.
Even though there were quite a number of monsters, they could not break the defense of the armored soldiers. At first glance, they seemed terrifying, but upon a closer encounter, one would realize that aside from their leaping ability, their methods of attack were very singular.
The armored soldiers filling the walls were more than enough to keep the creatures at bay.
Chen Yi, sitting on the Frozen Throne, leaned back in his seat, eyelids drooping as he feigned sleep to recover his vital energy. Although he hadn’t done much in the Wasteland map, he was still there.
And had been pulled into this map by Zhou Ping right after coming out.
So he was a bit tired.
Now was as good a time as any to get some rest.
In front of his Frozen Throne were the armored soldiers, ready to take the lead if necessary.
…
“A summoning prop, huh?” Read exclusive content at empire
The middle-aged man standing near the Activation Point, his pupils flashing with a cold light, looked at the armored soldiers on the wall, and his heart sank a little.
It seemed that Chen Yi indeed didn’t need him at all to speed-run this map alone.
He had fantasized that if Chen Yi couldn’t hold out and came to beg for his help, he would take the opportunity to insult Chen Yi to regain his own face.
But now it was clear that he wasn’t needed at all.
Chen Yi was stronger than he had thought.
The individual combat power of those armored soldiers was even greater than some players, and because they lacked emotions, they could perform to an even greater extent, fighting to the death.
Indeed, someone who could casually toss out 300,000 Points was not someone he could afford to provoke.
He felt regret for a moment, a hint of gloom flashed through his eyes as he hesitated and stood silently without speaking.
To stir up such a person for the sake of face, was it a bit irrational?
“Honey, he hasn’t even glanced at you from beginning to end.”
At this moment, the woman who was curled up in his arms suddenly complained, “He’s outright looking down on you, old man.”
The man who was about to soften instantly turned cold upon hearing this, looking at Chen Yi’s figure on the city wall and scoffed, “Right, they look down on us, let this expert lead us through the level then.”
“After all, as long as we clear the level, there’ll be clearance rewards, it’d be foolish not to take the freebies.”
“This feeling of someone working for us is quite nice, huh.”
“Come on, don’t just stand there.”
The man pulled out a deck of playing cards from his embrace and sat down cross-legged on the spot, “Got nothing better to do, let’s play some Fight the Landlord.”
“Pair of threes!”
“Pair of fours!”
…
“Hmm.”
The Tuberculosis Rabbit, perched on the edge of the parapet, looked down at the man below and said in a calm voice, “Black Trench City’s accent, I’ve picked it up; they don’t distinguish between their rolled and curled tongues when they speak.”
“Eighty percent from Black Trench City, twenty percent from the villages around Black Trench City.”
“But being able to find some lackeys, eighty percent chance he’s from the city.”
“After all, a figure capable of hitting the Global Vehicle Leaderboard should have some renown even in Black Trench City, just ask around there, and it should be easy to find out.”
“Hmm.”
Chen Yi, leaning on the throne with drooping eyelids, said nonchalantly, “I’ll take a stroll to Black Trench City later, just to walk off the meal I just had.”
The first wave of monsters was quickly slaughtered to the last.
After a five-minute break,
the second wave of monsters arrived.
The voices of Zhou Ping and others behind the wall grew louder and louder, full of sarcasm towards someone, nearly calling names directly—perhaps because the map’s regulations stated players couldn’t attack each other, they spoke with exceptional volume.
Chen Yi glanced at the time.
It was now August 11, a little past 6 PM.
Their meal had been at 6 PM, since the June regulations required three meals a day per person: one at 8 AM, noon, and 6 PM.
They’d have to sleep from 9 PM to 10 PM.
Finding Zhou Ping and the others after leaving the map would be a bit challenging.
But fortunately, Black Trench City wasn’t too far from Yancheng.
If they were quick, they should manage to make it in time.
This map might indeed be challenging for the average player, but for Chen Yi, who possessed the Frozen Throne, facing this sort of wave assault would just cost a handful of Points to resolve everything.
And he wasn’t exactly short on Points now; the Wasteland map had given him quite a lot.
Moreover, summoning a heavy-armored soldier only cost 10 Points, so the cost wasn’t very high.
Before long,
Chen Yi and the others faced the 10th wave of monsters, and from start to finish, not a single monster had crossed the wall to reach the Activation Point.
As the map neared its end,
Zhou Ping, sitting near the Activation Point on the ground, suddenly stood up, his face cold as he stated word by word, “This matter isn’t over.”
“I gave you face, and you didn’t want it.”
“Since you don’t want it, then we’ll play this out slowly.”
“Don’t worry, you’ll hear my name again soon, I have plenty of time to play with you.”
No sooner had his voice faded,
than a notification sounded in everyone’s ears.
「Ding, congratulations to all players for successfully resisting 10 waves of monsters, rewards will now be calculated…」
As the notification sounded,
Chen Yi and his companion felt a flash of white light before their eyes and when they came to their senses again, they were already back in their rented room.
It was now half-past seven.
Time for bed soon.
Chen Yi glanced at the rewards summary and prepared to activate the sled to head to Black Trench City.
But just as he arrived at the rooftop, he found a familiar figure squatting there.
“Sword Without End?”
Chen Yi raised an eyebrow with some surprise as he looked at Sword Without End squatting on the rooftop and only after a quick glance at his condition, he spoke, “Jiaye mentioned you were looking for me, saying we should tackle some map with a bit of difficulty next.”
“Judging from your state, this map is no walk in the park, right?”
At that moment, Sword Without End’s Tang suit was covered in bloodstains, and even his hair was a mess, like a crow’s nest, squatting by the edge of the rooftop with a creased cigarette between his fingers, his state looking somewhat downcast.
For someone like Sword Without End, who valued his image and face, it was inconceivable to appear before the public in such a disheveled state.
Unless there was something so pressing that he had no time to care about his appearance.
Sword Without End turned his head towards Chen Yi, his left eye covered with a bloodstained eyepatch, he stared directly at Chen Yi with a raspy voice, pronouncing each word clearly.
“This map is different.”
“Unlike any other map we’ve been to, unlike any you’ve been to.”
“Have you ever encountered other people inside any map you’ve been to before?”

chapters.title: Chapter 103 - 103 - 102: "The new mission is to kill a criminal, the criminal’s name... Li Bei.
chapters.content:
Chapter 103 – 102: “The new mission is to kill a criminal, the criminal’s name… Li Bei.
“Is there anyone else inside the map?”
Chen Yi frowned and pondered for a moment before speaking, “You mean players?”
“No.”
Sword Without End’s demeanor was evidently a bit off, his spirit somewhat wilted as he shook his head, tremblingly bringing a wrinkled cigarette to his lips and speaking with some weakness.
“You mean people other than players?”
“Do bosses count?”
Chen Yi remembered a theme park map they had encountered before, which featured a Little Demon who loved lollipops; that Little Demon even left him a card that, once activated, could summon the Little Demon to attack his enemies for him.
“No, I mean people other than bosses and players!”
“Haven’t seen any.”
Chen Yi shook his head, looked at the time, and said, “So what’s the situation? Spit it out, I’m in a hurry to go out and kill someone here. If I go later, there won’t be enough time; it’s almost time to sleep.”
“The day before yesterday, I went to a map that was quite difficult. I came to Yancheng to find you, but Jiaye said you weren’t there.”
“So I joined a few other high-level combat players to enter.”
“That map is huge… It’s the largest map I’ve ever seen, easily two or three times the size of Yancheng.”
A flicker of panic and fear surfaced in Sword Without End’s eyes. He took a deep drag of his cigarette, calmed his heart, and continued, “Actually, that map was a city.”
“A very bustling city with skyscrapers everywhere, most of them hundreds of stories tall, the whole city filled with neon signage.”
“There were also hovering cars, devices in the air specifically for traffic control, looking just like traffic lights.
“Countless hovering cars shuttled back and forth between the buildings.”
“There were many people on the streets, but many of them had cybernetic limbs, cybernetic eyes, arms, thighs, heads, or even whole bodies!”
“But these people walked on the streets without anyone nearby showing any signs of surprise; I even saw some people walking dogs that were mechanized.”
“Damn it, can you imagine someone walking a mechanized dog in the street?”
“And… ”
“Wait a second.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, keenly aware of the information in Sword Without End’s words, furrowed her eyebrows and spoke gravely, “You mean, the map you went to was a very bustling city, and in the city, there were… lots of people?”
“Who were these people?”
“Yes.”
Sword Without End took a deep breath before he began recounting, kneading his temples, “We initially thought those people were just NPCs in the map, as it’s quite normal to have some NPCs in maps.”
“Although we’d never seen NPCs in maps before, that doesn’t mean there can’t be NPCs.”
“We initially ignored those NPCs, as everyone was freely exchanging information about the mission and skills, since the map was difficult, we had to be serious.”
“But while we were exchanging information, we suddenly noticed something was off, those NPCs around us seemed to understand what we were saying, and they were all looking at us with strange eyes.”
“We then did some probing and to our astonishment, we discovered every single person in the city had extremely high intelligence; I found a tobacconist and tried to converse.”
“The owner could respond to me very smoothly, not at all like the intelligence an NPC of the map should have.”
“Can you, can you understand that feeling?”
“It wasn’t the feeling of being inside a map at all, but like crossing over, in that moment all of us had the sensation of having crossed into a strange world.”
“Do you know what this means?”
“Don’t rush, talk slowly.”
Chen Yi shook his head, interrupting Sword Without End’s narrative. He hadn’t liked Sword Without End much before, but after watching the video about Sword Without End in Theater of Life,
he felt a faint increase in affection for the middle-aged man who cared about his image.
At the very least, a man willing to sacrifice himself to buy time for others to escape couldn’t have a bad heart.
“What’s the map’s clearance mission? What level is the map?”
“There’s no level.”
“That map is called the ’Pioneer Map’; it doesn’t have an ABCD rank system. The clearance mission requires us to go to the slums and destroy a signal transmitter held by a beggar.”
“Then escape to a designated activation point.”
“There were 9 players in total who entered the map, and only 5 players came out alive, each of them heavily injured.”
“To be precise, 4 players were killed on the spot, and 1 player was captured alive.”
“But the map rules clearly stated that any player not reaching the escape point within the designated time would be wiped out, so that captured player’s chances are slim.”
“After killing the beggar, shortly after destroying the signal transmitter he had, unmanned drones suddenly hovered above us, followed by a shrill alarm.”
“Then seven or eight hovering cars chasing us with sirens blaring.”
“The drones even extended a Gatling gun below and began firing at us.”
“And the escape point was on the other side of the slums; with no other choice, we scattered and fled towards the slums, luckily, I had Traceless Green Peak which allowed me to escape quickly to the evacuation point.”
“Yet even so, I was seriously injured.”
“And the most important thing is—”
With a flicker of fear in his eyes, Sword Without End’s voice trembled as he spoke, “Those sirens on the hovering cars chasing us, the voice blasting from the loudspeakers wasn’t telling us to surrender.”
“But it means… you damned players dare to set foot in City 13 again!!!”
“Do you know what that means?”
“It means that those people in the maps aren’t simply NPCs; they’re more like real, living beings in a world!!”
“After I came out of the map, I looked for you first. As far as I know, you’re the strongest player I’m aware of, and I think you should be informed about this.”
“This matter is related to our future life or death.”
“…”
Chen Yi remained calm and silent, not speaking a word. In reality, he had already suspected as much, and Sword Without End’s information today had made his suspicions even clearer.
He had a suspicion in his heart.
The Snow Sea Project Team was training troops, continuously filtering Blue Star players until they assembled a massive army to help the Snow Sea Project Team invade other worlds.
The Wilderness, Sands of Time Map—they were all created by the Snow Sea Project Team for the purpose of training troops.
And maps like the one Sword Without End went to were the actual objective of the Snow Sea Project Team, to deploy players into other worlds and have them complete the invasion for the Snow Sea Project Team.
Just like Sword Without End’s mission this time, to destroy a signal transmitter in the hands of a beggar.
Possibly, that thing wasn’t a signal transmitter at all but something detrimental to the Snow Sea Project Team; the Snow Sea Project Team planned to destroy this object, so they dispatched a player in the form of a mission release, to have the player destroy it.
“Chen Yi, do you understand what I’m saying?”
Sword Without End’s eyes were full of anticipation and a plea for agreement as he stared intently at Chen Yi, his dry lips trembling slightly, obviously still shocked by the incident.
“I understand.”
Chen Yi nodded, fell silent for a while, then continued, “So why did you come to me?”
“I want to invite you to go to this map again.”
Despite a look of fear, Sword Without End’s expression was resolute as he clenched his lips tightly: “This time we won’t rush to complete the mission first, but instead try to find a way to log into that city’s internet forums or something, to see if we can find any information about the Snow Sea Project Team!”
“Then, perhaps we can really understand the reason for the existence of the Snow Sea Project Team!”
“As well as the purpose of the Snow Sea Project Team choosing Blue Star, and what exactly that world is all about.”
“Just one more entry, and I believe we can understand many truths.”
Chen Yi stood in place, looking up at the sky: “I understand, you don’t have to say anymore, some things become dangerous if discussed too much.”
Sword Without End was taken aback, then also looked up at the sky, instantly understanding and nodded without speaking further.
“Can we enter that map again?”
Chen Yi asked.
“No, after a few of us completed the mission and escaped successfully, the entrance to that map disappeared.”
“But I believe the map will reappear someday. When it does, I hope I can invite you to enter that map with me.”
Just then—
Sword Without End suddenly froze, a trace of alarm flashing in his eyes as he looked up at Chen Yi.
“The map has reopened, there’s a new mission.”
“The new mission is to kill an offender arrested within the Law Enforcement Bureau, by the name… Li Bei.”
“The name is unfamiliar, but… I suspect that this offender mentioned in the mission is likely the same person I was just telling you about who got captured!”
“The map opening time is in 1 hour.”
Chen Yi’s eyes narrowed, and he stood there staring at Sword Without End, lost in thought. Continue reading stories on empire
This exchange contained a lot of information.
The two biggest pieces of information.
The Snow Sea Project Team seemed in a hurry to silence someone, but it was obvious that the Snow Sea Project Team didn’t have the capacity to kill the captured player; it seemed like the Snow Sea Project Team was worried the captured player might leak some information.
And the rule of the map is that players who fail to escape to the evacuation point in time will be eradicated.
But this Li Bei didn’t die.
So, does that mean the Snow Sea Project Team actually doesn’t have the ability to wipe out a player?
Or rather.
The ability to wipe out a player has failed?
“Huh!”
He let out a light breath, looked up at Sword Without End: “In your condition, can you still enter the map?”
“I can, I have a healing prop, and my injuries are healing progressively.”
“Hmm.”
Chen Yi nodded, jumped onto a nearby sled: “Come on, accompany me to kill someone in Black Trench City first, then let’s go check out this map you’re talking about.”
…

If there’s no additional release, it will be a guaranteed three chapters, any additional releases will be published together.

chapters.title: Chapter 104 - 104 - 103: "We shouldn’t need a bonfire in this weather at all.
chapters.content:
Chapter 104 – 103: “We shouldn’t need a bonfire in this weather at all.
“Black Trench City?”
On the sled, Sword Without End carefully removed his eyepatch, sterilized his wound again, and put on a new eyepatch before he couldn’t help but grimace in pain and said.
“Who are you all going to kill there? An old enemy?”
“I just went to Black Trench City to finish off someone a while back.”
“A trash-talker with a foul mouth.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit cursed irritably, “It’s Zhou Ping, the one who was bragging about competing with us on the leaderboard recently. Yi didn’t bother with him at first, to be honest, Yi didn’t take him seriously at all.”
“And then this guy just dragged us into a map.”
“How come?”
Sword Without End was startled for a moment, frowning, “Did this guy attack you in the map? That’s pretty sneaky.”
“Nothing like that, if this guy really had the guts, I would have thought better of him.”
“But what this guy did was find a map where players can’t attack each other and, in that map, he taunted Yi for over an hour. He didn’t lift a finger, just ran his mouth.”
“Maybe this guy still thinks it’s like the old internet society where you can anonymously flame someone online, and no one can find you once you log off.”
“We definitely couldn’t tolerate that, so we’re preparing to send that guy off early.”
“Heh.”
Upon hearing this, Sword Without End couldn’t help but laugh, “That’s really something. Does Black Trench City specialize in producing trash-talkers?”
“The guy I went to kill in Black Trench City a while back was a trash-talker too.”
“When I found him, he was rummaging through a trash can, too scared to venture into the city to kill monsters, didn’t even have a Point to buy a bun.”
“That’s not important.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit shook his head.
“Just a villain, easily killed, no hassle at all.”
“But what’s important is what you mentioned just now, about how you got into that map. A pass?”
“That’s not it.”
Sword Without End furrowed his brow and pondered for a long time before he spoke, “Didn’t I tell you guys about an organization before? It’s an organization that formed spontaneously by many powerful players in the later world, which they’ve named ’Skywake’.”
“This time it was a player from that organization who found me, saying they invited some capable people to join the map, and I didn’t refuse.”
“But I didn’t expect it to turn out this way.”
“The players who entered with me were all quite strong, but unexpectedly, we were caught off guard.”
“The later world is the common term nowadays; the world after the game’s arrival is called the later world, and the time before that is known as pre-later world.”
“But this time it was in the form of a mission offered to me, the others who went in with me the first time should’ve received the notification too.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit nodded and said no more.
For a moment, nobody spoke, everyone was silent.
The distance between Yancheng and Black Trench City wasn’t far.
Just a matter of ten minutes or so.
…
“You know Zhou Ping?”
Tuberculosis Rabbit casually picked up a Grade E Prop and waved it in front of a young man, smiling at the sudden sparkle in the young man’s eyes, “Lead us to him and this is yours.”
Grade E Props are mostly useless.
They’re generally for life-related purposes.
Like that coffee machine, the mirage food series props, and so on.
They’re usually items that don’t help with combat ability but can provide assistance at certain special moments, mostly serving as collectibles in Tuberculosis Rabbit’s backpack for Chen Yi and the others.
But to most players.
Having one more Grade E Prop, even the most useless one, is still a good thing.
The young man before them was just someone they happened to find upon arriving at Black Trench City, solely for the purpose of asking directions, after all Zhou Ping ranked tenth on the Global Vehicle Leaderboard.
In Black Trench City, he should be well-known, and finding his residence wouldn’t be difficult.
Just like how Sword Without End easily found Chen Yi’s home and waited for him on the rooftop in advance, all the players in Yancheng might not know the name of the current head of the Law Enforcement Bureau, but they would definitely know where Chen Yi lived.
“Sure thing!”
Without any hesitation, the young man before them nodded vigorously, then firmly pointed towards the suburbs, “There’s a villa over there, Zhou Ping and his men live in one of those villas.”
“Originally, that villa wasn’t Zhou Ping’s.”
“But after the later world, Zhou Ping moved into the villa, what the Law Enforcement Bureau calls asset redistribution.”
“I’ll lead the way for you.”
“Get in the car.”
“Alright, then.”
…
“It’s right there.”
The young man stood in front of a single-family villa, the windows seeping light and servilely said with a grin, “Gentlemen, I’ve brought you here. Can I take the Prop now…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit didn’t speak, just turned to look at Yi.
Chen Yi, leaning on his cane with one hand, stood in place and through the wall, saw Zhou Ping celebrating inside, he said in a calm voice, “We’ve got the right place.”
“Alright.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit nodded, twirled the Grade E Prop a few times in the air, and then casually tossed it into the arms of the young man, patting him on the shoulder, “You’ve got this routine down pat, kinda reminds me of traitors leading the way in the old days.”
“Take the Prop and scurry on home to sleep. Bedtime’s almost upon us.”
“Alright, thanks a lot, brothers.”
After speaking, the man didn’t delay and, tucking the prop into his chest, he scurried off quickly.
“Thanks, huh.”
Your next chapter awaits on empire
After the man had left, Tuberculosis Rabbit turned his head with a look of regret and glanced towards Sword Without End: “I really do feel a bit reluctant to take out those treasures of mine. They might not be worth much, but I have a bit of a collecting obsession.”
“It’s really hard to part with those collections of mine.”
“And it made you waste an E-rank prop.”
“…”
Sword Without End’s mouth twitched slightly with a touch of helplessness: “That’s not necessary, an E-rank prop isn’t worth much anyway. Players of our level don’t usually care much about an E-rank prop.”
“There’s no need to make a big deal out of it.”
“By the way, Chen Yi, do you need my help? There are quite a few people in the villa, so sneaking in and assassinating could be tricky.”
“No need.”
Chen Yi shook his head, swapped out the Five-Spice Milu Deer, and installed the Mechanical Elk.
Before Tuberculosis Rabbit and the others standing outside the vehicle could react, Chen Yi aimed the head of the sled at the villa in front of him and floored the accelerator.
“Boom!!!”
A massive crash suddenly erupted in the night, making the ground tremble as if from an earthquake.
The villa, which had been brightly lit just a moment ago, was reduced to dust and debris floating in the air in the blink of an eye.
Simple and brutal.
That 30-meter-long ultra-blade had not even been detached yet. At extremely high speeds, it could literally destroy everything in its path without exaggeration.
Don’t think this thing can only chop trees because it’s quite convenient for it; it’s capable of so much more.
In just an instant, the standalone villa had disappeared from sight, completely flattened by the passing sled, leaving only a pile of building rubble on the empty lot.
That was much more straightforward than any demolition by explosion.
Sword Without End’s mouth gradually opened wide, and he stiffened in place, struggling to believe the ruins of the villa before him. He instinctively turned to look at Three-Foot Qingfeng beside him.
Take a look at that vehicle.
Then take a look at your own vehicle.
These aren’t even in the same league. No wonder that vehicle ranks first on the Global Vehicle Leaderboard—with an unreasonable destructive power like this, the first place is indeed well-deserved.
And the young man, who hadn’t run far with the prop in his chest, upon hearing the noise behind him, instinctively turned to look back. When he saw that the villa, which had stood on the lot moments ago, was now reduced to ruins, his heart skipped a beat.
His legs pumped even harder, sprinting away into the distance.
The first rule of being a traitor:
Leave the crime scene immediately after showing the way.
This was an ancestral teaching passed down from his great-grandfather’s generation.
…
“Whew.”
Chen Yi controlled the sled hovering above the villa’s rubble, jumped down from the sled, and began to search with his cane.
It was uncertain whether any bodies would be found.
He had aimed and struck, and although the acceleration was short and the speed not at its maximum, it was not weak either.
Such speed flinging debris would blow blood and dust together into the air.
But just to be safe, he decided to search anyway, in case Zhou Ping somehow survived the hit and came back to life, causing him endless troubles.
That would be pretty annoying.
“That…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, looking at Yi who was diligently searching through the ruins, muttered somewhat absently: “No need to look anymore, Zhou Ping’s name has already disappeared from the Global Vehicle Leaderboard.”
“It vanished in that instant.”
“He must be dead beyond a doubt.”
“Honestly, it would be very difficult for a normal person to survive under these circumstances, right?”
“Indeed.”
Chen Yi patted his hands, jumped onto the sled with a hint of regret, and stopped it beside Tuberculosis Rabbit: “Get in, let’s head to the map Sword Without End mentioned and have a look.”
“He’s dead already?”
“To think that a top ten figure on the Global Vehicle Leaderboard would be so easy to kill.”
There was still half an hour left before they reached the map.
A task meant to be completed in an hour was resolved in just half an hour, and suddenly, there was a sense of boredom.
“Here.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, sitting next to the sled, kindled a fire, sat cross-legged beside it, and casually tossed a cigarette to Sword Without End: “You look about 40, don’t you, so how come you talk just like us youngsters, without a generational gap at all?”
“That…”
Sword Without End also sat cross-legged beside the fire, feeling the heat wave from the flames, hesitated for a moment before he questioned cautiously: “Although there is a chill at night, the season is still in the heat of summer.”
“Surely we don’t need a fire right now, do we?”
“Look at you.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit glanced at Sword Without End with some speechlessness: “I just said there was no generation gap between you and us young people, and here it is right away.”
“That way of thinking is outdated.”

chapters.title: Chapter 105 - 105 - 104: "Little friends who like to tattle will have their mouths sewn shut, you know.
chapters.content:
Chapter 105 – 104: “Little friends who like to tattle will have their mouths sewn shut, you know.
“When you need something, you get it; when you’re thirsty, you drink; when you’re hungry, you eat.”
“That’s pragmatism.”
“What do our generation of young people value? We value romanticism.”
“What do you mean by romanticism?”
“Romanticism is about wanting something even when you don’t need it, just for the sake of romance. Like you said, it’s summer; we don’t need a campfire.”
Enjoy new chapters from empire
“But don’t you think it’s romantic to sit by a campfire under the night sky, feeling the warmth of the flames, and enjoying this momentary comfort?”
Tuberculosis Rabbit looked at Sword Without End with disdain, as if he was looking at an antique.
Sword Without End remained silent, not speaking. He couldn’t quite grasp this mindset. No matter how much Tuberculosis Rabbit went on and on, he still firmly believed that lighting a campfire in the hot summer was a fool’s errand.
It had absolutely nothing to do with romance.
After a moment, he spoke up again.
“I’m only 34, not as old as you say, and probably only a few years older than you guys.”
“No wife?”
Tuberculosis Rabbit took some snacks out of his pocket and spread them on a cloth on the ground, making the atmosphere look a bit like a picnic. He then added, “Just look; I brought them out as props for the ambiance, don’t actually eat them.”
“They’re just unfilling prop foods; I’ve nibbled on them already—they’ve got my saliva on them.”
“I had one.”
“Divorced?”
“She died.”
Sword Without End, with droopy eyelids, casually said, “We’d been married for less than two years, and one day she wasn’t feeling well and went to the hospital for a check. We thought it was a minor illness, but the diagnosis came back as advanced cancer, and she died not long after.”
“That time was quite painful. We were just in our honeymoon phase, the best time in our relationship, and then she died.”
“Sometimes I think, if she had died after more than a decade of marriage, maybe it wouldn’t have been so painful for me. But then, I feel like that kind of thought is really inhuman.”
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, who had been all smiles, suddenly fell into an awkward silence. After a while, he touched his nose and said, “Uh, sorry about that, I didn’t know… um…”
“It’s okay.”
Sword Without End seemed quite nonchalant as he shook his head and said with a smile, “It’s been a while since it happened. Birth, old age, sickness, death—everybody goes through it. It’s just that some people reach the end of their journey sooner.”
“I’ve come to terms with it.”
“What about… your parents?”
“My mom had complications during childbirth and died.”
“My dad borrowed a lot of money to try and save her, and afterward, to pay off the debt, he worked four jobs a day. On the day I got into college, after finishing work on the construction site, he drank a bottle of chilled iced tea and suddenly died, without even leaving a will.”
“The doctor said it was the chilled iced tea that shocked his system. If he hadn’t drunk that iced tea, he might not have died.”
“Yep, just died a pointless death.”
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, who had just picked up a piece of roast chicken and was about to eat it, froze when he heard Sword Without End’s words, staring blankly at the chicken in his hand, motionless.
He vaguely felt that eating roast chicken wasn’t suitable considering the current mood.
How did the conversation get here?
He was sure that just moments ago, the mood was light and cheery.
Nightfall, a gentle breeze, a campfire, a few good friends, a picnic.
What a romantic thing it was, but now it had turned into this.
Seeing that the atmosphere had become somewhat awkward, he finally spoke up after a long silence, “Look on the bright side, at least you still have relatives, as well as…”
“All my relatives are dead.”
“In my second year of university, it rained heavily for three days straight in my village, triggering a mountain flood.”
“The village at the foot of the mountain was inundated, and all the relatives I can remember were wiped out that day.”
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit silently placed the roast chicken on the cloth, expressionless, and turned his head to look at Sword Without End, “You must have in-laws, right?”
“They’re dead too.”
“When my wife was 19, they died on a highway, crushed into a pulp between two heavy trucks.”
“What about your wife’s relatives?”
“My wife was from my village. That flood took away all of her relatives too.”
“Friends, you must have friends, right?”
“I don’t have friends. The few best friends I grew up with also died in that flood; they just happened to be visiting the village that day.”
“Colleagues?”
“After my wife died, I stopped working. I’ve had no colleagues for a long time.”
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit fell silent again, and after several minutes,
he solemnly knelt down, facing the food on the cloth spread on the ground. He inserted three lit cigarettes into the ground and kowtowed towards the open space.
“The conditions are a bit lacking, so I’m using the cigarettes in place of incense.”
“I hope all the uncles and aunties can forgive me.”
“There’s some food here, please enjoy it at your leisure, uncles and aunties.”
“Uh…”
Sword Without End felt a little embarrassed, “Did I spoil everyone’s picnic? I didn’t mean to mention all that; you kept asking, so I just went along with it.”
“It’s fine, just kowtow with me.”
“Today we’ll commemorate the uncles and aunties.”
“Maybe you should put that stuff away,” he suggested, “My wife doesn’t eat food that others have touched, didn’t you say your saliva was all over these things?”
“Oh.”
…
Several minutes later.
A flash of white light momentarily passed before Chen Yi and his group, and when their vision returned to normal.
They found themselves inside a coffee shop.
Soft music was playing in the café, and the patrons were chatting quietly amongst themselves, creating a tranquil atmosphere that instinctively made one lower their voice.
Glancing out the window.
The neon lights under the cloak of night added a touch of glamour to the city, making the ceaseless flow of traffic seem especially vibrant.
Before they could take a closer look.
A panel popped up before their eyes.
「Map Name」: City 13.
「Mission」: Proceed to the Law Enforcement Bureau on 78th Street and assassinate the criminal under trial named Li Bei within 8 hours.
「After completing the mission, escape to the evacuation point within 15 minutes.」
「Players who fail to complete the mission within the time limit or fail to escape to the evacuation point in time will be eliminated.」
This was their mission.
“Hmm.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit glanced at the mission panel that had popped up and didn’t pay any more attention to it, instead continuing to survey his surroundings, and he said thoughtfully, “We just arrived directly into this café without drawing any attention, meaning we didn’t just appear out of nowhere.”
“This doesn’t quite line up with your guess,” he continued.
“After all, if, as you speculated, we entered this real world as ’players,’ we should have arrived in some secluded place, otherwise we’d definitely draw the attention of people around us.”
“Suddenly appearing out of the blue in broad daylight would be quite conspicuous, after all.”
Chen Yi didn’t speak, instead knocking on the glass wall beside him with his knuckle.
Their table was situated next to a window of the café.
“Thud.”
When his knuckle made contact with the glass wall, a slightly muted sound emanated, and the feedback from both the sound and touch felt very real.
“Let’s go.”
Chen Yi didn’t sit for long, he just quickly scanned the coffee shop’s interior, then got up and headed towards the exit without any staff trying to stop them.
Standing on the sidewalk, Chen Yi instantly felt many eyes sizing them up, their gaze … filled with fear?
The people on the street were indeed as Sword Without End had described.
Everyone had mechanical organs, suggesting the city’s technology was more advanced than that of Blue Star, where such augmentations had not yet become commonplace for everyone.
Including the hovering cars and the corresponding low-altitude traffic control—none of these existed on Blue Star.
This city’s technology was decidedly more advanced than that of Blue Star.
Chen Yi quickly made a judgment in his mind.
“Do you gentlemen need any assistance?”
“If you are being coerced or watched, you can signal by blinking.”
Just then—
An officer wearing a police uniform, both of his eyes mechanical, approached them confidently, rested his hand on his waist, and looked around with a wary undertone as he whispered.
“Um…”
A flicker of possibility passed through Chen Yi’s mind, and he asked thoughtfully, “Why would you think we’re under duress?”
“A person without any mechanical organs like yourself usually wouldn’t come to a slum like this.”
The officer in front of them replied solemnly and respectfully.
So it was as he had guessed.
Their lack of mechanical organs was the reason why the passersby looked at them with fear, presuming them to be part of the so-called aristocratic class of the city?
“No need,” he replied.
He shook his head, replying instinctively, “We’re just looking around, thank you for the warning. You can leave now if there’s nothing else.”
As soon as he finished speaking.
The officer’s pupils constricted instantly, his body tensed as he crouched slightly, masking his emotions well as he rasped, “Then I won’t disturb you gentlemen any further.”
Afterwards, he walked briskly into the distance and melted into the crowd.
And quickly stepped into a narrow alley.
Once the officer ensured no one was following and looked at his wristwatch, he reported in an anxious and rapid tone, “Officer 231 with an urgent report, suspecting…”
However, the next second.
The voice stopped abruptly.
“Thump!”
The sound of something blunt echoed in the secluded alley.
Tuberculosis Rabbit tucked the towel-wrapped stick back into his coat and took out a needle and thread, starting to sew the mouth of the passed-out officer, his expression serious as if mending a torn teddy bear at home.
“That’s not good at all,” he murmured.
“Tattletales need to have their mouths sewn shut,” he continued naggingly, his hands fluttering rapidly as he stitched the officer’s mouth and occasionally lifting the stick to reinforce the anesthesia.
They didn’t dare to kill him.
It might trigger an alarm from the city’s Law Enforcement Bureau, so it was safer to just sew the man’s mouth shut and prevent him from communicating the incident.

chapters.title: Chapter 106 - 106 - 105: "After successfully stitching up a corpse, there really is a sense of accomplishment.
chapters.content:
Chapter 106 – 105: “After successfully stitching up a corpse, there really is a sense of accomplishment.
Chen Yi stood still, looking up to inspect both sides of the alley, checking for any surveillance cameras.
When he had subconsciously said thank you and saw the reaction of the officer before him,
he knew he might have said the wrong thing.
If what the officer said was true, that a person without any mechanical organs like himself held a high status in this city, then people like him wouldn’t use words such as “thank you”.
They were supposed to be superior, right?
It was clear that the class structure in this city was rigid.
Beneath the veneer of a modern city lay an extremely strict social hierarchy.
The one thing that truly shocked him was that such a bustling area was described as a slum by the officer.
The most bustling cities on Blue Star were not as busy as this place.
If this was considered a slum, what were the cities on Blue Star? Garbage dumps?
There were no cameras.
This alley was a dead end, squeezed between two high-rises, probably less than two meters wide, littered with trash and reeking of a strong urine smell, with dried feces visible everywhere.
In a corner of the alley lay a stray cat, covered in scars, fur curled, eyes warily fixed on them, ready to flee at any moment. Notably, all of the cat’s legs were mechanical.
Even a stray cat had mechanical legs; how peculiar.
Compared to the clean and tidy streets outside, this place did have a semblance of a slum.
Chen Yi crouched down, took the wristwatch from the officer’s hand, and toyed with it in his hands. The officer had been communicating with someone on what seemed like a communicator.
The screen was still on.
But he didn’t touch it, as the screen still displayed a prompt.
“Inputting message…”
Well, it seemed that the message the officer had been trying to send hadn’t gone through yet.
He didn’t try to operate the wristwatch, as he didn’t want to be hunted immediately upon his arrival. A random touch might trigger some sort of automatic alarm.
After getting a rough idea of what it was, he tried putting the device around the officer’s neck.
By now, Tuberculosis Rabbit had finished sewing the officer’s mouth shut tightly, using fishing line instead of ordinary thread, making it incredibly durable.
He then tied the officer’s hands and feet together, stuffed him into a trash bag, and tucked it into a garbage bin in the corner of the alley. This would ensure that, at least for a while, the officer wouldn’t be able to leak any information about them.
Having done all that,
Tuberculosis Rabbit dusted off his hands, looking pleased with his work, “Let’s go. We’re done here. How about we go and see the city, eh? Kind of feels like a little tour; it’s not bad.”
“That…
Sword Without End looked at Tuberculosis Rabbit’s smooth operation and couldn’t help but mutter in stupefaction, “What did you used to do? You seem so skilled.”
“Oh, I worked as a security guard in a morgue for a while, and I was an encoffiner for some time, specializing in stitching up bodies from accidental deaths.”
“Last time I had to stitch up a body where the driver crashed right into a guardrail.”
“The metal sliced the upper body in half. It was a bloody scene, with white fat globules mixed with flesh, easy enough to make one throw up their lunch.”
“Stitching that up was quite simple. It’s more troublesome with bodies that are totally mangled.”
“First, you have to identify any recognizable organs, like the mouth, nose, fingers, and so on.”
“Then, according to information from the relatives, you create a mold of the same height.”
“After that, you need to arrange the body parts and organs inside the mold, kind of like assembling a puzzle. But in most cases, a lot of the flesh is lost during transport and at the scene, making it difficult to put together a complete body.”
“So you need to add some pork or something, line it all up, sew it together, apply makeup, dress it up, and present it to the family for one last look before cremation.”
“That’s child’s play, really. Next time, I’ll show you how to create a head out of thin air. Like when the deceased’s head is reduced to mush, and the family wants me to reconstruct the head based on a photo.”
“That’s more of a technical job. You have to use a variety of materials to recreate such a head.”
“We usually start with a 3D modeler, and then we combine 3D printing with pork to get the desired result. It’s more complex, but the families pay well, so we earn more.”
“…”
Sword Without End’s mouth slowly dropped open as he incredulously stared at Tuberculosis Rabbit, feeling a chill down his spine and instinctively took a step back, “Did Chen Yi also do this kind of work?”
“Nope, Yi used to find customers for us.”
“It’s a pricey service, and most families can’t afford it, so Yi had to go out and drum up business.”
“This… this service, you actually go out looking for customers? You don’t just go knocking on doors, do you?”
“Not exactly, you just look for families that seem to have money, and then you go for a drive and hit them; that’s Yi’s job, my job is to take the order.”
“…”
Sword Without End felt a new chill creep up his spine and took a few steps back.
“Just kidding. That would be murder.”
“We’re good people after all.”
Seeing Sword Without End’s reaction, Tuberculosis Rabbit couldn’t help but laugh, lighting a cigarette and putting it to his lips as he waved and walked toward the mouth of the alley, “Yi used to handle the interaction with customers for us. I don’t exactly look trustworthy, so customers wouldn’t trust me.”
“Customers trust Yi more, with his blank expression. They think he’s reliable.”
“Just making a bit of pocket money for a living, but it’s indeed quite stress-relieving. I’ll recommend you try it some time if you have the chance.”
“After successfully stitching a corpse, it really gives you a sense of accomplishment.”
“Stress-relieving…”
Sword Without End was silent and didn’t speak, simply looking at the list of players on the map. He couldn’t help but speak up, “Apart from the three of us, other first-time players have also received tasks.”
“But not a single one has entered; they all chose to give up.”
“Right now, there are only the three of us players on this map.”
“Hmm, no rush, let’s go out and scout the situation first.”
…
After Chen Yi had walked several rounds on the streets,
he finally ascertained three things.
First, pedestrians on the street couldn’t see the title above his head.
Second, there were no internet cafes in this city.
Third, they seemed too conspicuous; along the way, countless women had deliberately posed in a sexy manner as they passed by, though they didn’t approach to start a conversation, the way they acted clearly suggested they would throw themselves at him the moment he waved.
“The watch…”
Chen Yi stood on the sidewalk pondering without speaking. The wristwatch should contain each person’s identity information, and after briefly looking around, he deduced that to log into the city’s network system, one must log in on the wristwatch.
But they didn’t have such a thing at all.
Nor did he see any shops selling watches along the way.
However, he did see several employees from mechanical organ shops catching stray cats off the street, chopping off all four of their legs, and then attaching mechanical organs.
After asking about it,
they said it was for practice.
It was akin to pet store employees on Blue Star often capturing stray cats to neuter them, using them for practice—the wild rats were free for the taking.
The reason passersby displayed their mechanical organs so openly
was due to the Law Enforcement Bureau’s forceful requirements.
No matter what kind of mechanical organs were embedded in their bodies, they were not to be covered by clothing and had to be exposed. Even if your thing turned mechanical, you had to cut a hole in your pants to let it show.
This information also came from the mouths of employees at the mechanical organ shops.
The general reason was that these mechanical organs often possessed a variety of powers, and they had to be exposed so that others could be aware of the person’s aggression.
Furthermore, each mechanical organ contained a tracker and a backdoor from the Law Enforcement Bureau.
Meaning, if the Law Enforcement Bureau wished, they could shut down a person’s mechanical organs at any time, even if it was something non-aggressive like a mechanical heart.
This might be why those people’s gazes towards them were filled with fear and envy.
Because all of their own organs lacked the hidden backdoors left by others, and they could control them as they pleased.
Chen Yi casually glanced at the women flaunting their figures nearby and, tilting his head, gestured with a pursed lip to Tuberculosis Rabbit before falling into thought.
Every mechanical organ has an offensive function.
For example, a mechanical arm could greatly enhance the strength of an arm and could be fitted with various attachments, such as octopus claws for rapid climbing, tether ropes for quick escapes, sleeve daggers for lethal strikes, or even be assembled into firearms.
And from what he observed, almost everyone he saw had mechanical organs, meaning each person had substantial attacking capabilities.
Yet the scene seemed peaceful without any hint of a combat atmosphere.
Explore more stories at empire
What’s the use of such strong offensive capabilities?
It’s like a village that’s been peaceful for a hundred years, but the villagers sharpen knives every night—it’s extremely irrational.
To find out what’s really going on, they’d still need to grab someone and interrogate them.
“You.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit scanned the surroundings and carelessly pointed to a woman not far away, beckoning, “You, come here.”
“Me?”
The woman’s eyes sparked with a tinge of excitement and anticipation. Clutching her skirt, she jogged towards Tuberculosis Rabbit in an affected manner under the envious gazes of other women, seemingly afraid Rat might change his mind.
And the envy was evident in the eyes of the other passersby looking at this woman.
What luck, to be able to latch onto someone from the upper city.
She might even be taken out of the slums.
“Yeah.”
After contemplating for a while, Tuberculosis Rabbit finally said, “I want to take you to rent a hotel room with your identity information. Any problem with that?”
“I understand, I understand, no problem at all,”
the woman nodded excitedly and continuously.
People from the upper city seeking fun would never leave their own identity information behind—a fact she understood well.
“Good you understand. Lead the way.”
“Pick a decent hotel, and you’re paying.”

chapters.title: Chapter 107 - 107 - 106: "Good Luck.
chapters.content:
Chapter 107 – 106: “Good Luck.
“So cooperative?”
Tuberculosis Rabbit looked at the woman who was already leading the way ahead, sizing up Yi and his companion with a strange scrutiny. The reason he let this woman pay was that they literally had no money in their pockets.
So far, they had no idea what the circulating currency in this map was.
They couldn’t pay at all.
He had planned to use some excuse, like promising big future benefits or other such enticements, to trick this woman into paying for them. Unexpectedly, before he could articulate his plan, the woman took over all the talking.
It seemed that people like them, without mechanical organs on their bodies, really did have high status?
“Isn’t this a bit too exaggerated? Even driving a multimillion-dollar luxury car on Blue Star wouldn’t get you this kind of treatment, right?”
“…It’s not necessarily so.”
Sword Without End said quietly from the side.
“Keep up.”
Chen Yi didn’t say much, but, leaning on his cane, he looked ahead at the back of the woman, through whose clothes he could vaguely see a lot of things.
Underwear, panties, smooth skin.
No strange tails or tentacles or the like.
At least it showed she was a normal person, not some kind of alien.
He vaguely remembered seeing an advertisement on Blue Star.
A man was sneaking a bite of a Snickers bar when his girlfriend suddenly burst in. In a panic, he placed the Snickers bar behind his neck and embraced his beloved girlfriend.
Then a mouth suddenly appeared on his neck and slowly swallowed the Snickers bar.
The ad ended with a line—
Tasty snacks, not even to be shared with your lover.
Well, he had never seen such a stupid ad before, and it had given him a psychological shadow about these aliens. Before that, he had never thought a commercial could leave such a big scar on him.
The woman quickly led them into a skyscraper with several hundred floors. At the elevator, she dutifully blocked the door, bowing and scraping towards Chen Yi and the others at the entrance, with a flattering smile.
The scene was quite ridiculous.
There was a strong sense of dissonance.
In ordinary eyes, women with tall figures, pretty faces, and outfits consisting of black stockings and short skirts shouldn’t be so obsequious, but should have a sense of pride of their own. This level of obsequiousness was indeed strange.
But the gazes of the people around them didn’t contain a hint of disdain for her, only envy—envy so intense it had turned into jealousy, almost as if they wished they could immediately take her place.
Soon, the elevator stopped at the 44th floor.
Standing at the front desk on the 44th floor, Chen Yi saw the woman interacting with the staff behind the counter using her wristwatch. He didn’t hear the exact content, but he roughly understood the payment method of this map.
Payment was through the wristwatch, somewhat similar to the QR code payments on Blue Star.
…
“Miss.”
A woman in uniform behind the counter, with a professional smile on her face, looked at her: “Unfortunately, the balance of your account does not allow you to book an exquisite luxury suite. You can opt for a more economical king-size room.”
The woman in black stockings appeared slightly anxious as she lowered her voice, “I’ve already applied for an overnight loan. Please, pay attention and quickly approve my application.”
“You should also see the status of the people behind me, right?”
“Don’t just make it difficult for me. If you really affect their mood, do you think you can please them?”
“…”
Jealousy flickered in the eyes of the woman at the counter, who intentionally dragged her feet before finally saying, “The room has been prepared. It’s room 4418. A member of staff will guide you to your room.”
“Good luck.”
An overnight loan is a unique form of loan in City 13.
When Upper City People come to the Lower City looking for fun and choose a Lower City Person to take to a hotel room but lack the funds, they can apply for this loan.
Instant approval.
This loan is a collaboration between banks and hotels.
No background checks were needed; if the borrower accompanied an Upper City Person, approval was granted.
The banks also believed that a Lower City Person who had spent a night with an Upper City Person, even if they were previously jobless vagrants, could soon repay the money. After all, the little that trickled through the fingers of the Upper City People was more than enough for these individuals to live lavishly.
…
“Gentlemen, I’ve got the room ready.”
The woman spoke with a coy tucking of hair behind her ear, standing in front of Chen Yi and the others, “Let me lead the way, please follow me.”
“I don’t know why.”
As Sword Without End watched the woman leading them down the hall with a swinging gait, he murmured with a touch of emotion, “For a moment just now, I thought about persuading her to take the right path and not to keep heading down the wrong one.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit patted Sword Without End’s shoulder, speaking in a resigned low voice.
“Those are words for after the fact, you’ve got the process wrong.”
“Let’s follow her first.”
As soon as they entered the room.
Before Chen Yi and the others had a chance to take in the decor, they saw the woman had already shut the door and knelt down with knees together, in a posture that suggested she was at their disposal.
“Can you get online? It’s something like the internet or another name that might be used, where people can exchange information in a kind of virtual space.”
Chen Yi pulled out a chair from within the room, sat in front of the woman, and lifted her chin with his cane, staring into her eyes as he spoke slowly and clearly.
The woman’s self-perceived sexy attire didn’t interest him in the slightest.
He was more concerned about whether the woman’s next words would contain any lies.
According to psychology, if you keep staring into someone’s eyes while speaking and pretend that you can discern the truth from their eyes, the other person will subconsciously reduce the frequency of lying. Moreover, they’d also have subconscious little movements like eye dodging while speaking, which could indeed help in discerning the truth from their eyes.
“Are you talking about… the Spirit Web?”
A flash of panic crossed the woman’s eyes. Feeling the cold cane against her skin and facing the man with an expressionless face sitting before her, she couldn’t help but press her legs together a bit more tightly.
The pressure from the Upper City people was so overwhelming.
Just humiliate her like this, wantonly destroy her dignity.
Yes, that’s right.
Treat her like a lowly Lower City person, and vent your frustrations on her!
“I can… everybody can, don’t the Upper City people use this?”
“I ask, you answer, no backtalk.”
Chen Yi, staring emotionlessly into the woman’s eyes, calmly said, “Search for the Snow Sea Project Team and tell me the information related to it.”
“Oh.”
Although the woman was somewhat unclear about the situation, she obediently did as she was told, projecting the searched information into the air.
“Wow.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit touched his nose, looked at the information panel floating in the air, and couldn’t help but mutter, “This is really high-end.”
He had only seen such scenes in science fiction movies.
Although Blue Star also had this function after global gamification, Blue Star’s technology hadn’t developed to this extent before the advent of the future world.
However, the information searched was somewhat different from what they had expected.
To be precise, it was different from what Sword Without End had expected.
The term Snow Sea Project Team, as it appeared, wasn’t even a valid index; the search results were about a few companies having a project group called the Snow Sea Project Team, but it was completely different from the Snow Sea Project Team they knew of.
After carefully perusing the information for a while, Chen Yi spoke again.
“Search for Blue Star.”
“Okay.”
“Search for global gamification.”
“Search for the Snow Sea Project Team and global gamification.”
“Search for the Snow Sea Project Team and players.”
“Search for players.”
After a while. Continue your journey with empire
Chen Yi and his companions gathered by the window, each frowning and lighting a cigarette to their mouths, silently contemplating without speaking.
After a lengthy pause, Sword Without End hesitantly spoke up, “Could I have guessed wrong?”
Without finding any news about the Snow Sea Project Team and Blue Star, according to Sword Without End’s speculation, the purpose of the global gamification by the Snow Sea Project Team might have been to train warriors to invade other worlds—players, that is.
But now it seemed that this possibility had greatly diminished.
“Not entirely wrong.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit shook his head, frowning as he looked out the window at the busy traffic and said, “The first time you left this map, the law enforcement that was chasing you said something about you damn parasitic players.”
“This at least shows that these people are aware of the existence of us players.”
“Even if the major direction was off, some minor directions of speculation could still be correct.”
Chen Yi didn’t speak but pondered for a moment before returning to the woman, “How big is your world?”
“The world?”
The woman looked up at Chen Yi, bewildered, not searching immediately this time but hesitating for a while before speaking, “Our world used to be very large, but a long time ago, it faced a crisis.”
“Until now, only 13 cities have carried on the inheritance. Apart from the 13 cities, all other places have been destroyed.”
“It’s not very clear how big the 13 cities are specifically, maybe a few tens of millions of people. There’s no detailed information online; I’ve only known to live in this city since I was born.”
“Bullshit.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit couldn’t help but laugh in exasperation, “Do you realize that such a large city relying mostly on self-sufficiency would lead to starvation for most of its population? Not to mention, where would the food come from?”
“Where would those coffee shops get their coffee beans from?”
“Moreover…”
The voice suddenly stopped.
Tuberculosis Rabbit suddenly realized something, his eyes flashing with shock as he looked sideways at Chen Yi.
Chen Yi had also come to an equally startling conclusion at that moment, without any hesitation he made his way outside the building and left a message for the kneeling woman.
“Wait here for me.”
“Don’t go anywhere until I return.”
Then he quickly left the hotel with Tuberculosis Rabbit and the others, heading towards the building’s exit.
After going downstairs.
With a unified purpose, they moved silently, striding toward the coffee shop where they had arrived.
Just then, a nearly unanimous yet somewhat improbable answer had suddenly appeared in their minds.
Before long.
They returned to the very coffee shop where they had arrived, and without any hesitation, they pushed open the door and entered.

chapters.title: Chapter 108 - 108 - 107: "Tell me, where did you get these Meat Worms from?
chapters.content:
Chapter 108 – 107: “Tell me, where did you get these Meat Worms from?
“Hello, sir, please…”
The waiter standing at the entrance of the coffee shop had barely bent down and hadn’t finished his sentence when Chen Yi and his group entered briskly.
Without the slightest pause.
Their target was the coffee shop’s kitchen.
“What are you guys up to?”
Seeing the aggressive approach of the group, the coffee shop staff rushed over, angrily shouting, “Looking for trouble here, do you want to die…”
But they couldn’t finish their sentence. Upon seeing the sniper rifle in Chen Yi’s hand, they all hugged their heads and squatted on the ground, signaling they meant no harm.
“Bang!”
Tuberculosis Rabbit kicked open the glass door of the coffee shop’s production room and couldn’t help but feel nauseous at the sight within. He covered his mouth to forcibly suppress the urge to vomit.
Inside the production room,
there was a steel frame at least ten meters long, and strapped to it were more than thirty men.
Not one of them was clothed.
When Tuberculosis Rabbit kicked in the door, several coffee shop staff were busy using coffee cups to collect freshly pressed coffee.
The men tied to the frame were blindfolded, with a transparent tube in their mouths that led to the ceiling, where coffee flowed into their bodies from time to time.
Just as they had guessed!
This city, the 13th City,
one of the main reasons it could remain self-sufficient despite being cut off from the world for who knows how long was the use of props, like this coffee shop.
They didn’t need to buy any coffee beans at all. With enough men, they could produce an endless supply of fresh coffee.
Coffee that was rich and full-bodied.
And they didn’t waste those men’s buttocks either—the output was turned into pastries.
A few coffee shop staff were constantly producing coffee and pastries in the operating room. When they saw Chen Yi and the others burst in, they all seemed a bit at a loss.
“Huh!”
Chen Yi took a deep breath before striding into the operating room and pointing the gun at a worker’s forehead. “How are these people producing coffee?”
“That…”
The worker quickly raised both hands, his voice trembling with a sobbing tone as he pointed to a machine about two meters tall in the corner. Clearly, he’d never imagined that a coffee shop could be the scene of a robbery.
Who ever robs a coffee shop?
Chen Yi didn’t speak but walked up to the machine. It was over two meters tall with countless clear plastic tubes extending to the ceiling and then to the mouths of the men tied to the frame.
He placed his hand on the machine. Stay tuned with empire
No prop panel emerged as he had imagined.
But he did see a message engraved on a copper plaque attached to the outside of the machine.
“Yongji Brand Coffee Machine.”
“Instruction Manual: After starting this coffee machine, just insert the tube into the Meat Worm’s mouth, and it will continuously produce fresh and full-bodied coffee.”
“Operating Principle: This coffee machine can make Meat Worms drink coffee and transform the urine excreted by the Meat Worm into coffee.”
“Essential Ingredients: Yongji Concentrated Coffee Extract, which contains coffee and a diuretic, can ensure that the Meat Worms will continue to produce coffee.”
“Usage Restrictions: This machine has a maximum of 48 ports and can catalyze up to 48 Meat Worms at the same time.”
“Warranty Information: …”
Even without a prop panel, the information before him was enough for him to understand how this coffee machine operated. It was almost identical to the Skill “A Cup of Coffee” that he had acquired.
The difference was this was a machine,
whereas what he had was a Skill.
Although they were in different worlds, they shared the same medium. To say there was no connection between the two would be unbelievable even to a fool.
“…”
Chen Yi stared at the instruction manual on the machine without saying a word. He felt as if he was on the brink of understanding something, but when he tried to articulate it, he couldn’t pinpoint the rationale.
It was as if he stood before a thin sheet of window paper,
which he could puncture with just a slight force, yet he couldn’t muster that bit of effort.
He paused for a moment and then turned to look at one of the workmen: “Are all the coffee shops in the 13th City like this?”
“Are there any that aren’t?”
Looking innocently at Chen Yi, the worker was about to speak when he noticed that there was not one mechanical organ on Chen Yi’s body. He suddenly realized with a fluster and hurriedly explained.
“That, sir, all the coffee shops in the Lower City are like this.”
“It’s common knowledge. Sir, you may be visiting the Lower City for the first time. Only Upper City People are entitled to enjoy products made from real coffee beans, freshly ground.”
“Down here in the Lower City, everyone drinks coffee made from Meat Worms.”
“The customers outside know about this too?”
“Everyone knows, you can go out and ask if you don’t believe me, sir.”
“No need.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, who had slipped out unnoticed, returned to the operating room. “I’ve already asked. Those customers outside, they all know where the coffee comes from.”
“These people are incredible. Knowing what this stuff is made of, they can still drink it so enjoyably.”
“Especially those pastries, they actually tasted pretty good. I swear, even if I starved to death, I could never eat those damn things!!”
“Tell me, where did you get these meat worms?”
“Bought them.”
With hands raised and a face full of grievance, the staff member spoke, “Our boss bought them. Prisons sell inmates like if someone’s sentenced to ten years, they’ll sell those ten years out.”
“Then places like cafés will buy these meat worms to produce coffee and return them once the time’s up.”
“If the sentenced time isn’t up, but the inmate sadly dies midway, a compensation fee must be paid.”
Chen Yi and his companions didn’t speak anymore, they just quietly left the café and went to a stir-fry restaurant next door.
Then, in the back kitchen of this stir-fry restaurant they saw a load of meat worms.
The naked meat worm with a fish-flavored shredded pork A4 paper stuck to its body was tied to a rack, continuously pooping out fish-flavored shredded pork onto a clean plate below.
As soon as a serving was done, the staff member would take something like a wine stopper and plug the meat worm’s behind.
Only to remove the stopper again when another customer ordered the dish, pushing a clean plate back under.
Besides that, there were all kinds of meat worms.
Sichuan twice-cooked pork meat worms, spicy crawfish meat worms, braised beef with twister fries meat worms, ice-cold cola meat worms, ice-cold draft beer meat worms, and so on.
These were what composed the back kitchen of this restaurant.
Meanwhile, in the outside dining hall, many excited patrons were happily clinking glasses, savoring the delicious dishes on the tables, enjoying the brief comfort after a day’s work.
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit’s mouth and nose twisted in disgust at the scene before him, standing frozen with his body trembling slightly. He had seen countless corpses in his lifetime, but even those mingled with white fat granules and blood didn’t seem as disgusting as this.
“Blegh!”
Sword Without End couldn’t hold back, turning his head to violently vomit into a nearby trashcan!
When they first arrived on this map, they hadn’t started on their mission right away but ate at a restaurant, even commenting on how fast the service was.
But it turned out to be…
“Blegh!”
The more he thought about it, the harder he vomited, feeling as if he would throw up even his stomach acid.
He had thought that ready-to-cook meals were already the restaurant industry’s bottom line.
It didn’t occur to him, a capable enterprise should have no bottom line.
“You didn’t eat this stuff the first time you came here, did you?”
The curious voice of Tuberculosis Rabbit rang in his ears.
It made Sword Without End stiffen before he vomited even more frantically, sticking his fingers down his throat to force himself to vomit.
“There aren’t enough meat worms.”
Chen Yi saw through the essence of this matter almost instantly. If every restaurant was using meat worms, there simply wouldn’t be enough, after all, how many prisoners could there be?
Even if they distributed them all, it wouldn’t be enough for these restaurants to use.
He was starting to sense the filth beneath the seemingly prosperous surface of the city.
These things were meant for Lower City people to eat, not for Upper City People.
Just then—
Alarm sounds came from outside the window.
“Attention inside, you are surrounded.”
“…”
Clearly, someone had reported an alarm, but it was unknown whether it was the café next door or this restaurant that had raised the alarm.
…
“Hmm.”
Hearing the alarm sounds outside, Tuberculosis Rabbit silently nodded and said, “It seems like this sentence is universal across worlds, as if it’s the first thing police must silently repeat dozens of times when they start their shift.”
“Can’t they come up with something new?”
Chen Yi did not respond, instead, he pulled out a mirror from his chest and dove straight into it, followed closely by Tuberculosis Rabbit and the others.
They didn’t want to have a direct conflict with the Law Enforcement Bureau of City 13; they’d prefer to understand certain things before any firefight broke out.
This action, however, left the nearby staff member dumbfounded in place.
Having easily escaped the encirclement of the law enforcement officers, they returned to the alley next to the café, dragging out the enforcement officer they had knocked out from the trashcan.
Stripping off his clothes, the few of them carried him toward the restaurant they had just visited.
No sled was used.
The reason was the same as before, they didn’t want to cause too much stir—at least not just yet.
Discretion was key.
Though the sight of two men carrying a completely naked man down the street was bizarre, especially since the carried man’s mouth was sewn shut, and both his arms and legs were tied up.
But no one on the street approached to ask, they all steered clear, even avoiding glancing over.
Clearly, they did not want to be noticed by the Upper City People.
It was Upper City People’s privilege.
The person who reported them, if he had noticed that Chen Yi and others had no mechanical parts on them, might not have chosen to report this at all.

chapters.title: Chapter 109 - 109 - 108: "I’ll wait for you in hell!
chapters.content:
Chapter 109 – 108: “I’ll wait for you in hell!
Soon.
Chen Yi and his group carried the man back to the hotel.
Tuberculosis Rabbit removed all the stitches from the man’s mouth, then poured a basin of cold water over him. Looking at the middle-aged man slowly waking up, he brought his face close to his and started to smile.
“Awaken?”
The slowly awakening middle-aged man felt a sharp pain on his skin. Memories rushed into his mind like a tidal wave, and then he looked at the head so close to him.
With force, he spat a thick glob of phlegm onto Tuberculosis Rabbit’s face, his expression fierce and angry as he yelled.
