“Rule two: You need to infer the characteristics of the role you are playing based on certain information.”
“Rule three: If your performance evaluation at the end is below 30%, you will lose half of your props at random. If it is below 60%, you will fail and be removed from the game. If it is above 90%, you will pass perfectly.”
“Map content: You need to impersonate a character and will receive a performance evaluation at the conclusion of the map.”
The brief prompt sounded in Chen Yi’s ear, and with a flash of white light before his eyes, he found himself inside a room, approximately ten or so square meters in size.
There was a single bed with the quilt messily pushed to the corner, along with some clothes that had been haphazardly stripped off and crumpled into a pile; a few pairs of socks were thrown on the floor, and the curtains were tightly closed with no lights on, casting the room in a twilight gloom.
In the whole room, besides a bed and a wardrobe, there was only a computer desk.
On the computer desk was an ashtray stuffed with cigarette butts, with several butts spilling out; the desk was also sprinkled with some ash.
It was clear that the owner of the room was not particularly fond of cleanliness.
However, the computer screen was brightly lit, with a dozen browser tabs open, indicating the room’s prior occupant had been quite studious.
Yet the titles on the browser made one’s skin crawl.
“What solvent can perfectly dissolve human hair?”
“How long would it take for a pet dog weighing around ten pounds to consume a hundred pounds of meat?”
“Can a strong acid solution completely remove bloodstains?”
“Can bloodstains cleaned with a strong acid solution still be detected by police ultraviolet light?”
“How to completely eliminate dander, fingerprints, and hair from the house.”
“…”
Chen Yi silently looked at the browser pages displayed on the computer screen, lightly sniffing the barely detectable scent of blood in the air, he could roughly imagine the scene he would encounter upon opening the door and stepping into the living room.
At that moment—
A panel popped up before him.
“Ding, the role you are playing is a young man whose personality has greatly changed due to a failed business venture and who is now completely immersed in games every day. As you refuse to interact with the outside world because of your addiction to games, your wife could no longer stand it and claimed she would go out to work, or else all three of you at home would starve to death,”
“But you didn’t allow it, as you had your wife quit her job to become a full-time housewife when your business achieved some success.”
“You took her claim of wanting to find a job as an insult to you, and a fierce conflict arose between you and your wife.”
“In an accidental loss of control, you killed your wife.”
“After the initial panic, you quickly calmed down, convinced that you couldn’t let the rest of your life be ruined like this, you decided to destroy the body, dismembering your wife’s corpse completely.”
“However, dealing with a corpse turned out to be more difficult than expected. Just when you had finished disposing of it, the people living downstairs had already reported to the police due to the strong smell of blood coming from your floor—because before they smelled the blood, they had heard loud arguments from upstairs which had suddenly stopped, followed by the overpowering odor of blood.”
“The police will arrive in 4 minutes. You have these 4 minutes to think about how to better play the identity you are now impersonating,”
“ps1: The map evaluation will score you based on how perfectly you play this identity.”
“ps2: If you manage to successfully exculpate the identity, you will earn bonus points and there will be secret rewards,”
Chen Yi narrowed his eyes as he stared at the pop-up prompt before him, his mind quickly beginning to race.
He had 4 minutes left.
…
“The scent of hell is truly fragrant, isn’t it?”
Sword Without End stood with one hand behind his back, his foot on Wang Yimei’s head; beside him, a three-foot Green Peak sword trembled slightly mid-air. After gazing distantly towards the horizon for a long time, he finally looked down at Wang Yimei, whom he was stepping on, and said with a hint of emotion,
“Now, why would you provoke anyone other than Chen Yi?”
“Chen Yi specially sent me to kill you here in hell,”
“Have you lost your mind?”
Wang Yimei, his head ruthlessly pinned under Sword Without End’s foot, struggling violently to no avail, couldn’t help but scream in desperation: “How much did he pay you to kill me, even going so far as to descend into hell to do it?”
“Besides, I have no grudges with him. Why would he target me like this!”
“The only conflict we had was on the Werewolf Kill map, but he was the one who attacked first. He tricked us into that dark courtyard, and in the darkness, he struck without warning. If there is any grudge, it’s mine against him!”
“Why is he targeting me?”
“You cursed him,”
“Impossible, I’m not an idiot. Chen Yi is the player who killed a boss with a single shot in a world event. As long as my brain isn’t faulty, I would never curse him,”
“That’s what I thought,”
Sword Without End nodded solemnly, agreeing, “Logically speaking, not many dare to curse Chen Yi to his face these days, but the reason for your death given by Chen Yi is indeed because you cursed him. If it wasn’t because you cursed him online, then it’s very likely that you cursed him in your heart and got caught.”
“It looks like Brother Chen Yi must have a prop that allows him to hear others curse him in their hearts.”
“A prop?”
Wang Yimei, still angry just moments ago, suddenly froze, his eyes filling with intense regret. He had indeed cursed Chen Yi in his heart, more than once, but who would have thought Chen Yi possessed a prop that could hear one’s inner voice!
Had he known this, he definitely wouldn’t have cursed Chen Yi.
But Sword Without End didn’t waste any more words.
With a little force on his right foot, Wang Yimei’s head beneath it burst open like a ripe watermelon!
’Ding——’
As Wang Yimei’s consciousness rapidly dissipated, a notification sounded abruptly in his ear.
’At 3:21 PM on June 18th, in the SSS-tier map, Hell, you were completely eliminated and will permanently lose the chance to return to the main game. From now on, you will become a janitor and spend the rest of your life in this role.’ Your next journey awaits at Novgo
He floated in the darkness for who knows how long.
When Wang Yimei opened his eyes again, he felt his consciousness momentarily stall, his body seemed to have changed, a bit bloated. Struggling to look down at his body, his eyes filled with terror!
Somehow, his stomach had swollen to a full two meters in diameter, the whole person was sporting an enormous belly!
Immediately after.
He discovered a panel popping up in front of him, and his body moved uncontrollably, drifting far into the void in front of him.
’Ding, unfortunately, Wang Yimei, due to your complete defeat in the main game, you have become a janitor.’
’As a loser of the game, you need to make yourself useful here until the end of your remaining life.’
Before him lay nothingness.
It wasn’t like the universe, but rather a vast and boundless grey space, and not far away, a sizable piece of trash was slowly drifting in this space.
Wang Yimei, filled with terror, found that his body was completely beyond his control, flying straight toward that piece of trash.
As the distance to the trash grew larger, he could see clearly what it was.
It was the carcass of a long-dead Minotaur Monster!
“No, no, no!!!”
Wang Yimei couldn’t help but scream in near panic, his eyes filled with fear, yelling, “No!”
However, as if destiny doesn’t bend to human will, Wang Yimei’s body slammed directly into the dead Minotaur Monster and then opened his mouth wide, biting fiercely into the carcass in front of him!
One bite, two bites, three bites!
Just three bites were enough for Wang Yimei to completely swallow the long-dead Minotaur Monster.
His mouth had changed as well, becoming large enough to swallow a person!
The intense stench of decay and the pungent smell of blood, along with the wriggling maggots he could feel, filled Wang Yimei’s eyes with tears, and he screamed silently in utter breakdown.
He finally understood the fate of the monsters he had killed outside the city—their corpses disappeared in a flash of white light, but he never knew where they went.
Now he knew.
They ended up here.
The so-called janitor was to swallow the carcasses of monsters slain by players into his own stomach.
He had imagined countless times what might happen after death: walking the Road to the Underworld to drink Meng Po Soup, going to Heaven to confess before God, being reincarnated to live another life, or simply fading into nothingness, losing all consciousness.
But of all the possibilities he imagined, he never thought that he would become a janitor after death, swallowing the long-decayed carcasses of monsters in this vast and void space.
Wang Yimei looked up into the distance, his face full of despair. In this space of nothingness, there were still many monster carcasses floating around, most of them long decayed, their stench so foul that it induced vomiting just by approaching them.
One, two, three!
After he had eaten who knows how many,
Finally, a panel popped up in front of him.
’Ding, congratulations, you have completed the janitor’s tutorial. You should now be clear about the janitor’s duties and how to perform your work. From now on, you will have full control over your body.’
’Every day, you need to swallow at least three monster carcasses to complete the daily task, and if you fail to do so, you will be punished.’
At that moment—
He suddenly spotted another janitor player with a distended stomach, floating not far away. It appeared to be a man, but this man’s face did not show fear; instead, he seemed quite relaxed. Upon seeing Wang Yimei, a hint of amusement flickered in his eyes.
“Yo, got a new guy here?”
“Don’t worry, the tutorial might look a bit scary, but being a janitor isn’t that disgusting. Most of the time, it’s quite normal.”
“Now that you’re here, we’re all brothers. As an old-timer, it’s naturally my duty to teach you some tricks of the trade as a janitor.”

chapters.title: Chapter 147 - 147 - 146: "Prop Name": Human Dao Si.
chapters.content:
Chapter 147 – 146: “Prop Name”: Human Dao Si.
After their conversation,
Wang Yimei finally stopped crying, with difficulty she raised her arm to wipe the tears from her eyes, and nodded, looking into the void: “You mean, every monster killed by a player is immediately transported to this space.”
“Those powerful janitors will swallow these fresh monster corpses right away, and while there is still the smell of blood, at least there isn’t the stench of decay.”
“And those janitors pushed to the edges just have to devour monsters that have been killed a while ago, like the Insect Race from the Extraterrestrial Invaders, whose corpses have not been dealt with for so long they are rotten and covered with maggots—all to complete their daily tasks?”
“That’s right.”
The man floating beside Wang Yimei said nonchalantly, “Like me, I’m a level 6 janitor. Although I can’t devour the freshest monster corpses, at least I can ensure that the monster corpses I devour don’t have maggots, just a rotten smell.”
“Within this space, there are three major powers; these levels were created by them. Depending on the level, the degree of decay of the monster corpses we consume is also different.”
“Although I know you’re unwilling to be here, you’ll get used to it eventually. Everyone is resentful when they first arrive.”
“But if you think about it from another angle, we’re already dead. To be able to extend our lives in this way isn’t too bad, right?”
“Moreover, if you devour more monster corpses after completing your daily tasks, you will receive points as a reward.”
“And with points, you can exchange for many things in the janitor’s store, such as freshly roasted chicken, chilled cola, and so on. While they can’t take you out of this space, they can give you a taste of the pleasures of the living world.”
“Don’t think too much—since you’re here, just do the job well.”
“However, there is one thing you must be mindful of: the daily tasks must be completed, or you will be punished.”
“What kind of punishment?”
“You wouldn’t want to know… If you’ve experienced it, you would remember it vividly.”
…
“Another one handled.”
Sword Without End looked down at the battered corpse at his feet, then after biting the cap of his pen, he satisfactorily crossed out Wang Yimei’s name from his notebook.
“Now there is only Gao Yiming and that Uncle Wei left.”
He put the notebook back into his chest pocket, ready to move on when he suddenly fell silent, a trace of desolation flickering in his eyes.
Hell is no different from Blue Star.
Aside from a slightly darker sky, maintaining a constant crimson color, it’s almost identical to Blue Star, with cities and environs beyond.
Props and skills that were not dropped from the backpack in life, upon death and entrance into Hell, are all transformed into Hell props and skills, and can all be used normally, just with renamed titles.
Here too, you can kill monsters, and killing monsters also gives a chance to drop Hell props and receive Hell Coupons.
You can also purchase props in the Hell Store, or by buying a Map Access Pass or other means, you can enter the map as a Hell Player.
If you kill a total of 10 players from the base game, you can successfully return to the base game.
There are two types of stores in the Hell Map.
One is the regular map, made for Hell Players, where they can only encounter other Hell Players and can earn props and skills as rewards in this type of map.
The other is the return map.
Entering this type of map often requires a high-priced Map Access Pass. Besides oneself, the other people in this map are usually normal players from the base game. Apart from the map’s tasks, the hidden task is to kill other players.
This feature was also updated after the June 1st version update in Hell. Before that, players who entered Hell had no chance to return to the base game.
Only upon arrival in Hell did they realize that the game on Blue Star had a name, called “Base Game.”
It sounds like a shortcut to promotion, with a strong sense of incongruity.
The only thing that made him feel lost was that only players who died after the start of the Base Game would enter into the Hell Map—his wife and family were not eligible to enter.
This completely shattered his hope of finding his family.
Originally, he never had any illusion about it, but after learning of Hell’s existence, a faint fantasy suddenly arose in his heart; now, that fantasy was thoroughly crushed.
Standing in place, Sword Without End gazed silently into the distance for a long time before he sighed lightly and slowly turned his head to look at a fat man hugging two young women at the street corner, murmuring.
“The loving part ways in life and death, yet it’s people like this indulging in carnal pleasures who get to cling to each other day and night. Oh heavens, you truly are blind.”
He didn’t speak again, and just walked straight away.
However, before he left, a stroke of Green Peak, luminous with flowing light, shot straight into the forehead of the fat man behind him.
The light in the fat man’s eyes vanished instantly, his pupils dilated rapidly, and his body slumped powerlessly to the ground.
Sword Without End, with an expressionless face, strode steadily into the distance.
Feeling down, he wanted to kill some people for fun.
For those who don’t respect love, killing them is no loss, nothing but beasts.
The next second—
“Dad!”
“Dad!”
The two young women kneeling beside the man were full of terror and grief, crying out as they lay on the belly of the heavyset man, “Dad, don’t leave us behind!”
“Why is heaven so unfair to us? Our whole family died in the map and we’ve already come to hell, but why can’t we have even one peaceful day here?”
“Dad, if you’re gone, what are we going to do?”
“Mom is at home waiting for us to return with groceries!”
“Dad!”
“Who killed my dad? Stand up! If you had the guts to kill my dad, then just kill our whole family and let us go together, whole and complete!”
“…”
Listening to the cries behind him, Sword Without End, who had been leaving expressionlessly, suddenly stumbled and hesitated for a few seconds before he turned around and walked back to the middle-aged man lying in a pool of blood with several holes in his forehead.
He took out a prop from his chest and placed it on the man’s body, immediately choosing to activate it.
’Prop Name’: Human Dao Si.
’Prop Level’: B-grade.
’Prop Effect’: Once this prop is activated, it can pull a dying player back from the brink of death, requiring 10,000 Points. If a player has been dead for less than 30 seconds, they can also be pulled back from the depths of hell, but this requires the use of a globally unique prop.
This prop can be activated at will, and when a player faces death, it will automatically search the player’s backpack for any globally unique props. If there is one, the prop will be activated to pull the player back from the depths of hell and randomly consume one globally unique prop from the backpack.
’Prop Restrictions’: Number of uses (2/4).
’Prop Description’: “Let me save one more, just one more!”
It could still be used twice. He had used this prop twice when he was severely injured and soon he would only be able to use it once more.
The prop was activated, and a dazzling white light burst forth from Sword Without End’s hand and flowed into the forehead of the middle-aged man.
As a price, a globally unique character action in Sword Without End’s backpack gradually dimmed until it completely vanished.
Immediately following—
The man who had just been lying lifelessly on the ground slowly opened his eyes, looking around bewilderedly, “Where is this…?”
“Dad, you’re awake!”
The two young women who had been crying by his side saw the heavyset man regain consciousness and pounced on him, weeping with joy, “Dad, you scared us to death just now.”
“We thought we’d never see you again.”
Sword Without End silently withdrew the prop, without saying a word, and turned to walk away into the distance.
What a fucked up situation.
What the hell is all this? Does anyone know how hard it was for him to collect a globally unique character action? He went through that damned Human Theater map five times and perfectly imitated an emotional and crazed entrepreneur who had failed and become a wife murderer!
And only then did he obtain a globally unique character action.
He hadn’t used it many times before it was wasted just like that.
But there was no helping it; it was his own fault. He owned up to it.
Someone else’s family was living peacefully, and he suddenly killed that man—it was indeed a bit unreasonable. Although it hurt a bit, he had to save the man; otherwise, he wouldn’t be able to get past the guilt later on.
He had originally thought that the man was a rich, greasy guy who kept two young beauties, but who would have thought he was actually the father of two daughters.
It was just that the price was a little too steep.
The uses of a B-grade medical prop, and a globally unique character action, all wasted.
Your next journey awaits at Novgo
Just as Sword Without End was walking away, he suddenly stopped, his expression blank. He turned around and walked back towards the middle-aged man—this was a globally unique character action after all, to be used to save this man was beyond wasteful!
Did anyone know how much he treasured his globally unique character action?
The more he thought about it, the angrier he became!
Seeing Sword Without End turn back, the two young women kneeling by the man finally realized and bowed, their faces showing gratitude as they tremulously spoke.
“Thank you, big brother, for saving our father’s life.”
“If there is a chance in the future, we will repay you for saving our father’s life, this kindness…”
Before the two young women could finish speaking,
they saw Sword Without End stride directly to their father, then, without any hesitation, kicked the man’s head several times with substantial force before turning around once again, his expression grim, without uttering a single word.
After delivering those kicks, he indeed felt more comfortable, but he also felt like an idiot.
What a shitty situation.
He hadn’t done anything and suddenly found himself at a significant loss, stewing in his own frustration.
“…”
The two young women looked at Sword Without End’s retreating figure and at their father, now sporting a large bruise on his head, and fell silent, utterly baffled.
Why did this man save their father, only to come back and beat him up?

chapters.title: Chapter 148 - 148 - 147: "I Killed Her.
chapters.content:
Chapter 148 – 147: “I Killed Her.
Could those kicks actually be a special form of treatment? That would make sense. It surely couldn’t be that the sole purpose of reviving their father was just to kick him a few times, could it?
But from start to finish, this ’big brother’ hadn’t spoken a single word to them. He really was the epitome of aloofness.
…
Three minutes had already passed for Chen Yi.
He had even heard the sound of police sirens starting up below the apartment complex, estimating that in less than a minute, the police would break through the door.
By now, Chen Yi had finished reading all the diaries on the computer.
Yes, there was a hidden document on the desktop containing the daily diaries written by the original owner of the identity, recording everything from his modest business achievements to his emotional journey after the business failure.
It also detailed many minor points.
For example, the original owner of the identity liked to bite his fingers when anxious.
Another point was that the wife under this identity was exceedingly punctual and rarely left home; she had no friends and didn’t go shopping.
Usually, she bought clothes online and groceries were delivered to her door.
She would only leave the house once or twice a month, just like the original owner of the identity, preferring to stay at home.
However, the couple slept in separate rooms, not due to marital problems, but because the wife couldn’t stand the smell of her husband’s cigarettes.
Chen Yi sat in the living room, glanced at the bloodstain in the corner that had not been cleaned up, put his fingers to his mouth, and quickly scrolled through the wife’s phone, beginning to check the relevant information.
This game’s map wasn’t too difficult; as long as he could act convincingly as the male owner of the identity through the information seen and inferred, he would pass.
But obtaining the hidden mission was harder.
The hidden mission was to escape the crime.
Even though the wife’s body had already been disposed of, the bloodstains around the house were not thoroughly cleaned. The moment the police would break in, he would have to admit guilt and face the law on the spot.
Escape the crime? With what?
But after reading the diaries recorded by the original inhabitant of the computer, he discovered that this map actually offered the possibility of escaping the crime for the player.
In the self-narration in the husband’s diary,
His wife was a birth policy violator from the village, who, due to early fears of fines by her family, was never registered in the household, nor did she attend school, working instead in small workshops. Her family had also passed away early, leaving virtually no relatives behind.
Then she met him.
And had been with him ever since, the wife disliking going out to work and preferring life inside the home.
And to this day, the husband’s wife had no identity in the eyes of the police, unregistered and undocumented.
However, when the wife left the residential area or went downstairs to take care of other matters, she would still socialize with the security guards, and the neighbors could hear the couple’s quarreling.
In other words,
The husband’s wife existed only in the mundane world and had no trace within the official system.
If that was the case… there was room to maneuver.
Chen Yi once again confirmed that all accounts on the wife’s phone, including the SIM card, chat software, shopping apps, etc., were registered in the husband’s name.
Inside this house, there were traces of the wife everywhere.
The only place that lacked any trace of her existence was within the framework of rules.
Suddenly ——
“Bang! Bang!”
The sound of police battering the door echoed from outside; without any questioning, they initiated a forced entry, obviously already regarding him as a suspect.
Without any hesitation, Chen Yi swiftly typed a script into the Life Editor and invited himself to take on the role of actor.
“Bang!”
The door was smashed open!
Stay updated through empire
“Put your hands up, don’t move!!”
“Squat down with your hands up, squat in place and don’t move, let me see your hands!”
As the door burst open, a dozen fully armed police officers rushed into the room, guns pointed directly at Chen Yi, who was sitting on the sofa, and shouted at him.
The scene inside the room made their pupils constrict sharply!
The room was filled with a chaotic scene of a struggle, the corner of the living room was covered with bloodstains, and the pungent smell of blood filled the air, while the man was sitting on a bloodstained sofa with a cigarette in his mouth, his eyes lifelessly fixed on a dagger on the coffee table!
On the coffee table lay a dagger with a crimson blade, smeared with bloodstains!
The entire scene was that of a quintessential homicide!
There wasn’t even a need to investigate; executing him on the spot would not have been a mistake!
Throughout it all, Chen Yi never spoke, instead sitting on the sofa with a blank and disoriented gaze, allowing the burning cigarette between his fingers to scorch his skin without seeming to feel it at all and without removing it.
Even when several law officers pinned him down on the sofa and cuffed him with silver handcuffs, he didn’t utter a single word.
…
“Confess.”
Inside the interrogation room.
A few law officers, their faces stern and cold, looked at Chen Yi, who was handcuffed to the interrogation chair, and said word by word, “Where did you hide your wife’s body? Come clean for leniency, and perhaps you could have an opportunity to apply for a reduced sentence.”
“I hope you know that we have already obtained sufficient evidence of your crime; we brought you here for questioning not to collect evidence, but to offer you a chance to reduce your sentence.”
“Given the severity of this case, if you don’t come clean, you won’t be able to escape the death penalty.”
“Think carefully about it.”
Seated in the interrogation chair, Chen Yi murmured after a long silence with a dispirited look in his eyes, “I used to make money too. During that time, my wife was very obedient to me.”
“But when my business failed, she immediately changed her attitude towards me.”
“She began to detest the smell of my smoking, to complain about me not cleaning up my messy room, to resent that I didn’t make money and couldn’t afford her shopping habituals, to find fault with many things I did.”
“Until today, when we had a conflict.”
“I killed her.”
“I stabbed her in the abdomen with the dagger from the coffee table.”
“Then I searched online for how to clean up a body. I dismembered her corpse and fed it to the pet dog, cleaned all the blood in the house, and dissolved her hair with a solution and flushed it down the toilet.”
“Don’t blame me, she was the one who changed first, she deserved to die.”
“The abdomen?”
A law officer sitting behind the desk suddenly narrowed his eyes and looked at the bandaged wound on Chen Yi’s chest, “Where exactly was the wound?”
“About below the right chest, I think. I wanted to stab her heart.”
“But the fruit knife was a bit short, her breasts were too big, and I was worried that it wouldn’t penetrate the breast and reach the heart, so I stabbed below the right chest.”
The law officers exchanged glances without speaking, feeling that something was amiss.
Before Chen Yi was taken to the interrogation chair, they had found a puncture wound on him, located just below the right chest.
The evidence of the wound was clear: it was self-inflicted.
They had always assumed that he attempted suicide out of guilt before they arrived, but now… something seemed subtly off, didn’t it?

chapters.title: Chapter 149 - 149 - 148: "Shouldn’t She Die?
chapters.content:
Chapter 149 – 148: “Shouldn’t She Die?
Stay updated via
Chen Yi paid no heed to the complex emotions within the eyes of the law enforcement officers, instead, he appeared distant, as if on the verge of a mental breakdown, muttering to himself.
“I heard her agonizing screams.”
“I killed her.”
“It was her fault, she shouldn’t have treated me like that. After my business failed, she should’ve encouraged me, not suppress and doubt me every day, she was asking for death.”
“She deserved to die!!!”
Suddenly, he lifted his head, sitting in the interrogation chair, staring at the officers behind the desk with eyes red and near to bursting as he screamed, “You tell me, did she deserve to die?!”
“Didn’t she deserve to die?”
The officers exchanged glances, then rose in silence to momentarily pause the interrogation, taking the transcript in hand to consult their colleagues in the evidence department, preparing to verify a hunch they had.
“The suspect has confessed, he killed his wife with a dagger, and had his pet dog consume her dismembered body, washing away the blood with strong acid.”
“Do you in the evidence department have any leads?”
“Something’s not quite right.”
A young staff member from the evidence department sat at the computer table, flipping through photos with a frown, saying, “The forensics team has given a preliminary verdict. The meat in the stomach of the suspect’s pet dog is not human flesh but chicken breast.”
“And the blood on the floor is the suspect’s own; no other person’s blood was found.”
“Colleagues are now out collecting hairs, dander, and other evidence at the crime scene, we should soon have some information.”
“However, the records department says there is no name of Li Xiuqin as mentioned by the suspect; they can’t find any file on her. The outreach department has already sent people to inquire around the neighborhood.”
“The message from the outreach staff is that this Li Xiuqin seldom came downstairs, spending most of the time shopping online, and on the rare occasions she did go out, she didn’t greet others, keeping to herself and strangers to her intentions.”
“Additionally, the security guard at the suspect’s residential complex mentioned that the man was a complete recluse, barely leaving home, especially never with his wife. Never would they have imagined that this recluse could muster the courage to do something like killing his wife.”
The two interrogating officers exchanged looks again, then narrowed their eyes, murmuring thoughtfully, “So you mean to say, as of now, no one has seen the suspect and the victim together in public.”
“Yes, the intelligence we’ve gathered indeed confirms this; it seems their relationship was indeed very distant.”
…
Chen Yi sat calmly in the deserted interrogation room, his head bowed, silent, not speaking a word.
The original inhabitant of this body may have had a good attitude towards study, but his methods were lacking, the blood in the living room and the corner wasn’t thoroughly cleaned.
After a complete cleaning, he changed it to his own blood.
He might be rusty in other areas, but cleaning up a crime scene was his old line of work.
But he was injured again.
Chen Yi wanted to touch the wound on his right chest, but since his hands were cuffed to the chair, he couldn’t move; the wound still throbbed with a dull pain. By now, the police must have started to harbor doubts.
Though the wound was self-inflicted.
Blood and such were easy to clean, and a body could be hidden for a while, but hair and dander were tough to clear away.
When he walked out of the room to the living room, he saw a female corpse; it seemed she hadn’t been decomposed yet, and he only had a few minutes, so there wasn’t enough time to deal with the body.
Carrying a body bag down from the apartment complex was obviously too conspicuous.
Pressed for time, he could only wrap the woman in several layers of cling film from the kitchen, turned on the water heater, stuffed the body inside, and then reinstalled the heater properly.
Fortunately, the woman’s body was small enough to fit into the narrow space of the water heater.
This hiding place was not secure, merely temporary, but it was sufficient; when the police eventually found the body, he would’ve successfully exited the map and secured his hidden reward.
The only challenging aspect…
Was the hair and dander in the house.
Even a meticulously clean person would leave behind a lot of hair and dander in their home; without special methods and a lot of time, it’s impossible to thoroughly clean it up.
Particularly the bedsheet, clothes, pillows…
These are places where dander sticks, and to clean it up quickly, there is only one way, which is to burn it completely.
No need for a big fire, just an open flame inside the house; DNA in any area affected by the direct flame would be completely destroyed.
Destroying DNA isn’t that hard after all.
White vinegar, limewater, and such can effectively destroy DNA. Give him an hour, and he could ensure not a trace of DNA was left in the corners of the house; this was his expertise and not too difficult a task.
But the map only gave him less than ten minutes to prepare, and within those ten minutes, he had to check the diaries left by his original identity on the computer, leaving no time for such tasks.
Hence his solution was… to disregard it all.
DNA is a useful tool in investigations, but it requires that the victim’s DNA be previously cataloged for comparison. The problem is that the victim, according to societal rules, was entirely invisible.
Without even basic identification like an ID card or household registration, even if you find DNA from the victim, there’s no way to match it with any existing DNA records.
…
“The colleagues from the Evidence Department have a result, apart from the suspect, there is hair and dander from another person at the crime scene. They’re already extracting DNA, and the results should be out soon.”
Outside the interrogation room.
The young fellow from the Evidence Department was reporting the work progress to two colleagues standing in front of him.
“Hmm?”
The few police who had just interrogated Chen Yi furrowed their brows tightly, their train of thought abruptly interrupted. Initially, they had suspected that Chen Yi hadn’t killed anyone, and that it was a split personality disorder—his other personality had just killed itself.
But now, a significant amount of hair and dander from another person was found at the crime scene.
That situation didn’t add up.
“We have a result.”
The young man from the Records Department raised his eyebrows at the news from his colleague, “There are traces of DNA on the main bedroom bed and those women’s clothes at the crime scene. They have been DNA-matched.”
“Two types.”
“One is from the suspect, the other isn’t in the DNA database, and it’s unclear if it’s Li Xiuqin’s. We can’t compare it unless we find Li Xiuqin’s body.”
“You’re saying… there are DNA traces on those women’s clothes?”
“That’s right.”
A few interrogating officers nodded, some understanding in their minds. They pushed open the door to the interrogation room again, staring straight at Chen Yi with a cold expression and said each word deliberately.
“I’ve got good news for you, the collection of evidence has made significant progress.”
“We’ve found a lot of the victim’s DNA traces on the bedding and in the wardrobe at the crime scene.”
“If you confess now, we’ll deal with you leniently.”
Chen Yi hung his head in silence, not speaking. He really wanted to say impatiently that he had been confessing all along, otherwise what had he been doing all this time?
But he couldn’t say that, as such a tone was not quite suitable for the role he was currently playing.
Regarding this officer’s claim to have found the victim’s DNA traces, it was complete nonsense.
At most, they had found a stranger’s DNA traces. The DNA of the original identity’s wife wasn’t even in the database, so who could they compare it with?
However, no matter how the police questioned him, Chen Yi didn’t say another word, remaining silent. Although the officers were anxious, they were somewhat at a loss without definite direct evidence; they could not close the case.
The biggest problem now was the inability to find the victim’s body, only some DNA that couldn’t be compared or verified.
And right at that moment—
The colleague from the Evidence Department pushed the door open and whispered in the interrogator’s ear, “We found something on the suspect’s computer; come out and take a look.”
…
Outside the interrogation room.
The officers who conducted the interrogation were staring solemnly at a self-written diary on the computer. The diary detailed the suspect’s triumph when his business succeeded and the downfall after the failure, along with the stark difference in his wife’s attitudes before and after.
Through the text, one could vividly sense the suspect transitioning from pride to hysterical madness, every word filled with intense bitterness.
Then, they pulled up the browsing history the suspect had deleted.
Extensive pornographic site browsing records, along with messy web pages on how to deal with a corpse.
In the diary, they sharply noticed something unusual.
The suspect would call a prostitute every time his wife went out shopping, to put on his wife’s clothes and serve him personally; and today, this act was discovered by the victim, which led to a violent confrontation and resulted in him killing his wife, Li Xiuqin.
“Hurry, hurry, hurry!”
The interrogating officers fixated on the computer and urgently said, “Find the prostitute that the suspect found; this is an important breakthrough.”
“Not so fast.”
A colleague from the interrogation team furrowed his brows and spoke, “Look at the times these pornographic sites were browsed, they’re mostly at one or two in the morning. Put yourself in the shoes of a man for a moment—would you be looking at this stuff if you had a family?”
“What’s so strange about that?”
The colleague from the Records Department sitting at a nearby table touched his nose awkwardly, “After all, sometimes, you prefer the feeling of being in control.”
“Once or twice I can understand, but this browsing is nearly every night.”
“Would a normal man resolve the need by himself every night?”
“What’s so odd about that? Some men just don’t like women and prefer their own hands.”
“If he doesn’t like women, then why would he call a prostitute?”

chapters.title: Chapter 150 - 150 - 148: "Ding, congratulations to player Chen Yi for perfectly playing the role of Wife Murderer...
chapters.content:
Chapter 150 – 148: “Ding, congratulations to player Chen Yi for perfectly playing the role of Wife Murderer…
“You mean they had marital issues with their sex life?”
The colleague from the archives department was somewhat confused by the question, “The suspect would rather solve it himself every night than go to his wife?”
“No!”
The eyes of the police officer who just conducted the interrogation narrowed as his brain raced, “My guess is that there was no victim in this case at all, the only thing that died was the suspect’s second split personality!”
“I had this possibility in mind when I saw the wounds on the suspect, but now I’m nearly 70% confident that the victim is just a second personality split from the suspect.”
“The reason the suspect browses adult sites every night instead of seeking out his wife is not because he prefers his own hands, but because his subconscious knows that there is no wife of his in the master bedroom next door.”
“He was the only person in the entire house.”
“The DNA traces on the master bedroom’s bed and clothes came from the prostitutes the suspect hired, as stated in his diary that he would get a prostitute whenever his wife went out and have her wear his wife’s clothes and lie in bed, which also explains the source of the unfamiliar DNA in the room—the DNA belongs to the prostitute herself.”
“As for why the female clothes around the house all have traces left by the suspect, there is only one answer: the suspect would wear these clothes himself, assuming the role of the woman of the house.”
“The suspect wrote in his diary that his wife, due to overbirth in her early years, had no household registration or ID card, her family died early, she rarely went downstairs, and all of these were identities he fabricated for his second personality!”
“How could all this be such a coincidence!”
“We only need to find one thing now to confirm my guess, that is to locate the prostitute who left the unknown DNA, and we can get to the bottom of this by checking the DNA against that of all the prostitutes in the city.”
“All the prostitutes in the city?”
The colleague sitting next to the database yawned disinterestedly, “95% of the foot massage parlors, bath centers, clubhouses, or so-called lifestyle lounges in our city aren’t legitimate operations. There are at least thirty thousand prostitutes in these places alone.”
“And that’s just the ones with official employment, you might say they are the regular forces.”
“Those unregulated ones scattered in the dingy hair salons or foot massage shops in narrow alleys are countless.”
“These are still formally engaged in the industry, not to mention those who occasionally take a job, or those who have regular day jobs but pick up clients on the side after work, or students who can’t resist the allure of money and take on a few jobs and so on. Add them all up, and there must be at least a hundred thousand people.”
“You want to gather all these people for a check? You must be kidding. Aside from whether we have the capability to round up so many prostitutes.”
“Moreover, if the unknown DNA in the house belongs to a prostitute found by the suspect, then it will be even harder to find. Prostitutes whose DNA hasn’t been recorded are basically untraceable.”
“The only method is to find the contact information between the suspect and the prostitute.”
“However, we’ve checked all incoming and outgoing messages on the suspect’s phones, and there are no clues.”
A few people looked at each other, and they were stuck again.
The problem now was that they didn’t have enough evidence to prove that the suspect had committed murder since they hadn’t even found any information about the victim or the body.
But they also couldn’t prove the suspect hadn’t committed murder because there were just too many suspicious points.
They were in a sort of limbo.
The victim’s phone at the crime scene seemed like a normal woman’s phone; she would search on video platforms for things like how to do makeup, how to dress up, and so on, except that the real-name information logged in all the applications was the suspect himself, without any points of suspicion.
“Wait a minute!”
The police officer who was conducting the interrogation suddenly had a realization, his eyes lighting up with intensity, “Someone who wears makeup regularly will definitely leave cosmetic residue on their cheeks which can’t be completely removed with make-up remover!”
“We need to check for cosmetic residue on the suspect’s face!”
…
Chen Yi, who was on the verge of falling asleep in the interrogation chair, saw the interrogation room door burst open, with the police officers who had been interrogating him followed by someone in a white coat who looked like a doctor.
As soon as he entered the room, he pushed the door open without saying a word, started scraping skin flakes off Chen Yi’s face as if preparing to take them for testing.
Seeing this.
Chen Yi sighed with relief; these people had finally thought to test for makeup residue on his face. Just as some skin flakes had been scraped off and before these people could take them for testing, he silently activated the “Life Editor” prop.
The next second—
“Ah!!”
A piercing scream suddenly echoed in the interrogation room.
Chen Yi suddenly began to struggle violently on the interrogation chair, fear flashing over his face as he cried out with a trembling voice, “Don’t kill me, don’t kill me, I was wrong!”
“Don’t kill me, ah!”
The sharp and piercing voice startled the few policemen in the room, making them instinctively take a few steps back, their hands at their waists as they cautiously regarded the suspect in the chair.
However, before the police officers had a chance to proceed further, the fear in Chen Yi’s eyes vanished in an instant, replaced by venomous and fierce resentment as he glared at the air before him.
“You must die!”
“You deserve to die, don’t you?”
“What was your attitude toward me when I was successful in starting my business, and what was it after I failed?”
“Doesn’t a mercenary woman like you deserve to die?”
It was practically instantaneous.
The resentment and fierceness in Chen Yi’s eyes vanished once again, replaced by a look of full-blown fear, as he pleaded with a trembling voice, “I was wrong before, I admit my mistake, I truly realize I was wrong.”
“…”
Several police officers inside the interrogation room watched this scene with lingering trepidation, and only after Chen Yi’s head drooped as if he had fainted did they quietly leave the interrogation room.
…
Outside the interrogation room, half of the Law Enforcement Bureau’s personnel had gathered in an office, continuously replaying the scene of Chen Yi’s outburst that had just taken place in the interrogation room.
“Do you think there’s a chance that this was all an act?”
“No.”
The head of the Evidence Department shook his head firmly and said, “Although my position doesn’t allow me to make such definitive statements, if you look closely at the emotion transitions in the suspect’s pupils, every change and outburst is extremely natural.”
“An act?”
“If someone could mimic these emotions so perfectly, using them to escape murder charges would be a waste of talent; that person would certainly be Oscar-worthy if they entered the entertainment industry.”
“I agree with the head,” another person chimed in, “such emotions can’t be faked. I’m starting to believe that the deceased might really have been just another personality of the suspect.”
“I’d like to request a psychiatric expert to get involved and diagnose the suspect.”
…
“How does it look?”
Outside the interrogation room, a dozen or so Law Enforcement officers looked expectantly at the psychiatric expert who was walking out of the interrogation room and asked.
“Not too good.”
The casually dressed psychiatric expert shook his head: “Based on the preliminary observations, the suspect’s pupils are mostly dilated and unfocused, which are typical symptoms of someone suffering from a split personality disorder.”
“And almost all patients with split personality disorder have a hostile relationship with their other selves, with only a few forming friendly relationships with their alternate personalities.”
“Based on the current situation, it appears that the patient and his other persona became husband and wife, which seems to have happened after his business failure. The highs of business success, the lows of failure—the intense disparity could indeed trigger severe emotional fluctuations.”
“In the absence of anyone to stand behind the patient, the emergence of a second personality is indeed possible.”
“It seems that the patient knew his daily decay inside his house was a form of escapism, but after the failure of his last venture, he was unwilling to face reality. As a result, what began as a comforting second personality became increasingly critical of the patient himself under his own influence, eventually becoming hostile toward him.”
“This is quite a normal phenomenon.”
Explore more at Novgo
“If someone goes through a major issue, and blames themselves for it, detesting themselves every time they think of it to the point of self-loathing and continuous self-verbal abuse, gradually this persona might separate out, becoming vocal and berating the host regularly.”
“All abusive alternate personalities are not autonomous; they are manifestations of the patient’s own inner critical voice, the one that knows oneself best and cuts deepest, speaking through the mouth of the alternate persona.”
“Under such circumstances, it makes sense for the patient to choose to kill his second personality.”
And at that moment—
A colleague from the Evidence Department approached: “The lab results are in. There are indeed traces of makeup on the suspect’s cheeks.”
This meant that the suspect had been applying makeup regularly.
But why would a normal man wear makeup every day, unless he believed he was a woman?
All evidence at this point indicated one thing, that the suspect had killed his second personality, and the only victim in this case was the suspect himself; no other person was harmed.
“Let’s release him for the time being once the interrogation period is over.”
The interrogating officers waved their hands somewhat helplessly; they had thought to score a major success, but it turned out to be nothing more than a performance by a mentally ill person.
There wasn’t even a need to wait for psychiatric certification.
They hadn’t found a body, and afterward, a psychologist would provide psychological counseling to the suspect.
…
Inside the psychology consultation room.
Chen Yi listened intently to the psychologist in front of him as he went on incessantly with his counseling.
“Your wife has been taken away by us. She will never see you again. You can be at ease now. I hope you can make an effort to go downstairs more often, to feel the beauty of this world, to observe it more closely.”
“You must remember…”
Meanwhile, a notification sounded in his ear.
「Ding, congratulations to player Chen Yi for perfectly portraying the role of the Wife Murderer, with a performance accuracy of 96%, and…」
…
ps: There are some logical issues with the third chapter tonight, so I need to do a major rewrite; it will be posted a bit later, in about an hour or so.

chapters.title: Chapter 151 - 151 - 149: "Title Name": Wife-Killing Maniac.
chapters.content:
Chapter 151 – 149: “Title Name”: Wife-Killing Maniac.
“Ding, congratulations to player Chen Yi for perfectly playing the role of a wife murderer, with a perfect play rate of 96%, and successfully clearing the suspicion of wife killing.”
“Map Evaluation”: Through your exquisite acting and the logical traps you set, you successfully shifted the police’s attention. You not only played your own role to perfection but even perfectly acted out the role of the victim.
You are a natural-born actor and criminal. Given enough time, I believe you have the capacity to create the perfect crime.
You utilized almost every usable point, and the only imperfection was that shortly after you left, the police discovered the body hidden in the water heater and immediately identified you as the sole suspect and issued a warrant for your arrest.
Although you have already left the map, your method of exoneration wasn’t perfect; you did not manage the aftermath of your departure well.
“Map Reward”: Because your role-playing perfection reached 96%, you have obtained the final reward of the map, the globally unique character action “July Flying Snow”.
“Hidden Reward”: For completing the hidden quest of the map, you have earned the exclusive limited title “Wife-Killing Maniac”, as well as clean grey stone*2, 10,000 Points, and one B-grade random Prop Chest.
“ps: You have obtained the final reward of this map, you will no longer be able to enter this map again.”
A flash of white light.
Chen Yi didn’t return to the rooftop of the residential complex; instead, he arrived in a blank room where a series of scenes continuously scrolled across the large screen in the room.
There were scenes of the Law Enforcement Bureau discussing the case before departure, scenes of the evidence department collecting evidence, of interrogation police repeatedly watching his performance of the role switch.
Scenes of evidence technicians sealing the room and searching trace by trace with a UV light.
And scenes from about seven or eight days after he left, when the neighbors next door complained about a strong stench of decay emanating from the scene of the crime, prompting property management to check and discover a maggot-infested female corpse inside the water heater.
There were also scenes of the Law Enforcement Bureau fully mobilizing to start a city-wide manhunt for him.
However, all these events took place seven or eight days after his departure, fast-forwarded in his view, showing him, in the form of images, some of the information he couldn’t see while in the map.
When all the scenes finished playing.
The room where he stood began to slowly shatter, and after everything settled back to tranquility, he found himself securely standing at the edge of the residential complex rooftop, while Tuberculosis Rabbit and the others were gathered around a bonfire they had lit on the ground.
The fierce wind had died down a little, but it was still strong.
Causing the flames of the bonfire to flutter continuously.
Also, the sound of Tuberculosis Rabbit and others chatting could be heard nearby.
“I’m telling you, Tie Chui bro, I know that every time Yi gives you a cigarette, you only take it and never smoke it because you can’t bear to light it up.”
“But think of it this way, what if you suddenly died, and right before dying you realized you never smoked any of the cigarettes Yi gave you, wouldn’t that be an even bigger regret?”
“Think about it, don’t I make sense?”
At the instant Chen Yi’s silhouette reappeared on the spot.
The voice of Tuberculosis Rabbit came to an abrupt halt, and then he waved and called out loudly toward Yi’s back with a laugh, “Yi, come on over, we’re having grilled meat, the kind cooked over pure charcoal fire.”
“Hmm?”
Chen Yi did not turn around but instead observed the sky for a moment before furrowing his brows slightly and walking over to Tuberculosis Rabbit, asking, “How long was I inside?”
“Probably a little over an hour.”
He nodded slightly and sat on a small wooden stool by the fire reserved for him. He had spent around 30 hours inside the map, but only an hour had passed outside.
It seemed there was a discrepancy in the flow of time, a situation he had encountered before and had gotten used to.
Just that he felt a bit puzzled when he came out from the map and saw that there was not much change in the outside world’s daylight.
Chen Yi sat on the wooden stool and took a skewer of grilled meat passed to him by Tuberculosis Rabbit, staring at the spices on the skewer, which emitted a fragrant aroma. He suddenly realized that he was not hungry at all.
He had barely eaten anything during his more than 30 hours in the map, only drinking some water, and had not slept.
Yet, when he emerged, he felt neither hunger nor fatigue.
As if he had just finished a meal and woken up from a good sleep.
He did not dwell on it but instead turned his head to look at what he had gained from the map this time.
First, there was the globally unique character action of July Flying Snow. He’d glanced at the special effects briefly; they looked good, the coverage range was extensive, and it was a lot more attractive than those store-bought character actions that cost 1,000 Points each. It was worthy of the “globally unique” prefix.
No wonder Sword Without End, despite the risk of losing his backpack props, had ventured into this map several times.
The globally unique character action must have been too alluring for Sword Without End, but he was currently in Hell, with no news from him yet.
When Sword Without End died, his chat panel with Chen Yi dimmed.
It seemed that players here couldn’t communicate with those Hell Players.
He had no idea what the scene below might be like.
He wasn’t worried about Sword Without End not being able to come back, as with Sword Without End’s abilities, killing 10 ordinary players in the map shouldn’t be too difficult.
As for the title he was awarded, its quality was quite good; it was red.
“Title Name”: Wife-Killing Maniac.
“Title Quality”: Red.
“Title Effect”: The title effect seems to be obscured by some dust, perhaps using a ’clean grey stone’ could clear the dust and reveal the title effect.
“Title Origin”: “In the Life Theater C-grade map, complete the hidden quest to obtain.”
Title Effect was obscured by dust again, but fortunately, this time the Map Reward included 2 clean grey stones. Together with the 2 clean grey stones Tuberculosis Rabbit gained from the last map, they now had a total of 4 clean grey stones.
Without hesitation, he took out a clean grey stone and smashed it onto the title.
Immediately, the true effects of the title revealed themselves before him.
“Title Effect”: When you truly fall in love with a woman and kill her with your own hands, you will have a powerful buff effect where all props and skills have no cooldown and no cost for the following hour.
“Title Restriction”: Number of uses (3/3).
“…”
Chen Yi stood there with an expressionless face, silently pondering whether he had been too impulsive. Clean grey stones were precious, and it seemed a bit wasteful to use one on this title.
So far, the ways to obtain clean grey stones were scarce.
They were mostly gained by achieving hidden accomplishments or completing hidden quests in certain maps.
He still had several fully enhanced props that needed clean grey stones to unlock, and now, using one on this title, it turned out such a trashy effect.
Looking solely at the effect, it was definitely very powerful.
An hour without cooldowns or costs meant he could trigger the Septagon Badge infinitely, killing instantly!
No matter how strong or how many enemies there were.
Anyone who caught his eye would be killed in an instant, and just this effect alone could be considered underrated in red – it would be enough to warrant the effect being a rainbow or even black quality.
But the trigger condition was a bit too harsh.
Truly fall in love with a woman? How does one determine “truly”?
There’s no specific criteria, and you also have to kill the woman you love by your own hand.
Such a prerequisite can only be described as a tasteless and cruel hobby.
Chen Yi shook his head, casually wore the title on his head, and ignored its effect. He didn’t think he would ever get the chance to activate it.
First, he wasn’t sure if he would truly fall in love with a woman. But even if he did find a woman he truly liked, his intention would be to protect her, not to kill her by his own hands.
Unless he went mad.
“Yo-hee.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, who was sitting cross-legged on the ground chatting with Tie Chui, suddenly noticed the new title above Yi’s head and was momentarily stunned: “Is this the new title from the Map Reward, Wife-Killing Maniac… Looks like a pretty twisted title name there.”
“Yi, did you get the final reward?”
“I did.”
Chen Yi nodded, took out the pass in his hand, and placed it on the ground: “This pass can be used 4 more times, allowing for 4 more entries. See if you want to go in.”
“As for the Map Difficulty, it mainly depends on acting performance.”
“But I can use the Life Editor to guide you through a segment of the story. That way, when you enter again, you’ll have a better idea of which direction to perform in.”
“Jiaye, you should not enter. The identity played in this map is a man, only allowing male players to enter, so you can’t go.”
“And Tie Chui, think about whether you want to enter.”
“No, no, no.” Enjoy exclusive content from Novgo
Tie Chui, voraciously consuming meat, shook his head frantically at the mention, fear flickering in the depths of his eyes as he stuttered, “Don’t want… don’t want… I won’t enter, thank you… Yi.”
Sixty thousand times…
Sixty thousand times…
Who can understand what it means to have gone through the script with Tuberculosis Rabbit sixty thousand times on the rooftop? When he returned to reality, Tie Chui had even forgotten his own name.
And that was just a simple play.
If he were to enter the map Yi talked about, they’d probably have to rehearse at least two hundred thousand times.
Two hundred thousand times…
Just thinking about that number made Tie Chui shiver with fear, the terror in his eyes growing clearer. How could such a horrific form of torture exist in this world?
Seeing Tie Chui like this, Chen Yi didn’t press further. After all, such maps that relied on acting weren’t really suitable for Tie Chui, just as maps where props were ineffective, like Werewolf Kill, didn’t suit him either.
Everyone has maps that aren’t suitable for them.
If it weren’t for a forced invitation, one would naturally select the map that suited them best.
“Then you go,” Chen Yi said, pushing the pass to Tuberculosis Rabbit. He was about to advise him on something, when suddenly a prompt sounded in his ear.
“Ding, you have been forcefully invited by Hell Player Gao Yiming to enter the ’Reincarnation Map’.”
“Ding, it has been detected that you own the ’Great Demon King’ title.”
“You can choose to decline this forceful invitation.”

chapters.title: Chapter 152 - 152 - 150: "Remember in your next life, don’t talk too much before killing.
chapters.content:
Chapter 152 – 150: “Remember in your next life, don’t talk too much before killing.
“Gao Yiming?”
Chen Yi’s brows furrowed slightly as he looked at the prompt popping up in front of him, letting out a somewhat annoyed sigh. Was this bastard truly indomitable, clinging to him like a relentless specter?
This was the first time he saw the words “Hell Player” in an official system prompt.
During the updates for the previous few events, there was never any mention of Hell Players, indicating they must be a hidden setting.
This kid seemed to really enjoy forcing others into joining maps.
Without much deliberation, he chose to reject the forced invitation.
The title Great Demon King was meant for moments like this.
Although he really wanted to enter this “Reincarnation” map and get rid of Gao Yiming once and for all, since the other party was forcing him, they must be confident for a reason. No one knew the rules and contents of this map, but it was clear that the map was to Gao Yiming’s advantage, not his.
To rush into a disadvantageous and unknown map to battle an enemy.
Such an act was too foolish.
After all, Gao Yiming could only stir up trouble in Hell for so long; he naturally wouldn’t agree. Sword Without End had already gone down there, and with his strength, finding Gao Yiming and ensuring his complete disappearance from this world shouldn’t be any trouble at all.
Afterwards, he gave a few instructions to Tuberculosis Rabbit, who stood by his side waiting, before he witnessed Tuberculosis Rabbit entering the map.
…
“Rejected…rejected?”
In the depths of Hell, at a café in the city, Gao Yiming looked at the system prompt that appeared before him and was dumbfounded on the spot, finding it difficult to accept.
’Ding, your forced invitation has been forcibly rejected by player Chen Yi.’
’Your “Reincarnation” Map Access Pass’s last use has been exhausted, and it will no longer be usable.’
“Why was it forcibly rejected?!!”
Unable to accept the reality, Gao Yiming angrily slammed the table and roared, “If it’s a forced invitation, why could it be rejected? Do you guys even understand what the concept of a forced invitation is?”
“Forced, forced!”
This “Reincarnation” Map Access Pass was something he had obtained by flattering and paying a substantial sum to a powerful player he happened to encounter in Hell.
With only the last use left, he had already failed in his move against Tuberculosis Rabbit and had grown a bit wary of Rabbit. He shifted his target back to Chen Yi again, only to find that the expensive item he’d obtained had gone to waste without even having an effect!
If he was rejected, how could it ever consume his use without even entering the map?
This map was a perfect trap for killing players; he was 80% sure that if he could just pull Chen Yi into the map, Chen Yi would surely die here!
But now… everything was illusory.
Unfortunately, no one answered Gao Yiming’s question.
Many things in the Hell Map were replicas from the original game, yet there were still many differences, such as the original game having customer service while the Hell Map did not, meaning no one would answer Gao Yiming’s questions.
And at this moment—
A mechanical notification suddenly sounded in the café.
’Ding, a disturbance has been detected inside the shop, chaos level lv.1, initiating eviction process.’
Shortly thereafter.
A servant, dressed in a black vest and white shirt, approached Gao Yiming with an expressionless face, bending down and gently whispering, “Sir, could you please leave the store for a moment?”
“…”
Gao Yiming’s face went through several changes, turning from red to white, and after a few seconds of hesitation, he chose not to argue with the servant and instead got up to quickly leave the café with his head down under the gaze of everyone present.
Not everything in Hell was human; there were also ghosts.
At least the players referred to these beings as ghosts, or perhaps as order maintainers.
Places like cafés, convenience stores, restaurants, and the like, aside from a small number run by players, most shopfronts came with the Hell Map itself and had their own waitstaff.
They seemed just like the players, but it always felt like they were just people in skinsuits, lacking a complete human soul.
When players caused trouble in these shops, these skinsuit beings would assign a level to the disturbance and then give the appropriate response.
He had witnessed with his own eyes two men brawling in a restaurant being torn to pieces by these skinsuit waiters and thrown into the kitchen’s garbage bin.
Although he felt somewhat humiliated, he did not have the courage to talk back.
Don’t be fooled by how gently the servant spoke. If he had resisted, he probably would be sitting in a garbage bin right now.
After being kicked out of the café, Gao Yiming didn’t lose heart but instead stood on the sidewalk with eyes full of resentment, clenching his fist and gazing into the distance with a resolute expression, word by word, he said, “I won’t give up. You’ve ruined everything for me, and I won’t let you have an easy time either.”
“Wait for me.”
“When I show up before you again, I will bring you endless fear.”
“You will regret everything you did before.”
Just then—
A mocking voice suddenly rang in his ear.
“`
“Tsk, what’s going on here?”
“Too much anime lately, always like to say some cheesy lines to motivate yourself before doing anything?”
Before Gao Yiming could respond, he felt a strong hand land on his shoulder. A middle-aged man had appeared behind him out of nowhere and pulled him into an embrace.
“Look.”
Standing at the entrance of the coffee shop with his arms around Gao Yiming, Sword Without End seemed rather pleased as he gazed into the distance towards the twilight and lamented, “This world is truly beautiful, even coming to Hell, it feels just as wonderful.”
“Tell me, why can someone like you live so carefree in the former world, prospering even after the latter world descended, and still not completely dead to this day?”
“Whereas my wife, who never did anything wrong in her life, never even talked back when scolded by a vendor at the market—instead, she’d run back to the bedroom alone and wipe her tears. This woman, who never quarreled with anyone, should be blessed with longevity. So why did she die so young?”
“The world is really unfair.”
“What do you say, Gao Yiming?”
“Who are you?”
Gao Yiming slowly slid his hand into his pocket, ready to pull out a Prop and activate it at any time for a counterattack. This person knew his name, which meant he was the target, increasing the likelihood that the visitor meant no good.
“Don’t rush.”
Sword Without End shook his head with displeasure: “Don’t interrupt my train of thought, although this world is very unfair, it can also be fair.”
“Like that evening when my wife secretly ran back to the bedroom to cry, I took a wooden stick and a sack to find the market vendor and beat him severely in a place without surveillance.”
“After the latter world descended, I saved that vendor’s life twice and even gave him several life-saving Props, fearing he might die accidentally.”
“Whenever I miss my wife late at night, I find that vendor and beat him severely, which reminds me of the little moments with my wife.”
“She was too sick and left too quickly, without even leaving a letter for me to read when I miss her. The only link between me and my wife now is that market vendor.”
“Really… why do people like you deserve to live, while those who don’t, die.”
“Because you’re poor.”
“Your woman was scolded by the vendor at the market, probably because she was picky and haggled, making the vendor unhappy. Being selective when shopping indicates your financial status, only enough to allow your woman to hesitate over a few cents at the market.”
“Your woman wasn’t crying because of the market vendor but because of your incompetence.”
“If being concerned about a few cents when buying groceries and not having money for treatment leads to death by illness, isn’t that quite normal?”
Gao Yiming said emotionlessly, “The only reason your woman died of illness is because you’re poor. It’s because you don’t have the ability to make money in the market, because you’re useless. That’s why you regret your woman’s passing.”
“The person who should die the most isn’t me, it’s you.”
Your journey continues with Novgo
“If your woman had been with me, she definitely wouldn’t have died of illness. I have lots of money to treat her.”
“The world is unfair because people like you who lack the ability still want to grasp what you don’t deserve.”
“As for now—”
A cold light flickered in his eyes as he looked at the prompt panel only he could see in front of him.
「Charge time 4 seconds remaining.」
「Charge time 3 seconds remaining.」
「…」
「Charge complete. C-level Ultimate Sword Formation Prop ready for activation.」
“—it’s time for you to die!”
Gao Yiming roared furiously as he suddenly activated the Prop he had been hiding in his pocket. The moment the Prop activated, Gao Yiming was abruptly teleported into mid-air, looking down on Sword Without End standing on the street.
Behind Gao Yiming, a shadow of a bamboo grove appeared out of nowhere. The grove quickly solidified and then all the bamboo shattered in an instant, transforming into swords of bamboo shooting towards Sword Without End on the ground!
The moment the whooshing sound started,
The pedestrians on the street had already scattered to both sides, either fleeing into the distance or into the shops behind them.
In Hell,
Those ’ghost’ owned shops are not allowed to have riots or attacks, but other places, such as other players’ shops or on the streets, have no order at all.
In most cases, these ’ghost’ owned shops can serve as semi-safe zones.
Gao Yiming stared down at Sword Without End with a vicious expression, ready to relish the sight of this inexplicable man being killed by Ten Thousand Swords Piercing the Heart!
He didn’t know who this man was or why he was looking for him!
But the malice in the man’s words was clear enough. He’d been patient, responding to the man only to buy time, allowing his C-level Ultimate Sword Formation Prop to fully charge!
Now, the charge was complete.
He’d gained the upper hand.
“Remember in your next life, don’t talk too much before killing someone.”
Gao Yiming, floating in mid-air, looked down at Sword Without End who was about to die from Ten Thousand Swords Piercing the Heart and let out a somewhat relieved cold chuckle. While he couldn’t kill Chen Yi, taking out this fool eased some of the frustration within him.
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 153 - 153 - 151: "Thinking of revenge? You can’t get out, just focus on your work.
chapters.content:
Chapter 153 – 151: “Thinking of revenge? You can’t get out, just focus on your work.
“…”
Sword Without End didn’t raise his head, simply keeping it lowered in silence without speaking. It wasn’t until those hundreds of bamboo swords were about to pierce into his body that he slowly looked up at the bamboo swords in front of him and said softly,
“I hate this world, I hate all of you.”
“My wife was merely sick; she could have lived with just a little bit of money, but she died just like that.”
“I begged so many people for help, but not one person lent a hand.”
“Do you know?”
“After gaining power in the later era, my first thought was to destroy the whole world and kill everyone, to have you all accompany my wife in death.”
“But my wife always told me while she was alive to be kind and happy.” Discover more stories at Novgo
“I did as she said.”
“But that doesn’t mean I don’t feel resentment inside.”
For some reason.
When Sword Without End looked up at those bamboo swords about to pierce into his body, the swords, which were only inches away from him, suddenly stopped in mid-air and began to tremble slightly.
And the indifferent voice of Sword Without End resounded in the air above the street.
Gao Yiming watched this scene anxiously, frantically pulling out the prop from his trouser pocket to check it over and over again, not understanding why his bamboo swords had suddenly stopped in mid-air.
But now was obviously not the time to study this.
He clenched his teeth slightly, deciding that a gentleman’s revenge could wait ten years, and it was better to flee now. Then he pulled out another prop and activated it instantly; a pair of glowing flip-flops appeared beneath his feet.
He moved extremely quickly, stepping on the air and dashing towards the end of the street, nearly disappearing from sight in a matter of seconds.
“Kill me with a sword?”
Sword Without End looked at Gao Yiming’s vanishing back and said with an impassive face, “I was in a very good mood, you evil-minded fellow.”
“You really deserve to die.”
The next second–
The bamboo swords that had been frozen in the air in front of Sword Without End suddenly changed direction, shooting towards Gao Yiming’s back at an even faster speed!
Title Name: I Have a Sword, Who Dares Answer?
Title Level: Black.
Title Effect:
1: You are the Master of Ten Thousand Swords, able to control all sword-type props or vehicles at will.
2: Possessing Sword Tomb protection, no sword-type vehicle or prop can harm you.
3: When your sword indicates my will, any sword-type vehicle or prop you have will receive an additional amplification effect.
Title Restriction: The sword is the king’s way, and you must not coexist with others. After equipping this title, you will be unable to wear any other titles, and any previously equipped titles will be forcibly removed.
Title Source: In the B-level ’Sword Slashing Demon’ map, continuously slash your own Heart Demon 100 times.
ps: This title is unique.
“Puchi!”
The hundreds of bamboo swords returned at a faster pace, chasing down Gao Yiming and, after piercing hundreds of holes in his body, the sound of a heavy object hitting the ground was heard.
“Thud.”
Gao Yiming’s eyes were vacant as he lay in a pool of blood, his expression a mix of terror and ferocity as he clawed his way forward with difficulty, leaving behind a long trail of blood that caused onlookers’ hearts to quiver.
And the pedestrians on the nearby streets avoided the area immediately.
Once bustling with activity, the street now had only Gao Yiming lying in a pool of blood, clawing his way forward with difficulty.
One step after another.
Perhaps Gao Yiming also knew that he couldn’t escape this way, but he preferred to struggle a bit more before dying rather than to wait for death doing nothing. Even though it was useless, he couldn’t accept just waiting for death.
And at that moment.
“Thump, thump, thump.”
The somewhat dull sound of footsteps rang out beside Gao Yiming’s ears. He raised his head with difficulty to see the man standing in front of him, blocking his way. His eyes were full of blood, and he couldn’t even see Sword Without End’s face clearly.
Through the haze of blood, he could only see a figure blocking his path.
He harbored a glimmer of hope, his eyes filled with pleading, and with a trembling voice he said, “Please let me go, we don’t have any deep grudges, I shouldn’t have struck at you first, I’m sorry, I’m so sorry.”
“If you let me go…”
Before he could finish.
A large foot suddenly came down on his head. In the last moment before his consciousness faded, he heard the sound of his own skull shattering along with the sound of a notification.
“Ding, on June 18th at 17:37, you were completely eliminated in an SSS-ranked map called Hell, and will lose the chance to return to the main game forever. From now on, you will become a janitor and spend the rest of your life as one.”
“…”
Sword Without End looked down at the head he had crushed with his foot and stood there with a calm expression, silent without a word.
This man wasn’t wrong.
The person he hated the most was himself, the one who didn’t have the money to afford his wife’s treatment.
Perhaps if that lovely woman hadn’t ended up with him but had gone with a wealthy man instead, she really could have lived happily instead of dying of illness in his arms.
He had thought many times about destroying the world, filled with intense violence within, wanting everyone to accompany his wife in death, and even more to kill himself, the real culprit behind his wife’s death.
But before his wife died, she had made him promise to strive to live on for her, to be kind, and to live well. She would be watching over him from heaven.
He didn’t know what to do with himself.
He only remembered that before his wife fell ill, during their playful moments, he had acted out the roles of a Sword Immortal and a mortal woman with her. Perhaps she would find it amusing to see him become a land-bound Sword Immortal from heaven?
After a while.
Sword Without End stood in a pool of blood mixed with bits of flesh, looking up at the dusk above and suddenly burst into a grin.
“Don’t get me wrong, dear, I haven’t been killing indiscriminately. He was a malefactor, and I was merely eliminating injustice,” he said.
“I promised you I would be kind, that I wouldn’t kill without cause.”
…
“Where is this place?”
Gao Yiming, who had been drifting in darkness for an unknown time, finally came to his senses. Realizing he had not died but had become a cleaner, his eyes filled with delirious joy and he let out an excited roar.
“Wait, when I return, we will settle these grudges one by one.”
Just then.
A ghostly voice reached his ear.
“Still thinking of revenge? You can’t leave. Better get to work.”
“Who’s there?!”
Gao Yiming swiftly turned his head to look beside him, only to see a man with a huge belly floating in the void. His pupils flashed with horror—could a human belly possibly be two meters in diameter?
His belly was so huge.
Yet his limbs remained unchanged, which looked extremely bizarre!
“You seem quite surprised. Perhaps you haven’t yet looked down at your own belly,” the man said.
Gao Yiming faltered for a moment, a disturbing possibility flickering through his mind. He looked down at his own belly with some difficulty.
“No!!!!”
