It wasn’t that he had granted permissions.
It was that these defense props didn’t detect him at all.
Take, for example, the Grade C prop he had installed on Jiaye’s wall, Mr. Gecko.
Any behavior involving passing through or breaching the wall would alert Mr. Gecko, causing it to emit a piercing scream as a warning. But as he passed through the wall into the room, Mr. Gecko had no reaction whatsoever.
Hovering on the ceiling of Jiaye’s room, Chen Yi, with a demon-like gaze towards the model gecko on the wall, spoke thoughtfully
The principle wasn’t hard to guess.
Mr. Gecko could only detect three-dimensional invasions of the wall. His way of passing through didn’t count as invisibility and wall-phasing, nor as destroying the wall. It was more like finding a crack between two and three dimensions to slip through.
In other words,
It was like how guns in movies can’t kill the viewers. Different dimensions.
No matter how strong the effect, it was useless; he was completely unaffected.
Of course, this was just his speculation. What his current state was and the principles behind all these events, nobody could offer him a reasonable explanation. As for customer service… their role was merely to make you feel cared for by the game, not that the game genuinely cared about you.
They were just some servers hired by players. Could one count on them to answer such complex questions?
Chen Yi put these thoughts aside, not dwelling on them any further. Instead, he gazed down at Jiaye lying sweetly asleep on the bed and fell silent. After a long while, a trace of compassion flickered in his eyes. He slowly descended beside Jiaye and wrapped his arms around her.
Of course, he couldn’t actually move Jiaye’s body.
He could only approximate a gesture.
He couldn’t touch the tangible, nor could he feel the warmth of Jiaye’s skin; it was as though he did not belong to this world.
These past few days, Jiaye had suffered quite a bit of unjust treatment.
While Jiaye never brought it up, he was keenly aware that dying repeatedly entailed pain that couldn’t be trivial. Only now that it was all over could she sleep so soundly.
In the future, if possible, he’d try not to activate the Wife-Killing Buff again.
After all, she was his woman; he couldn’t just kill her every day.
A moment later, he softly kissed Jiaye’s head and was about to rise and leave when he noticed her eyelashes tremble slightly, and she murmured softly,
“Yi, it hurts.”
“…”
Chen Yi froze for a second before he noticed the sanitary pad on the bedside table. Had Jiaye been on her period these past few days?
Being killed so many times during her period was indeed a cruel fate.
Thinking about it,
If one died and descended into hell during their period, then revived and came back, would the period still be there?

chapters.title: Chapter 335: 296: "Directly Maxing it Out for You!
chapters.content:
Chapter 335: Chapter 296: “Directly Maxing it Out for You!
“`
The Jiaye in his dreams looked extremely pitiable, her trembling eyelashes tempted one uncontrollably to plant a kiss on them.
In fact, Chen Yi had done just that.
But very quickly—
he realized he was facing an exceptionally serious problem.
Although this spirit body state had extremely strong defenses, and up to this point, he was not clear on which prop could affect him, not even those props that could see through invisibility seemed capable of finding him. But the problem was, he surely couldn’t maintain this state forever, could he?
Even though his injuries were gone, he himself was also gone!
Wasn’t this problem even more serious?
“…”
Chen Yi’s mouth twitched slightly as he floated alone to the balcony, hovering mid-air, and began to silently ponder this issue.
His current state.
Immune to damage, immune to injury, but without a physical existence.
To exit this state,
he had to lift the “Seems Like A Demon” title effect, but once he did so, it meant he absolutely could not die from sustained damage—without this effect, he would immediately perish and fall into hell.
Then, he’d have to climb back from hell.
And on the return map, he would have to sit in a beach chair, and once he left the beach chair, his body would rot again, dying on the return map to face permanent death.
But the problem was, he couldn’t attack while lying on the beach chair.
How could he clear the map without being able to attack?
Wasn’t that a dead loop?
Unless… unless he killed Jiaye once more, using the Wife-Killing Buff to limitless use the B-rank prop “Forever Pure,” in order to return from hell safely.
“…”
Thinking this, Chen Yi’s mouth once again twitched involuntarily. What kind of situation was this, to be stuck here again.
He had just secretly sworn in his heart that he would never kill Jiaye again, unless it was a critical moment—a real man doesn’t kill his own wife day in, day out, what kind of behavior is that?
But now, it seemed he needed to?
Meanwhile—
Tuberculosis Rabbit and Sword Without End among others, seemed to have also woken up, stretching as they walked onto the rooftop.
First checking around and not seeing the familiar beach chair of Yi, Tuberculosis Rabbit shrugged somewhat uninterestedly: “Seems like Yi hasn’t woken up yet. What do you think, Sword Without End, what shall we do today?”
“Not woken up?”
Sword Without End scanned around doubtfully: “That’s not right. Didn’t you hear the song that has been playing by our ears all this time?”
“I did. I was sleeping so soundly when it disturbed me.”
“Then that settles it. The system announcement indicated that the song is Yi’s activation of the ‘Seems Like A Demon’ title, which is then played beside every player’s ears worldwide. If Yi has activated the title, how could he possibly still be asleep?”
“Yeah.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit paused, then suddenly realized and scratched his head: “If Yi is up, why isn’t he on the rooftop? Where did he go?”
“Still inside the building?”
“Don’t know, shall we check?”
“Okay.”
After that, Tuberculosis Rabbit and Sword Without End chatted casually while walking towards the palace at one side of the rooftop.
By this time, their rooftop was completely transformed beyond recognition.
First of all, the beach chairs had turned the rooftop into a huge sandy area, which occupied far more space than the original size of the rooftop, and in one corner of the sandy area, Yi’s Crimson Palace was placed as their residence.
The precursor to this Crimson Palace was the Crimson Throne.
But after the title “Violators Annihilate Nine Clans” was promoted to “Violators Annihilate the Whole Clan,” the original title effect of the Crimson Throne evolved into the Crimson Palace, which had pretty decent decoration, ambiance, and defenses.
It was more than suitable to use as their den for sleeping.
With this palace, they had not gone back to their original rental house to sleep for a long time, instead, every member moved their homes into this Crimson Palace, including Sword Without End.
Sword Without End was the type who was satisfied on his own, so he didn’t have much to move during the relocation, except for some mementos of his deceased wife, he didn’t bring anything else.
Chen Yi, who had witnessed all this from beginning to end, raised his eyebrows silently without speaking a word, completely unnoticed by Tuberculosis Rabbit and Sword Without End, who had absolutely no idea that there was a person floating above their heads.
Seems like I need to be careful with my words in the future.
It’s best to keep confidential matters under wraps.
Walls have ears, after all; in what seems like a safe environment, no one knows how many ears and eyes could be concealed around them.
There is always a higher sky, and beyond every person, there is another.
Just then—
A system notification popped up before him.
“Ding, the Starfield Project Team has sent you a private message.”
“Starfield Project Team: Player Chen Yi, hello. First of all, thank you for obtaining two monuments for the Starfield Project Team, a unique existence in the history of current games.”
“For a single Starfield to hold two monuments from the same player, it is truly unprecedented.”
“Thank you for the immense effort you’ve put forth for the Starfield Project Team, and for bringing great glory to us in the gaming world.”
“Starfield, because of your emergence, player Chen Yi, has the opportunity for self-naming.”
“Considering the significant contribution you’ve made for Starfield, we’ve decided to grant you this naming opportunity. Any name you choose will forever be the official title used by Starfield in external negotiations.”
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 336: 296: "Maxing You Out Immediately!"_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 336: Chapter 296: “Maxing You Out Immediately!”_2
“…Hmm?”
Chen Yi’s eyebrows raised slightly, a trace of surprise flashing in his eyes.
He remembered someone from Club 33 saying that it wouldn’t be long before the Ding Qi Starfield Project Team would contact him, asking him what would be a good name to change for the Ding Qi Starfield Project Team. Originally, he didn’t take this matter to heart.
Because he knew that within the Ding Qi Starfield Project Team, there were quite a few of his sworn enemies.
For example, the so-called Feng Family.
The Feng Family stood behind the Solar Star Project Team, and they had also planned the invasion of Blue Star by Logitech Star. The Feng Family occupied nearly a quarter of the power within the Ding Qi Starfield Project Team, wielding no small influence.
With such people sabotaging from within, this naming right surely wouldn’t fall to him.
He had even thought that the Feng Family might give the Ding Qi Starfield Project Team some name that would humiliate him.
Such as Yi Son Starfield or something like that.
To his surprise, the Ding Qi Starfield Project Team actually did give him this naming right.
Had the Feng Family temporarily backed down? Or was the Feng Family’s power within the Ding Qi Starfield Project Team not as great as he had imagined?
He didn’t dwell on it, but instead pondered the naming matter carefully and after a long while, he gave his answer.
“Just call it—”
“Annihilation Starfield.”
‘…’
The Ding Qi Starfield Project Team on the other end was also somewhat baffled. Normally, most players would choose a name with their own distinctive characteristics under such circumstances; why would they choose such a name that seemed to have little connection with Chen Yi?
What would be the meaning of such a naming?
Take, for instance, Dad Qi Starfield.
Although the name is a bit common, the usage is not wrong. It provides player Wang Qi with enough respect, and on the other hand, it firmly ties Wang Qi and Dad Qi Starfield together, instilling a sense of responsibility.
This is like why in some tribes, children often take the father’s surname; it is the fathers who name them.
The principle is the same,
If the child, bearing your name, encounters a problem, will you not take care of it?
A surname has long been a manifestation of the binding power of a sense of responsibility.
The naming of a starfield follows the same principle.
Although this naming right is given to the Ding Qi Starfield Project Team, by convention in the upgrade game, this naming right is gifted to the player who earns the monument for the starfield, to firmly bind the player to that starfield.
Annihilation Starfield… this name is not very good.
“Does it have a special meaning?”
“Yes,” Chen Yi nodded calmly, “I wish the upgrade game would come to an end soon, and the world achieve peace.”
‘Um… Player Chen Yi, hello, we had a bit of a bad signal just now and didn’t get your message. Could you repeat that, please? By the way, we forgot to tell you earlier, in order to provide better service to players, all conversations between project teams and players are archived in the cloud for the upgrade game to access and review at any time.’
“I wish for wars to end soon and for peace to return to the world.”
“Understood. Then, according to the player’s wishes, the Ding Qi Starfield will be renamed Annihilation Starfield, and this statement will serve as the external declaration of the Annihilation Starfield.”
The next second—
A system announcement echoed in the ears of some.
“`
“Ding, from this moment forth, Ding Qi Starfield is officially renamed as Annihilation Starfield.”
“Let it be known to all.”
“Declaration to the public: May the wars cease and peace return to the world.”
Not everyone could hear this system announcement.
Only members of the Starfield Project Teams, Seed Players of the Fourfold Planet game, and some leaders of races from the Fourfold Planet and above could hear it.
Hearing this prompt also meant that one had officially entered the core layer of the Fourfold Planet game.
As for players at a slightly lower level, whether they heard it or not didn’t make much difference. Even if they did hear the announcement, they wouldn’t understand the meaning of it, let alone grasp its significance.
Meanwhile, the 33 Club chat group was continuously filled with various congratulatory messages.
“Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi”: “Congrats, brother, Annihilation Starfield is a great name, very impressive. But I think Yi Daddy Starfield sounds even more imposing.”
“Northwind Starfield, Beimu Qi”: “Congratulations to Brother Chen Yi on the successful naming and officially becoming the spokesperson for Annihilation Starfield. In the maps to come, you’ll need to showcase your abilities, so that certain people won’t underestimate you.”
“Li Mu Starfield, Li Mu”: “That’s right, but Chen Yi, you don’t need to worry. When the time comes, we will all be there to support you. It’s an old tradition of the 33 Club to ensure the newcomer earns enough respect. Such occasions are also a time for team building. Speaking of which, where’s Li Yi?”
“I’m Really Fucking Awesome Starfield, Li Yi”: “Right here, right here. Don’t shout, it’s just the cost of a team-building event. In the time it takes to send a message in the group, I’ve already earned it back. I, Li Yi will cover all expenses for this team-building event.”
“Wait a minute?”
Chen Yi furrowed his brows, speaking with a hint of confusion, “By the sound of it, why does it seem like I’m about to be forcefully thrown into a map?”
The more he read the chat in the group, the more something felt off.
At first, he thought they were just telling him to perform well in future maps, to prevent others from looking down on him, but that was strange. His performance in the maps wasn’t even known to Blue Star players, so how could other players know?
But as the conversation went on, it became even more peculiar. They were going to support him, he would need a crowd for his next map? It was some tradition of the 33 Club?
What was all this about?
“Northwind Starfield, Beimu Qi”: “It seems like the staff of the Annihilation Starfield Project Team might have been a bit lax in their duties, not communicating such important information to Brother Chen Yi right away.”
“Let me explain briefly. It’s like this: when you secure a Monument for a certain starfield and successfully name it, after meeting these two criteria, you must enter a map.”
“This map will be live-streamed in real time to all players from Triple Planet and higher starfields.”
“There are two main purposes. One is to spread the news of the starfield’s renaming through this method, making it widely known. The other purpose is for you, as the spokesperson of this starfield, to demonstrate your strength and your fangs to the outside world.”
“As for the map itself, it’s something you and your Annihilation Starfield Project Team decide internally.”
“Generally speaking, you will choose a map that fits you perfectly, so that you can express your strength to the fullest.”
“For instance, if your strength lies in unmatched individual power, then your project team will find a map that allows you to best showcase that single power, without any Prop restrictions or strength limitations.”
“Take for example ‘I’m Really Fucking Awesome Starfield’s Li Yi, whose strength is having an endless amount of Points, an overwhelmingly strong business acumen. On the day of his ascent, his starfield project team picked a map for him where he started naked in an uninhabited desert.”
“It took Li Yi three days to walk out of the desert and reach a city on the map. He spent another three days eating, sleeping, shopping, and drinking, and in the last three days, he turned a Steel Coin that he picked up off the street into one million Gold Coins right under everyone’s eyes.”
“He became famous in one battle!”
“At the same time as everyone learned of ‘Bing 997 Starfield’ being renamed to ‘I’m Really Fucking Awesome Starfield,’ they also came to know of a player with an insanely talented business acumen and the one who had secured the Monument.”
“Every member in the 33 Club chat group has lived through this moment.”
“You can think of the last Entire Star System announcement as a teaser, and this full map live broadcast is the first step for Annihilation Starfield, and you, Chen Yi, to step into the public eye.”
“Make it count. When the time comes, the members of the group will be there to support you.”
“As for saving face.”
“We’ll max it out for you!”
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 337: 297: "Profession": God of Wealth.
chapters.content:
Chapter 337: Chapter 297: “Profession”: God of Wealth.
The people in the 33 Club chat group talked in great detail, which in layman’s terms, meant live streaming the completion of a single-player map under the watchful eyes of the majority of players.
Moreover, the difficulty of this single-player map wouldn’t be too high and would perfectly match the player’s strengths and advantages.
It somewhat resembled a performance match.
It was merely a window for external promotion.
It wasn’t an official expedition into the map.
In theory, he should just prepare the Wife-Killing Buff in advance and wreak havoc during the performance match.
But for some reason, he felt an ominous sensation within.
Chen Yi furrowed his brows slightly, remaining silent, as he hadn’t forgotten that in the Annihilation Starfield—formerly Ding Qi Starfield—there was a faction within the Annihilation Starfield Project Team that was a sworn enemy of his.
The so-called Feng Family.
In terms of naming rights, the Feng Family hadn’t tried any dirty tricks behind his back, but what might happen during this performance map was unpredictable.
After a while,
he tentatively asked in the group: “If there is a dispute between a player and the project team, is there any way to kill a member of the project team?”
“…”
“…”
Soon, a series of ellipses once again traveled through the 33 Club chat group.
“I’m Really Fucking Awesome Starfield, Li Yi”: “Dude, you couldn’t possibly be a god of slaughter incarnate, could you? Do you only deal with issues through force? Does your definition of human relationships equate to ‘those who oppose me perish’?”
“Li Mu Starfield, Li Mu”: “What’s the matter, Brother Chen Yi, are you at odds with the Annihilation Starfield Project Team? There’s not much that can be done about that, theoretically. The project team and players shouldn’t be able to interact at all, but due to some vested interests, project team members still end up in contact with certain players, and the game has yet to fix this bug, or maybe it doesn’t regard it as a bug, so it has remained.”
“But only the game itself has the authority to deal with project team members; you can think of the project team as employees of the game and a symbol of it, and players are not allowed to kill any project team member.”
“Players absolutely cannot kill project team members; there’s no way at all. It’s a supreme rule. Even if a player does manage to kill a project team member through some bug, it would be a severe insult to the game’s dignity, and the end result would be the player being crushed by the game.”
“Whether we are players or part of the project team, we all exist under the game’s rules. Step on the game’s face, and there’s only one possible outcome.”
“I would advise you, Brother Chen Yi, to avoid having such thoughts.”
“Moreover, in most cases, the interests of players and project teams are intertwined; the project team needs you as a player to score more points and gain promotion qualifications, and you likewise need the project team to access insider information and privileges. Both sides should be helping each other; why would there be hatred?”
“Take the Annihilation Project Team, for example. You’ve acquired two Monuments for them. They should be praising you rather than making an enemy of you, right? There shouldn’t be any grievances between you.”
“…”
Chen Yi stayed silent, not replying. Theoretically, it was true, but the situation was a bit more complicated for him to explain in detail. According to what he knew so far, most of the Annihilation Starfield Project Team staff were friendly towards him, but he hadn’t had much contact with the Feng Family, so he wasn’t sure about their attitude.
If the Feng Family was willing to wipe the slate clean of past grudges, he wouldn’t mind letting the Feng Clan live a little longer before he had the power to act.
“Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi”: “There’s actually a way. If the project team makes a mistake, they will be punished; the severity of the punishment can vary. If you can make the project team commit a mistake, they will naturally face the appropriate punishment from the game.”
“Remember how a few years ago, that top player did just that?”
“Having grudges too deep with their own Starfield project team, which couldn’t be resolved, they eventually snapped after being backstabbed by the project team again, and caused their tribe over the course of three months to slaughter all players of their Starfield.”
“After three months, not many of that top player’s tribespeople were left either.”
“After committing genocide against their own race, that top player committed suicide on the spot, leaving not a single surviving player in the entire Starfield. The project team of that Starfield was consequently eternally imprisoned in the depths of hell to serve as Scavengers.”
“Though the price was steep, it got the job done.”
“Beimu Qi Starfield, Beimu Qi”: “Why are you telling Chen Yi about this? You’re not suggesting he should do the same, are you?”
“Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi”: “No, that’s not what I was implying. Just chatting and mentioning it happens; such actions are too foolish, as mutual destruction is always the worst strategy.”
Chen Yi stopped paying attention to the conversation in the 33 Club chat group and decided to remove the Seems Like A Demon Title Effect first, then head to the underworld to regain his human form.
Even though his body would bear a permanent wound that would never heal and he could only sit in a beach chair, at least he would still have a human form, unlike now where he was turned into nothingness, with not even his own existence perceptible to himself, only his consciousness remaining.
This feeling was too eerie.
Just at this moment—
A notification box suddenly unfolded before his eyes.
“Ding, congratulations to player Chen Yi for securing two Monuments for the Annihilation Starfield, thereby securing a permanent place in the history of the game.”

chapters.title: Chapter 338: 297: "Occupation": God of Wealth._2
chapters.content:
Chapter 338: Chapter 297: “Occupation”: God of Wealth._2
“One hour from now, player Chen Yi will enter the map ‘Rogue Star’, and the entire process of clearing the map will be broadcast live in front of players from the entire star system,” the announcement read. “We hope Chen Yi can make a name for himself on this map, promote the Annihilation Starfield, and seize his exclusive title.”
“ps1: Upon successfully clearing the map, the player will be awarded an exclusive title that reflects the player’s actions on the map. This title possesses absolute uniqueness and is extremely rare, only available to players who capture the Monument and successfully clear their debut map.”
“ps2: Once the title is obtained, the player can freely choose to display all titles or just this one.”
“ps3: The map was selected by the ‘Annihilation Starfield Project Team’ and is rated at difficulty level S, just so player Chen Yi is aware.”
“ps4: Additionally, upon clearing the map, there will be an opportunity to obtain an exclusive profession. Only players from planets with sixfold or higher and players who have captured the Monument can unlock the professional system to choose their own profession. Below is a brief description of some of the professions as a reference for players.”
Soon, four vertical tip-boxes popped up in front of him.
“Profession”: Thief.
“Occupational Effect”: Forbidden to carry any props, but can randomly steal 10 items from another player’s backpack for temporary use for three hours. After the time expires, the items automatically return, and the stolen props will not have any consumption and can be used continuously three times without cooldown.”
“Occupational Restriction”: Using the skill once will result in a 12-hour cooldown period.”
–
“Profession”: Lawyer.
“Occupational Effect”: Can set three custom laws. Any player who breaks these laws in the lawyer’s presence will receive corresponding punishment, including the lawyer themselves. As a lawyer, breaking your own laws will result in even harsher punishment.”
“Occupational Restriction”: Changes to custom laws must be spaced at least a month apart.”
–
“Profession”: Gunman.
“Occupational Effect”: When using any firearm props, there will be no consumption and both power and effects will be doubled. However, it will be impossible to carry any firearms in the backpack.”
“Occupational Restriction”: Even an E-grade Air Food Series Prop cannot be carried.”
–
“Profession”: Gold Miner.
“Occupational Effect”: Once a day, can randomly throw a hook that will grab something from the entire game at random. This could be anything from props, Skill Fragments, staff from the project team, a boss from some map, pebbles, trash, or Scavengers, etc.”
“Occupational Restriction”: Using it once will result in a 24-hour cooldown period.”
–
The four panels that popped up were just an introduction to four professions, not for him to choose from, but to give him an overview of possible professions.
As long as he could clear this map,
He would also be able to obtain an exclusive profession of his own.
Chen Yi frowned in thought without speaking. These professions seemed more like amplifying a certain aspect of an originally versatile player while weakening other areas.
For instance, the “Thief” profession seemed potentially strong or weak.
To randomly steal 10 items from a player.
If one managed to steal powerful items, they’d instantly rise to power, but if all that was stolen were trash-like Air Food props, one would truly be waiting for death.
The cost to pay was the prohibition of carrying any props.
A player,
If unable to carry props and relying only on titles and a few limited skills, would see their strength greatly reduced and might even fail to form an effective combo.
Moreover, the stolen items were not permanently owned, but merely borrowed; after three hours they would have to be returned.
Borrow and return—that still smacks of professional ethics.
The lawyer profession seems a bit vague, with custom laws. It’s similar to a player version of a new rule each month. Players can set their own rules, which suits some of the more sensitive players.
For instance, if a player can’t stand the smell of smoke.
They could set a rule that no one is allowed to smoke, so any player who smokes in their presence would face corresponding punishment.
Just don’t know if there are any limits to this custom law-making. Otherwise, if someone sets a rule that no one can breathe, wouldn’t that be a group AOE strike? Wherever they go, they’d hit, effectively becoming a human-shaped, autonomous nuclear weapon.
Plus, the specifics of this punishment haven’t been clarified.
The remaining gunner and Gold Miner professions also seem to have their own pros and cons.
But before this, he’d never learned about the professional system. After hesitating for a moment, he still decided to ask in the 33 Club chat.
“Do you guys understand the professional system? I just got a system notification that in an hour, I need to enter a map. After getting through it, I’ll get an exclusive profession based on my performance in the map.”
“Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi”:”Hey, almost forgot to tell you, it’s been so long since a newbie joined the group, I’ve almost forgotten the process. In most cases, planets of sixfold and above will initiate the professional system. Then every player can pass through the map trial to get their own exclusive profession.”
“The system will present you with three professions that match your performance for you to choose from, and you can pick the one that suits you best.”
“Why do you think the power gap between sixfold planets and fivefold planets is even greater than between fivefold and onefold planets?”
“It’s because the sixfold planets have an additional professional system, which greatly enhances the collective strength of race players. Of course, this is still too far off for your planet, seeing as your planet hasn’t even finished the newbie protection period yet.”
“Besides, each player who captures the upgrade game monument can break this limit. As long as you clear your first debut map, you can get your own exclusive profession and a special title based on your performance in the map.”
“It’s a nice benefit for those who have taken the upgrade game monument.”
“Li Yi’s profession is the God of Wealth, which fits him perfectly. In front of Li Yi, no matter how strong other players are, they have to show him some respect, why? Because his profession falls under the category of Rule Kill.”
Soon.
Wang Qi in the 33 Club chat group, sent up a screenshot of the profession introduction.
“Profession”: God of Wealth.
“Occupational Effect”: Once activated, you’ll engage in a mandatory comprehensive wealth contest with a player within your line of sight. The player with lesser wealth will be deemed dead, effective immediately. Wealth includes Points, Skills, Props, etc., but excludes investments, bonds, equities, etc.
“Occupational Restriction”: After use, it enters a 24-hour cooldown period.
“Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi”:”How about it? Isn’t that title cool? With Li Yi’s financial power, even players from five and sixfold planets, who would dare disrespect him in his presence?”
“When it comes to wealth, how many in the entire upgrade game can match up to Li Yi?”
“I’m Really Fucking Awesome Starfield, Li Yi”:”Guys, can you not blow smoke up my ass? If this gets out, won’t I be laughed to death? My little Points, in the whole upgrade game, are nothing!”

chapters.title: Chapter 339: 298: "Wish me a triumphant return, everyone.
chapters.content:
Chapter 339: Chapter 298: “Wish me a triumphant return, everyone.
「Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi」: “Apart from this, there are many interesting professions, such as the Thief profession. In most cases, this profession is considered pretty lackluster since everyone’s bag is filled with who knows how many props except for new players.”
“Randomly stealing ten props, it’s hard to steal anything too powerful.”
“Even if you do steal a powerful prop, what’s the use if you can’t carry props yourself? That disadvantage is too significant. What if you see a dropped prop on the ground and you want to pick it up but can’t? That’s practically like sitting in jail.”
“But rumor has it that in a certain map, there was a once-in-a-blue-moon encounter of ten players whose profession was all Thieves. It’s strangely coincidental.”
“It’s said that during that map, the ten players just stared at each other, completely bewildered.”
“Their occupational effect was that they couldn’t carry any props and could only steal from others, but the problem was that nobody had any props in their bags to steal from, which left everyone dumbfounded.”
“That’s not even the funniest part.”
“The craziest thing happened in a map that can hold 20 players, where 19 of them were Thieves, and the one remaining player was a Gunman. As soon as the map started, the props in the gunman’s bag were completely plundered by the 19 Thieves.”
“His bag was utterly empty.”
“He declared surrender, tears welling up with no tears to shed.”
“A Gunman player without any Firearms props, what could he do? There’s nothing to do except wait for death. Usually, Gunmen serve as the main force of a team, and there would be at least three players tasked with protecting him. No one knew why that Gunman decided to enter the map alone that day.”
“With the Professional System in place, the strengths and weaknesses between different professions have become clearer, leading to a higher dependence on teamwork.”
「F*cking Awesome Starfield, Li Yi」: “My profession is actually not very useful in most situations. It’s more of a deterrent or symbolic profession. When it comes to true combat power, it’s Wang Qi’s profession that’s reliable. His profession is Bloodthirsty Butcher, a name well-known across many Starfields.”
Soon—
Li Yi also posted an introduction chart for the profession of Bloodthirsty Butcher in the group.
「Profession」: Bloodthirsty Butcher.
「Occupational Effect」: Upon activation, one will absolutely not die within one hour, but the injuries received will not be reduced in the slightest.
「Occupational Restriction」: After one activation, it will go into a 24-hour cooldown period.
–
Chen Yi looked at the profession introduction in the chat window, pensive but not speaking. It’s another new profession, and the occupational effect sounded decent with an hour of enforced invincibility.
This occupational effect paired with his Wife-Killing Buff would be a sure kill.
It was much more effective than his Absolute Defense beach chair; lying on that chair, he couldn’t attack or use any skills, whereas this occupational effect wouldn’t affect any attacks at all.
But for Wang Qi, this occupational effect still had its drawbacks.
After all, though one wouldn’t die within an hour, the injuries wouldn’t diminish by a bit. If one ended up being beaten to a pulp, even if not dead, there would be no combat ability left, just a conscious mound of mush.
But for him—
With his Wife-Killing Buff, he could infinitely activate “Forever Pure,” and as long as the injuries weren’t fatal, he could recover in an instant.
His eyes narrowed, and suddenly a flicker of anticipation rose within him for this so-called debut map.
If he could obtain this profession, then his strength would level up further!
He initially didn’t feel much for this debut map, but now it seemed to be somewhat useful after all.
According to the chat in the group,
The so-called professional choice is dependent on one’s performance in the map, randomly presenting three professions to choose from, where one will select a final profession.
He didn’t know what kind of performance on the map could land him the Bloodthirsty Butcher profession, but of all the professions he’d seen, he favored this one the most.
Even if Li Yi’s “God of Wealth” profession seemed to be a bug, capable of Rule Kill, he felt nothing for it.
Firstly, he was not clear on the priority level of the Rule Kill rules, secondly, he didn’t have that many Points, and most importantly, even if he had enough Points, he had no interest in this profession which could only kill one person at a time.
After killing one person, it would enter an extremely long cooldown period, too insignificant.
The only things that could be used infinitely in the Wife-Killing Buff were the title, props, and skills—it was clearly noted. Obviously, occupational effects can’t be used infinitely. Without infinite use, this occupational effect was almost useless to him.
He barely had any chance for mano-a-mano combat.
Or rather, any enemy worthy of his personal attention would never appear alone.
They would often present themselves as an entire clan.
He felt indifferent to other professional introductions; only this one interested him somewhat.
And at that moment—
The detailed introduction of the map finally popped up in front of him.
「Map Name」: Rogue Star.
「Map Difficulty」: S-Level (Chen Yi’s solo debut map)
「Map Content」: The player Chen Yi will land on an all-NPC planet called ‘Rogue Star.’ Within this planet, the identity with which the player descends will be randomly selected from the following lower-class statuses: Beggar, Convict, Pork Butcher, Thief, Madame, Death Row Inmate, Slave, etc.

chapters.title: Chapter 340: 298: "Wish me a triumphant return, everyone." _2
chapters.content:
Chapter 340: Chapter 298: “Wish me a triumphant return, everyone.” _2
The players’ mission is to become a D-level dark forces leader in the city of their domain within a month’s time.
“Map Restrictions”: All props, skills, titles, and other abilities granted to players by this game will be temporarily restricted on this map, and players can only rely on their personal abilities to clear this map.
“Map Introduction”: “In an interview program with billionaires, ninety percent of the billionaires openly admitted that if they had to start over, it would be almost impossible for them to achieve this status again. If you were to start over, would you disappear into the crowd, or would you continue to stand out and soar above the rest?”
“…”
Upon seeing the map introduction for the first time, Chen Yi’s face instantly darkened.
According to the information provided by the members of the 33 Club, the Annihilation Starfield Club had chosen a map that perfectly fit his advantages, allowing him to show off his power to the outside world and showcase the prominence of Annihilation Starfield.
But what was his advantage?
It was his overwhelming individual power!
It was his terrifying AoE attacks!
It was his undying Demon God persona!
It was his ability to rival a clan by himself!
His terrifying, nearly bug-like strength was his confidence and his advantage!
And what the hell was this map?
This map completely negated all of his advantages, expecting him to rely solely on his personal ability to rise to the position of a D-level dark forces leader on a planet?
What kind of advantage was that?
Was his advantage supposed to start from scratch?
Clearly, they just wanted to see him make a fool of himself.
He took a deep breath, his face calm as he looked into the distance without speaking. At the moment, he was still in a spiritual body state, and his physical body had not yet reformed. There was less than half an hour left before he would enter this map.
Even knowing he had been deceived, there was nothing he could do.
Perhaps the map could be changed after all?
However, he couldn’t contact the Annihilation Starfield Project Team directly. It was always them that initiated contact; he had no authority to reach out to the Annihilation Starfield Project Team.
And soon, a private message from the Annihilation Starfield Project Team popped up in front of him.
“Ding, you have received a private message from the Annihilation Starfield Project Team.”
“Annihilation Starfield Project Team”: “Hello Player Chen Yi, we are very sorry that there was an accident with your debut map. The original map selected for you was ‘Insect Calamity,’ a map that could fully showcase your personal terrifying group AoE attack advantage. But due to some unforeseen events, your map has been changed to ‘Rogue Star.'”
“We sincerely apologize for this; however, the debut map announced can no longer be changed.”
“This incident is due to our work oversight. We hope for your understanding and also hope that you will not harbor any bad thoughts because of this.”
“Most members of the Annihilation Starfield Project Team do not hold any hostility towards you, Player Chen Yi, and have an amiable attitude towards you, but some members have deceived us and have tripped you up.”
“We will deal with this matter, but for the debut map happening in half an hour, we can only hope that you, Player Chen Yi, can do your best.”
“Our apologies once again!”
“…”
Chen Yi didn’t speak but swept his gaze around. He felt like having a smoke, but in his current spiritual body state, he couldn’t even feel his own breath, let alone touch anything physical, making the act of smoking impossible.
The intentions of the Annihilation Starfield Project Team were quite clear now.
The Feng Family had set a trap for him privately.
It seems that the reason the Feng Family did not interfere with his naming rights for Starfield was that they were waiting here to catch him. Since they couldn’t kill him, they wanted him to make a fool of himself on this map.
He could guess what the Feng Family was thinking.
You think you’re strong?
You think you’re awesome?
Let’s see how you handle being at the bottom, and experience that torment under the watchful eyes of all the players, losing all your dignity.
But—
With a calm expression, Chen Yi suddenly let out a light laugh.
It seemed the Feng Family didn’t really understand him.
Before the Ascension game came along, he had been a bottom-feeder in society, his life neither too good nor too bad.
A snake has its path, a rat has its own way.
He was all too clear on how the little guys should live.
If you want to see me make a fool of myself, then I’ll show you how a small fry climbs step by step to become a big shot.
Become the leader of a D-class dark force within one of the Ascension domain cities in a month?
No, no.
This target is too small.
If it’s going to be Chen Yi’s debut map, if you all want to see me embarrass myself,
why not raise the stakes a bit higher?
How about becoming the leader of the world’s largest dark force on Rogue Star within a month?
“Huh!”
Chen Yi took a deep breath, stretched lazily in the depths of his mind, and started warming up his muscles to face the upcoming map, not knowing which character he might be randomly assigned; as long as it wasn’t a prisoner, it was pretty much a godly start.
Being a prisoner locked up in jail, with just one month’s time, you probably couldn’t even finish serving your sentence, let alone dominate the world, you probably wouldn’t even have the chance to leave the prison.
If I were to be tormented in jail for a month, not only would I lose face in front of all the Starfield players, but the Annihilation Starfield Project Team’s plot by the Feng Family would succeed. I can only hope the Goddess of Luck favors me now.
A prisoner start multiplies the difficulty by several times.
Meanwhile, the members of Club 33 also learned about Chen Yi’s debut map content.
I have no idea how these people obtain their information, even getting the content of my debut map almost immediately. The speed of their intelligence gathering is indeed quite fast.
“I’m Really Fucking Awesome Starfield, Li Yi”: “Brother Chen Yi, I was puzzling over why you’d have the idea of wiping out your own project team, but now I understand. This project team is indeed awesome, this is after all the seed players’ first public showcase after changing their Starfield’s name, an event that draws the attention of millions, a debut map that many players watch, one that doesn’t come around every two or three years, and they dare to set traps? That I did not expect.”
“Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi”: “There’s nothing to say, it’s your own Starfield’s first public showcase, and your own people have set such a huge trap behind your back. I can’t blame you, Brother Chen Yi, for having such thoughts. Your project team does have some unique talents, I wouldn’t acknowledge their sanity is intact, doing something so self-destructive.”
“Beimu Qi Starfield, Beimu Qi”: “Who doesn’t know Brother Chen Yi’s strength lies in his incredible individual power? The Annihilation Starfield Project Team not arranging a map that fits his advantages, but instead setting up a completely disadvantageous one for his debut, at such a critical moment, it’s practically like a vendetta over a father’s death. If it were me, I wouldn’t let this go.”
“Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi”: “What else can you do then? You don’t have the authority to kill the project team members. You can’t possibly, like that senior did, drag the entire Starfield down to destruction with you?!”
“Beimu Qi Starfield, Beimu Qi”: “If truly driven to desperation, why not? Even a pig climbs a tree when cornered, let alone a player? Which player who has gotten this far is afraid of death? And which player who was afraid of death could have come this far? They would have died in the very first batch!”
“Li Mu Starfield, Li Mu”: “Brother Chen Yi, don’t worry. Even if you can’t clear the map, it’s not a big deal. Anyone with eyes can see that you were targeted deliberately, so anyone who mocks you is someone with low vision and narrow-mindedness, not worth your concern. We’ll be there to support and stand by you, and let’s see who dares to gossip then.”
“Thank you all.”
After expressing his gratitude in the group chat for everyone’s encouragement, Chen Yi diverted his gaze from the chat, floating in the air, looking at Sword Without End, Tuberculosis Rabbit, and Jiaye on the rooftop, who were looking up at him with eyes full of worry.
He couldn’t talk or interact with the physical world,
but the buddy chat channel was fully functional.
He had already informed Tuberculosis Rabbit and the others about his current situation and whereabouts through the buddy chat channel.
Although they weren’t sure of his exact location, they were still looking his way, the worry evident in their eyes, signaling that they also understood what this journey into the map meant.
Chen Yi’s first show?
No, rather, it was very likely that Chen Yi, who had just started to make a name for himself, would spend a month in the spotlight, embarrassingly stumbling at every turn.
No one cared whether it was a conspiracy or not.
Everyone just wanted to see Chen Yi, who had annihilated the Ten Clans, in a pitiful state on his debut map.
Drama equals public delight.
Chen Yi looked down calmly at the few people below, glanced at the countdown to map opening that only had a few seconds left, and silently mouthed,
“Wish me a triumphant return.”
“Everyone.”

chapters.title: Chapter 341: 299: "G, I can only say G.
chapters.content:
Chapter 341: Chapter 299: “G, I can only say G.
The next second—
He suddenly felt the scenery around him whirl wildly, followed by his vision blurring to an extreme, as if he had instantaneously become a nearsighted patient with a 9000-degree prescription, unable to distinguish male from female just a meter away.
When his vision restored, he found himself in a rather dilapidated hut.
There was a semi-transparent system pop-up window in front of him.
Chen Yi first swept his gaze around the room and then raised his eyebrows slightly. This transition had incorporated quite a few special effects; it was a blurry transition, unlike the previous ones, which were just a flash of white light and hastily done.
From this detail, he could infer the official nature of this map.
Or perhaps, its difficulty.
The difficulty level of this map was S.
He had never ventured onto an S-level map before. This was his debut map, as well as his first S-level map.
Although the people from the 33 Club had made this map sound extremely challenging, and he could clearly and distinctly feel the malice from the Feng Family of the Annihilation Starfield Club, he actually didn’t think this map was that difficult.
It was only limiting his individual strength.
He simply had to revert to an ordinary person’s status and establish a D-level dark force within this map.
It was akin to a reality show where a street thug rises to power.
This level of difficulty being called S-grade genuinely made him somewhat look down upon S-level maps.
Before the enhancement game began, he wasn’t some tender shoot raised in a garden. He understood the ways of the lower strata of society. It wasn’t as though being limited in individual strength and reduced to an ordinary person would make him a laughingstock during the numerous players’ live streams.
“Hmph.”
Chen Yi pushed these thoughts aside, the corner of his mouth curling into a tight cold smile, a hard edge flickering in his eyes.
In a situation where everyone was an ordinary person, his starting point was even higher.
The place where he descended was a rather dirty and untidy tent, clearly not cleaned for a long time, filled with dust and even visible cobwebs. Sticking his head out, it was underneath a flyover.
After confirming that there was no immediate danger surrounding his landing spot,
he then turned his attention to the system pop-up window in front of him and carefully began to read.
“Ding, you have descended into the S-grade map ‘Rogue Star’.”
“The city you have descended into is Rogue Star’s C-grade city—Ao City.”
“Main Quest: Become the leader of a D-grade dark force within one month.”
“Side Quest: Kill 4444 native residents.”
“The identity you’ve randomly obtained is—Prospector.”
–
“Identity Name”: Prospector.
“Identity Content”: Slightly better than a beggar but not by much. Not exactly of no fixed abode, rather homeless by choice, with the primary source of income being to lurk at the sites where battles are about to take place in order to be the first to inspect the scene for any ‘junk’ to pick up after one side is annihilated or emerges victorious.
A sophisticated prospector will use their own methods to provoke fights between two individuals with no prior grudges, thereby profiting from the conflict.
Sometimes, they also live stream the battle scenes as they unfold to profit from them.
Of course,
many times, this behavior is despised by many, especially by those experts who have been treated as pawns. Being a prospector and being casually killed is only to be expected, but at least it’s a step up from being a beggar, after all, they are not without a roof over their head.
Instead, the world is their home.
What’s the difference between the two?
The former is compelled by life, the latter driven by dreams.
“Identity Introduction”: A Prospector with dreams naturally picks up enough ‘junk’ to one day whitewash and start afresh.”
“…”
Chen Yi’s eyebrows slightly furrowed as he looked at the somewhat ambiguous system pop-up in front of him, silent, not speaking. He was somewhat puzzled as to what the system window intended to convey, but he still roughly understood his own identity.
It was that of a trash-picking beggar.
Just stoking fires to get people to fight to the death, then heading to the site to pick up trash.
Not as lowly as a beggar’s status, but more despised than a beggar.
Not a bad start.
At least he wasn’t a prisoner, not directly thrown into a jail.
After that, he started to scan his surroundings, preparing to collect some weapons for self-defense.
“Hmm.”
Chen Yi pulled a somewhat rusty awl from the dirt on the floor inside the tent, tucking it into his chest with satisfaction.
And he even amused himself by creating a little sound effect for his find.
“Ding, congratulations on acquiring a rusty awl.”
Awl.
A fine weapon, indeed. As long as you aim for the fatal parts like the eye socket, nostrils, ears, mouth, or the rear, minimal force is needed to deprive a person of their fighting ability. Even if it’s not enough to be lethal on the spot, the bacteria carried by the rusty awl are more than enough to give the opponent trouble.
He was very pleased with this weapon.
Besides that, he gradually found a few more items that could serve as weapons.
A very thin steel wire.
It could be used to set traps, such as at a highway intersection, providing a stark surprise to those fond of motorcycling.
And some steel nails.
“Eh?”
Chen Yi’s eyes suddenly lit up as he rummaged through a pile of disordered clothes and pulled out a nail gun, hastily loading the newly found nails into it and aiming it at the side of the tent on impulse, pulling the trigger.
“Bang!”
Accompanied by a somewhat muffled sound, the steel nail shot out from the barrel at a speed almost too fast to catch.
Piercing through the tent, shooting out!

chapters.title: Chapter 342: 299: "G, I can only say G."_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 342: Chapter 299: “G, I can only say G.”_2
…
Chen Yi, who found the steel nail in the sand under the overpass after emerging from his tent, couldn’t help but crack an excited smile.
Not bad at all.
The range was somewhat lacking, only about fifteen meters or so.
But the close-range power was nothing to scoff at, and in a modern society where firearms aren’t easy to come by, a nail gun was enough to give him a significant head start. It was a very good beginning.
Next, he would start by getting to know the local customs of this city and the so-called composition of the dark forces.
Chen Yi, with ambitions swelling, grinned and stuffed all the weapons he had collected into his pocket. Just as he was preparing to stand up and leave the overpass, he suddenly heard a mocking laugh near his ear.
“Do you think you hid it well?”
“…”
Chen Yi’s eyes narrowed as he slowly raised his hands and didn’t resist right away. Instead, he said in a low voice, “Let’s talk this over slowly.”
He wasn’t sure where the enemy was.
The voice sounded like it was coming from behind him.
This meant he didn’t have the upper hand, and initiating an attack at this moment would be foolish. He needed to stabilize the enemy first, to give himself time to turn around before taking the initiative.
However, the next second—
An old man’s hoarse voice also rang out beside his ear.
“I didn’t even hide; you’re just too slow to find me.”
“What?”
Chen Yi was startled for a moment. Now he could hear clearly that the voice seemed… seemed to come from above his head?
He instinctively looked up, only to see above his head.
A middle-aged man and an old man were floating in mid-air, confronting each other, their eyes filled with murderous intent—as if they were about to come to blows the second they disagreed.
“Phew!”
He breathed a sigh of relief. It seemed he had misunderstood; that statement wasn’t addressed to him, but to the old man.
He thought so.
He had just arrived; how could he already have enemies?
Without any grudges, enemies needed some justification to attack him, especially in an S-level map where some logic was expected.
Listening to their conversation,
It seemed that both parties had some longstanding grievances. The middle-aged man had been seeking revenge and finally found his adversary. Years of hatred could finally be vented today—it looked like there was about to be a major battle.
After quickly analyzing the situation, Chen Yi decided to leave the place temporarily without disturbing the two, to avoid being involved for no reason. But just as he prepared to move, he suddenly froze, realizing something didn’t quite add up.
Then, with a slightly stiff posture, he swallowed hard and looked up again at the two people floating in mid-air above him.
This time he saw it clearly.
There was nothing under their feet.
They were just floating there.
Wait, is this scientific?
Were you supposed to be standing on some floating device, but because the server for this map is subpar, the floating device under your feet didn’t show up? Or is it that the floating device graphic plugin expired today, and the copyright holder revoked the rights?
Chen Yi felt a sudden sense of dread inside.
Soon,
The scene before him intensified that sense of dread.
“Good, good, good.”
After the middle-aged man sneered a few times, he didn’t waste any words. He abruptly spread his arms wide, his expression turning fierce as he roared, “Since you’re so arrogant, there’s nothing to say. Let me see what level of prowess you’ve gained with seventy years of cultivation!”
The very next second—
A line of scarlet characters abruptly popped up above the middle-aged man’s head.
‘Lv.26, knight.’
Following the middle-aged man’s roar,
A new set of scarlet letters appeared again above his head.
‘B-level Skill: Endless Falling Blossoms!’
Then, the entire sky was suddenly shrouded in dark clouds. A tornado made of flowers mixed with a torrent of water struck with irresistible force toward the old man on the opposite side!
It was a sight that threatened to annihilate on the spot!
In contrast, the old man didn’t panic. His face was emotionless. He slowly pushed out his hands.
“Puny beings.”
‘Lv.38, Smoky Ghost.’
‘A-level Skill: Smoky Ghost Descent!’
An elder, too, had a crimson line of text appearing above his head.
Afterward, behind the elder, a ghost about seven meters tall unexpectedly materialized, with a cigarette in its mouth, its entire form somewhat ethereal and illusory. As soon as it appeared, it cackled at the scene unfolding in front of it.
The next second—
The elder’s body almost instantly became emaciated, while in contrast, the ghost behind him quickly filled out, looking as if its vitality had been sucked away by the ghost in an instant!
The moment the Smoky Ghost appeared, it effortlessly exhaled a mouthful of smoke toward the tornado of flowers in front of it. The originally bright flowers withered the moment they were shrouded in smoke.
Following that.
The remainder of the smoke enveloped the middle-aged man unabated.
Seconds later.
A pool of blood mixed with clothing fell from the sky.
The dark clouds gradually dispersed.
And once again, the sky turned clear.
The elder then twisted his neck, reabsorbing the ghost into his body, and sneered at the blood that had fallen to the ground, “Overestimating oneself.”
Afterwards, he laughed uproariously and strode away.
A display of extreme arrogance.
…
“…”
“…”
“…”
Chen Yi sat expressionless on a stone in the sandy terrain of the overpass, looking at the pool of blood that had plummeted from the sky not far away. He rummaged through his pockets, found a pack of cigarettes that came with this identity, lit one, and put it in his mouth.
After a deep inhale.
It was only within the swirls of light blue smoke that he seemed somewhat absent-minded, gazing into the distance and murmuring.
“Smarter than I thought.”
“It’s you guys who know how to play.”
He had come to understand.
This map probably gave everyone these identities and props, none of them ordinary in strength, all a bunch with supernatural abilities. And yet, only he, a real player, had nothing.
Nothing but a burning heart and a pair of iron fists likely never to smash anyone.
Quite good.
Originally, he thought the difficulty of this map was how to regain a noble position after becoming an ordinary person.
Now, he saw clearly.
The real challenge of this map was to turn from a lamb among hungry wolves into a ferocious tiger.
“…”
At this thought, Chen Yi couldn’t help but twitch the corners of his mouth. How to play?
How was he supposed to play?
He really had no idea.
…
This debut map of Chen Yi’s was only open to players from Threefold Planet and above. At this moment, a large number of Starfield players had gathered in the livestream, eager to see how the recently famous Chen Yi would perform on the inside.
A Whole Starfield announcement.
Not common.
And an unveiling of the Star System Monument game even rarer.
The last player to get the opening debut of a Star System Monument game was a long time ago.
Every free player from the Threefold Planet had gathered in that livestream.
Players from the 3rd Star System didn’t have the privilege to watch the broadcast and didn’t even know about Chen Yi’s debut map.
As for Blue Star, because it was Chen Yi’s home planet, it too could watch the livestream of Chen Yi’s entire debut, despite not being a Threefold Planet.
And that battle just now was witnessed by many viewers in the livestream room.
“G, all I can say is G.”
“Originally, Chen Yi’s advantage was his individual strength. Selecting such a map already baffles most, but now, everyone in the map except Chen Yi is immortal—I can only comment with a complete G.”
“A true warrior is never limited by their surroundings. If Chen Yi really has strength, he wouldn’t perform poorly even in this environment. Otherwise, he’s nothing but a poser looking to hook in reputation.”
“The map must have a way for Chen Yi to become stronger. It wouldn’t really have him start as an ordinary person to establish a D-tier Dark Force. It’s just a lower starting point. Let’s see if Chen Yi can realize this. If he does, it wouldn’t be a hopeless situation.”
“Is this the ruthless person who wiped out the Ten Clans not so long ago? Honestly, he seems quite average.”
“I think so too, he looks kind of foolish.”
“Why didn’t Chen Yi help just now? Watching the middle-aged man die in front of him? I knew he was cold-blooded, but didn’t think he’d be this indifferent. Seeing an imminent battle, why not call the police? Why not intervene? Isn’t that a bit morally deficient?”

chapters.title: Chapter 343: 300: "Teacher, this way please.
chapters.content:
Chapter 343: Chapter 300: “Teacher, this way please.
“Why didn’t Chen Yi save him from death?”
When this barrage comment stood out conspicuously above the entire live-streaming room, the room suddenly quieted down, with visibly fewer comments flying across the screen.
And many Starfield players who were watching from their own rooms found themselves exchanging confused looks, not knowing what to say upon seeing the player who had sent this barrage.
The player ID of the sender was “Shang Ruxue.”
This player belonged to the “Mao Rabbit Clan,” located in the “Cangxue Starfield.”
This Race had also once seized a milestone, and the name Cangxue Starfield was given by those Race Players. The player’s planet had already reached the status of Fourfold Planet, an existence not to be taken lightly in the entire leveling game.
If it had been some ordinary person who sent this barrage, they would only scoff, mocking the diversity of life as there would always be some idiotic individuals.
Living beings are adaptable, especially in the process of facing a Race crisis, evolving abilities or traits to face those crises.
For example, a Race that lived on the ground might face a sudden great flood one day, leaving them with only two choices: evolve the ability to breathe underwater quickly or face extinction.
In the leveling game environment, even the kindest of people before might inevitably become selfish.
They might remain indifferent even to their own kin’s internecine struggle, not to mention rescuing two NPCs fighting each other. Only someone with a diseased mind would say such a thing.
But the problem is… Shang Ruxue really was “sick.”
This player’s motto was to stop all killing in the world.
Not a hypocrite, but truly acted in such a manner.
All players of this Race were like that, without a single exception, as if stopping killing was their nature, or perhaps, their mission.
The players of this “Mao Rabbit Clan,” except for the weak and feeble who stayed on their own planet, went to various Starfields to stop any killings they witnessed, even at the cost of their own lives without hesitation.
In the entire leveling game, the “Mao Rabbit Clan” players had a significant reputation!
Many players had been helped by a “Mao Rabbit Clan” player when they were in crisis in the wild.
This even gave rise to a proverb.
If you’re in the wild, fallen into a trap, surrounded by 100 Alien Race players.
Then you can only await death in despair.
If among these 100 Alien Race players, there is one from the “Mao Rabbit Clan,” you will be rescued, or there will be more to be buried with you.
It’s that simple and straightforward.
Helping without seeking any conditions, nor holding favors over others, asking nothing in return—such Race Players were highly admirable in the entire leveling game environment.
And because of that.
The “Mao Rabbit Clan” players, even though they often wander alone in other Starfields, generally do not suffer harm from Alien Race players.
Because everyone understands that “Mao Rabbit Clan” players have no hostility, and secondly, there is no need to offend them since who knows when one might need their help. Even inherently chaotic players from the Dark Race would respectfully let the “Mao Rabbit Clan” players pass when they see them.
The most important point.
Among the whole leveling game, the “Mao Rabbit Clan” were hugely famous and well-liked. Although not the strongest in terms of Race strength, if they were to call upon all their favors, that force would be virtually unstoppable.
…
“…”
God of Wealth, Li Yi, sat on his throne, looking at the barrage in front of him with a helpless sigh, at a loss for words to defend his little brother. At that time, shortly after his planet had advanced to a Threefold Planet,
because everything had been smooth sailing and his actions were extremely arrogant, he had almost been wiped out.
In the end, the “Mao Rabbit Clan” got wind of it, spent nearly ten million Points for a Starfield pass, and personally came over to help him resolve the conflict, thus averting a disaster for his Race.
Although he paid back ten times the Points after he recovered,
he still owed a huge favor and didn’t dare to retort much.
He also understood the personality and vision of “Shang Ruxue,” this woman wanted to do something big, to stop players from killing each other, and wished everyone would just kill monsters on the map instead.
She wanted to bring peace to the leveling game.
But…the idea was too naive.
He knew it was a good thought, but it was basically impossible to achieve.
However—
The somewhat corpulent Li Yi, sitting on his throne, shifted his body with difficulty, then took a deep breath and looked around the live-streaming room with curiosity. Although Shang Ruxue was extremely extreme in her ideals, she was not stupid.
Chen Yi might have stood by and not intervened in death, but those were NPCs.
Wasn’t Shang Ruxue always protecting players? Since when did she start protecting NPCs as well?
If NPCs couldn’t be killed, then she might as well just wait to die on the map.
Just then—
A familiar voice reached his ear.
“Don’t you get it?”
The nonchalant Wang Qi, draping his arm around a scantily clad woman and casually smoking while striding over to Li Yi, pushed the woman in his arms carelessly into Li Yi’s embrace and spoke indifferently.
“Shang Ruxue obviously doesn’t like Chen Yi. Seeing any action of his now disgusts her, and that’s why she would say such a thing,”
“Otherwise, Sang Ruxue normally wouldn’t object to killing NPCs at all.”
“Makes sense.”
Li Yi nodded thoughtfully. Shang Ruxue hated those players who killed other players most. To someone like Chen Yi who had just exterminated the Ten Clans, in Shang Ruxue’s mind, he was the kind who would be straightaway put onto her blacklist.

chapters.title: Chapter 344: 300: "This way, teacher." _2
chapters.content:
Chapter 344: Chapter 300: “This way, teacher.” _2
“`
Although they had never met, Chen Yi’s impression of them plummeted straightaway.
Wang Qi casually glanced over the livestream room, “This term’s Shang Ruxue is even more nosy than the last one. It’d be okay if she just trash-talked Chen Yi in the comments, but if she keeps it up once Chen Yi gets out of the map, it’s going to be uncomfortable for him.”
“Even if it’s Fourfold Planet, if they provoke Chen Yi, I’m not optimistic about the ‘Mao Rabbit Clan.’
“Which term are they on now? If I’m not mistaken, it’s the ninety-first, right?”
“Seems like it.”
Li Yi pondered for a moment, then ambiguously nodded his head, as he also couldn’t remember clearly.
The first Shang Ruxue, who had won the Monument for Cangxue Starfield, had died long ago.
It was a very old story by now.
Of course, “died” didn’t mean completely dead, but rather fallen into hell. However, the mission to return to the map was to kill ten other players, which could be players from the same Race or from an Alien Race, but this mission was against Shang Ruxue’s principles.
So…
The woman chose to stay permanently in hell, never to return.
According to her own rationale that got out,
It is only when one’s principles are broken that one truly dies.
This Race of players were all eccentrics, preferring to die in the map rather than attack other players. Up to now, it seems there aren’t many official players of this Race left, and they are almost on the brink of extinction.
“Alright.”
Li Yi shook his head and stopped thinking about it, “Let’s not bother with her, let’s keep watching the livestream. I wonder how Chen Yi will deal with his first map debut. It seems quite difficult. If I were to go, I wouldn’t be very confident either.”
…
“…”
The old man left, taking Chen Yi’s ambitions with him.
Chen Yi sat on a rock under the flyover, expressionlessly staring at the pool of blood that had fallen from the sky not far away, silent and speechless.
The power system at this time was somewhat similar to the leveling-up game.
He opened his identity panel with some disbelief:
‘Profession’: Prospector.
There were no professional abilities or skills, just a pair of iron fists, or rather, a rusty crowbar.
Hell Level difficulty.
Of all the maps he had experienced, this one was the most difficult.
“Forget it.”
A moment later, Chen Yi got up and went over to check the pool of blood. After confirming there was nothing he could pick up, he left from under the flyover.
He was ready to observe the city he was in, ‘Ao City.’
It seemed that this planet had no laws.
A blatant case of deliberate murder under broad daylight, and yet no one came to investigate for quite a while, as if no one knew about it.
The streets were bustling with people, and although the cars were not numerous, they were not few either.
It seemed rather modern.
The battle that just occurred must have been witnessed by many, but not a single person stepped forward to investigate or ask questions, including… huh.
Chen Yi’s expression gradually became weird.
He realized something was off.
All the vehicles on the street were modified, like the jeep that just drove past, thoroughly armored with thick steel, and with a heavy machine gun on the roof that seemed ready to spew fire at any moment.
There was a motorcycle that was even more outrageous.
The entire bike was wrapped in explosives, looking like a terrorist ready to self-detonate at any moment.
A sign stood on the motorcycle’s rear seat, with a few clear sentences written on it:
‘If you want to attack me, be prepared to go down with me.’
“…”
Not very smart, huh? How far can your bomb’s explosion reach? I just have to shoot you from afar and detonate your bomb, can your explosion reach me?
Other vehicles on the street were no different.
All of them were fully upgraded in terms of defense and offense, as if they were all ready to resist unknown attacks at any time.
The pedestrians were even more exaggerated.
Everyone kept a distance of at least three meters from each other.
If anyone crossed this distance, both parties would immediately reach into their clothes, as if ready to pull something out, while glaring fiercely at each other. Then, in unison, they would slowly back away until they reached a safe distance, and quickly disperse.
Each person wore a mask.
Many people were even wrapped in ammunition belts.
The guns in everyone’s hands were as common as canes, almost one in each hand.
The caliber, the ammo belts, judging from the look, one could tell that being shot wouldn’t be pleasant.
“Rumble rumble…”
Just then, a roaring sound came from the end of the street.
A monstrous war truck, modified from a giant hauler, was driving towards them, trailing black smoke from its rear.
The entire vehicle was clad in steel armor of unknown thickness, even the driver’s cabin was sealed with steel plates, with multiple cameras used to observe the outside world to control the vehicle. On top of the hauler’s cabin, there were about a dozen small windows.
From each window protruded a Fire God Gatling.
On the roof of the cabin, there was even a missile launcher, ready to fire at any moment.
A large red skull was painted on the front of the truck with red paint.
The already wary pedestrians on the road became even more tense upon hearing the rumble of the hauler, hiding in corners, reaching into their clothes, ready to retaliate at any moment.
“…”
Chen Yi took all of this in, touched the somewhat rusty crowbar in his coat, and his mouth twitched without saying a word. Is your civilian firepower a bit too much?
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 345: 300: "This way, teacher." _3
chapters.content:
Chapter 345: Chapter 300: “This way, teacher.” _3
It’s just an S-level map.
Is it really that serious?
You might as well call it the Reincarnation Map, for any player who enters this map will be forcibly reincarnated.
Forget it.
Although I don’t know what these people are up to, by the looks of the pedestrians on the street, I can guess it’s not anything good. Better to avoid them for now.
However, just as Chen Yi was about to turn around and find a place to hide, he suddenly noticed that those hiding pedestrians seemed to not only look at the approaching truck with fear in their eyes but also looked at him with fear and apprehension.
Hm?
Fear him?
You’re all wrapped in ammo belts, and he has nothing on him, not a single weapon in his hands; fear him?
Are you mistaken?
But almost instantly, he figured out why these people were afraid of him.
In this city, where everyone is clearly looking out for themselves with no sense of security, a person who dares to walk the streets alone without any weapons must not be thought of as a lamb unless they’re a fool.
Chen Yi narrowed his eyes slightly and remained silent. This might be something he could use?
And at that moment—
The modified armoured truck stopped right in front of him, the thick white smoke from the rear slowly dispersing. A steel plate in the middle of the vehicle suddenly opened, followed by the sliding door beneath it, and a middle-aged man with a gas mask, aided by his subordinates, came out in front of Chen Yi. After bowing with considerable respect, he stood up and began to speak in a harsh, hoarse voice.
“Teacher, hello.”
It must be some kind of voice changer; the sound was unpleasantly sharp.
It was like nails on a chalkboard, slightly unsettling.
“Please allow me the impertinence of introducing myself. I am the deputy leader of the E-grade local force ‘Red Skull’ from C-grade city ‘Macau’, commonly known as Mute.”
“We’ve encountered some difficulties recently and are seeking the help of a Professional. I wonder if you, teacher, may have some spare time.”
“As for the reward, you just name it. As long as it’s within our ability, we won’t bargain.”
His manner was extremely respectful; there was no fault to find.
“…”
Chen Yi kept his expression calm and silent. His mind was spinning fast, as he was beginning to understand the power system of this world.
The strength of most ordinary people still depends on firearms and melee weapons.
But above these common folk exist ‘Professionals,’ beings with abilities far beyond ordinary individuals, as he had witnessed upon his arrival in that battle.
Clearly, both this vice-leader of the ‘Red Skull’ and the pedestrians on the street had mistaken him for a Professional.
After all, in such a city fraught with danger.
A man who dares to walk the streets unarmed is either a Professional or a fool, and Chen Yi’s demeanor, coupled with his natural aura of a formidable person, didn’t seem foolish.
He was now weighing his options.
Perhaps he could pretend to be a Professional, but the risk of being exposed was substantial. According to the information he had just acquired, during combat, a Professional’s vocation and vocation grade would appear above their head, and even when using a skill, the Skill Name would manifest above them.
These were things he couldn’t fake.
That meant, should a combat situation arise, his cover would be blown instantly.
The consequences of that need no elaboration.
“…”
After a long silence, Chen Yi slowly pulled a cigarette from his bosom, brought it to his lips, lit it, and inhaled deeply. Through the blue smoke, he met the expectant and pleading gaze of the middle-aged man in the gas mask and spoke softly.
“Take me to your boss.”
The next second—
A thick murderous aura emanated from Chen Yi’s body, as if it were tangible, enveloping the entire city.
The middle-aged man in the gas mask turned deathly pale almost instantly, his mouth dry, his legs uncontrollably trembling. He sensed an extremely intense murderous intent emanating from this man before him.
Such murderous intent…
One must have taken at least tens of thousands of lives to build it up.
Those who have killed before are extremely sensitive to such an aura. With one look, they could tell the predator from the prey.
Even though his props, titles, and skills were all restricted.
The murderous aura formed from countless lives, like some sort of magnetic field, was something that couldn’t be erased.
“Gulurong.”
The middle-aged man swallowed his saliva silently, struggling to control his mind before he spoke in a raspy yet respectful tone, “Very well.”
“Teacher, this way, please.”
He had noticed this man earlier while on the truck. The man’s stature and demeanor were starkly different from the people of this city.

chapters.title: Chapter 346: 301: There is not a single good person in the whole building.
chapters.content:
Chapter 346: Chapter 301: There is not a single good person in the whole building.
“Watch the steps, Teacher.”
The man with the gas mask was carefully escorting the young-looking man onto the heavy truck parked behind him, originally guessing that the younger man could be a Professional.
But after the brief exchange with the young man, he was even more convinced that not only was he a Professional, but also one of those high-ranking ones.
Such a demeanor…
It’s not something that can be mimicked by just anyone.
Nonetheless, he still held a trace of suspicion; when Chen Yi stepped onto the heavy truck, the man narrowed his eyes slightly towards the nearby warning light.
There was no reaction.
No alarm sounded.
Should anyone carrying firearms or other heat-emitting weapons cross that warning light, it would start beeping. But when the young man crossed, the light didn’t react at all, proving that he wasn’t carrying any heat-based weaponry.
He truly walked the streets of Ao City alone, unarmed.
That didn’t just require courage.
It required confidence.
After realizing this, the middle-aged man with the gas mask became even more respectful and ushered Chen Yi into the vehicle. Once Chen Yi was seated inside the compartment, the man ventured to ask.
“You are not a local from Ao City, are you, Teacher? The accent doesn’t quite fit.”
In truth, he couldn’t tell whether Chen Yi had a local accent or not.
But this was a common tactic used by their kind to probe for identities. Of course, they couldn’t outright ask, “Where are you from?” That way of inquiring was too direct, strongly hinting at snooping intentions, and could easily make people feel hostile and defensive.
This was not the way to ask.
So, claiming the other party isn’t a local became a handy trick.
No matter how the other party responds, yes or no, you could obtain some information.
Chen Yi, sitting on a couch inside the compartment, with his eyelids slightly drooped, did not speak, clearly showing no intention to respond.
Seeing he was getting nowhere, the middle-aged man did not dare to get angry. He just awkwardly chuckled twice before sitting back down on a chair nearby and silently waved his subordinate away. He then picked up a teacup from the table and poured a cup of tea for Chen Yi before sitting down quietly in his own chair.
He placed his hands flatly on his thighs.
He looked like a committed student listening attentively in a classroom.
