The only thing out of place was the large gas mask on his head.
…
Meanwhile, the live stream chat was furiously active.
“I get it now, Chen Yi wants to pose as a Professional in this world? Not a bad starting point, but he’s been exposed too easily.”
“Exposed too easily? With those obvious words above the Professional’s head, how can it be faked? The moment he takes action, he’ll be busted instantly, and once that happens, death is all Chen Yi has left.”
“More than just death… haven’t you seen what kind of character these NPCs in the maps have? This is in no way a normal city. Once they find out Chen Yi has deceived them, forget death, he won’t escape torture. That’s when the real torment begins, unable to live or die.”
“With such a debut on the first map, it’s going to be hard for Chen Yi to lift his head. This live stream is being watched by all the Starfield players, and I thought we’d get to see Chen Yi strut his stuff in the map. I heard from a friend in Annihilation Starfield that Chen Yi’s individual strength is freakishly over the top, the kind that can single-handedly take on a clan, overwhelmingly dominating… It’s just too bad, we probably won’t get to see Chen Yi in action this time.”
“Exactly. With so many people in the chat, who isn’t here to see the badass who could wipe out the Ten Clans with a single move? But the Annihilation Starfield Project Team directly chose such a map for Chen Yi, seriously sickening.”
“…”
Laying on the throne, Li Yi struggled to turn his body before glancing at the live stream and said to Wang Qi nonchalantly, “What do you think? If it were you, with the map’s progress up to now, what would your breakthrough be?”
“Me?”
Wang Qi frowned and pondered for a long while before speaking, “So far, all I’ve seen is that these Professionals possess unimaginable abilities, and it’s not clear whether firearms can harm them.”
“But one can clearly deduce that this world is dominated by Professionals.”
“If it were me, I might gather some desperadoes and then figure out a way to arm them with a batch of firearms, fighting our way through.”
Hearing this, Li Yi shook his head, smiling helplessly, “Typical of the man who named Qi Daddy Starfield, always so brute in his actions. Fighting and killing aren’t the best ways, we need positive energy.”
“Cut the nonsense,”
Wang Qi glared at Li Yi discontentedly, “If it were you, do you have any strategies?”
“Of course, I do.”
Li Yi took the cigar offered by a beautiful assistant and took a deep breath before tossing the cigar casually into the nearby swimming pool, “From Chen Yi’s perspective, as you must have seen, this world, although chaotic, still has shops, vehicles, office buildings.”
“What does this imply?”
“It implies that while the social order of this world has become extremely chaotic, it still retains the basic commercial operation system.”
“As long as there is commerce, I can use my means to take control of this world again.”
“No matter how strong people are, as long as there is Li Yi, everyone can be reaped.”

chapters.title: Chapter 347: 301: In the whole building, there isn't a single good person._2
chapters.content:
Chapter 347: Chapter 301: In the whole building, there isn’t a single good person._2
“Although one month is a bit short, it’s enough. If I were Chen Yi, I would first consider ways to make a fortune,”
“So what ways to make a fortune have you considered now?”
“Not a single one, the information available is too limited.”
Li Yi shook his head firmly, giving his answer.
“…”
Wang Qi looked at Li Yi somewhat speechlessly, and said irritably, “Then what the hell are you talking about!”
…
Inside the Annihilation Starfield Project Team.
Feng Gang, who was somewhat aged, stood in front of a large screen, holding a glass of red wine in his hand. He took a sip before looking at the calm image of Chen Yi on the screen and sneered.
“I wonder how long you can maintain this pretense?”
The screen was showing a live stream of Chen Yi’s position on the map.
He clearly understood Chen Yi’s thoughts. Isn’t he just trying to pose as a Professional? A simple enough idea, but it’s not so easy to masquerade as a Professional, is it? Unless you pretend to be a Professional who never takes action.
But the NPCs in the map aren’t fools. Do you think if you say you are a Professional, they will just believe you without doubt?
The day you get exposed is the day you start to enjoy torture.
“How wonderful.”
Thinking of this scene, Feng Gang couldn’t help but smile, provoking those of the Feng Family. You wouldn’t think that just because you have taken over two Monuments, everything will be as if nothing had happened.
He wanted Chen Yi to always remember one thing.
The players the Feng Family wanted to deal with.
Even if you have the power to reach the sky, they can still press the sky down on you.
Reach the sky?
Their project team is the sky of this game!
And at that moment—
Fatty Two’s voice came through, sounding quite young.
“Grandpa, someone from the project team has come looking for us, they’re probably here to demand accountability.”
Feng Yuan stood worriedly behind the elder, whispering a report. When his gaze inadvertently swept across Chen Yi’s silhouette on the screen, a few hints of bitter hatred couldn’t help but leak from the corner of his eyes.
He was the person in charge of the Solar Star Project Team of the Threefold Star System.
He had high expectations for Solar Star and even used some methods to send an S-grade Prop to Three Solar Star.
Normally, it would be almost impossible for a player from a Onefold Planet to obtain an S-grade Prop.
Not the slightest chance.
If it weren’t for his secret intervention, would Solar Star dream of getting an S-grade Prop? Pure fantasy. Just when everything was ready, and Solar Star was about to fully enter the twofold trial map.
As long as they cleared it, they could advance to twofold.
After that, threefold, step by step, moving towards the Annihilation Starfield Project Team.
This would have been his greatest achievement.
Everything was going smoothly until that moment, when Chen Yi appeared. Chen Yi appeared in the twofold trial map of Solar Star, exterminating all players of Solar Star.
His years of hard work vanished overnight.
He hated.
How could he not hate?
How could he possibly not hate?
And how would he not hate?
So he used his own power and family influence, rushed several Threefold Planets to the Threefold Star System, seeking to exterminate Blue Star, to soothe the hatred in his heart!
Who knew that Chen Yi would be like a cockroach that couldn’t be killed, stubbornly surviving in the map, causing his plans to fail again!
He thought this issue would be put to rest for a while.
But who knew that the next day, Chen Yi would come storming into the Annihilation Starfield!
Fuck!
At that time, it was still damn called Ding Qi Starfield!
There’s no need to go into details about what happened afterwards. Chen Yi single-handedly exterminated Ten Clans in one day, and his fame spread far and wide. In contrast, the reputation the Feng Family had built over many years was almost instantly shattered.
Thanks to the Patriarch of the Feng Family, the elder before him, who quickly thought of how to restore the Feng Family’s reputation.
To let all those who were ready to laugh at the Feng Family know one thing.
The Feng Family is still the Feng Family!
Even Chen Yi, who extinguished Ten Clans in a single day, so what?
As long as the Feng Family is willing, they can still play with the opponent in the palm of their hands.
“Accountability?”
Feng Gang slowly turned around, looked at Feng Yuan behind him, and sneered with contempt, “Even if we admit the fault is ours, do they dare penalize us?”
“Do they really think the Feng Family is an easy target within the Annihilation Starfield Project Team?”
“Think they can pinch us whenever they please?”
…
Meanwhile, over at Rogue Star.
Chen Yi, sitting silently in the heavy truck cabin with a calm expression, leaned on the sofa. Glancing through the tiny window of the heavy truck, he took in the view of the city.
This city.
Or rather, this planet was chaos.
It seemed like everyone here was worried about getting killed by someone else at any moment.
The term ‘panic-stricken’ couldn’t be more apt to describe the scene.
Finally, the heavy truck stopped.
“Please, Teacher.”
When the heavy truck stopped by the side of a street and opened its compartment, what came into view was not the abandoned warehouse or some nightclub that Chen Yi expected—the usual meeting places for dark forces in his cognition.
Instead, it was an office building with bright glass exterior walls.
It seemed to have more than thirty floors.
The middle-aged man wearing a gas mask waited respectfully by the truck, looking at Chen Yi.
…
Chen Yi stepped out of the carriage and when his feet touched the ground, dozens of subordinates armed with guns already stood in two lines, extending from the heavy truck to the entrance of the office building.
Following a glance from the middle-aged man.
The few dozen armed subordinates bowed respectfully and announced loudly in unison, “All members of the E-class power ‘Red Skull Head’ welcome our distinguished guest!”
…
Chen Yi looked at the subordinates standing in two lines before him and the glitzy office building not far away, slightly perplexed inside. He asked, “Your power’s territory is here? Inside an office building?”
As the words fell.
The middle-aged man standing by his side, looking quite respectful, said a little embarrassedly, “Our power’s foundation is still shallow, so we can only rent an office space to use as our operating area. A standalone building is beyond our reach for now; it’s a bit laughable before the Teacher.”
…
Chen Yi nodded silently without saying anything further.
He led the way, walking towards the office building along the path between the human walls.
There was nothing to laugh at.
It was just a bit baffling.
In this day and age, the underworld can openly operate out of an office building?
He could understand that going legit and making it big wasn’t out of the ordinary; it wasn’t impossible even for higher places like the Red Hall, but had they actually gone legit? That heavy truck with its missile still parked at the entrance, and just walking into an office building like that?
Does this planet have a government at all?
Before long, he entered the lobby on the first floor.
There were no security guards to be seen in the rather empty lobby. Instead, a wall listed the companies on each floor for easy searching.
‘First floor: E-class power “Red Moon”, D-class power “Hate-the-Sky High”.’
‘Second floor: F-class power “SpongeBob”, E-class power “Striving to be the cutest Patrick Star!”‘
‘Third floor: E-class power “What do you call me?”, E-class power “What’s your name?”‘
…
…
Chen Yi stood in front of the wall in the office building’s lobby, silent for a long time without speaking. He finally understood that this office building was filled with dark forces!
There was not a single good person in the entire building.
No wonder there were no security guards.
What’s the use of security in a place like this? To protect the safety of these people? Protecting oneself from getting killed by them seems more important, right?
This planet was quite interesting; dark forces could actually set up blatantly in office buildings and seemed to be running them like legitimate businesses.
“Please.”
At that moment, the man with the gas mask came up from behind and said respectfully, “Teacher, please this way, our territory is on the 18th floor. That elevator over there only goes to odd-numbered floors. To go to even-numbered floors, we have to take the stairs on this side.”
“I’ve sent a message ahead to our ‘Red Skull’ leader. At this time, our leader has already prepared tea in the office, waiting to welcome you.”
“The reception might be a bit simple; I hope you will forgive us, Teacher.”

chapters.title: Chapter 348: 302: "A man must not catch the wind at dusk.
chapters.content:
Chapter 348: Chapter 302: “A man must not catch the wind at dusk.
“Good.”
Chen Yi nodded, didn’t express any further opinions, and let the middle-aged man lead the way in front of him as he stepped into the elevator to begin his ascent.
Throughout the journey, he made no defensive moves.
As if he was fully confident.
Or as though he didn’t care about his own life.
But only he knew that if he wanted to successfully navigate this map, he would have to resort to some extraordinary means, as the normal approach would definitely not work, or even if it did, it would be an extremely embarrassing success.
“Ding.”
The elevator quickly reached the 18th floor.
Before stepping out of the elevator, Chen Yi heard a crisp female voice outside, as if she was on a phone call.
“Oh daddy, I know, but the problem is, where am I supposed to find someone who’s good at calligraphy for you? You know what the situation in Ao City is like, and even though we’ve already put out the recruitment ads, how many people have the courage to come for an interview? I’m working hard, so stop rushing me.”
The woman had shoulder-length hair and was dressed in a somewhat sexy outfit consisting of shorts and a short-sleeved shirt, her gestures oozing a charming allure.
She stood roughly 176 cm tall.
A height that could easily make many men feel inferior.
A pair of straight and long legs that made one uncontrollably fantasize like a pervert, drooling at the sight.
The woman, seeing the elevator doors open, casually glanced at Chen Yi and his group as they emerged from the elevator, flipped her hair, and while still on the phone, entered the elevator, continuing to speak with some complaints on the other end.
Following her were 8 fully armed and sunglass-wearing tough men with cold expressions.
They looked like they weren’t to be trifled with.
Chen Yi did not dwell on the woman for long, but followed the middle-aged man in front of him towards the territory owned by the “Red Skull” on this floor.
On the 18th floor, there were territories belonging to 4 different forces; one plate being that of the “Red Skull.”
What he didn’t know was…
At this moment, countless players in the live-streaming room were feeling sorry for Chen Yi.
The instant that woman appeared just now…
A pop-up emerged in the live-streaming room.
“Hidden task: Perhaps you could be the one who’s good at calligraphy. Completing this task might result in some unknown rewards.”
“Rewards: Unknown.”
–
“Such a pity, Chen Yi is clearly focusing all his attention on the ‘Red Skull’ right now, missing such an obvious task hint.”
“I know, right? But it’s normal. It’s said that Chen Yi is just a newbie player who hasn’t even left Newbie Village, so he probably doesn’t have much mapping experience. It’s normal for him not to notice such task hints. Maybe Chen Yi hasn’t even encountered such hidden tasks before and thinks only system-generated tasks are actual tasks.”
“It’s a real shame, the difficulty of this map is already high, and this hidden task could have been a ray of hope.”
“Based on my deduction, if I’m not mistaken, as long as more than half an hour has passed since Chen Yi arrived on the map, no matter where he is, he’ll come across this woman. Maybe the way to clear the level is to catch up with this woman? To marry her and take her home?”
“Eh? Your reasoning seems plausible. This woman looks like she has a complicated background. If one’s own strength isn’t enough to become the leader of a D-level chaotic force, maybe opting for a sugar mommy isn’t a bad choice? As long as you please the father-in-law, isn’t it easy to snag the leadership of a D-level force?”
“Money is often related to power.”
“And power, in turn, is inseparable from beauty.”
Li Yi, lounging in his chair, shifted his plump body and smiled as he looked at the picture on the live-stream: “Such a pity I’m fat now; if it were during my peak years of attractiveness, taking down a chick like that would have been no problem at all.”
…
Chen Yi, almost at the entrance of the Red Skull’s territory, seemed to glance nonchalantly behind him at the closing elevator doors. He looked at the woman inside, still on the phone, paused for a moment, and then suddenly let out a soft laugh.
At that moment…
A solemn-faced middle-aged man in a suit came to meet them.
“Good day, teacher; I heard the deputy chairman introduce you just now.”
“Sir, your esteemed presence is an honor to our establishment.”
“I just wonder what it is you’re looking for from me?”
The rapid changes in address within three sentences made it unclear whether it was intentional or impromptu.
But seeing the beads of sweat on the middle-aged man’s forehead, it seemed more like someone who had no real education but was desperately trying to imitate a scholar, getting anxious and sweating upon realizing they misspoke.
“Let’s talk inside.”
Chen Yi didn’t respond, but walked straight into the territory of the “Red Skull.”
It’s called a territory.
But it looked more like a company.
Its size was roughly 800 square meters.
There were many workstations.
Computers were at every workstation, and quite a few employees were sitting in front of their computers working. Around them, on the couches, sat numerous gunmen. The scene was incongruous—in fact, it seemed a little like the setting for a phone scam operation.
But he didn’t think for a second that Red Skull’s source of profits was something like phone scams.
The reason was simple.
In the old Blue Star, before the leveling-up game came along, people were relatively innocent, and it was understandable when someone was deceived. It was a peaceful society after all, and people tended to be relaxed in their daily lives.
But this planet was obviously not normal.
People walking on the streets were worried about being stabbed to death by the person next to them.
Phone scams in this world?
You’d have to be dumb to fall for a scam in a world where you don’t know if you’ll live to see the next day, wouldn’t you?

chapters.title: Chapter 349: 302: "A man must not catch the wind at dusk."_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 349: Chapter 302: “A man must not catch the wind at dusk.”_2
Even if there really were.
By the time this batch of people dies out, there wouldn’t be anyone left to deceive, right?
A project without repeat customers can’t serve as the main source of income for a major interest group.
Remember that.
Chen Yi walked into the territory of a place called Dark Forces, which in fact looked more like a company, and found the room labeled ‘President’s Office,’ walking straight in.
After spinning a few rounds in the boss chair placed by the floor-to-ceiling window, he propped his feet up on the desk, lit a cigarette and brought it to his lips, taking a deep drag before exhaling a stream of light blue smoke.
He waved to the Red Skull President, who was standing by and still seemed a bit lost about the situation, signaling him to come over.
“This…”
The middle-aged man dressed in a suit was momentarily at a loss. The young man’s series of actions didn’t show much respect for him, or rather, he didn’t regard him at all, holding a posture that seemed to put himself above him.
But the more this was the case, the less he dared to act rashly.
Here, nobody was a fool.
If someone shows you respect, it means you can bully them as you please.
If someone doesn’t care about you at all, then you should start worrying about how long you can live.
The man glanced uneasily at the vice president standing at the office door, who gave him a few meaningful looks. After only a moment’s hesitation, he put on a ingratiating smile and approached Chen Yi, who was sitting in what should have been his seat.
“Master, what are your orders? Just say the word.”
Before he understood the young man’s professional rank, he decided to be on his good side first.
Bend a knee, say some nice words.
It didn’t take much effort.
Prestige?
In Ao City, or rather, in the entire Rogue Star, prestige was the cheapest thing, not worth a penny!
When the President brought his head closer, Chen Yi showed a pleased smile, gently stroked the bald head of the middle-aged man, and after a moment, pulled him in close, pointing out towards the scenery beyond the floor-to-ceiling window.
“See that?”
“Uh…the beautiful dusk scenery?”
“No.”
Chen Yi shook his head softly and said, “Such a big city, and you can only sit in a tiny corner of an office building to greedily admire this city’s beauty. Don’t you feel too insignificant during the quiet of the night?”
“You seem to be the president of a force, having some status in Ao City.”
“Much better than those pedestrians walking on the streets.”
“You have quite a few people under you, and when you walk out the door, you’re impressive enough, driving a heavy truck that makes passersby get out of the way.”
“But when you meet someone like me, whose depth you don’t know, you can only play the grandson to avoid potential crises. Don’t you find your current self too pitiful? Like a lame duck scrambling to stay alive.”
“…”
The middle-aged bald man’s forced smile slowly solidified on his face, his body gradually straightened, a trace of bloodthirstiness flashed in his eyes as he looked directly at Chen Yi, who was sitting in his chair, and said word by word without expression.
“Is Master here today to look for trouble?”
“I don’t want to die.”
“But this doesn’t mean I’m willing to be humiliated until I die.”
“Perhaps my last retaliation before death will make you truly recognize my strength.”
As his words ended.
A dialog box suddenly appeared above the bald man’s head, and the originally still office began to have wind blowing from somewhere, howling.
‘Profession: Barber.’
‘Lv.11.’
Barber.
Chen Yi glanced casually at the profession label above the bald man’s head, nodded thoughtfully, having come across another Professional, Barber, which sounds like a profession that uses razors and the like for attacking.
It’s one of the stronger offensive kinds.
But does a Barber need to shave his own head first?
He only glanced and didn’t speak further, just continued to prop his feet on the desk, blowing out a puff of smoke to admire the city in the dusk. Tuberculosis Rabbit would have really liked this city if the ‘Raising the Game’ event hadn’t happened before.
Tuberculosis Rabbit would feel like a fish in water here, he really likes places that aren’t bogged down with too many rules.
For Tuberculosis Rabbit, there isn’t much difference between here and Heaven.
Seeing himself reveal his cards, yet Chen Yi remaining unfazed with a nonchalant demeanor, the bald man’s bloodthirstiness in his eyes slightly dissipated, standing there somewhat embarrassingly, not knowing whether to make a move or retreat.
He had thought that once Chen Yi realized he, too, was a Professional, there would be a ripple of reaction, or at the very least, some respect should be due, but Chen Yi’s current response clearly conveyed an attitude, one that suggested his professional ranking was simply inconsequential in Chen Yi’s eyes.
Both being Professionals, yet different in rank, meant their strengths were worlds apart.
Even though he was in a difficult position, as the saying goes, to get to where he was,
he had long since discarded concerns about saving face.
The bald man took a deep breath, suppressing all the frustration in his heart, and once again bowed respectfully towards Chen Yi: “Teacher, I am a simple man, unable to grasp your intentions.”
“Whatever your instructions, Teacher, just say the word, and as long as it’s within my power, I shall carry it out.”
This time, his bow was even deeper than before.
Upon hearing this,
a slight smirk involuntarily curved the corner of Chen Yi’s mouth.
The fundamental logic behind business negotiations and courting a woman are essentially no different; first and foremost, you must achieve one thing, and that is to unsettle the other party’s mind. Normal people, when interacting with strangers, will instinctively establish a psychological defense in their hearts.
This has a professional term in psychology.
For instance, distributing flyers to a stranger during the day might be met with acceptance or perhaps indifference, devoid of other choices and mental processes.
However, if you were to hand out flyers to a stranger at midnight, the recipient would most likely have only a few choices: to scream and run, or to scream, run, and then call the police.
Flyer distribution at midnight is a breach of common sense, and any such breach will raise people’s guard.
Furthermore, a woman, active at midnight, would definitely have a ‘defend against men who seem to harbor ill intentions’ psychological defense line; this is a certainty.
Of course, the environment also plays a part.
Distributing bar marketing flyers outside a bar in a bustling area, as opposed to distributing cemetery sales flyers in the deep woods, yields different effects because of the environment and the product being promoted.
Similarly,
this bald middle-aged man also had a defensive line in his mind before his arrival.
A line of defense against him.
And the provocative words he had just spoken were intended to first break through that defense, and then to continue speaking, thereby affecting the bald man on a deeper level.
He wasn’t worried about the man making a move against him.
Outside the office,
many slogans were hung on the walls.
One of them was particularly interesting: written in brush strokes, it said “Be Cautious and Careful.”
From the initial respectful behavior of the Vice-President who made contact with him, Chen Yi concluded that the enterprise culture of this company, or rather this dark force, was one of caution.
Without fully understanding his background, the bald man wouldn’t act rashly and risk bringing potential deadly harm upon himself.
In a place like Ao City, being a bit wary isn’t a bad thing.
Chen Yi then slowly stood up, opened the window next to the French window, and the outside air poured into the office; the high-altitude airflow brought a touch of coolness onto the faces of the few people inside the office.
Chen Yi stood in front of the French window, hands in pockets, overlooking the city wrapped in twilight, and said softly.
“Once, someone said something to me.”
“A man should never stand in the wind at dusk.”
“Do you know why?”
“…”
The bald man standing behind Chen Yi, feeling puzzled and anxious, mustered his courage to speak: “I’m not sure, please enlighten me, Teacher.”
“The breeze of the twilight can cause a man’s ambitions to stir inappropriately.”
“I wonder if you’ve ever had a moment of fantasy while sitting here, overlooking this city.”
“And now, here I am.”
“I will help you realize your fantasies.”
“The sole ruler of Ao City, how does that title sound to you?”

chapters.title: Chapter 350: 303: "So ferocious, seeing hallucinations, need to sleep a bit more.
chapters.content:
Chapter 350: Chapter 303: “So ferocious, seeing hallucinations, need to sleep a bit more.
“The only ruler of Ao City?”
The bald man was startled for a moment, then a flicker of realization flashed across his eyes. Although somewhat reluctant, he still didn’t have a clear idea of the man standing before him, so bowing his head for the time being was not a big deal.
If the man before him was truly powerful, then acknowledging him as the boss wouldn’t be a loss.
In Ao City, having a strong boss like that could mean a longer life for him.
If he later discovered that this man was just putting on an act, he would naturally let him understand the methods of the “Red Skull”.
At that time, don’t blame him for being cruel.
After taking a deep breath, he awkwardly knelt on one knee behind Chen Yi, lowering his voice and said hoarsely, “Subordinate Wang Zhongyi wishes to acknowledge Teacher as the leader, from now on I will be like a sword in Teacher’s hands.”
“Wherever Teacher points, will be where I fall in battle!”
“All members of the ‘Red Skull’ will recognize Teacher as their new master.”
“Go.”
Then he turned his head to look at the vice-chairman standing at the office door, still somewhat unclear about what was happening, and hoarsely said, “Spread the word, the new leader of the Red Skull shall be this Teacher here, it’s just that I don’t know Teacher’s name is…”
As he said this, the corner of his mouth twitched slightly.
What the hell is going on here?
He had handed over the “Red Skull”, which he had carefully built up, without even knowing the man’s name.
Truly fucked up.
“Ah? Oh, okay, got it, boss,” the vice-chairman standing at the door of the office said, despite not understanding what had happened, prepared to spread the message immediately, but couldn’t help but have some doubts in his mind. If this young man became the leader, what would happen to the boss?
If the boss became the vice-chairman.
Then what about him, the vice-chairman?
Become a vice-vice-chairman?
Damn, why did he suddenly get demoted without any warning?
Why did he stop the heavy truck in the first place, was there something wrong with his brain?
“No need.”
Chen Yi, who had been standing with one hand behind his back, turned and looked at Wang Zhongyi, who was kneeling on the ground, furrowing his brows slightly in dissatisfaction, “When did I ever say I wanted to be the head of your ‘Red Skull’?”
“An E-level power, wanting me as the leader?”
“Am I even worthy?”
“What?”
Already somewhat resentful, Wang Zhongyi was completely dumbfounded at these words and stuttered, “Isn’t it you, Teacher, who wants to become the ruler of Ao City, and then take us in?”
“…”
Chen Yi looked down at the bald man kneeling before him with a speechless expression and said flatly, “Not me, you, understand?”
“Me?”
Understanding this time, Wang Zhongyi became immediately flustered and got up from the ground, waving his hands repeatedly and saying, “I can’t do it, I can’t. How could I, just an E-level power leader, possibly become the boss of the entire Ao City?”
“No, no, I’m not capable.”
“Don’t rush.”
Chen Yi didn’t expect Wang Zhongyi to agree immediately; after all, Wang Zhongyi lacked a bit of confidence. What Chen Yi intended to do was to help build up his confidence. He reclined in the boss chair and casually asked, “Who’s the current head of Ao City?”
“Ao City has no head, but the strongest force in Ao City is the ‘Red Mansion Pavilion’, a B-level force and the only B-level force in Ao City.”
“Hmm.”
Chen Yi nodded, then took out another two cigarettes from his pocket, lighting one and passing the other to Wang Zhongyi, “Within two weeks, I want you to bring down the head of the ‘Red Mansion Pavilion’ chairman personally.”
“I will support you and help you step by step to become the King of Ao City.”
“I will take care of all your enemies.”
“All you need to do is one thing, cultivate your own demeanor, and make yourself worthy of the position.”
“This…”
A glint of temptation appeared in Wang Zhongyi’s eyes. He didn’t know the details about this young man, but from his tone, the professional level should be at least lv.30 or above; otherwise, he wouldn’t talk so big.
If they had a professional that powerful to support them.
‘King of Ao City’ was something he still didn’t dare think about, but advancing to a D-level power should be no problem.
Then he carefully asked, “May I know what percentage Teacher plans to take?”
“Percentage?”
“Yes, yes, how much did other powers used to give Teacher?”
In Ao City, many of the dark forces collaborated with some powerful professionals, with the professionals providing backing and the dark forces collecting money, then offering tribute periodically.
He had a rough expectation in his mind.
If this Teacher could really help him promote the “Red Skull” to a D-level force, he could accept yielding 70% of the Red Skull’s profits!
Even if it was just 30%.
But he believed that at that time, he would earn much more than he did now.
“Percentage?”
Chen Yi quickly understood and shook his head with a light chuckle, “I don’t want a single percent.”
“Eh…”
Wang Zhongyi’s guard went up suddenly, and after hesitating for a while, he still spoke up, “Teacher, there’s no free lunch in this world that isn’t spiked with poison.”
“These worldly possessions are not my goal.”
Chen Yi fell silent for a while, then suddenly stood up with his hands behind his back, gazing into the distance with an expressionless face and said softly, “Everyone on the guard against each other, everyone slaughtering, without any rules, acting wantonly.”
“Is such a world really what we need?”
“What I want is a brand new world.”
“What I want is for my children to see not mindless killing when they are born, but peace, kindness, and the blessings of people.”
“Shouldn’t the world be like this?”

chapters.title: Chapter 351: 303: "I'm delirious, seeing hallucinations, I need to sleep some more." _2
chapters.content:
Chapter 351: Chapter 303: “I’m delirious, seeing hallucinations, I need to sleep some more.” _2
“…”
Wang Zhongyi stared in confusion at Chen Yi’s retreating figure, feeling that today’s dusk seemed somewhat dazzling. He could understand each of those words, but when combined, they seemed strangely unfamiliar. He could only mutter blankly.
“But this world has always been like this, hasn’t it? It has been this way for a very long time.”
“Always like this.”
“Just because it has always been like this, does it make it right?”
Chen Yi suddenly turned to face Wang Zhongyi, raised his right arm with fierce conviction, and spoke with a voice that rose and fell with controlled passion, “Right?”
“Don’t you want your children to be able to walk the streets in peace?”
“Don’t you want your children to have a carefree childhood?”
“What I want is not just to be the King of Aomarket, but the King of Rogue Star!”
“This world has been in chaos for far too long, fending for itself with no rules to speak of. The only reason I have emerged is to cultivate a ruler in every city, and ultimately, restore peace to the entire world.”
“This is what I want.”
“What profit margin? If it were for that meager profit, why would I bother speaking with you?!”
“The reason I chose you is that when your Deputy Leader stopped his truck to find me, his respectful demeanor made me think your force still possessed a shred of conscience.”
“What I want is world peace.”
“Perhaps we may not achieve it, but the next generation, the one after, passing down this legacy, will eventually achieve world peace.”
“But all this must begin with someone brave enough to take the first step.”
“Yes, the mortality rate of pioneers will be the highest because we are against the entire world.”
“But if no one ever takes that first step, what will become of this world? Will it continue in chaos forever? Will the first thing our children see when born always be senseless slaughter?”
“If no one is willing to stand up, then I, Chen Yi, am willing to stand up.”
“As a man, to die for the people is the highest honor!”
Chen Yi stood before Wang Zhongyi, backlit by twilight, delivering his impassioned speech with spittle flying, and then, with a lingering sense of purpose, he wiped his mouth, turning to look with some concern at the petrified Wang Zhongyi.
Normally, he didn’t really have many opportunities to give speeches.
He wasn’t sure if his words had moved Wang Zhongyi.
One could only do their best and leave the rest to fate.
As the saying goes, when you come to a new world, your greatest advantage is possessing what that world lacks.
To have what others do not is the true advantage.
This world has everything: Professionals, firearms, chaos, bloodlust.
But it seems to lack peace… and someone willing to lead them toward it.
The people of this world long for peace just as much, but they are also extremely wary of everyone around them. This inner conflict makes everyone here immensely suffering.
On the way here.
He saw a man quickly walking down the street, leading his child by the hand—a rare sight. In such an environment, taking a child outside basically means preparing for the child’s death on the roadside.
The child was probably only two or three years old.
Stumbling as he walked.
Struggling down the road following his father, the child caught sight of a pendant on the waistband of a man nearby, his eyes instinctively shining with interest as he reached for it.
The man noticed this and initially froze, then a smile appeared in his eyes, intending to take off the pendant to give to the child.
Just at that moment.
The child’s father noticed as well and his expression changed dramatically. He stuffed his hand into his jacket as if to draw a gun, and with his eyes fixed on the man, he began to step back cautiously, his face full of vigilance.
The same was true for the man.
The smile in his eyes disappeared instantly as he too stuffed his hand into his jacket, retreating until he reached a safe distance, heaved a sigh of relief, then quickly turned and left.
As the saying goes, details reveal the whole.
From this, it was evident that the world’s inhabitants still yearned for peace; it was just that the chaotic environment forced them to be constantly on guard against strangers.
At this time, if someone stepped forward, bearing something that has never existed in this world, it might bring a different change to this world.
That thing which has never existed is the idea of creating peace, an idea that had never occurred to anyone in this world.
“Peace…”
The bald man stared up at the man before him. The light of the setting sun shone on the man, feeling warm yet piercing. Thoughts triggered a moistness in his eyes as he let out a gritty roar.
“Good, Teacher Dade!”
“For the sake of peace!”
He had never dared to think this way, but it didn’t mean he hadn’t thought about it in the depths of the night.
To this day, he couldn’t forget that scene.
When he was very young, he accidentally threw a sandbag out of the yard. Locked behind the gate, he couldn’t get out and sat at the door begging for help for a long time, but no passerby would help him.
Just when he was about to give up.
A big sister stopped at his door. Seeing no one around, she hesitated for a moment before picking up the sandbag, intending to throw it back into the yard.
But at that moment.
His father returned and without a moment’s hesitation, shot the big sister dead.
He watched the big sister fall into a pool of blood with a look of astonishment and regret in her eyes. He couldn’t describe how he felt at the time but suddenly realized that perhaps the world had always been like this.

chapters.title: Chapter 352: 303: "I'm delirious, seeing hallucinations, I need to sleep some more." _3
chapters.content:
Chapter 352: Chapter 303: “I’m delirious, seeing hallucinations, I need to sleep some more.” _3
Later, his father explained that he thought the older sister was about to throw a bomb into the yard.
Yes.
If the world became peaceful, would that older sister still have to die?
And… would his father still have to die?
The bald man’s eyes reddened even more, he gritted his teeth, placed his right fist on his chest, and bellowed, “I’ve wanted to do this for a long time, why should this world continue to be in chaos, we want peace!”
“We want our children to be able to run on the streets carefree!”
“We want our children not to worry about their father possibly not returning home, dead in the street, every time he goes out!”
“We want peace!”
“Teacher, you’re right, if everyone is indifferent, then I am willing to be a Walker!”
“I might die!”
“But I believe that the world will surely change because of me!”
“That is enough! To die without regrets!!!”
The man’s tears finally uncontrollably slid down his cheeks, he screamed with all his might, as if to vent all the emotions he had accumulated over the years.
“…”
This time it was Chen Yi who was baffled.
Wait, isn’t this effect a bit too good?
You’re acting, aren’t you?
You must be acting, right?
After all, he’s a leader of the Dark forces, a figure of murder and arson on ordinary days, and just by his speech, he’s been completely enlightened and thoroughly reformed?
Isn’t your reaction a bit too much?
Chen Yi didn’t know what to say for a moment; he was having trouble following the script, which seemed to deviate from the route he had anticipated.
He had only intended to create a sufficiently noble image for himself, but now it seemed… he felt as though he had become a savior.
Wait a minute!
His mission was to become a D-level head of the Dark forces, not some savior!
Was this straying from the main storyline?
After remaining expressionless and silent for a long time, Chen Yi ultimately decided not to dampen the bald man’s enthusiasm and hesitantly spoke up.
“Have you decided, then? You might die.”
“To die without regrets!”
Wang Zhongyi, filled with frenzy, raised his right fist, looking at Chen Yi with an emotion in his eyes that he had never felt before. At that moment, he felt a confidence he never had before, not understanding why.
Perhaps it was because he knew he was on the right path.
The Dark forces might be very powerful.
But they could never bring the sense of glory and mission that comes with fighting for peace!
He could never bring back the older sister who tried to help him when he was a child, but he could prevent such things from happening in the future, or even not at all!
For the first time in years, he spoke with full confidence.
This feeling suddenly made him somewhat addicted; perhaps this was the… correct path.
In the live streaming room, many viewers watching the live broadcast were dumbfounded, unsure of what to comment.
…
“Am I seeing things? Did I just see someone who annihilated the Ten Clans talking about sacrificing himself for peace?”
“That hit hard. I must be hallucinating; need to sleep more.”
“Do you believe Chen Yi loves peace, or do you believe I am the mastermind behind this MMORPG?”
“Isn’t the most important thing here that there’s something wrong with the NPC’s character set-up in this map? A chaotic planet or a leader of the Dark forces, why after a speech they start to have a heart-wrenching epiphany and want to redeem themselves? Isn’t a villain supposed to lust for murder and arson? What the hell kind of villain pursues peace, did the character design jump the shark or what?”

chapters.title: Chapter 353: 305: ...don't do this, I suddenly can't bring myself to laugh.
chapters.content:
Chapter 353: Chapter 305: …don’t do this, I suddenly can’t bring myself to laugh.
“Teacher, where should we start with our first step?”
The bald man, whose mood had undergone a significant shift unknowingly, suddenly lost the timidity and caution he had shown in front of Chen Yi initially, and became extremely euphoric, showing a hint of excitement.
It was as if he had suddenly found a mission.
The bald man, realizing his own transformation, began to have some inner revelations. He wasn’t clear on why he no longer felt fear; perhaps he had always known that what he was doing was wrong, which was why he had always been so cautious.
But after suddenly becoming filled with positive energy, he felt fearless instead.
This fearlessness did not come from a lack of dread of death, but from knowing that what he was doing was right.
If the bald man had known the history of Blue Star…
He might have found an explanation for his change of heart in the ancient texts.
However, the culture of this planet did not have a clear explanation for such mental shifts, and Wang Zhongyi could not find a reason for his change of mood, only feeling distinctly different from before.
“…”
After a long silence, Chen Yi placed his hand gently on the bald man’s head with a soft voice, “I’m pleased with your transformation. When the new world descends and people face judgment in the kingdom of God, I will absolve you of your sins.”
“Before that, I need to know about the previous profit-making methods of your ‘Red Cavern’ forces.”
“This…”
When it came to this point, Wang Zhongyi seemed guilty, like a child who had done something wrong, standing in front of Chen Yi with his head bowed, somewhat hesitant, “Our previous methods of profit mainly came from clearing the wilderness.”
“By killing the monsters in the wild, we would acquire enough living resources and sell them at high prices to the residents.”
“Understood.”
Chen Yi nodded his head, noticing the shame on Wang Zhongyi’s face, and softly said, “Every person has sins; a person is born with sins, or perhaps the very reason you have come into this world is with sins.”
“You have come to this world to atone for your sins.”
“When your sentence is complete, you will naturally leave this prison.”
“As long as you do good deeds afterward, you will cleanse your sins.”
“Come into this world?”
Wang Zhongyi paused, with some hesitation trying to probe, “Teacher, I don’t understand what you mean by that. We didn’t quite catch it.”
…
At this moment, the players watching the live broadcast were discussing anxiously in the barrage.
‘It’s over. Is Chen Yi planning to reveal to these NPCs that they are NPCs? Even new players wouldn’t be this ignorant, right?’
‘I’m not sure either. I originally thought Chen Yi seemed to be quite intelligent, but now he suddenly seems a bit slow.’
‘Does Chen Yi not realize the consequences of revealing the truth about this game and the NPCs?’
‘Let’s just watch and see. I think Chen Yi probably won’t disclose the true nature of the game, since it wouldn’t benefit him in any way. Could it be that he wants these NPCs to realize they are just strings of data and then band together to rebel against the game to pass it this way?’
‘Stop joking. The last player who tried that is still enjoying Scavenger’s eternal buffet.’
…
“You are not from this world.”
In disbelief of all those watching the live stream, Chen Yi slowly turned around, his back to Wang Zhongyi, gazing toward the distant twilight with a distracted voice, “You originally belonged to an extremely beautiful world.”
“With the sun that appears on time every day and the gentle sunlight.”
“With the light rain that feels as comforting as the tender warmth of youth’s ambiguous love.”
“With twilight so enchanting that no matter how many times you admire it, it still moves the soul.”
“Where everyone lives in peace, everyone follows the law.”
“Where the doors need not be shut at night, and lost valuables are not coveted.”
“A world without sin, without slaughter, without crime, where everyone lives in an utterly joyful and carefree world.”
“Then…”
With some yearning, Wang Zhongyi murmured the image of that world in his mind, “Why have we come to this world filled with sin?”
“Because you were the anomalies in that world.”
Turning to face Wang Zhongyi, Chen Yi spoke calmly and deliberately, “Because you did atrocity after atrocity in that world, disrupting its peace, sullying that world.”
“So the god of that world punished all those who committed evil there by sending them to this world.”
“This world, rife with killings, is where you have been cast to atone for your sins.”
“But now —”
“The judgment of the new world is soon upon us, and all the people of this world will be subject to God’s judgment once again. If God deems that your sins have been washed away,”
“You may return to that world.”
“Otherwise, you must continue in this world, reincarnating for tens of thousands of years, bearing the consequences of your crimes.”
“…”
Wang Zhongyi blinked in bewilderment, looking at Chen Yi before him, momentarily at a loss for words.
Just moments ago, he felt passionate about bringing peace to the world, but now, how had he suddenly become marked with sin?
And according to the teacher…
He wasn’t supposed to be in this world?
But his memories told him that he had lived in this world since childhood, he was familiar with every detail of this world, with no memory of any other world. This was simply too fantastical…

chapters.title: Chapter 354: 305: ...don't be like this, suddenly I can't laugh anymore._2
chapters.content:
Chapter 354: Chapter 305: …don’t be like this, suddenly I can’t laugh anymore._2
Fantasy so extreme it was like listening to a myth.
Just when he was a bit unsure of what to say,
a snide female chuckle suddenly filled his ears.
“Pretentious, just a Mart trickster.”
“I actually thought you were someone with great ambitions and important endeavors, but now it seems you’re just another Mart trickster. What’s next? Are you going to say that with just a little money, one can purchase an ‘Order of Atonement’ from you and wash away their sins?”
“These clichéd tricks might fool others, but do you think they can fool me?”
As the voice faded away,
a scantily clad woman, escorted by eight fully armed men, strode into Wang Zhongyi’s office. She crossed her arms as she looked toward Chen Yi, who stood by the window, her eyes filled with mockery and scorn.
This woman was the same one who had just entered the elevator.
Originally, she had just come here to take care of some business.
But when she had stepped into the elevator earlier, the young man before her caught her attention. This young man’s face wore a look of indifference that was all too common in the faces of everyone in Ao City.
It was an indifference to the lives of others.
In this world, indifference was a requisite skill for survival.
However, the indifference on this young man’s face was different from that of the other inhabitants of this city. It was like… as if he was out of place in this world, as if everything before him was nothingness.
Furthermore, the way this young man looked at her carried neither the lust found in bold men’s eyes nor the fear and caution present in timid men’s eyes. It was as if… as if she were a log, non-existent.
This feeling intrigued her greatly.
So, when the elevator stopped on the ground floor, she decided to go back to the 18th floor with her bodyguards, curious to discover what kind of person this young man was. Just as she reached the entrance of the Red Skull Faction leader’s office, she heard this young man’s speech.
“If no one else is willing to be a Walker, then I am willing.”
“This world always needs people who might seem foolish but are filled with courage.”
“We want peace.”
This speech was something she had never heard before.
It was something she had thought about in her heart.
But she dared not mention it to anyone. To speak up would only lead to being treated as an outcast.
For a woman to take over her father’s business in this world was extremely difficult. Even though she had proven her excellence, the veterans of her father’s powers always hindered her. Especially if she dared to express any opinion about peace.
The veterans would instantly see her as a weak leader.
She would lose all qualifications to inherit her father’s power.
And at that point, not even her father could do anything about it.
However, just as she unexpectedly started to idolize and yearn for this young man she had only met once, the speech he continued with shattered the thoughts that had just arisen in her heart.
So he was nothing but a Mart trickster after all.
She had actually believed he was a hero willing to oppose the world with great ambitions.
Indeed.
In this world, preserving oneself was already a luxury.
Saving others?
Was there any luxury greater than this?
Afterward, as she looked at Chen Yi standing by the window with a hint of contempt and loathing flashing in her eyes, she suddenly felt that this young man wasn’t so different after all. Just as she was about to order her bodyguards to kill this Mart trickster in front of her,
the man suddenly began to speak.
“Do you think you’ve seen through the truth?”
“Do you know what’s the most pitiful thing about you? You’ve killed all those who wanted to save you.”
“What now?”
Chen Yi slowly turned his head to look at the woman standing by the office door, his steps leisurely as he walked up to her. Looking down at the woman who was shorter than him, he spoke quietly with a calm expression.
“You want to kill me?”
“Do you think you can kill me?”
“I may not be the first to come to save you, but I will definitely be the last. You don’t have much time left. Are you sure you want to kill me?”
“I…”
The woman who had always shown herself to be strong suddenly felt somewhat tongue-tied, looking at the young man approaching her and subconsciously stepping back. But then she flew into a rage because of this step back!
She was actually intimidated by a Mart swindler!
“Fine, fine, fine!”
The woman glared at Chen Yi, raging and enunciating each word, “Since you say we do not belong to this world, but are here to atone, then our original world must certainly have its own culture, right?”
“Come on, tell me about the culture of the world we originally belonged to.”
“If you can’t articulate it, you can leave your life here today.”
Exactly.
Wang Zhongyi, who was just about to step forward and show his support for his teacher, also came to the same realization, looking forward to Chen Yi’s reply with expectation in his eyes.
Many things can be faked.
But the culture of a world is systematic; it cannot be fabricated, and even if conjured up on the spot, it would be full of holes and easily shattered. Since the teacher claimed they were not of this world, he must surely know the culture of their original world.
As long as the teacher says it out loud.
It would prove that everything the teacher said was true.
At that time…
After completing the atonement, could they really return to that peaceful world?
Wang Zhongyi’s eyes became even more filled with anticipation. As a child, he loved playing with beanbags. In his textbooks, a long, long time ago, there was a game many children enjoyed, called throwing beanbags.
The rules were simple.
One child would throw a beanbag to another, and then it would be passed around in turn.
But the beanbags he played with as a child were always thrown against a wall.
The only time someone played beanbag with him was with that elder sister, and then that elder sister was killed by his father.
If they could return to that peaceful world, might he too be able to freely play with beanbags?
“…”
After hearing this woman’s demand about their culture, Chen Yi calmly smiled, put one arm behind his back, took down a walking stick hanging on the wall, held it in his hand, and slowly paced around the office.
“Since you want to hear it, then I shall tell you.”
“The world you originally came from boasts tens of thousands of years of culture.”
“It has countless splendid or fleeting cultures that come and go like a night-blooming cereus, or those that endure, benefiting many generations.”
“These are the most glorious achievements of your ancestors.”
…
The audience in the live stream room began to feel unsettled.
‘Damn, this is spoon-feeding, why would she ask such a question? I could answer this too, doesn’t this seem like the map is suddenly lowering the difficulty?’
‘This woman isn’t really going to be hoodwinked like this, right? She clearly seems to come from a high background. What if she really believes Chen Yi, thinking he’s a savior sent by the gods?’
‘I’m serious, if Chen Yi clears this using such trickery, I’ll be the first to call BS. Who can’t swindle? Get me in there, and I’d do it too!’
‘Do you think you’re funny, the guy above? The map has limited all of Chen Yi’s powers, what else should he use if not trickery? Come on, tell me what you would use?’
‘What I would use is none of your business, I just find this kind of bluffing distasteful. Even if he clears it, I won’t give him any credit, that’s what I’m saying.’
‘Your words just made me laugh. How about you stop talking in the chat and say it to Chen Yi’s face once he’s out of the map?’
‘Hahaha, then Chen Yi would probably immediately ask which tribe he’s from, after all, Chen Yi never takes revenge on just an individual.’
‘No, he’d probably ask which Starfield he’s from.’
‘…don’t be like that, I suddenly can’t laugh anymore, is it still possible to change my Starfield registration now?’
…
Chen Yi held the walking stick in one hand, standing in the gentle twilight glow, and with a voice rhythmic and resounding, he raised his left arm and began to speak.
“Set a heart for the heaven and earth, establish a life for the living people, continue the lost teachings for the sages of the past, and create peace for all generations to come.”
“This is a timeless saying left by Mr. Zhang Zai, simple yet profound, its legacy unceasingly revered throughout the ages.”
“Have you ever heard of such timeless sayings?”

chapters.title: Chapter 355: 306: "But this world forces us to have no choice.
chapters.content:
Chapter 355: Chapter 306: “But this world forces us to have no choice.
“To lie on brushwood and taste gall, nursing one’s wrath for dozens of years before making a triumphant return, do any of you still remember such a person?”
“To dance through the streets without fear of ridicule, swallowing all grievances only to achieve success and fame later on—do you have any knowledge of this?”
“At the age of 17, he went on military campaigns, and by 23, he became a renowned general who intimidated all quarters. People thought he would carve out a new chapter in history, but the heavens envy the talented, and he died young, just like his predecessors.”
“In the beginning, there was a bowl…”
“…”
As Chen Yi recounted the heroes from Blue Star’s history one by one, the woman, who had been full of mockery and doubt, saw her expression gradually stiffen. For a moment, she was at a loss for words.
She really wanted to find loopholes in the young man’s stories.
But… it was difficult.
The historical tales spoken by this young man weren’t isolated; they were interconnected, allowing one to glimpse the shadow of the next protagonist from the current story.
Such fascinating tales, capable of stirring the soul, were incredibly hard to fabricate even if one tried.
Much less fabricating so many of them.
Even a novelist known to her, such as Wang Xin, lacked the capacity to create thus. It was an impossible feat—a normal person could not come up with such captivating stories in a short time.
They were consistent with no contradictions.
Each piece connected smoothly to the next.
Such a feat was beyond human capability unless these stories had been crafted in someone’s mind for a long time. But who in their right mind would do such a thing, especially in a place as perilous as Ao City? Who would have the luxury to entertain such thoughts?
Unless this young man had been brewing this affair for a very long time.
The woman was still somewhat incredulous, yet this time she wasn’t as adamant. Instead, she hesitated before speaking, “How am I to know whether what you speak of is the history of our original world or merely tales you concocted?”
“Stories are limited, but history is boundless,”
Chen Yi was in no hurry. Leaning against the crowd, he gripped his cane and looked out the window at the setting sun, continuing to speak, “Culture encompasses more than just history. It includes many things, one of which is poetry.”
“Poetry was the most brilliant aspect of your world’s culture.”
“I’ve studied the history of your world and found only a few lines of poetry that exist solely within the realm of rhyme, completely devoid of any artistic conception.”
“Indeed.”
“In a world consumed only by sin and slaughter, such things would never arise.”
“Let me recite some poetry from your world, that should suffice.”
“In all corners of the world, there’s not one who understands me; at the ends of the earth, we might as well be neighbours.”
“At a crossroads without a cause, children share a handkerchief, wet with tears.”
“…”
“In the corner, several branches of plum blossoms braving the cold; they bloom alone.”
“From afar, it’s clear it’s not snow, for the faint scent of their fragrance arrives.”
“…”
“The reeds are lush against the azure sky; white dew turns to frost.”
“The so-called beloved, across the water she stands.”
“…”
“Ten years of life and death beyond recall; without contemplation, indelibly etched in memory.”
“Across a thousand miles of lonely graves, no place to share the stark desolation.”
One poem after another, Chen Yi recited dozens of poems with a voice that seamlessly melded with the mood of each piece. With these poems, he delivered a striking blow in a world culturally barren—no matter how vast this map might be.
It was as large as a whole planet.
But after all, it was just a map.
Clearly, the team that designed this map had not considered culture at all, and perhaps they did not expect that players entering this map would care about its culture, considering it to be a place filled with nothing but killing.
According to the designers, players should pick up a knife and fight their way down the path, aiming to defeat the leader of a D-class power or die within the map. That would be the norm.
A map rife with killing—why bother with culture?
To craft a cultural system that perfectly fits Rogue Star would require an immense amount of effort.
As he expected, when these trans-world poems were heard for the first time by these people, they were immediately stupefied and stood still in shock.
…
“Ten years of life and death beyond recall; without contemplation, indelibly etched in memory,”
the woman murmured disorientedly as she stood in the office, gazing at Chen Yi’s retreating figure, her eyes reddening slightly.
Without contemplation, indelibly etched in memory.
The emotions she had suppressed for over a decade were effortlessly described in this line of poetry.
It was as if it were about her.
She had always thought that no one understood her, seeing only her outward dominance. But who knew that she really wished to be a cat cuddled in her boyfriend’s arms, a beloved and cherished woman—but she could not.
She was her father’s successor; the moment she showed even a hint of vulnerability or womanly traits, elders would immediately suggest revoking her successorship.
She could only keep her emotions hidden deep within, never daring to show them, even in the solitude of night.
But at this moment,
the poem struck a chord with her.
After a long time,
the woman, with tears in her eyes, trembled as she spoke, “Is there more to this poem?”
“…”
With one hand behind his back and the other leaning on his cane, Chen Yi looked serenely out at the nearby sunset and remained silent.
This was a bit challenging.
He suddenly couldn’t remember the rest of the poem.
Which was indeed somewhat awkward. He had never attended school, and the only reason he could recite so many poems and historical facts was that he had taken advantage of the benefits offered by the upgrade in the game.

chapters.title: Chapter 356: 306: "But this world forces us with no other way."_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 356: Chapter 306: “But this world forces us with no other way.”_2
At the start of the leveling up game, they encountered a map that tested their vocabulary of idioms.
It was only after that he began to cram knowledge in subjects such as Chinese, math, geography, and history.
In case they entered a map that required this knowledge later, they wouldn’t be completely in the dark.
So, it’s being put to use now?
All the historical events and poetry he had memorized back then were being called upon, but the problem was he hadn’t used Memory Paper to memorize them—it was all done in his mind, and now he had begun to forget…
About a minute passed.
He still couldn’t remember.
“No more.”
Chen Yi looked out of the window with an expressionless face, without a single ripple of emotion, “This is a eulogy composed by Su Shi to mourn his first wife, Wang Fu.”
“After writing the first two lines, Su Shi was overcome with such sorrow that he jumped into the river to join his wife in the hereafter.”
“However, it is said that there are a few more lines to this poem, supposedly left by Su Shi before he jumped into the river, but they have never been revealed. Since then, this poem has become an unfinished piece, as well as the last poem Su Shi wrote in his life.”
“Just as Su Shi himself said, no one’s life could be perfect.”
“The life of the otherwise perfect Su Shi ended with an unfinished verse.”
“Later, to commemorate Su Shi, people specifically established a festival for him, named the Dragon Boat Festival.”
“On this day, people are supposed to wrap zongzi and throw them into the river so that the shrimp soldiers and crab generals within the water would consume them rather than desecrate the body of Mr. Su Shi.”
“This festival continues to this day.”
Having said this, Chen Yi couldn’t help but twitch the corners of his mouth slightly.
Teacher Su Shi, if you have a spirit in the sky.
Forgive me.
It’s not malicious fabrication on my part.
It’s just that I wasn’t familiar with it at the time. After this is over, I will definitely review your life story and make sure to recite this poem fluently.
At this moment, he realized what was meant by “books are invaluable at the moment of need.”
Isn’t the Dragon Boat Festival meant to commemorate Su Shi?
Dammit.
I will definitely catch up on it when I get back.
…
“Uh…”
At this time, a Blue Star player who was watching the live stream looked bewilderedly at Chen Yi, who was speaking eloquently. It took the player a long while before he turned his puzzled gaze to his friend.
“Is the Dragon Boat Festival really in commemoration of Su Shi?”
“It seems so.”
The player beside him also felt strange, “Although it doesn’t feel right, since Yi says it is, it must be so. Yi wouldn’t be wrong.”
“But I thought the Dragon Boat Festival was to commemorate Qu Yuan?”
“Are you suggesting Yi is wrong?”
“No, no, that’s not what I meant at all. What I mean is, the history books might have recorded it wrong. Clearly it commemorates Su Shi, but the history books have it all mixed up.”
“Exactly, those who compile textbooks should do more proper research.”
…
“No one’s life is perfect…”
The woman standing in the office, upon hearing Chen Yi’s words, felt as though struck by a heavy hammer, and she staggered in place, seemingly slipping into some sort of trance.
All her problems, worries, and concerns over the years were solved in the face of these words.
Indeed.
Why overthink it all?
So what if she had made mistakes?
So what if things weren’t right?
Why insist on a perfect life? Why force every single thing she does to be correct? No one’s life is perfect. Even Su Shi, who created such an exquisite verse, left an unfinished poem before his death, making his life not so perfect.
“`
Why should her life be perfect?
After a long while.
The woman wiped the tears from her eyes, her face streaked with tear marks as she looked toward Chen Yi’s silhouette at the window, her voice clear and forceful, brimming with an energy she had never had before as she declared, “Teacher, I’ve realized.”
“You’re right, we come to this world to atone, this world should not be filled with slaughter, it should not be a place where everyone turns to evil.”
“Just like you said, Teacher, Judgment Day is about to come, and if we want to return to our own world, we must pass the test, but I don’t know what the test is.”
“I have already told you.”
Chen Yi, leaning on his cane with one hand, slowly turned and faced the woman behind him, calmly saying, “World peace, only through world peace will your gods believe you’ve truly cleansed yourselves of sin, and I will also offer my suggestions to the gods.”
“As a spokesperson for the gods, I’m willing to help you, but the condition is that you truly need to let go of the slaughter in your hearts and pursue peace.”
“… This.”
The woman hesitated for a moment before speaking weakly, “Teacher, world peace is too hard. I’ve heard what you said, I’ve realized, but others haven’t heard it, and it’s really difficult for everyone to let down their guard.”
“Just one person like me is too insignificant when it comes to world peace.”
“Come.”
Chen Yi waved his hand, signaling the woman to step forward, then he picked up a piece of white paper from the table, spread it out, and dropped a speck of ink onto it.
The black ink on the white paper was striking.
“Do you see it?”
“Teacher, does that mean that even if our actions are like a drop of water in a bucket, we should still do it?”
“No.”
Chen Yi slowly shook his head, his internal voice tinged with speechlessness as he said, “What I mean is, in a world full of slaughter, no matter how insignificant we are, we still stand out.”
“As long as we stand up.”
“There will be people who follow us.”
“Remember one thing forever, the world is always lacking those who dare to stand out, followed next by those who dare to be the first to follow.”
“Since others haven’t heard our words, then let them listen.”
“Besides, you’re not just one person.”
“There’s also me.”
Wang Zhongyi, who had been standing to the side with tears brimming in his eyes, stepped forward with his voice full of sorrow and trembling, raised his right arm and roared, “I’m sick of this world full of slaughter, I’m sick of sitting on the toilet worrying about whether there’s a bomb hidden inside.”
“I’m sick of living life on tenterhooks.”
“I’m sick of a life where people can’t truly open up to one another.”
“I don’t want to go whoring, nor do I want to abduct a woman to bear my children; I want to experience a love as depicted in history books, mutual and consensual, not just lust, I want a woman who can truly love me and whom I can truly love in return.”
“I want world peace, I want to return to our own world as soon as possible and enjoy a real life.”
With his eyes full of tears, Wang Zhongyi stood in the twilight, his right arm raised high, resembling a fervent believer.
“And me.”
The seemingly inconspicuous vice president of the ‘Red Skull,’ removed his gas mask, revealing his pockmarked and worm-infested cheeks that looked terrifying and said with a cry in his tremulous voice.
“Starting at age 3, my dad taught me to chop people.”
“I was timid by nature, afraid to take action.”
“Until I was 7, when someone suddenly burst into our home with a gun, killed my whole family, leaving only me alive, my face ruined by a bomb, but sparing my life like a dog’s. We had no acquaintance with that man, no grudges.”
“Later when I grew up and found him, I learned he had only planned a big heist, but since he had never done it before and was somewhat uncertain, he thought our family was an easy target to practice on.”
“I realized then, in this damned world, you have to kill. If you don’t kill others, they will kill you.”
“I don’t cherish such a world at all.”
“I want peace.”
The usually mellow vice president also raised his right hand high.
“Us too.”
The eight fully armed subordinates standing behind the woman, who at first had been cold, now all had red eyes and hoarsely said, “Actually, we also don’t like killing, we don’t enjoy putting on such a cold front.”
“But this world forces us to.”
“If possible, we too want peace, and I know there are many more brothers who really want the world to be peaceful, just like us. They just need someone to lead.”

chapters.title: Chapter 357: 307
chapters.content:
Chapter 357: Chapter 307
“Okay.”
Chen Yi’s expression was calm, his eyes shining with a compassionate glow as he nodded heavily, equally raising his right arm, he said in a deep voice, “Then let it begin today.”
What followed seemed to have hit the fast-forward button.
The woman told Chen Yi her name, saying she was called Qin Le, and her father was the leader of a D-level force in Ao City, not too low in status.
After “Red Skull” members were gathered to listen again to Chen Yi’s passionate and powerful speech, Chen Yi gained his first force, although he was not yet its leader, the force was already at his disposal.
Immediately afterward.
After Qin Le brought her father over to listen to Chen Yi’s speech.
This man with white hair and a body riddled with bullet holes and scars, teared up for the first time, also believing in what Chen Yi said, under irrefutable evidence, it was very difficult for them not to believe Chen Yi’s words.
It was a complete cultural system of a world.
It was their world.
It was where they were truly supposed to exist, not this world filled with slaughter.
On the seventh day on the map.
Ao City had nearly settled down.
…
Chen Yi, somewhat physically and mentally exhausted, lay dazed in a room prepared for him by Qin Le, feeling an unbearable dryness and pain in his throat, having just finished a speech in a city block.
In this world, his Combat Power had been completely restricted.
All he could use were the things in his head and his own mouth.
In these seven days, he had held a total of 291 speeches, almost without sleep, adding up to less than 10 hours of sleep, feeling that he was on the verge of a mental breakdown.
He gave speeches on high platforms in the city blocks under the night sky.
He gave speeches on the top floors of schools that were once glorious but now ruins.
He stood unprotected and naked but for a pair of underwear, giving speeches in front of an alarmed crowd.
He did this to show everyone listening to his speeches that he carried no weapons on him, and they need not be too wary of him.
In fact, he had already completed his task.
On the third day.
Qin Le, Wang Zhongyi, and others suggested he create his own force, use it as a prototype, and strive for world peace.
Naturally, there was no reason for him to refuse.
Initially, the force was only a lowest-tier E-level force.
In this world, a force’s ranking is automatic; as long as you have an item called “Force Creation Ticket”, you can create a force, and this item is dropped by the monsters out in the wild.
Most of this world’s life resources, including vehicles and firearms, drop from the wild monsters.
These monsters acted like the world’s factories, assuming various production functions.
A force’s rating was evaluated based on the comprehensive strength of the official member count, influence scale, reputation impact, activity range, number and level of Professionals, and more.
He named this newly created force “Utopia”.
With the entire Red Skull membership joining his force, and Qin Le leading some of her subordinates into his force, along with others who had recently been convinced to follow him, his force was promoted to a C-level force almost on the day it was created.
This power had far surpassed the main quest objective of the map.
The main quest’s target was to become the leader of a D-level dark force.
And suddenly, on the third day of entering this map, he had accomplished that goal, becoming the leader of a C-level dark force.
That day, a panel appeared in front of him.
‘Ding, congratulations on completing the main quest beyond expectation: Within one month, become the leader of a D-level dark force.’
‘Side quest: Kill 4444 indigenous inhabitants, progress 0.’
‘You may now choose to leave the map, or continue to stay inside the map until you are automatically removed after a month.’
He had chosen to refuse to leave.
C-level?
He was not satisfied.
Given the current pace, if he moved a bit faster, he had the full opportunity to become the leader of an A-level force.
D-level was not his goal.
The Feng Family would naturally have to be dealt with once he was out.
But before that, he wanted everyone to know that no matter how they targeted him, he could perfectly resolve it and achieve the best outcome; all your maneuvers Chen Yi will catch.
But once he’s out.
Are you prepared for Chen Yi’s maneuvers?
This entire map experience was broadcast across several Star Systems, and he wanted to make a name for himself in this broadcast, a perfect score? Not enough, he wanted to exceed the perfect score.
The most important point is…
Chen Yi picked up a glass of ice water from the table and drained it in one gulp, struggling to stand and rubbed his dry throat, his hands in his pockets as he stood by the floor-to-ceiling windows looking down at the street below where children playfully threw sandbags at each other, his pupils reflecting a hint of complex emotion, silently contemplating.
He rarely felt soft-hearted.
But this time, he did.
He naturally knew why this world had become so filled with killing; the indigenous inhabitants of this world were NPCs, their innate nature may not be evil, but due to the nature of the live game-world setting, they had to kill each other.
This paradox made everyone live in pain.
When they put out the slogan of making the world peaceful so that children could run freely, when their force began to take shape, more and more forces began to join them voluntarily, choosing to follow them.

chapters.title: Chapter 358: 307_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 358: Chapter 307_2
This means that most of the indigenous people here yearn for peace; it’s just that no one has spoken up.
Seeing these children, who once had nothing but fear in their eyes, now playfully tossing sandbags in the streetlights at night without restraint, something inside him felt a stir. The parents standing by, watching their children, didn’t reach for AK47s when they saw their own kids toppled by sandbags.
Instead, they chatted and laughed with other parents.
Even so,
he could sense that these parents were still somewhat tense, obviously still worried that the person standing opposite might launch an attack at any moment, a psychological shadow left by years of conflict.
Everyone was cautiously and luxuriously enjoying this hard-won peace.
Just then—
The door of the house swung open.
“Mr. Chen Yi.”
Qin Le pushed the door open and looked displeasedly at Chen Yi, who was smoking by the window, and complained, “Mr. Chen Yi, the doctor and I both told you, you shouldn’t drink cold water when your throat hurts—it will only make it more uncomfortable. And you should try not to smoke as well.”
“Teacher, you haven’t slept for a long time. If you keep this up, you’ll have health issues.”
“It’s okay.”
Chen Yi stood calmly in front of the floor-to-ceiling window, bringing the cigarette between his fingers to his lips. He looked out at the street urchins through the swirling blue smoke and suddenly smiled, “You know, I’ve killed a lot of people.”
“I know.”
Qin Le, standing behind Chen Yi, spoke softly, “The vice-chairman of Red Skull told me about his first encounter with you. He said the killing intent in you was so intense it was frightening. He told me that without personally killing tens of thousands, one wouldn’t have such an aura.”
“Hm.”
Chen Yi nodded slightly, “I’ve killed many people, so many that I can’t even remember the count. I might have killed more than all the people in your world combined.”
“Ah?”
A flicker of disbelief crossed Qin Le’s eyes as he stammered, “The people you’ve killed outnumber the population of our world? Our world has a population close to a hundred million—is it more than that?”
“Not just a bit more, it is several points more.”
“Does… does that make a difference?”
“A bit more means moving the decimal point one place to the left; several points more means moving the decimal point several places to the left.”
“Several… places to the left?”
Qin Le looked down at his ten fingers, pondering for a long time before the thought struck him. Hundreds of billions of people?
The teacher had killed hundreds of billions of people?
Where on earth did he kill all those people?
Chen Yi paid no attention to Qin Le’s shock. Perhaps, in his heart, he felt that after this task was over, there wouldn’t be much interaction with Qin Le. He had said many things he shouldn’t have.
“Hm.”
“They were all people who opposed me.”
“Actually, I’m a person who loves peace. A long, long time ago, I had a brother in life and death, his name was Tuberculosis Rabbit.”
“Back then, although we didn’t earn much, we lived happily and joyfully.”
“That kind of life was very interesting.”
