“Then things gradually changed. I became stronger, but also attracted some foolhardy people. I don’t understand why they provoked me. I tried to remind others not to provoke me by using slaughter.”
“But they seemed not to understand.”
“Or maybe, they always confidently believed that they could handle me.”
“Just like this time.”
After being silent for a while, Chen Yi pinched out the cigarette in his hand and flicked it away, muttering to himself as if he was talking to no one in particular, “The Feng Family from the Annihilation Starfield Project Team, are you disappointed in me? It seems I haven’t made too many blunders in this map.”
“And I’m about to complete it successfully, even exceeding the mission objectives.”
“Actually, before you switched the debut map for us, I even thought that as long as you came to apologize, the grudges between us might be settled. But then you tripped me up from behind.”
“What should I do about this?”
“You think the project team is unkillable?”
“Do you really believe that?”
“Is that your confidence?”
“Enjoy your moment, for you will be the first step in my quest for world peace. I’ve been thinking about how to end all this absurdity, and now it suddenly became clear to me.”
“I want to bring peace to the world.”
“Return to the calm life of the beginning.”
Qin Le, standing behind Chen Yi, couldn’t quite understand what Mr. Chen Yi was talking about, but she grasped something. She knew the teacher wasn’t from this world, he was a spokesman for the gods, yet it seemed like he was discussing matters of other worlds.
“Teacher, are you considering how to bring peace to other worlds?”
She ventured tentatively.
“Hm.”
Chen Yi regained his composure with a calm expression, nodding lightly and smiling without saying a word.
“So, Teacher, do you plan to bring peace to other worlds as well?”
“Yes.”
“Like the way it is now?”
“A bit different.”
“Different how?”
“There are two ways to achieve world peace, one is like on Rogue Star.”
“And the other?”
“When everyone in this world dies, it naturally becomes peaceful.”
“…”
Qin Le looked up at Chen Yi’s clear eyes somewhat blankly, at a loss for what to say next.
…
Downstairs.
The president of Red Skull, Wang Zhongyi, with red-rimmed eyes, gazed at the children playing enthusiastically with sandbags under the night sky on the street below, his lips tightly closed, not speaking. This was a scene he had dreamt of countless times as a child.
He had thought such scenes would never come to pass.
Yet in his lifetime, it had truly happened.
Though he was too old to join in, and the sister who had first played sandbags with him had long since passed away, he had… finally seen this moment.
He looked up at the shadow of Chen Yi in front of the high-rise’s floor-to-ceiling window.
If not for the Teacher.
He would have never seen this scene in his life.
In this life, he had no regrets.
…
Fourteen days had passed.
It had been fourteen days since Chen Yi entered this map. Starting from Ao City as his base, he began to radiate his influence to the surrounding cities. Their ideology spread through the population at an extremely rapid pace, much like a virus.
At first, they had to actively conquer the local dark forces that refused to repent, showing the local population a glimmer of hope.
But as their power grew, so did their fame.
More and more forces began to join them willingly.
Most people yearned for peace.
Of course, some leaders of the dark forces were very resistant to Chen Yi and his team; if peace was restored, their current social status would plummet in an instant, and they would lose the prestige they held today.
They organized a large group of Centaurs to resist the existence of Chen Yi and the others.
Chen Yi, however, did not need to act; he only need to command from the rear.
Large forces following him would, with excited and thrilled expressions, bellow for a righteous battle, unleashing greater combat power than ever before, fearlessly charging toward these adversaries!
They crumbled almost instantly.
Every native who died in battle for him received his personal reception.
Chen Yi told everyone that those who died fighting for peace would skip Judgment Day and directly return to their previous worlds; when they opened their eyes again, they would find a world of peace and harmony.
With this assurance,
Countless were willing to die in battle for him.
Everyone thought it an honor to die for peace. Although he possessed neither combat power nor professional abilities, he had faith. When one person becomes the faith of all, it no longer matters whether that person has abilities.
…
In Ao City, a young man looked displeasedly at the distant back of Chen Yi and whispered to his elderly father beside him, “Father, do you really believe what that man says about Judgment Day and the old world?”
“It feels like everyone is under some kind of spell.”
“I do not.”
The old man, leaning on a cane with an aged face, replied with a raspy, smiling voice.
“Ah?”
The young man was taken aback, bewildered and disbelievingly said, “Dad, are you listening to yourself? If you don’t believe, why did you join Chen Yi’s forces with the heritage that’s been passed down through generations in our family?”
“If you don’t believe, why are we supporting him?”
“Does belief matter?”
The elderly man glanced at the young man beside him and gestured meaningfully towards the playing children in the background, “What does it matter whether we believe or not?”
“What difference does it make whether it’s true or not?”
“Sometimes, people need to be a bit foolish to be a bit happier.”
“Like now.”

chapters.title: Chapter 359: 308: Gleaming Star Level Title 'Peace Envoy'! (Extra 10,000-word mega )
chapters.content:
Chapter 359: Chapter 308: Gleaming Star Level Title ‘Peace Envoy’! (Extra 10,000-word mega chapter)
The noise of children playing nearby sounded particularly grating.
If it had been before, he certainly would have noticed such a jarring sound, but today he stood right beside it without realizing it even once, the young man somewhat stunned in place, as if suddenly enlightened.
These days, he had grown accustomed to the noise of children playing near his ears.
It seemed like a normal thing.
Something that was absolutely impossible before.
The world was starting to change subtly, even managing to deceive him.
“What difference does belief or disbelief make,”
the young man murmured to himself, then looked up again at the long-lost smile on his father’s face—the kind that had never been there, no matter how big a project they had landed.
But now.
Despite having entrusted all his family business to Chen Yi, the smile on his father’s face had grown more frequent.
No longer did he have that somber look with a murderous aura from morning till night.
And he… he even dared to question his father.
He never would have dared to before.
He had just realized this; perhaps his father had become too affable lately, making him feel less need to tread on eggshells.
Were all these changes brought about by that young man?
Suddenly enlightened, the young man looked again at Chen Yi’s silhouette on the stage in the crowd, his eyes devoid of the previous doubt and confusion, now filled with gratitude instead.
He understood what his father meant.
Belief or disbelief, it wasn’t important.
Whether it’s true or not is also not important.
People needed an excuse, an excuse to unite, to bring peace back to this world. People needed a faith, and faith is never created.
It is needed.
Every faith originates from suffering.
At that moment—
The young man on the stage looked over.
The countless throngs around him raised their right arms toward Chen Yi’s gaze, shouting feverishly and excitedly, “For peace, for peace!”
Seeing this,
the young man was momentarily stunned, then shook his head and laughed helplessly, raising his right arm excitedly and shouting, “For peace!”
At this moment, he kind of understood what his father had said.
The people needed to be a bit foolish for the world to be happier.
Being too clever, many things could not move forward.
He once thought these people were foolish, deceived by such naive lies, but now he understood that perhaps most of them were well aware, but they chose to deceive themselves.
It wasn’t Chen Yi deceiving them.
It was them deceiving themselves.
The elderly man beside the young man laughed and raised his arm too, shouting, “For peace.”
He wasn’t afraid of being deceived.
He was just afraid no one would dare to deceive him again.
At least he didn’t dare to step out and deceive others anymore.
He lacked the power and the courage.
…
Day Twenty-Nine.
On a street in a certain city.
A large group of Centaurs with a sticker of a peace dove on their faces, armed with various weapons, enclosed several hundred people in the center.
Among the hundreds, a man leading them with a ferocious expression and eyes full of fear clutched his hands tightly, looking around at the Centaurs surrounding them and shouted with a tremulous and agitated voice, “You’ve all been deceived, there’s no such thing as Judgment Day, no new world!”
“That man is a swindler!”
“You’ve all been tricked!”
“We’re just NPCs, that man is a player, he’s just completing a mission. Once he’s gone, the world will go back to how it was at the start, you’ve all been duped!”
“You bunch of fools!”
“Don’t believe him, he’s just using you, I am one of you! We’re all family here!”
As his words fell,
Wang Zhongyi in the crowd coldly sneered, loading his rifle smoothly and aiming the muzzle at the bearded man they had surrounded, scoffing, “What a joke!
“Spouting nonsense, still daring to slander the teacher when facing death.”
“Stop resisting, you are the last stubborn force resisting, just by annihilating your faction, the world can finally achieve complete peace, there will be no more slaughter or strife, and schools can be reestablished.”
“I can also pursue a real relationship.”
“A better world is on the horizon, and it’s only delayed by a few seconds because of you people, truly despicable.”
Just as Wang Zhongyi was about to pull the trigger,
the surroundings suddenly became silent.
He paused for a moment and instinctively looked back, only to see Teacher Chen Yi walking slowly from behind the crowd with a cane in hand, whereupon the fervent and respectful Centaurs parted ways and bowed their heads.
“Teacher,”
Wang Zhongyi also hurriedly bowed respectfully.
“Hmm,”
Chen Yi nodded lightly, and with cane in hand, he slowly walked up to the ferocious-looking, terrified bearded man, staring calmly at him for a moment before finally speaking, “Who told you those words just now?”
“Others… other players,”
“There were players before, and I listened to their conversations, whenever a player descended into our city, I would arrange for my men to eavesdrop. I created this faction just to keep tabs on players!”
“With each restart of the world, everyone else loses their memories while I still remember everything. I know your world is called the Ascension Game, and I know you players don’t regard us NPCs as human beings.”

chapters.title: Chapter 360: 308: Gleaming Star Level Title 'Peace Envoy'! (Extra 10,000-word mega )_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 360: Chapter 308: Gleaming Star Level Title ‘Peace Envoy’! (Extra 10,000-word mega chapter)_2
The bearded man seemed to summon his courage, his eyes filled with a deathly resolve as he bellowed in fear, “Don’t try to scare me, I’m not afraid of you. I know that you players entering this map have no abilities; all your powers are restricted. You’re just like the most ordinary citizens; anyone can easily kill you.”
“This world has already been rebooted 98 times!”
“Every time new players come and go, this world is rebooted, and it’s as if nothing has ever happened, just like before.”
“Everyone’s memory will be erased!”
“Except for me!”
“Only I know what the truth of this world is: we’re all just NPCs in a game, our memories aren’t real at all, our memories have been altered!”
“You think I don’t wish for world peace?”
“But even if you make the world peaceful now, what does it matter? After you leave, this world will be rebooted again, and everything will be as it was at the beginning, unchanged. At that time, everyone will lose these memories, and only I will remember this!”
“But I don’t want to live on aimlessly any longer.”
“I’m fed up with living in such a virtual world; I have my own thoughts, my own way of thinking, I can decide my actions; I’m a real person!”
“Kill me!”
“I’ve longed for death. Living in such a virtual world is a painful thing. What is the point of existence in a world that’s continuously rebooted? You players never care about our life or death. After you complete your missions and leave, who will care for us?”
It was like a roar before death.
The man roared with all his might, his face twisted as if he was extremely angry at his own existence.
Chen Yi looked calmly at the man before him without speaking. This man must be the bug in the map. He had also just learned that the map would be rebooted when the players left.
From this perspective, his prolonged stay in the map no longer seemed meaningful.
With every reboot, this man’s memory was not erased.
He could understand this feeling.
Any normal person living in such a world would collapse and start questioning the reality of their world.
He could have simply ordered the execution of these few hundred people, including the bearded one before him.
But after a moment of silence, he suddenly took another step forward, speaking softly.
“Perhaps the truth is indeed as you believe.”
“But does that matter?”
“I still have a day before I leave. Maybe you can at least enjoy one day of peace, can’t you?”
“Put down your weapons.”
“I don’t want to escalate the killing any further; enjoy this last day of peace.”
“I…”
The bearded man, whose face was originally fierce, halted in place when he heard what Chen Yi had to say, and after a moment, he fell to his knees in front of Chen Yi, his voice trembling with a sob.
“Teacher… I want to leave this world.”
“Can you take me with you?”
“I can accept death, but I want to live in the real world, not in this fake one that could be rebooted at any moment. Even in death, I want to experience real death.”
“I don’t want to be an NPC; I want to be like you players… can I?”
“…”
Chen Yi calmly raised his hand and gently stroked the bearded man’s head, then after a moment spoke, “I don’t have that power, but perhaps in the future, you might have that direction.”
“Your planet is different from others.”
“You are more real.”
“Now get up, at least enjoy a day of peace, right?”
The bearded man gave a bitter laugh, took out a pistol from his bosom, opened the trigger, and pressed it against his temple in despair.
“You don’t understand me at all.”
“I’m not afraid of death.”
“I just don’t want to live in this fake world anymore. Why do you think I’ve been stubbornly resisting?”
“Is it because I’m naturally brutal?”
“No, it’s because I know that after enjoying this day of peace, every day after the world restarts, I’ll be in agony. They will all lose their memories, but not I; only I will remember everything.”
“If I am offered a day of light only to fall eternally into darkness, I’d rather not see that day of light.”
“When the ending of a story is tragic, there’s no point in starting the story at all.”
“Death?”
“I’ve been wanting to die. If it wasn’t for confessing to Liu Yue down the street 98 times without success, hoping to try for the 99th time, I would’ve died long ago. Now it seems that after 98 failures, there’s no need to try for the 99th.”
As his voice faded away.
“Bang.”
The bearded man forcefully pulled the trigger.
His gaze rapidly fading as he fell into a pool of blood.
Following the suicide of the bearded man, his subordinates lost their pillar and one by one laid down their weapons and knelt in surrender.
As Wang Zhongyi and the others surged forward.
It signified that the last resistance force on Rogue Star had been conquered, and the entire world was completely restored to peace.
The crowd was noisy.
Countless Centaurs shuttled back and forth around Chen Yi.
Standing in the midst of the noisy crowd, Chen Yi silently gazed at the body of the bearded man on the ground, his expression calm and speechless.
NPCs no longer wanting to be NPCs.
But who knew that they, too, no longer wanted to be players.

chapters.title: Chapter 361: 308: The Gleaming Star Level Title 'Peace Envoy'! (Extra 10,000 Character Mega Chapter)_3
chapters.content:
Chapter 361: Chapter 308: The Gleaming Star Level Title ‘Peace Envoy’! (Extra 10,000 Character Mega Chapter)_3
Whether players or NPCs, or even the project team, they’re all just pieces in this game.
Who can truly control their fate?
It’s just… the time hasn’t come yet, and until then, one must endure in silence.
One can’t even express the slightest dissatisfaction with the game.
But what he had just said to the bearded man wasn’t a lie.
The NPCs in this world did indeed seem unlike NPCs, each with their own way of thinking, nothing like the NPCs he had encountered in previous maps, not like those that were created.
...
It was more like… a whole planet had been transformed alive into a map.
And the original inhabitants of this planet were remodelled into players.
Suddenly, a roaring shout from the surroundings interrupted his contemplation.
“World peace!!!”
A bare-chested man, holding his firearm aloft, bellowed excitedly.
Following that voice,
others around him also started shouting with thrilled emotions.
Seeing this,
Chen Yi chuckled lightly, chose not to speak, and slipped away from the crowd unnoticed, planning to leave this map tomorrow.
His original power “Utopia,” after completely unifying the globe, had now ascended to SSS-level status.
It was also the only SSS-level power on Rogue Star.
It had far surpassed the D-level power of the main mission, and not by just a little bit.
Rest for tonight, and leave tomorrow.
…
The night grew deeper.
Outside the building, however, the lights shone bright, and the noise of the people was incessant; with the recent unification into peace, everyone was too excited to sleep, taking to the streets to experience everything they had never felt before.
Upon seeing that people around them truly weren’t attacking each other anymore, they couldn’t help but scream in excitement.
Every person was cautiously yet vigilantly enjoying this rare peace.
“Mr. Chen Yi.”
Qin Le pushed open the door to Chen Yi’s room, looked at the silhouette by the floor-to-ceiling window holding a half glass of red wine, and spoke tentatively, “May I come in?”
Chen Yi didn’t turn around but swirled the red wine in his glass, looking at the reflection in the glass of what was behind him, and said casually with a smile, “Your half-foot is already in the room, isn’t asking that question superfluous?”
He was in a good mood at the moment, willing to indulge in a few jokes.
“Heh.”
Qin Le stuck out her tongue and, with her hands behind her back, shuffled her feet to stand behind Chen Yi. After hesitating for a moment, she asked tentatively, “Mr. Chen Yi, was what that man said before he committed suicide true?”
“Will you really leave tomorrow? Will the world really reset once you’re gone?”
“…”
Chen Yi’s expression suddenly became tranquil, the smile gradually fading from his face. After a moment, he slowly sipped the red wine and said softly, “Perhaps it will.”
He felt somewhat powerless.
He had exerted much effort, nearly sleepless for a month, to bring this world back to peace.
To him, it was a fulfilling accomplishment and the feeling of helping others felt good; seeing children running unrestrained in the streets filled him with contentment, but all his success would be forcibly reset after his departure.
This inevitably brought on a sense of powerlessness.
In the face of the game’s upgrades, the significance of one’s efforts seemed as laughable as a stand-up comedian stuttering through a marriage proposal.
“…”
Qin Le, with her hands still behind her back, did not ask about the old world or Judgment Day, instead standing behind Chen Yi and, after some time, said with a firm yet shy voice, “If we won’t meet again after today, and the world will reset tomorrow, wiping my memory,”
“I want you to know something.”
“I like you.”
“If you’re willing, I can serve you tonight; I am clean, and you don’t have to worry about any responsibilities.”
“I have a girlfriend.”
Chen Yi shook his head and said in a low voice, “And she’s probably watching us right now, and even if she’s not, I still wouldn’t agree to it. I might not be a very faithful person, but I owe her a lot.”
“I can’t offer her the peace that other girls enjoy.”
“But at least, I don’t want to disappoint her.”
“…”
Qin Le looked downcast, her courage melting away as she lowered her head and said softly, “In your world?”
“Mhm.”
“An existence like you?”
“Mhm.”
“What’s her name?”
“Jiaye.”
“It’s a nice name, is she pretty?”
“Very pretty, with a good personality, very sensible, except sometimes too much so; actually, there are times when I wish she didn’t have to be that sensible,” replied Chen Yi.
“Oh.”
Qin Le, looking down, fell silent and didn’t speak again. After a long while, she glanced at the slow-moving clock on the wall, then firmly yet timidly said, looking at Chen Yi’s back,
“If we won’t meet again after today and the world will reset tomorrow, erasing my memory,”
“I want you to know one thing.”
“I like you.”
“If you’re willing, I can serve you tonight; my body is clean, and you don’t have to worry about taking any responsibility.”

chapters.title: Chapter 362: 308: Gleaming Star Level Title 'Peace Envoy'! (Extra 10,000-word mega )_4
chapters.content:
Chapter 362: Chapter 308: Gleaming Star Level Title ‘Peace Envoy’! (Extra 10,000-word mega chapter)_4
“By the way,”
Chen Yi suddenly thought of something. Without turning around, he lit a cigarette and placed it to his lips, standing beside the floor-to-ceiling window while overlooking the city, he casually spoke, “I always wanted to ask you, why does a girl have a somewhat masculine name like Qin Le?”
Qin Le’s voice was a bit low, she bowed her head and whispered, “When my mother was pregnant, my father had already picked out the name. If it was a boy, he would be named Qin Le, and if it was a girl, she would also be named Qin Le. When I was born and they found out I was a girl, they still named me Qin Le.”
“Are you talking about ‘le’ and ‘yue’?”
“Yes, if it’s a boy it’s Qin Le with the ‘le’ pronunciation, and if it’s a girl it’s Qin Le with the ‘yue’ pronunciation.”
“Your father is quite good at naming.”
...
“He thinks so too.”
…
A day passed quickly.
It was still the same room.
There was only one minute left until the return.
Chen Yi glanced at the countdown timer for the return, leaned on his cane with one hand, standing by the window he turned and looked back. Smiling at Qin Le, he said, “If fate allows, we’ll meet again. Oh, don’t forget to return this cane to Wang Zhongyi.”
“It was taken down from the wall of his office.”
“No need for that.”
Qin Le, head bowed and speaking softly, said, “After all, the world will restart soon, and everything will go back to the way it was. This cane will return on its own. It’s just a pity for the people below.”
“Everyone is discussing reconstructing the schools and the Law Enforcement Bureau.”
“Now it seems all these are unnecessary.”
“Soon, everyone’s memories will be reset.”
Chen Yi, with a calm expression, fell silent for a moment before taking out a paper airplane from his chest and handing it to Qin Le, “At least you have the successful experience, at least you know that everyone at heart longs for peace.”
“If someone else stands up, the same can be achieved.”
“If there’s no one, I believe you can do it.”
“This paper airplane is from a child who gave it to me as a thank you after peace in Ao City, maybe you’ll like it.”
“Farewell.”
The next second—
A barrage of notifications suddenly rang beside Chen Yi’s ear.
‘Ding, congratulations on successfully completing the main quest of the S-level map ‘Rogue Star’: Main Quest: Become the leader of a D-level Dark Force within one month.’
‘You have exceeded the task by becoming the leader of an SSS-level Dark Force within one month.’
‘You have received the following extra rewards—’
‘Random S-level Prop Chest *1, Gleaming Star Level Title *1, Points *5,000,000, Galaxy Megaphone *3, A-level Prop Power of Faith *1, Starry Level Title *2.’
‘Ding, because you achieved peace in a world filled with sin and exceeded the main quest of the map, you have been awarded the Gleaming Star Level Title ‘Peace Envoy’!’
‘Ding, you’ve managed to pass an S-level map without killing a single NPC, thus you have been awarded the Starry Level Title ‘Inherently kind, never killing’!’
‘Ding, you’ve managed to pass an S-level map without suffering any injuries, thus you have been awarded the Starry Level Title ‘Undamaged Pass’!’
‘Ding, you have not completed the side quest ‘Kill 4444 natives’ on this map, losing the reward—Points *1,000,000, A-level Prop Collector *1.’
‘Ding, you have completed the ultimate hidden task of the ‘Rogue Star’ map—World Peace.’
‘Below is your map evaluation and rewards for completing this ultimate hidden task.’
‘Map Evaluation’: This is a cursed planet, just like the name of its star, Rogue Star. Under the curse shrouded in mystery, everyone is killing, devoid of trust, living in fear of each other, extremely chaotic.
At such a time, you stood up.
You didn’t accomplish your main quest through normal means, but used a method that normal people couldn’t even think of, let alone have no desire to try—or for many, no ability to. You exceedingly completed your main quest.
Your courage and strategy were sufficiently tested in this map.
What’s even more admirable is your sharp insight, as if you could easily penetrate to the softest part of a person’s heart and see their true thoughts. With your strong emotional influence, you inspired them to follow you.
As you said.
Belief is not made up, but needed.
You saw their need for faith.
You gave them faith.
You used a great lie to make many people face their inner selves, to free many from the curse, and to return the entire world to peace.
You were the 99th player to enter this map.
The ultimate hidden task of this map has always been just one, that is, under the player’s leadership, to restore the world to peace.
Before you.
Only 12 people completed the main quest, 27 completed the side quest, and you are the only one who has exceeded the main quest and completed the ultimate hidden task.
Therefore, you are rewarded—
Starry Level Title ‘Plot Explorer’ *1.
Gleaming Star Level Title ‘Mist Walker’ *1.
According to the rules, if 100 players enter this map and the ultimate hidden task is still not completed, the map will be permanently sealed and players will be forbidden from entering. This world will not be rebooted again, and all the people on this planet will continue to live under the curse.
Or when the player completes the ultimate hidden task, the map will also be permanently sealed, forbidding entry.
But the curse will be lifted.

chapters.title: Chapter 363: 308: The Gleaming Star Level Title 'Peace Envoy'! (Extra 10,000 Character Mega Chapter)_5
chapters.content:
Chapter 363: Chapter 308: The Gleaming Star Level Title ‘Peace Envoy’! (Extra 10,000 Character Mega Chapter)_5
“`
This world will not be reset; it will keep on spinning on its own, whether it’s to peaceful or chaotic times, no one can interfere; it’s the natural law of the world’s operation.
–
Chen Yi stood in a room enclosed by white walls, gazing at his map evaluation and the rewards for completing the ultimate hidden mission, he paused for a moment, then suddenly let out a light laugh.
It seemed his efforts had not been in vain.
He wondered whether they would remember him, the man who had led them to peace.
...
He wondered what direction they would take from here.
If he had the chance, he would like to return and see for himself, but perhaps there would no longer be such an opportunity.
And just at that moment—
He noticed that his award announcement was being streamed in the chatroom, where comments flooded the screen, making it impossible to read them all, and before he could take a closer look at what the players thought of him.
Suddenly, multiple notification tones chimed in his ear.
“Ding, congratulations to player Chen Yi for a perfect debut of his S-tier map. In this map…”
“…”
…
After Chen Yi vanished from the spot,
Qin Le closed her eyes tightly, gripping her carefully selected dress for the day, and tears began to roll down her cheeks, ruining the makeup she had applied that morning.
She never used to wear makeup before.
As a successor to the Dark Forces, she was not allowed to show any feminine demeanor.
For today’s farewell.
She had dressed herself with special care, but Chen Yi seemed not to have noticed at all, and before she could even remember to say a few more words to Teacher Chen Yi, he was gone.
The thought that she would never see Chen Yi again in her life.
Made her feel an emptiness inside, a heart-wrenching anxiety.
But perhaps this feeling would soon disappear anyway.
According to Chen Yi, their world would soon be reset, and they would lose their memories.
And just then—
“Bang, bang, bang!”
Urgent knocks sounded at the door.
Wang Zhongyi, excited, pushed open the door, poking his head in as he looked towards Qin Le’s back with an excited and rapid voice: “Miss Qin le, where is Teacher Chen Yi? Everyone’s discussing giving a unified name to schools all around the world.”
“There are two names tied for first place right now.”
“One is ‘Yi En School’, and the other is ‘Yi Bi School’.”
“What do you think, Miss Qin Le? Or should we ask Teacher Chen Yi’s opinion?”
“Is Teacher Chen Yi not here?”
Wang Zhongyi peeked into the office, looking around in confusion: “Isn’t Teacher Chen Yi usually here?”
“By the way, Miss Qin Le, why do you seem so much prettier today?”
This abrupt comment brought Qin Le back to reality.
Qin Le paused for a moment, then turned around in disbelief and with a trembling voice asked the figure at the office door, Wang Zhongyi: “You still have your memory?”
“I still have my memory too?”
“What memory retention?”
Wang Zhongyi, confused, scratched his head: “Miss Qin Le, what you’re saying sounds as strange as that suicidal bearded man the other day. I didn’t quite catch it, shall we first decide on the name for this school?”
Qin Le didn’t speak but rushed to the floor-to-ceiling window, looking down at the children who were still playing and fighting just like yesterday. She couldn’t help but cover her mouth with her hands and burst into tears with happiness.
The world had not been reset.
Everyone’s memories had not been erased.
The children were still running around.
Teacher Chen Yi, you did it, you stopped this world from constantly resetting, you turned this world into a real one.
Only…
After a long while,
She steadied her mind and took a deep breath before speaking: “Teacher Chen Yi has already left, he’s gone to save other worlds, he said his goal is to bring peace to all worlds.”
“But before leaving, I asked him about the name for the school.”
“He said to call it ‘Ai Yi School’.”
“Ai Yi School?”
Wang Zhongyi, somewhat baffled, scratched his head, unsure of what to say; the name didn’t quite seem like Teacher Chen Yi’s style. But since it was relayed by Miss Qin Le, it must be correct.
Only—
He licked the corner of his mouth somewhat dejectedly: “So Teacher Chen Yi has left? I didn’t get the chance to properly thank him.”
“I really like the world now, every day feels so meaningful.”
Seeing that Wang Zhongyi had no major questions about the name, Qin Le felt a sigh of relief in her heart, wiped the sweat from her palm on the hem of her clothes, and hesitated before asking.
“You said I look prettier today than before?”
“Yeah.”
Wang Zhongyi nodded seriously: “Today’s makeup really suits you, and the dress is quite pretty, it makes you look so much better than before.”
Qin Le felt a small surge of joy and pursed her lips, but it was a pity Teacher Chen Yi hadn’t seen her like this before he left. Just as she turned back to Wang Zhongyi, intending to return the compliment, she suddenly paused and asked in bewilderment.
“The scar on your face, how come it’s gone?”
“Oh, it faded.”
“That can fade?”
“Of course, it’s not that hard.”
“Then why didn’t you remove it before?”
“How could I dare to remove it before? Walking around the streets with a clean face would’ve just gotten me chopped, wouldn’t it? I gave myself that scar with a knife, and it hurt like hell.”
“`

chapters.title: Chapter 364: 308: Gleaming Star Level Title 'Peace Envoy'! (Extra 10,000-word mega )_6
chapters.content:
Chapter 364: Chapter 308: Gleaming Star Level Title ‘Peace Envoy’! (Extra 10,000-word mega chapter)_6
Thinking back on the past, Wang Zhongyi spoke with a sigh, “When I first started out, to make myself look tough, I cut many wounds into my flesh and didn’t even dare to wash my hair before going out, so I’d look all ragged and not someone to be messed with.”
“Now that the world is at peace, there’s no need for that anymore. Cleaning up a bit might even help me find my true love sooner, right?”
“I’ve long wished for a genuine and sweet romance. That’s practically my dream.”
Qin Le couldn’t help but laugh, “Alright, you’re the smart one. Off you go.”
“Got it.”
…
...
“I… I’m not dead?”
As the sun set half behind the mountains, a man with a goatee crawled out from a grave outside the city. At first, he glanced around bewilderedly, then gave a wry smile; in this damned world, even wishing for death was futile.
Perhaps that player named Chen Yi had already left?
The world had restarted.
All of the players’ memories had been altered.
Only he remembered everything.
But no matter to whom he told all this, no one would believe him, they’d think he was crazy. He had already told people about them being NPCs, but no one believed him.
Just then—
A shout suddenly came from nearby.
“There’s a living person over there.”
“Damn it!”
The man with the goatee’s face turned pale, and he quickly grabbed a somewhat sharp branch from the ground, holding it tightly as he stared intently at the nearly blurred figure in the darkness!
In the restarted world.
He was alone in the wilderness; being caught by someone usually had only one outcome.
Which was having his organs harvested and his body casually discarded in some corner.
He understood this all too well.
Soon, the person approached.
Just as he was about to strike first, he suddenly noticed that the weapons in these people’s hands were not aimed at him, but rather, they were looking at him with curiosity.
“Brother, what are you doing here?”
“You seem to have no weapons on you. It’s very dangerous to explore the wilderness unarmed.”
“Here.”
The leader of the group took out a pistol from within his coat and handed it to him: “There are a lot of monsters out there, take this for self-defense, and then hurry back to the city. It’s not wise to explore such dangerous areas alone.”
“…”
The man with the goatee stood frozen, taking the pistol from the leader, checking that the firing pin had not been removed, and that it was loaded with full ammunition without any issues. He then looked up, puzzled, at the people in front of him.
“You are…”
Had these people lost their minds?
Giving him a weapon voluntarily?
Were they not afraid he’d use it to kill them?
“We’re from the ‘Utopia’ stationed in Zheng City, Exploration Team Four. I’m the captain, Zeng Hao. Alright, we can chat more another time, hurry and head back to the city center for now. This place is dangerous.”
“We still have a mission to complete, so we can’t stay longer. Stay safe on your way.”
“Wait!”
An incredible possibility dawned in the eyes of the man with the goatee: “What’s the date today?”
“June 27th!”
June 27th!
The man’s expression changed drastically—seven days had passed since the player Chen Yi left, which meant the world hadn’t restarted?
The SSS-Level force ‘Utopia’ was the one that man had created!
Everyone’s memories hadn’t been blocked.
As the passersby left, the man with the goatee’s expression kept changing. After a long while, when the sun had set, he finally got up from the ground, his body feeling weak as he walked towards the city.
He was very familiar with this area.
He used to lead his men here to scavenge for resources often.
As soon as he entered the city,
He could feel the earth-shattering changes. Everyone on the streets wasn’t wary anymore, people were chatting joyfully amongst themselves, some even shooting the breeze in the middle of the road, and what’s more, nobody seemed to be carrying weapons.
This was a scene I could hardly believe before.
Walking the streets without a weapon was no different from suicide.
On the sidewalks, children were still playing and causing a ruckus.
The entire city was filled with an air of peace.
The bearded man went from disbelief at the beginning to not being able to control the smile spreading across his face and finally bursting out into uncontrollable laughter!
This commotion caught the attention of many people.
But no one sneered.
Instead, they all understood perfectly well and raised their right arms, joining in with loud laughter.
Clearly, everyone understood this emotion.
“Hahaha!!!”
“Alright!”
“Alright!”
Unable to hold back tears, the bearded man knelt down at the side of the street, raising his hands with red-rimmed eyes, excitedly roaring that the world hadn’t been restarted, that it was truly at peace, and everyone’s memories had not been altered.
He was no longer the outsider!
Everything was back to normal.
That player, Chen Yi, he really did it, he changed the world!
He made this originally illusory world into a real one!
Just then—
“Kuang Biao.”
A crisp female voice suddenly rang in his ear.
The bearded man was stunned for a moment. When he saw who was approaching, a hint of excitement flickered in his eyes, and he quickly stood up from the ground, dusted off his clothes, and then scratched the back of his head with a sheepish grin.
“Why are you here?”
Kuang Biao was his name.
Not many people knew his name; the woman before him was one of them.
The woman in front of him was named Liu Yue.
She was the woman he loved.
The world had been restarted 98 times, and he had confessed his love to Liu Yue 98 times, only to be rejected every time. He always thought he understood Liu Yue better each time and that he would surely succeed, but somehow, he was always rejected.
If it weren’t for Liu Yue, whom he couldn’t give up on, he would have long since killed himself to escape this endlessly restarting world.
Feeling awake while everyone else was drunk didn’t give him any sense of superiority, but rather immense pain, as no one could understand him—not even the woman he loved the most, who kept rejecting him.
“…”
The woman in short sleeves and shorts looked very ordinary. She bit her lip, hesitated for a moment before speaking, “Let’s put aside how you came back to life. Last time you said the world had been restarted 98 times, and you confessed to me 98 times.”
“Do you really like me that much?”
“I don’t think I’m anything special.”
“…”
The bearded man’s smile suddenly faded, and he fell silent, not speaking for a while before finally nodding, “Yeah, I’ve always liked you, even though I don’t know why you always reject me. But don’t worry, I won’t force you.”
“Do you know why I always reject you?”
“You don’t like me.”
“That’s not it.”
The woman in short sleeves tilted her head to look at the bearded man covered in mud and a bit disheveled, then suddenly smiled like a crescent moon, “It’s not that you’re the only special one. I’m a bit special too. To put it simply—”
“if I reject your confession 100 times in a row, I’ll get a very generous reward.”
Kuang Biao was startled, a hint of disappointment flashing in his eyes, “I understand what you mean. You want me to confess to you two more times so you can get that generous reward?”
“No.”
The woman sighed lightly, somewhat helplessly pulling the bearded man into a hug, “I’ve decided to give up that reward. Hurry and confess to me for the 99th time. I’m going to accept you.”
“Damn it, I was thrown into this map because of being lovesick, and now I’m lovesick again.”
“I just can’t resist.”
“Deserves me right to fall for a man in this lifetime.”
…
ps: Late night extra update of 10,000 words.

chapters.title: Chapter 365: 310: One begets Two, Two begets Three, Three begets All Things. (6k Mega Chapter)
chapters.content:
Chapter 365: Chapter 310: One begets Two, Two begets Three, Three begets All Things. (6k Mega Chapter)
The bearded man was taken aback for a moment, then, with an excited expression, he started to fumble through the pockets on his body, pulling out a bloodstained ring box from his trouser pocket and kneeling down on one knee to present the ring box to the woman, his voice trembling slightly as he spoke.
“Liu Yue.”
“I’ve been looking forward to this day for a long time, I never thought you would agree to me, this is my 99th confession to you, I…”
“Alright, alright.”
The woman pretended to be dissatisfied as she took the ring box from the man and took out a glittering diamond ring to put on her own ring finger, lifting the hand with the diamond ring up against the night sky, her expression dreamy as she admired it and murmured.
“I’ve accepted your confession, if you keep going, I might regret it.”
...
“Damn it, why am I having a lovesick moment again.”
Then, the woman looked towards the man who was still kneeling on the ground with a somewhat silly look and laughed, taking his arm and rising to her feet, walking into the night together, “Alright, stop standing there dumbfounded; we should head home.”
“Oh…”
The man was still a bit slow to react, scratching the back of his head in a simple-minded manner, the warmth from the woman’s body making him puff out his chest with pride like a victorious general.
“By the way, did you just say that you would get a generous reward after rejecting a confession 100 times? How did you know I was going to confess to you 100 times?”
“I didn’t know.”
The woman puckered her lips and spoke somewhat indifferently, “I am the ‘player’ you mentioned. Due to some mistakes, I was punished to be in this map, and I have to reject 100 confessions before I can return to my own world.”
“I was thinking that I was almost done with the task, just 2 more rejections and I would have succeeded, but then you suddenly committed suicide.”
“Although I didn’t know you would confess to me 100 times, since the system issued me this task, it would definitely make someone confess to me 100 times. After all, it can’t not give people the chance to complete the task, right?”
The man was startled for a moment, looking towards the woman beside him with some shock, “You’re a player?”
“Yeah, why look so shockingly surprised?”
“I…”
The man’s face turned a bit unsightly as he suddenly stood still without speaking. After a moment, he turned to look at the woman beside him and hoarsely said, “Does that mean that my liking for you is not a true feeling, but rather something the so-called system forcibly made me feel?”
“Just like how it forcibly fills this world with slaughter?”
“My feelings for you aren’t real? But are something your ‘system’ forced into me?”
The woman shrugged, “At first, I thought so too. Even though you were showing deep affection, I didn’t take it seriously. I always thought it was the system making you like me, and you didn’t truly like me, which is why I rejected you so straightforwardly at the beginning.”
“But… during these last several dozen times, I gradually felt your sincerity.”
“You don’t seem like an npc.”
“You have your own flesh and blood, you have your own thoughts, you even have your own little quirks.”
“You are just like a living person.”
“When I began to assume your feelings for me were genuine, many previously confusing points suddenly became clear. Do you think your feelings for me are controlled by your own mind or forcibly inserted by the system?”
“I…”
The man’s face turned unsightly again, slowly opening and closing his mouth without speaking. After a pause, he spoke seriously, word by word, “I can assure you, my feelings for you come from my own mind.”
“The first time I met you, I saw you feeding stray cats.”
“That was in a dimly lit alley.”
“You didn’t notice me.”
“In this world full of slaughter, a woman willing to feed stray cats, it’s hard not to make my heart flutter.”
“I am certain, that is my mind.”
“Well then, that settles it.”
The woman seemed to not want to dwell on the topic, wrapping the man’s arm as they walked towards the distance, their shadows stretching out under the street lamps as their voices gradually grew fainter.
“Didn’t you just say that if the mission failed, you wouldn’t be able to return to your original world?”
“Yes.”
“Ah? So what will you do now?”
“What else can I do, just not go back. Actually, the outside world isn’t as good as this one. I don’t have any relatives or friends, there’s no point in going back; it’s better to stay here.”
“But…”
“No need for ‘buts.’ Weren’t you curious about the player’s matters? We’ll have plenty of time in the future; I’ll tell you slowly.”
“I…”
“What ‘I’? Where’s the courage you had when you committed suicide?”
“Oh…”
…
At this moment, Chen Yi stood in a white space, not having had the chance to fully view the announcement of his harvest from this map when the prompt sound rang in his ears again.
He only glanced at it roughly.
The harvest seemed plentiful.
Among the titles he saw several, including one S-rank random Prop Chest, which was purely an unexpected reward. The rewards from this S-rank map were much more generous than he had imagined.
“Ding, congratulations to player Chen Yi for a perfect debut in the S-rank map, where player Chen Yi achieved a perfect clearance in an inconceivable manner. This represents the first debut map to the outside world from Annihilation Starfield.”
“Congratulations on delivering a satisfactory answer to all the viewers.”
“As a reward for successfully completing the debut map.”

chapters.title: Chapter 366: 310: One Gives Birth to Two, Two Gives Birth to Three, Three Gives Birth to All Things. (6k Mega Chapter)_2
chapters.content:
Chapter 366: Chapter 310: One Gives Birth to Two, Two Gives Birth to Three, Three Gives Birth to All Things. (6k Mega Chapter)_2
“Next, we’ll enter the award ceremony interview segment,”
“You have ten minutes to prepare.”
“During this time, you can purchase various outfits and such.”
“…”
Chen Yi looked at the pop-up window that appeared in front of him with an odd expression on his face.
It was a limited-time shop pop-up.
...
There were quite a few purchase options available.
“Golden Tuxedo”: 100k Points.
“Black Nightwalker Gentleman”: 270k Points.
“Suit Man”: 160k Points.
“…”
“Full Body Cleanse”: 10k Points.
“Babylon Cigar”: 100k Points.
“…”
…
The limited-time shop sold many items, but they were all related to appearance, with nothing to enhance combat ability; they seemed to be specially prepared for the upcoming award ceremony segment.
To prevent players from appearing too shabby on camera.
Without much thought
he didn’t buy any outfits; instead, he activated his most frequently worn black suit from his backpack and then took out the wand transformed from the Snow Eagle Sniper Rifle, leaning on it as he spoke with some sentiment.
“Long time no see, old friends.”
A whole month.
When he saw these props that belonged to him, he felt somewhat estranged.
He had a title that could forcibly decline map invitations, but he couldn’t decline this map. This invitation did not come from players; it was a mandatory invitation from the game itself.
During his month in the map, he wasn’t too disheveled.
He bathed and clipped his nails when needed.
However, because he was livestreaming, he wore shorts while bathing to prevent any accidental exposure, and he tried to cover up as much as possible when using the bathroom. If that still got broadcasted…
If he ever got the chance to find the project team that broadcasted this map.
Heads would roll.
Although making the whole world peaceful felt great, it took a whole month of his time, which was quite exhausting. He preferred nuking the world to peace, which only took a few hours—clearly much more efficient.
And most importantly—
No need to talk so much.
In the month within this map, he felt like he had said all the words he had for a lifetime.
He had given countless speeches.
Many times, he felt it was a pity not to go into pyramid selling.
This map should have been for Tuberculosis Rabbit—given its talents, it would have thrived here.
Then he glanced at the countdown on the wall.
“00:09:01”
The award ceremony segment would likely start after this countdown ended.
At that moment—
The chat channel on his personal panel for “The 33 Club Chat Group” was flashing nonstop.
“Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi”: “Yi, you’re awesome. Change into something nice inside, and I’ll toast to you later. I never imagined someone could clear this map in such a way. I’m impressed.”
“I’m Really Fucking Awesome Starfield, Li Yi”: “I’m not awesome, you are, Yi. Not only is your individual power strong, but your strategizing isn’t far behind either. Nothing to say, you’ll be directly under the camera soon, and we’re all outside waiting for you. Everyone has come to support you.”
“…”
Chen Yi nodded thoughtfully, it looked like the segment would be on some planet?
It seemed everyone from the 33 Club group was already there waiting.
With about eight minutes left, and having nothing to prepare, he decided to use this time to carefully check his recent gains.
First was the S-rank Random Prop Chest.
Looking at the random prop chest, a glint of anticipation flashed in Chen Yi’s eyes. It was his first true S-rank prop.
In the past, he had indeed obtained an S-rank prop admission ticket, but that was just a ticket. Ten people would enter a map, and only one would get an S-rank map. He hadn’t had the chance to enter that map yet, so the ticket was still sitting in his backpack.
After annihilating the Five Clans in the Annihilation Starfield, he had gotten quite a few race bounties.
Among them were several S-rank props and a large amount of Points.
But annoyingly, because newbie players could not receive gifts from other players from outside in any way, he could only automatically obtain these S-rank props after leaving the Newbie Protection Period.
What nonsense.
Even race bounties could be considered player gifts—were they inheritance now?
And this S-rank prop chest in front of him was his first real S-rank item.
The next second—
A flash of white light.
A brand-new prop appeared in his backpack, and a prop panel popped up in front of him.
Chen Yi pursed his lips slightly in dissatisfaction—as an S-rank prop chest, was that all the special effects it had after being opened?
“Prop Name”: Longevity as the Southern Mountains (Gift from Goddess Qianna 1/2).
“Prop Rank”: S-rank.
“Prop Effects”: After obtaining this prop, any creature you kill will permanently increase your Life Value by 1 point, with no upper limit.
“Prop Restrictions”: The prop is equipped automatically upon acquisition, cannot be dropped, traded, transferred, gifted, or unequipped.
“Prop Description”: “If I were to offer a wish, I hope you’ll have longevity as the Southern Mountains, fortune as vast as the Eastern Sea.”
“ps1”: This prop is part of a set. Acquiring another S-rank prop ‘Fortune as Vast as the Eastern Sea’ will activate set effects.
“ps2”: This prop is unique within the entire Star System, and the other prop is the same. Once both props are obtained by players, a confrontation of fate will begin. The victor will possess the complete set of props.

chapters.title: Chapter 367: 310: One produces two, two produce three, three produce everything. (6k big )_3
chapters.content:
Chapter 367: Chapter 310: One produces two, two produce three, three produce everything. (6k big chapter)_3
‘ps3′: Another prop has not yet been obtained by players.
Just a simple five-character statement.
This was the simplest prop panel he had ever seen, and such a simple prop panel was an S-rank prop?
“Every time I kill a creature, my life value permanently increases by 1 point?”
Chen Yi looked at the simple prop effect before him, and his mind was filled with just two words, confusion!
What the heck?
...
Since when did players have life values in this game?
Oh, right, some bosses indeed do.
Like the Valentine’s Day limited boss he killed on Blue Star, as well as the final boss in the world boss events, these bosses all had life values.
But when did players start having life values?
This feature was not made apparent at all.
Where does this life value get added to?
And killing any creature? What’s the definition of a creature? Does an ant count?
If so.
He could just find a bunch of queen ants, wipe out 999 breeds in one go, and stack how much instantly?
And what exactly is the concept of 1 point of life value? He had no idea what that meant, as he had never encountered a tangible concept of life value before.
When in doubt, seek advice.
After realizing he was completely baffled, Chen Yi decided to open the ’33 Club Chat Group’ and start asking questions. Why did he send out a red packet of 5 million Points in the group last time?
Wasn’t it so that he could get answers to his questions when he was puzzled?
Knowledge is worth paying for.
He understood that.
It must be said, the people in the 33 Club seemed to be very free every day, more reliable than customer service. He had barely posted his question when answers started coming in.
‘Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi’: “A prop that adds to life value? Yi, you got such a prop in your rewards? Nice, that’s a generous reward indeed, any prop that increases life value starts at top-notch A-rank at least. I just don’t know how much life value Yi’s prop adds? 800 or 1000? The top-notch A-rank props usually add around that amount.”
‘I’m so damn awesome, Li Yi’: “We players don’t have the concept of a life value; it’s not made visible. A fatal wound would kill us, but if you obtain a prop that can increase your life value, your life value will be datafied. From then on, theoretically, even if your stomach is turned into mincemeat by a Gatling gun, as long as you have 1 point of blood left, you can still move around as if nothing was wrong until your health bar hits zero.”
“That’s also why any prop that adds to your health, no matter how little it adds, is rare.”
“Everyone in the group should have this prop, right? It’s a must-have for anyone who wants to become a top fighter.”
“Let me show you mine.”
Quickly—
A prop panel was shared in the group.
‘Prop Name’: Fat Cat.
‘Prop Rank’: S-rank.
‘Prop Effect’: Your life value will be increased by 2700 points.
‘Prop Restriction’: After wearing this prop, your body will gradually become fat until it is three times the normal weight of your race, and this process is irreversible.
‘Prop Description’: “Chubby, the cutest of them all.”
‘Prop Owner’: Li Yi.
“…”
Chen Yi looked at the prop panel before him, and his expression became increasingly strange.
2700 points of life value? S-rank prop?
If he wasn’t seeing things wrong, his S-rank prop ‘Longevity as the Southern Mountains’ was unlimited, right? Theoretically, if he had this prop before exterminating the Five Clans, he could now have tens of billions of life value?
If the kills under the ‘Calm and Cool’ rule were counted towards him.
Although he had no idea what 2700 points of life value represented, or how much damage it could withstand, as he had never seen a prop description stating how much life value would drop from an attack, nor did he know how much damage 2700 life value points could withstand.
But since it qualified as an S-rank prop, it surely couldn’t be weak.
The life value of players must be different from that of bosses, as the bosses’ life values are measured in millions; a few thousand life value points would be somewhat laughable.
It’s just…
This thing can’t stop percentage-based props, can it?
Isn’t his Snow Eagle Sniper Rifle a percentage damage weapon? If he encounters such a prop, even if he stacks his Life Value to tens of billions, won’t he still be killed by several dozen shots?
If there’s a problem, come to Club 33.
The diligent and studious Chen Yi immediately voiced his doubts in the Club 33 chat group without any hesitation.
“Qi Daddy Starfield, Wang Qi,” “It’s not like that, the Life Value of players and that of bosses aren’t the same, let me briefly explain to you. When you get a prop that can increase your Life Value…”
“It will determine a base of 100 Life Value according to your durability level.”
“This will be the average.”
“For instance, if you added 900 Life Value and now have a total of 1000 Life Value, the damage that could have exactly killed you before can now only kill one-tenth of you, making you nine times more durable than before.”
“You can think of it as every additional 100 Life Value is like an extra life.”
“And the percentage damage is also calculated within this 100 Life Value. For example, if a weapon deducts a guaranteed 5% Life Value every attack, then when this gun shoots you, it will only deduct 5% of that 100 Life Value, not 5% of the overall 1000 Life Value.”
“This means you don’t have to worry about being killed in a few shots by percentage weapons no matter how high your Life Value is. This is also why these kind of props are valued highly. Just monetizing the health bar is already quite valuable.”
“It’s also because of this that two players with the same 1000 Life Value bars might differ in durability due to belonging to different races. After all, some races are naturally more durable, the specific calculation is quite complex…”
Wang Qi explained for a full three minutes.
A series of complicated words.
The algorithm was also very complex.
But he still understood it, in layman’s terms, just one sentence.
An extra 100 Life Value is equivalent to an extra life.
Only then did Chen Yi look at the panel of the S-level prop “Longevity as the Southern Mountains” that he had just obtained, his face breaking into a satisfied grin.
As expected of an S-level prop, it didn’t disappoint him.
But… where to stack it?
So annoying. Recently there haven’t been any races that provoked him. There is the Feng Family, but there are too few of them to stack up.
He can’t provoke those of too high a level either.
He doesn’t have the power to slaughter the entire Starfield.
The best-case scenario would be for a populous Threefold Planet to provoke him somewhat, giving him a justified reason to go and stack revenge buffs. After all, one must have a reputation to uphold; slaughtering several races without any reason would ruin his reputation pretty much everywhere.
The most important thing is, he can’t bring himself to do it.
If only someone would insult him.
Just then—
His eyes suddenly narrowed, a glint sparkling within as he looked towards a comment in the live stream chat.
“Bing Seventy-One Starfield, Emperor Treasure Star, Fa’erma,” “Truly brain-dead, this way of clearing the game is laughable. Do you believe there was no insider help? Is everyone a fool? Only Chen Yi is smart? You blabber and deceive so many to risk their lives for you? I’m amazed you all keep singing praises, seriously not sure if you understand at all.”
Emperor Treasure Star…
That’s a good name.
But exterminating a race for just one person’s curses seems excessively brutal.
Suddenly, another comment flashed through the live stream.
“Bing Seventy-One Starfield, Emperor Treasure Star, Fa’erma,” “It’s so fake. I don’t know why that Chen Yi is so pretentious? Watching him makes my skin crawl, the tone of his voice is deliberately nauseating. Does he think his voice sounds charming?”
“Heh.”
Seeing this, Chen Yi’s face broke into a satisfied grin.
Exterminating a race for insults from just one person is indeed too brutal.
But with two people, it’s a different story.
As the old Blue Star saying goes, “One begets two, two beget three, three beget all things.” Essentially, if two people from a race are cursing him, then surely the rest of the race is as well.
The extermination wouldn’t be unjust.
Chen Yi surreptitiously noted the name of this race in his heart. If there was ever an opportunity in the future, he wouldn’t need to show mercy when killing the players from this race.
…
ps: This nearly 6000 words, with an additional nearly 2000 words.

chapters.title: Chapter 368: I hope everyone will have a better future.
chapters.content:
Chapter 368: I hope everyone will have a better future.
Some things need to be said.
I haven’t checked the comments section for a long time, and there have been quite a few insults directed at me. At first, I said that subscribers could insult me as they please. After all, making money and taking some criticism seems fair. To this day, everyone must have felt very satisfied with their criticisms since I haven’t silenced anyone or deleted any comments.
Certain sarcastic and mocking comments are indeed a bit hard to take.
First, I must apologize.
I had promised daily updates of 10k words, but I haven’t lived up to that, breaking my promise and letting everyone down with false hope. For that, I deserve to be criticized. I said before that everyone is free to criticize me because I didn’t want anyone to feel like they didn’t have the right to express their opinions after spending money.
But truthfully, those comments are very hard on the eyes, yet in order to protect everyone’s rights, I didn’t delete them.
...
It’s been almost ten days since I last read any reviews. Those harsh words really stung, and I didn’t dare to look. Since I have to protect your right to give negative reviews, then choosing not to read them would solve everything, right? It’s a win-win situation.
But… not reading the reviews makes it very hard to know the readers’ feedback.
I don’t know whether readers like the new plotline.
I don’t know if readers find this part of the story boring.
I don’t know what suggestions everyone might have for the subsequent plot.
When an author stops reading the comment section, the quality of their book visibly suffers. So, not knowing what you all think lately, I myself feel that the quality has declined.
It’s quite painful for me.
After a long reflection,
I’ve decided to reopen the comments section and pay more attention to the readers’ feedback, but please, I hope for fewer negative comments.
Secondly,
I truly am sorry.
I didn’t fulfill the promises I made earlier, and I’ve let you all down, I will try my best to make amends.
In reality, just like every “I love you” uttered by a man when he confesses is extremely sincere, my previous promises were also sincere. However, I really am running short on time, and often there are unexpected incidents.
Those who have been with me for a long time might know that I started writing novels after failing in business.
These past two years, I managed to earn a bit of money from writing novels.
So I returned to my original passion and ventured into business again.
I started several projects that have been running for over a year now.
The earnings have been quite good.
But because it’s a small company with only a few employees who are all in execution roles, all of the decision-making, strategizing, and trial and error are up to me.
Including the operations on Meituan, multiple Douyin accounts, Jili Engine, Guangdiantong, Xiaohongshu, delivery, planning, training, etc., even every plan and piece of material on Jili, every title, I’m the one taking the shots and writing them.
I work over 16 hours a day. There are lots of people in the comments section saying that I don’t work hard enough.
They’re wrong.
I work harder than ninety percent of the people in this world, working from the moment I open my eyes to the moment I shut them. Even in my sleep, I can’t tell if I’m at work or on vacation. This has been going on for almost a year now.
In this book, the female lead Jiaye talks about wanting to start a company called Proposal Planning.
Yes, proposal planning is one of the projects we are doing. Organizing a proposal is genuinely exhausting. From the venue, photography, warehouse, staff, planning, and so on, I’m the one doing it all by myself.
Often in forty-degree weather, I sit on the hot grass, coordinating the setup below while communicating with clients, and at the same time, writing. This has already become the norm for me.
But I still enjoy doing it.
Just like the heroine in the book says, I love romantic gestures.
I also love novels because I enjoy creating a world of my own.
The company is also involved in educational training, which is something I enjoy doing. I like the feeling of teaching people to fish.
Beyond that, all the other projects of the company are things I enjoy doing.
I’m very fortunate; everything I do is what I love, and all with a decent income.
Actually, I don’t even know what I’m talking about anymore.
I just want to simply talk about my recent situation in hopes that you will understand if Wang Xin fails to update one day, it’s definitely not because he’s playing games or slacking off, nor is it because he doesn’t want to write.
It might be because I’m dealing with a troublesome client and simply can’t get away.
It could be that there’s an emergency at the event site that suddenly requires my attention.
It’s even more likely that I’m facing complaints, reports, failure to pass an audit, or incomplete qualifications, which are urgent matters I need to handle myself and can’t get out of.
Perhaps my update volume isn’t sufficient.
But my attitude is correct.
I’m not trying to fool my readers, but actually dealing with unexpected emergencies.
Today, I’m feeling a bit emotional.
Otherwise, I wouldn’t talk about these things that you might not care about; I’m just a bit tired.
A lot of people are putting pressure on me.
A lot of people.
I have to show a smiling face to my staff at the company; I can’t be sulking all the time.
When facing clients, I have to maintain a good service attitude; a smile is mandatory.
At home, I need to smile for my girlfriend, place the slippers properly, wipe the toilet after using it, go back to the room to smoke.
In reader groups, I have to show a good face to the readers, taking any insults without complaint.
Even when meeting with friends, I must smile; how’s everything going lately? All is well.
I’m tired of smiling.
Looking into the mirror before bed, I sometimes don’t even know how to smile anymore.
Today I don’t want to smile.
I feel like crying a bit.
I’m just too tired, not from work, for I never find work tiring. It’s more a sense of weariness in my heart. I don’t want to be relied on by so many people. I’m just born in ’99, only 23 this year. By all means, I should be a young person enjoying my youth.
SEND GIFT
1

chapters.title: Chapter 369: Hope everyone will be better in the future._2
chapters.content:
Chapter 369: Hope everyone will be better in the future._2
Why does everyone look at me?
Every pair of eyes looking at you is pressure and responsibility.
I’ve written about it in my books.
Being the protagonist is exhausting, when you see so many people looking at you, waiting for you to speak, you feel a responsibility that is truly wearying to the heart.
The protagonist in the book must be successful.
But I’m not.
...
I’ve failed many times, and every time I announce a new project has failed, the disappointed look in my girlfriend’s eyes always twists my heart; I can’t clearly tell her why I failed, I can only force a smile and tell her it’s okay, this time I know what went wrong, next time it will definitely be better.
Once you choose to be the protagonist, you only have success.
Because when you fail.
You’ll see so many disappointed looks, and those who criticized you at the beginning can’t help but jump out excitedly and say, “See, I knew you couldn’t do it.”
I’ve seen this scene many times.
It always looks so glaring to me.
In fact, I once wrote a brief plot in the book where the protagonist tries to start a business but fails and ends up eating dog food, everything that happened in that story actually happened to me, and it was truly miserable at that time.
I didn’t continue that part of the story because it deviated a bit from the main plot.
Many of the things I wrote about in my books have actually happened, and they all happened to me.
It was all okay, and I endured it.
Today, when I opened the book reviews and saw so many negative comments, I really couldn’t hold it in anymore, suddenly feeling that all the emotions I had suppressed for so long just exploded.
It’s a bit shameful to say.
I indeed cried.
But it wasn’t the book reviews that made me cry, they were just the last straw, it’s just that everyone has their own way of venting their emotions, and I don’t, I never have the chance to curse at anyone.
On the rare occasion that I finally have time to play a game, I get cursed at for being noob.
I bought a very expensive butterfly knife in CSGO, worth thousands; I don’t actually like that knife.
The only reason I bought it was because when I lent that knife to a teammate, they wouldn’t curse at me for poor gameplay, allowing me, who has barely any time to spare, to happily enjoy the fun of the game for once.
No one offers me any comfort.
Maybe it’s because I set my personal bar too high, and everyone thinks I don’t need comfort.
In my parents’ eyes, I am a son who became independent early, completely without relying on them, a son who could make his own way; what need is there for comfort, when nothing is a problem?
In my girlfriend’s eyes, I am a capable boyfriend, a person who can do everything other than clean the house, someone who should be admired.
In the eyes of my readers, it’s just a couple of criticisms for infrequent updates, and you can’t handle that? With a heart of glass, how can you write novels?
But—
The weight upon me is truly too much, today I couldn’t hold it in and I broke down.
I have the habit of writing diaries; I used to write them on my public account, often venting through a diary entry when I felt bad. Lately, I haven’t written a diary entry in a long time, I’ve been really too busy.
Today I originally planned to write about those book reviews, but I couldn’t help myself and wrote it down like a diary entry; well, let’s treat it as a diary entry. It’s better to write something out to feel a bit more relieved.
I’ve been suppressed for too long.
Having written it out, I feel much better, and when I wake up today, it’ll be a new day, everything will return to normal.
It’s actually quite normal.
Everyone has moments when emotions suddenly collapse, because of some trivial matter in life, all the suppressed emotions suddenly erupt; I am no exception.
Let’s leave it at that for today.
I don’t know what I’ve written, nor do I want to look back through it again.
I just know that my mood is indeed not as oppressive, and that’s enough for me.
Going forward, I will read the reader feedback on plot quality in the book reviews every day and strive to write higher quality stories. As the saying goes, it’s hard to please everyone with a single book. If you really don’t like it, then it’s better to leave.
As for the updates.
This month I’m not making any promises, I’ve consecutively failed to deliver my daily updates of ten thousand words for two months and have indeed disappointed many readers.
To be honest.
I really dislike disappointing people, but I always seem to disappoint many.
This month I’ll focus on stable updates, any extras will be considered a bonus, I’ll start improving my reputation from this month, I can’t always carry the reputation of someone who breaks their promises.
I am truly sorry for the broken promises of the past two months.
Here again, I apologize sincerely.
And for those who have abandoned the book, there’s no need to inform me personally, we can part ways if fate decides.
Those who insult my family will be permanently banned.
Overly harsh sarcastic comments will be deleted and the commenter banned by my assistant to prevent me from seeing them.
Monthly tickets and such are not needed for now.
Give them to other books.
I saw a comment in the section below that said, with so many readers cursing out the author, it won’t be long before the author claims their mentality has collapsed from the abuse, cutting the story and citing depression or something.
That won’t happen.
I actually have a very strong mental resilience, I’ve been living independently away from family since I was 14, and in terms of mental fortitude, I’ve always been strong.
And indeed, it is my fault.
When you make a mistake, you admit it, stand tall and take the hit.
Mart’s rules, I won’t just collapse and abandon the book, I plan to seriously finish this book and see if there’s a chance to write something I truly want to write at Starting Point for my next book.
Today my mentality did collapse a bit, but the comment section was just the fuse.
And yet I see readers saying they don’t read the book anymore, they just keep it on their shelf to enjoy watching the author post excuses and get berated every day, as a source of amusement.
If you want to watch, then watch.
Being considered as a source of amusement by others is in fact a reflection of one’s own value in society.
But what moves me is that there are quite a few people in the reviews supporting me, in truth I could have held up, but seeing those supportive folks, I just broke down in front of them.
Thank you.
I hope I can create better plotlines this month and plan my time better to offer a satisfying response to most of the readers who have been following and supporting me.
Looks like from the backend subscriptions and various statistics continually rising, the majority supports me, but most of them are silent.
Lately, because some negative reviews affected the quality of the plot, I’ve disappointed that group of readers, which saddens me.
I could have written better.
Regardless of the reason, not delivering on promised updates is always a poor behavior.
I’ll work hard this month.
I hope my future will be better, and I sincerely hope everyone else’s future will be better too.
Good night, everyone.
…
PS: I’m not clear-headed due to being emotional, many readers probably won’t understand what I wrote, so I’ll summarize it.
Here is a summary of the main points:
1: Apologies for the past two months of broken promises.
2: Starting today, I will pay attention to readers’ feedback on plotlines in the reviews to strive for quality content.
3: Starting today, my assistant will ban comments that are too provocative or insult my family.
4: This month I will focus on stable updates to try and salvage a bit of my reputation.
5: My occasional delays in updating aren’t for teasing readers; it’s because there are really emergency situations in life that I must deal with right away.
6: My name is Wang Xin, and today I’m feeling down, I’ve cried for a long time.
7: I hope everyone has a better future.
