Chapter 383: Chapter 317: “You’re actually quite nice.” (9K words long chapter)_5
The next second—
The white portal slowly emerged again.
And the hook on the stand drilled up again, shooting towards the white portal like an anchor at the end of the rope.
“Ding, you have activated the Gold Miner occupational effect, your hook has started randomly selecting targets in the universe, please wait patiently.”
“Hook return countdown—00:04:59”
“This time, give me something good.”
...
Chen Yi muttered a prayer under his breath, then turned to the title he received when he got the “Faceless One” profession, “God!”
He really wished he had “Fortune as Vast as the Eastern Sea,” that S-level Prop.
If his Luck Value could be maxed out, then every time he activated the Gold Miner occupational effect, the hook would bring back an S-level Prop for him—how fucking awesome that would be!
It’s just too bad.
By the time he had a chance to get the “Fortune as Vast as the Eastern Sea” S-level Prop, who knows if he would still have the chance to randomly get the “Gold Miner” profession.
And what Chen Yi didn’t know was.
In the past few minutes, several incidents had occurred in different corners of the upgrading game because of him.
…
“Finally!”
A player wiped the sweat from his forehead, his legs trembling uncontrollably as he looked at the last small monster in front of him, struggling to lift his weapon.
This was an A-level endless map.
So exhausting.
He needed to kill all 9,999 monsters on this map to leave it.
Even though there was no boss, the sheer number of small monsters was enough to bury anyone.
After killing day and night, he had only taken down 9,998 monsters, and this one in front of him was the last.
As long as he killed this last monster, he could finally leave this map.
When he got back, he was definitely going to sleep well.
But at that moment—
A white portal suddenly appeared out of place in the middle of the map, and just as he thought he had triggered some accidental plot, a hook connected to the end of a rope shot out of the white portal, targeting the last small monster on the map.
He didn’t even have time to react.
The last monster was snatched away, grabbed… taken.
Standing in place with a dumbfounded expression for a long time, his face paled and his lips began to uncontrollably tremble.
Fuck your mother.
Fuck your grandmother.
Fuck your fucking mother!!!
I’ve been killing for a whole day and night without even blinking, and just as I was about to succeed, the last monster disappears? Where the hell is my monster? FUCK!!! Where is my monster?!!
If he didn’t kill all the monsters on this map, he couldn’t leave it.
But now the monster was gone.
How the fuck was he supposed to leave?!!
After ten minutes had passed, once he was certain that he really couldn’t leave, and that the small monster wasn’t coming back…
The player completely lost his composure, his expression savage as he looked up and roared with a heartrending scream.
“Customer service!!!”
“Ding, we have connected you to a human customer service agent. There are 2,392 players in queue ahead of you, with an estimated wait time of 37 hours. Please wait patiently.”
“Motherfucker￥…￥%…￥&&*…&!!”
…
“Whew!”
In a deserted desert, a middle-aged man with somewhat blurry vision struggled to move forward in the night, knowing that he had to quickly get past this desert, or he might never make it out!
He hadn’t had water for a day.
His mouth felt parched and his tongue felt dry, but thankfully the map showed that just half a day’s more travel would get him through this desert.
I mustn’t give up, keep going.
In the haze of his mind, he glanced at the tattoo on his arm.
never give up!
His stomach started making growling noises again; he hadn’t eaten anything for two days, and he felt weak, dizzy, and light-headed from hunger, but luckily he was about to leave the desert, and that would be his salvation.
He sat down cross-legged on a patch of sand, trembling.
He took out an Air Food Prop from his backpack, ready to put it into his mouth. This little thing had saved him over the past few days; although it couldn’t really fill his stomach, at least it gave him a sense of fullness, allowing him to hold on until now.
But the next second—
“Whoosh!”
A white portal suddenly appeared before him.
“Hm?”
The man paused, then a flash of joy crossed his eyes. Could it be that the hardships of the past few days had triggered a title reward or a special event?
But then,
he saw a hook tied to a rope shoot out from the white teleportation portal, aiming directly at the Air Food Prop in his hand.
Immediately after.
The man looked bewilderedly at his now empty hands and the slowly dissipating white teleportation portal before him.
After being befuddled for quite some time,
he couldn’t help but jump up and point at the sky, cursing loudly, “Are you fucking insane? You’re robbing me for an E-rank Air Food Prop?”
“Are you out of your mind?”
“That’s covered in my saliva, aren’t you fucking disgusted?!!!!”
Although he had no idea what had just happened, he could pretty clearly deduce that someone had stolen his Air Food Prop.
After cursing nonstop for a full five minutes,
he finally calmed down a bit.
Sitting cross-legged on the sandy ground, he took out another Air Food Prop from his bosom and murmured, “Luckily I’m known as Liu Sanshou; I never prepare just one hand. Thank goodness I have another Air Food Prop.”
“Even if I’m down to one, it’s still enough; after all, I’ll be out of the desert in half a day.”
Just as he was preparing to soothe his emotions and enjoy his dinner,
“Whoosh!”
That familiar white teleportation portal appeared once again.
The man’s face changed dramatically, and almost instantaneously, with lightning-fast reflexes, he stuffed the Air Food Prop back into his backpack and then heaved a slight sigh of relief. But before he could fully exhale,
he saw the hook slash through the void and head straight for his backpack panel.
It bypassed his precious A-rank Props, B-rank Props, and all other one-use consumables, aiming directly for the Air Food Prop.
Hooked.
Gone.
All of it flowed as smoothly as drifting clouds and flowing water.
“…”
As the white teleportation portal dissipated once again, the man stood expressionlessly in place, silently staring at his backpack panel, speechless. He truly hadn’t expected that thing could reach directly into his virtual backpack.
Impressive.
Truly impressive.
This was a dimensional strike, wasn’t it?
At least he was unaware of what level of Prop was needed to directly invade another player’s backpack.
You use such an impressive Prop, just to rob him of an E-rank Air Food Prop?
He looked at the untouched A-rank Props in his backpack and fell silent, uttering in a resentful tone after a while,
“You’re quite a decent person, aren’t you.”
“Quite principled as a thief, you steal exactly what you say you will, without grabbing anything extra, right?”
Meanwhile, he made a decision deep down.
It seemed that leveling up in this game was more complicated than he had thought; preparing two hands wasn’t enough—he should be prepared with three hands from now on, he would have to change his name to Liu Sanshou.
…
“Hiss!!!”
In the depths of the universe, on a piece of Starfield Continent, a gigantic insect-like creature was hissing in anger!
This massive insect looked to be at least 4 meters in length.
Its body was milk-white.
Its snow-white belly was covered with eggs, resembling the eggs of a river snail, only larger in size and brownish-yellow rather than red.
The densely clustered eggs looked somewhat unnerving.
If taken out individually, they would resemble inconspicuous stones by the roadside.
And at this moment—
In what should have been a neat array of eggs, there now were two conspicuous gaps, as if two of the eggs had been forcibly removed.
And this,
this was the reason for the massive tentacled insect’s angry hiss.
Her children had been taken.
She could sense that her offspring’s presence was now far away from her. War had to be waged—to take back her son and kill those lowlifes who dared covet her children!!!
…

I have some matters to attend to this afternoon, and I’m not sure if I can return by evening, so I’m uploading this early. If I’m back early tonight, there will be another update.
If I return late, there won’t be any more updates tonight, and this chapter will be tonight’s update.
No separate notice will be posted.
Mistakes will be edited post-upload.
Also, special thanks to the boss “Little Ran, Happy Every Day” for another generous tip of 1500 Starting Point coins. Thank you; your repeated support brings immense validation and boosts my morale.
Thanks again, and I hope the boss is happy every day.

chapters.content:
Chapter 384: Chapter 318: “Only Yi should be able to handle this kind of fate.” (10,000-word mega chapter)
“War!!!”
“War!!!”
This giant insect, with a belly full of eggs, taut and snow-white, lay prostrate in the cave loudly howling with a menacing face!!
The shrill sound pierced through the rock walls and dispersed in all directions!
The information contained within this piercing roar rapidly spread out as well.
Soon—
...
From a bird’s-eye view, on the ground below that resembled a beehive filled with holes, a massive throng of insects began to swarm like a tide toward the central largest cave.
And at a distance of ten meters away from that cave, they lay prostrate on the ground, respectfully waiting for their king’s latest command.
That was their king.
At a glance.
At least several hundred thousand insects had gathered, and more were still arriving from afar. It looked almost indistinguishable from Heavenly Water, so dense that it could have caused anyone with claustrophobia or entomophobia to instantly collapse.
Each insect was about one meter in size, with a thick semi-circular shell on its back and a slender mouthpart filled with sharp barbs, approximately thirty centimeters long, while its head was no larger than an adult’s fist.
Beside the head, there were two long tentacles.
Crawling forward while being prostrate, under the shell was their soft, snow-white belly, studded with legs, roughly a few dozen a few centimeters long. They looked somewhat fragile, but their speed was not slow.
Like a ladybug covered in legs or perhaps a stink bug.
Stink bugs were still okay; many people played with them as kids.
But a one-meter long stink bug—probably not something many would want to play with. Imagine waking up at night to find such a thing suddenly falling from the ceiling onto your face. Any normal person, even if they didn’t die, would likely be left with a deep psychological scar for the rest of their life.
And the number of these insects was still rising.
Clearly, a war was about to begin.
And the giant insect inside the cave angrily howled, sensing the Starfield where her children were, the Annihilation Starfield!
As the Matriarch of a Void Clan leading seventy to eighty tribes, she could feel the location of her unhatched children, no matter how far away. This wasn’t an ability of any Prop; it was her innate ability!
It was an ability possessed by every Beetle Clan tribal leader!
Then she used her mind to bring up the Starfield transmission panel, a virtual panel with no words. As soon as the panel opened, a series of shrill noises began ringing in her ears.
This was the essence of the game, using this race-specific method of communication to spread information.
No matter what language you use, the game will let you understand the panel—even without language, there’s always a way.
After seeing the Points cost required to transport all her troops there,
The Insect Emperor’s howl suddenly weakened.
She didn’t know what that number meant, but it seemed to be many digits more than the amount of Points she had.
But quickly!
The angry howl resounded in the cave once again!
Forget this damned Starfield transmission. As long as her children managed to hatch successfully there, they could use their race’s unique ability to create a Void Portal. At that time, the Void Clan wouldn’t need a single Point to reach that cursed Starfield, and they would kill the entire race of thieves who had stolen their children!
“Roar!!!”
With an angry howl, it echoed inside the cave!
A piercing sound, like a beam of light, raced towards the sky, boring directly into the two rocks at Chen Yi’s feet on Blue Star.
Her children wouldn’t hatch for another three days!
To possess the ability to construct a Void Portal after birth, they required sufficient nutrients. The giant insect was telling her unborn children through this method that if they absorbed nutrients quickly after hatching and grew, they must swiftly establish the Void Portal!
She, the Void Queen!
Would show those insolent wretches the ferocity of the Void Clan!
…
Chen Yi, who was still chatting with Jiaye on the beach, suddenly turned his head in mild surprise towards the two rocks that his Gold Miner had hooked back. Was it his imagination, or did the rocks just seem to wobble a bit?
But he quickly looked away and thought nothing of it.
After all, the wind was quite strong tonight.
Sitting on the beach, gazing at the fishing rod that would never catch fish, chatting with Jiaye, he started to look forward to whether his Gold Miner could hook something that would bring him a bit of surprise on the next attempt.
After all, it was a profession worthy of a Sixfold Planet player.
Time for some uniqueness.
He had cast the line six times already, always hauling up random junk—a situation he found himself in despite having no Occupational Restriction. How about those Sixfold Planet players who chose this job with Occupational Restrictions? It would take them six days to hook such random items.
Six days to fish for this stuff.
The most valuable had been two E-grade Air Food Props.
That would be enough to infuriate anyone into swearing, right?
Soon, five minutes passed, and a new notification sound came to his ears—
“Ding, congratulations, you have activated the Gold Miner Occupational Effect, and your hook has randomly retrieved an A-grade Prop for you from across the entire game, please enjoy.”
The next moment,
The hook, which looked like a ship anchor, retracted back through the white portal in front of him.
And tethered to the end of the rope was something about the size of a computer tower, apparently a Prop.

Chapter 385: Chapter 318: “Only Yi should be able to handle this kind of fate.” (10,000-word mega chapter)_2
“Prop Name”: Annihilator’s Display.
“Prop Grade”: A-level.
“Prop Effect”: This is a bomb that, once activated, will start a 10-minute countdown to detonation; its explosive power is enough to completely destroy a city capable of housing millions of people.
“Prop Restrictions”: Once activated, the prop will enter an irreversible phase.
“Prop Description”: “You can use it to create or destroy worlds, but only if you can escape the blast radius within 10 minutes. I hope you’re fast enough.”
“…”
...
Chen Yi was slightly startled before a hint of a smile flashed across his eyes, an A-level prop, not bad at all.
This is only the seventh hook, and he already netted an A-level prop?
Not bad.
Better than he expected.
Although it wasn’t of much use to him, he didn’t particularly lack A-level props with area attacks; having one was better than none, especially since it was an A-level consumable prop that could come in handy the next time a large-scale attack was needed.
Wait!
Suddenly, he noticed something was off.
Why did it seem like there were numbers flashing on what looked like the bomb’s display?
’00:00:7′
’00:00:6′
’00:00:5′
Immediately after—
An irritating sound suddenly started coming from the bomb that looked like a display, accompanied by a flashing, blinding red light.
“…”
Chen Yi’s face changed dramatically, fuck, had the bomb already been activated?
And fucking hell, there were only 4 seconds left on the countdown!
In 4 seconds, there was no time for him to get the prop out of Yancheng; even if he survived, all the players who had crawled up from hell would be dragged back down to hell again.
Even if his Christmas sleigh was fast, it couldn’t transport the bomb far enough away in 4 seconds!
No, now it was 3 seconds!
Chen Yi’s complexion turned a bit pale, and he glanced back at the group of people preparing hotpot. With 2 seconds left on the countdown, a brilliant idea suddenly flashed in his mind, and he quickly reactivated the Gold Miner’s Occupational Effect!
With the familiar white portal appearing!
Without any hesitation, he shoved the bomb with only 2 seconds left on the countdown straight into the white portal.
Soon—
10 seconds had passed.
There was no occurrence around them, as if the timed bomb that had just appeared was nothing but an illusion.
Seeing this, Chen Yi breathed a sigh of relief, wiped off the nonexistent sweat from his forehead, and thought to himself that indeed the white portal could be used as a trash can.
It was a good thing he handled it in time; otherwise, Yancheng might have suffered an inexplicable disaster once again.
But this Gold Miner occupation, why does it feel a bit unreliable, hooking all sorts of weird stuff back?
He finally hooks an A-level prop, but it turns out to be a bomb with a nearly finished countdown. If it had been hooked even a few seconds later, there would’ve been no time to react, and they all would have had to be buried with this thing.
However…
Chen Yi suddenly thought of something and hesitated without speaking. That white portal led to other parts of the Blue Star game; throwing the bomb in there couldn’t have hurt other people, could it?
The bomb was still very powerful.
If he had killed a whole city for no reason, he would have felt some guilt.
After a long pause with no kill notification sound coming, he finally exhaled in relief. It looked like no one was bombed, probably just luck that it landed in some uninhabited desert.
After such an incident.
He temporarily lost the mood to mine and instead sat on the beach chatting about everyday life with Jiaye, not bothering with the Gold Miner anymore.
Twenty minutes later.
Tuberculosis Rabbit came up to them, telling them everything was ready, and after the hotpot restaurant owner and the staff retreated, Chen Yi and his group enjoyed their first gathering in a month!
Everyone was happily raising their glasses in celebration.
They were celebrating Yi’s safe return.
They were celebrating not just Yi’s safe return, but his triumphant return!
“Cheers!”
“No rest tonight until we’re all drunk!”
In the night, the group around the hotpot table, holding their glasses, stood up to toast and laugh together—the whole scene was extremely harmonious, making one want to join in.
…
“How nice.”
Outside the neighborhood, the hotpot restaurant owner led his staff and looked up at the lights on the rooftop of the nearby building and Chen Yi’s faint sounds of laughter, couldn’t help but remark, “With players like Yi in Blue Star, it really makes people feel safe.”
“Yi has reached such a status, and yet he still likes to eat hotpot.”
“Someone once said that those who like to eat hotpot have no class, that no matter what ingredients are used, even abalones and lobsters taste the same in the hotpot—they’re all about the seasonings.”
“But even at Yi’s status, he still eats hotpot. What does that tell you? It’s the mark of a man who is high in status but not haughty.”
After the hotpot restaurant owner ruminated for a while, he turned and walked towards the distance under the streetlights, his silhouette stretching longer under the lights, followed by nearly a hundred employees stretching their limbs behind their boss.
They looked somewhat like the mob.
“Let’s go, everyone’s heading back.”
…
“You all are going to die today!!!”
“Hahaha, go ahead and accompany me in death!!!”
In some deep place in hell, a man with a bare upper body and covered in strange tattoos was crazily raising a bomb that looked very much like a display, laughing ferociously at the surrounding people.

chapters.content:
Chapter 386: Chapter 318: “Only Yi should be able to handle this kind of fate.” (10,000-word mega chapter)_3
“Are you scared now?”
“Are you terrified?”
“Started running, have you?”
“Run then, less than 20 seconds left until the countdown ends, the power of this bomb can cover the entire city. I want to see if you can run fast enough to escape!!”
“What you did to me, now I will repay you a hundredfold!”
All players around were running away in panic and fear.
...
And seeing these people, the man holding the bomb in the middle of the square’s laughter even more exhilarated. With only 12 seconds left on the countdown, he looked at the world one last time with some reluctance.
Then he slowly closed his eyes, kissed the emerald ring on his thumb, and murmured in a trance.
“I’m coming to be with you, and I’ve brought some people along.”
“After we go down, I’ll let you judge them yourself.”
He was ready to die.
Of course, he was somewhat reluctant to leave this world.
But… a world without her should be destroyed!
He wanted to create a world with her in it, or destroy all worlds without her!
However, the next second—
A white portal suddenly appeared in front of him, and immediately afterward, a giant hook shot out and directly hooked the bomb in his hand, swiftly retracting it back.
The whole process was extremely fast.
Less than a second.
Before his eyes could even register, the bomb in his hand was gone.
Uncertain, he flexed his right hand a few times, feeling its emptiness, before he finally acknowledged that the bomb was really gone, and then, with a ferocious anger, he bellowed!
“Who is it!!”
“Why would you save these people?!!”
“Do you like playing the hero? Then why didn’t you show up when they bullied me, huh?!”
“Why didn’t you show up when she was humiliated?!!”
“What now, you’re playing the hero?”
Although he wasn’t clear about what had happened, it was obvious that a powerful person had intervened, taking the bomb from his hand, not allowing him to destroy the city. And once this prop was activated, it was irreversible!
But since that powerful figure dared to take his bomb, they must have had a way to deal with it.
Before he could curse once more, suddenly a prompt sound came to his ears.
“Ding, congratulations to player Zhou Liqiu, for using an A-level prop ‘Annihilator’s Display’, killing 1.21 million Void Race players, hereby you receive the following rewards.”
“Ding, because you killed over a million players in one go, you have received the red level title ‘Corpses Strewn Everywhere’.”
“Ding, because you remained still in one place but killed multiple Race Players from outer Starfields, you have received the black level title ‘Mastermind’.”
“Ding,”
“…”
A barrage of system rewards continued to ring out in his ears.
“Huh?”
Zhou Liqiu stared blankly at the suddenly appeared prompt sounds in front of him, and after a moment, he opened the Star Map and began to search.
Void Race…
A race from the Void Starfield, according to the information obtained, this race’s combat power is extremely strong, and its expansion speed is quite terrifying. They became the only race of the Void Starfield in just a few years.
And all other Race Players have been devoured.
It is said that all Star Systems and Planets under the Void Starfield are suppressing their own planetary strength, not allowing themselves to advance to a Threefold Planet, to go to the Void Starfield.
Otherwise, the only outcome is eradication by the Void Race.
This is a Race that doesn’t engage in relations; they only have one way for all other Race Players, which is to kill them and then absorb the nutrients.
It is also one of the few Starfields on the entire Starfield Continent that has only one Race up until now.
The search results indicated that this Void Race was formidable.
Only… this Void Starfield was too far from him. How far, exactly? To travel from his current Starfield to the Void Starfield, one would need to pay a single-person Starfield Shuttle fee of 50 million Points.
Generally speaking, for a nearby Starfield Shuttle, 1 million Points is enough.
For a slightly further one, passing through a few Star Systems, 5 million Points would do.
A single-person Starfield Shuttle fee of 50 million Points, that’s a distance of at least over a dozen Star Systems.
“That far…”
How did his Annihilation Bomb manage to travel that distance in ten seconds?
Zhou Liqiu was puzzled. He didn’t understand what had happened. He didn’t intend to kill those Void Race players; there were no grievances. So how did it end up killing over a million of them?
Before this, the total number of Race Players he killed hadn’t even reached ten thousand.
Now it had multiplied by more than a hundred times.
Void Race, quite a nice name.
It’s just that they died wrongly.
…
After having their fill of food and wine, Tuberculosis Rabbit and Sword Without End were still sitting by the table, drinking, chatting, and playing drinking games.
Tie Chui had left early, saying he had some important matter to take care of.
What it was, no one knew.
And Chen Yi was already back sitting by the beach, planning to try his luck once more to see what kind of effect the Gold Miner really had, but before he did, he decided to seek some advice.
But not from the 33 clubs.
The greatest strength of his ‘Faceless One’ occupation was its variability and difficulty to be targeted; he wasn’t very keen on revealing his occupation in the chat group.
Although so far, the 33 clubs had only shown him goodwill.
But no one can be sure about the future.
Completely exposing oneself to some strangers, even if these people have good intentions toward you, is never a good thing.

chapters.content:
Chapter 387: Chapter 318: “Only Yi should be able to handle this kind of fate.” (10,000-word mega chapter)_4
B-level Skill “Requesting the Mandate of Heaven” activated!
“What exactly is the occupational effect of the Gold Miner, is there a detailed probability table? Like a 1% chance to snag an E-level prop, 2% chance to snag something else? There must be a specific algorithm, it can’t be totally random, right?”
Soon.
After spending 100,000 Points, he got the answer.
“Reply: The Gold Miner’s occupational effect has no underlying algorithm, it is completely random, truly random, not the pseudo-randomness concocted by code. Theoretically, you could even hook an S-level prop, or even an SSS-level prop, directly through the Gold Miner.”
“But there is a certain mechanism in the process of randomly selecting the target to hook.”
...
“If the item chosen by the Gold Miner is owned, then the hooked item has a certain probability of being currently important to the owner of the item.”
That’s it.
The answer he got was just this.
Completely random, the only piece of information was that there is a chance that the item chosen by the Gold Miner is something the owner currently values.
Regarding this, he was somewhat speechless.
Could it be that those two E-level Air Food Series Props were also important to someone just now? Who would value these things? They hadn’t cared much about this prop during their initial novice period.
Unless someone ran into the desert and was about to starve to death.
Forget it, no useful information, keep on hooking.
After regaining energy from eating, Chen Yi and Jiaye sat by the beach, chatted, fished, and continued mining.
They were quite busy.
…
In some desert.
A man with a parched mouth and red bloodshot eyes was trudging through the desert under the night sky, endless dunes before him, and slightly shaky footsteps behind him.
Finally—
The man couldn’t help but fall onto the sand.
Licking his dry lips, he looked up at the starry sky, and murmured weakly.
“The bastard who stole my Air Food Prop, you won’t die a good death!!”
“Won’t die a good death!”
But then he paused slightly, licked his lips again, stared at the dense stars above, and wondered, “Is the starry sky in the desert this beautiful?”
He had been so focused on rushing through the past few days that he hadn’t taken the time to carefully observe the night sky above.
Hesitating for a moment, he simply lay down, planning to rest for a while and admire the extreme beauty of the hardship in the desert.
Right now, he only felt thirst and hunger, and he still had some props in his backpack for self-defense, ensuring he wouldn’t die here from hazards like hypothermia in the desert.
…
In the depths of hell.
Ping Ye, with a face full of unwillingness, saw that he had been pulled back into the depths of hell, scanned his surroundings, and after seeing the familiar sights, he roared in pain, “No!!!”
He had already gotten used to life in hell.
But just now, Chen Yi had pulled him out to have a look!
The freedom that had been dormant in his heart suddenly became active again!
He didn’t want to stay here and be a janitor any longer. He wanted to go back. He too had once been a player who enjoyed glory with five bases; he shouldn’t just die in obscurity here!
He wanted to return to the base-upgrade game!
Although he didn’t know how to go back, since Chen Yi could, and even seemed to come and go as he pleased, even pulling him out of hell, albeit for just a few seconds, he must also be able to find a way.
But for now, there were more important things to attend to.
Ping Ye took out a pot from his bosom, took a deep breath, buried his head over the mouth of the pot, and began to vomit forcefully, then he spat out all the chili oil, hotpot base, and ingredients he had just swallowed outside.
A moment later.
Ping Ye sat in front of the spicy hotpot, fanning it slightly with his wand, closed his eyes, and murmured in ecstasy, “The taste of freedom.”
In hell, devouring corpses could earn points, and points could be exchanged for some normal food, like fried chicken, but they were all basic. Luxurious food like hotpot was definitely unavailable.
He didn’t know how long it had been since he had tasted hotpot.
The mere scent of it was enough to give a taste of the air of freedom.
Luckily, he had moved quickly when he was dragged back, bringing some hotpot with him, otherwise, he would have returned empty-handed!
After a moment!
He stood in front of the bubbling hotpot, excited and slightly trembling, holding a pair of chopsticks, and declared.
“I’m starting now!!”
…
Men tend to get emotional when they drink, leading to chattiness.
At least that was the case with Sword Without End.
After a satisfying meal and drink, Sword Without End glanced at Yi, who had finished eating and gone to rest on the beach, and after a moment of silence, he began, “Did I ever tell you some of my past?”
“Ah…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit was taken aback for a moment, his lips twitching slightly without speaking. How should he put it? He didn’t really want to continue the conversation.
It was like that last time.
Everyone was enjoying a bonfire dinner under the night sky, everything was romantic and leisurely. Just when the atmosphere was at its best, due to his own loose lips, he asked Sword Without End about his family.
Only then did he learn that Sword Without End’s mother had died in childbirth, and his father had worked himself to death on a construction site not long after supporting him through university.

Chapter 388: Chapter 318: “Only Yi should be able to handle this kind of fate.” (10,000-word mega chapter)_5
All our relatives also perished in a flood.
Even my wife fell ill and died.
The atmosphere suddenly became a bit oppressive.
So this time, he chose to play dumb and simply wouldn’t join the conversation.
However, even though Tuberculosis Rabbit chose to play dumb, Sword Without End still murmured absentmindedly, “Did you go to school?”
“No.”
...
Tuberculosis Rabbit touched his nose with some embarrassment, “Yi and I came out of the orphanage. Back then, there was no such thing as compulsory education in the orphanage.”
“Then you’re quite lucky—students were the most miserable profession in the world before the upgrade game began. You’ve avoided a calamity.”
“…”
After pouring himself a glass of chilled beer with some confusion, Tuberculosis Rabbit drank it down in one gulp, took a deep breath with satisfaction, and only after filling his glass again did he speak up, “Why say that? Although I’ve never been to school, I’ve heard that being a student is the happiest job. You don’t have to endure the pressure of society under the sun and the wind. All you need to do is study.”
“When I was in high school, seventeen students died over three years.”
“Sixteen jumped off buildings, and one drank Paraquat.”
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit stared at the beer he had just refilled and, after staying silent for a while, said gloomily, “Seventeen students died in three years, and the school could still keep running?”
He had a guess about the situation.
Although it wasn’t nice to say and was somewhat an insult to someone’s character, he always felt that there was a pall of bad luck hanging over Sword Without End, or that Sword Without End’s fate was to bring death wherever he went.
Dooming his father, his mother, his wife, everyone close to him.
Not only did everyone close to him die,
but even Yi’s first injury happened after Sword Without End joined their team.
Now even his classmates were dying in batches.
Only Yi could probably rein in such a fate.
Not to mention other things.
During the time Yi was away, he choked on water four or five times, even managing to fall while walking—so much so that he didn’t dare venture into the field maps while Yi wasn’t around, fearing that he might accidentally get doomed by Sword Without End.
This ability was too strange.
It wasn’t a prop, it wasn’t a title, there was no panel information, just an ethereal aura.
Whoever entered this aura always died inexplicably.
Now he seriously suspected that the seventeen students who committed suicide when Sword Without End was in high school were affected by his aura.
“The schools in the county can push it down. The parents of the students are all farmers.”
“What do farmers understand? Make a fuss, get some compensation, and that’s it. Behind closed doors, they might even curse their children for being selfish.”
After pausing for a moment, as if recalling something, Sword Without End took out a cigarette from his chest pocket, lit it, and then looked toward Chen Yi’s back as he spoke softly, “Actually, I’ve always envied the relationship between you and Yi. Your bond is truly strong. No matter what difficulties you encounter, you’ll get through it because you both know there’s someone who will stand behind you unwaveringly in support.”
“But students won’t.”
“A student only encounters two environments, home and school.”
“If the parents fail to understand and the school cannot provide a sense of belonging, the student will feel like there is no place for them in this world. They want to rebel, but what can a student do?”
“The only rebellion they can muster is to jump off a building.”
“They know their parents love them, so they jump hoping to make their parents regret.”
“It’s a very foolish act, isn’t it?”
“Of the seventeen students I knew who jumped, not a single one committed suicide because of some earth-shattering event. The reasons were even absurdly simple, like their mother constantly berating them in front of the class during parent-teacher meetings.”
“Because in front of their classmates, their mother wouldn’t stop slapping them.”
“I watched the surveillance footage; the determination of that student as they turned and jumped off, as if it was not the seventh floor but the first.”
“Why do you think a student would leap from the seventh floor so resolutely?”
“They are not afraid of death. So what are they afraid of?”
“…”
Without any expression, Tuberculosis Rabbit looked down at the glass of beer in his hand. It was tough to drink now. He knew what else there was to be afraid of—were there any people left around you who hadn’t died? Of course, it was you they were afraid of.
Don’t you know yourself?
Practically the entire Blue Star Race almost died out, right?
“I said sixteen of them jumped off buildings, and one was poisoned, which is Paraquat.”
“Do you know Paraquat?”
“I know.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit nodded gloomily, “Many of my past clients drank that stuff. The bodies were easy to handle, much easier than those who collided at high speeds and got squeezed into mince. They were priced quite low.”
“She was my first love.”
“Pff…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit couldn’t help but spit out the beer he had just brought to his lips. Seeing the look in Sword Without End’s eyes as he turned to him, he said seriously, “I drank too fast and choked. You go on, I’m listening.”
“She was a very pretty girl.”
Lost in his memories, Sword Without End murmured, “A very gentle girl. At that time, my father worked hard away from home all year long. He worked too hard for the money he gave me; I couldn’t bear to spend it. I would only take a little, save the rest, planning to give it all back to him once I was in college.”
“So he wouldn’t have to work so hard.”

Chapter 389: Chapter 318: “Only Yi should be able to handle this kind of fate.” (10,000-word mega chapter)_6
“I would often go hungry at school, and that girl would occasionally share some of her food with me.”
“As time passed, we became familiar with each other.”
“Early love.”
“The greatest enemy in education.”
“The concern is always about academics. I’ve always felt that parents who hope their children can change the family’s future through education are quite pitiful. What do you think?”
“Having no success in society themselves, they place all their pressure on their children, expecting them to become superior through education and improve the entire family’s lot. Is that possible?”
...
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit expressionlessly said in a low voice, “It’s hard to say, I don’t have a father, nor have I been one.”
“In the end, our early love affair was discovered.”
“It wasn’t our interactions that were discovered, but rather a love letter I wrote to her. I secretly hid it in her textbook during the break between classes. I still remember the look on her face when she saw the letter during the third period.”
“Her profile lifted slightly in the sunlight, her eyes shaped like crescent moons, so incredibly beautiful.”
“We exchanged a glance across the noisy classroom.”
“There was an unspoken understanding between us.”
“Love during school days is always clandestine; who would dare to date openly in the light of day? In the noisy classroom we were far apart, yet it felt so close.”
“But she was too engrossed in reading the letter and didn’t notice the teacher walking down from the podium.”
“Call the parents.”
“Her mother, dressed simply, worked on a factory assembly line. Since I hadn’t signed the envelope, her mother rushed up to her as soon as she arrived at the school and slapped her face several times without warning.”
“I still remember that scene—her mother’s face twisted with rage, demanding to know who that ‘wild man’ was.”
“There were a lot of swear words, too.”
“‘Whore, you’re so young and already getting fucked, does it feel good?'”
“Things like that, which are hard to imagine being said by a mother looking back now.”
“But she just stayed silent. No matter how much she was pressured later on in the office by the teachers and her mother, she wouldn’t admit to being in a relationship, let alone know who sent the letter.”
“At that time, I really wanted to stand up and explain things, like at least make it clear that we’d only held hands, but before her mother arrived, she had signaled to me that she would take the fall for this alone. It was just a letter, after all, and as long as she denied the relationship and claimed it was from someone unknown confessing their love, there wouldn’t be any trouble. Otherwise, we both would have been expelled.”
“Many classmates were watching at the time.”
“She was quite pretty on ordinary days and had a good reputation, always talking with a smile. But that day, she just stood at her desk with her head down, silently clutching the edges of her clothes.”
“Taken home by her own mother.”
“That night, she drank Paraquat at home.”
“Two bottles.”
“She forced it down with her nose pinched, sweetened with sugar, for she was afraid of the bitterness.”
“Before she died, she left a suicide note blaming the torment of her life for her death, acknowledging that although her mother loved her and seemed tough on the outside but soft on the inside, if it’s a knife, it cuts deep every time; there’s no soft center.”
“The note said a lot. The next day, her mother, waving the suicide note and with tears streaming down her face, carried her daughter’s corpse to the school, demanding compensation.”
“She had searched online about the toxicity of Paraquat and found that while it could potentially be treated, the chances of rescue were zero. She wanted to let her mother witness her being taken to the hospital, to start regretting her actions during the time she was being rescued but not yet dead.”
“Unfortunately, her research wasn’t thorough.”
“After drinking two bottles, the dose was far too high, and there was no chance for rescue. The ambulance arrived but didn’t take her, leaving a note that ambulances don’t transport the deceased and then left.”
“Indeed, ambulances don’t carry the dead, and at times like this, most people would call me to transport the body. I’m familiar with the procedure.”
“Her mother didn’t even get the chance to sign a critical condition notice.”
“The suicide note didn’t mention me at all. Even in her final moments, she was still thinking of protecting me, hoping that I wouldn’t get expelled from school.”
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit stared at the beer bottles on the table, feeling that he really couldn’t drink anymore. Listening to it all made him feel some oppression. Sword Without End seemed to have lived a life that was somehow tainted with sin.
After taking a long breath, he reached out and patted Sword Without End on the shoulder to comfort him.
“It’s all in the past, at least… at least you’re still alive.”
Well.
He admitted that he was not very good at comforting people.
Sword Without End shook his head without speaking, just silently filled his cup with more alcohol, “I have never told anyone about this matter, in this story, my role is not something to be proud of.”
“People are always reluctant to share stories where their roles are not so honorable.”
“But tonight, for some reason, I suddenly feel a bit distressed.”
“She didn’t deserve to die.”
“At least, before she died, if she had left a word or two about me in her will, it would have been better.”
“It was probably to protect you as well.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit gave Sword Without End’s shoulder a comforting pat, “After all, you rarely had meals at school, she knew about your family’s poor situation, and she was more aware of her mother’s shrewish nature. If she mentioned you in the letter…”
“Her mother would definitely think you were to blame for her daughter’s death, and she would certainly harass you for compensation.”
Upon hearing this, Sword Without End was suddenly stunned, his eyes instantly reddened with emotion. The feelings he had been holding back finally burst forth, his shoulders trembling uncontrollably as he looked at the cup in his hand, having never considered this point before.
But perhaps this was the truth.
He just wondered if things would have turned out differently had he stood up and taken responsibility for everything.
If he had acted like a man, maybe everything could have changed.
He later got into university.
During that summer break, he also received the tragic news of his father’s death at the construction site.
Unable to control himself any longer, he leaned onto the table burying his head in the crook of his arm, his shoulders lightly shaking.
“Alright, alright, it’s all in the past now.”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, somewhat helplessly, patted Sword Without End’s back, clicking his tongue with pity.
Sword Without End’s life had indeed been pitiable.
To maintain such an optimistic character against that kind of background was quite rare.
He had seen plenty of movies where characters with a background like Sword Without End’s usually ended up as the main villain.
But it always felt chillingly eerie.
He couldn’t be cursed by Sword Without End, could he? He shouldn’t be. Yi should be able to watch over him.
…
Time gradually passed, and it was now late at night.
Tuberculosis Rabbit and Sword Without End had already started to drunkenly babble in each other’s arms, both of them emotionally charged and red-eyed shouting about something, clearly having had quite a few drinks, high on alcohol.
Meanwhile, Chen Yi continued to chat with Jiaye by the beach, planning to do something more intimate in their room after Tuberculosis Rabbit and the others had left.
Tie Chui squat seriously on a bare patch of land in the residential compound’s flowerbed.
He stared at two unremarkable-looking stones in front of him without blinking.
During dinner, he had seen these two stones hopping several times.
Each time he looked away, they would continue hopping, but when his gaze returned, they would stop. So he didn’t finish his dinner halfway, took the stones and pocketed them, then brought them downstairs, determined to figure out what was going on with these stones.
He decided that if there was no reaction, he would smash the stone and see what was up.
Why it would hop.
Although he wasn’t the sharpest tool in the shed, he knew that stones don’t just hop on their own.

chapters.content:
Chapter 390: Chapter 319: The Void Clan (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)
The night deepened.
All things began to drift into sleep, and after exhaustion, Chen Yi too embraced Jiaye and slowly entered dreamland. Just before losing consciousness, his mind subconsciously sorted through all the things he needed to do tomorrow.
The S-ranked Prop “Longevity as the Southern Mountains” needed to be farmed.
Haven’t cleared the map for the S-ranked Prop Admission Ticket yet.
And…
It was his personal habit to review the workload for the next day in his mind before falling asleep every day.
...
…
In the neighboring room, Tuberculosis Rabbit, alone and going to bed, lay on his single bed, turned his head to the moonlight shining through the window at the other empty single bed, and inexplicably clicked his tongue.
Then slammed a fist on his own forehead.
The whole person instantly fell straight back onto the bed.
Slipping into the dream world rapidly.
It wasn’t long before he began muttering again.
“Yi came back safely this time. It seems I don’t need to take any hits for him this time; this life’s Yi is a bit stronger,” he murmured.
“It’s just that his personality is still the same, as lazy and lackadaisical as ever.”
“It’s strange when you think about it.”
“Yi has been through so many lives, yet every time, he has the same personality.”
“You also saw this life’s world—it’s more complicated than the previous ones, but there are also more fallbacks. Otherwise, Yi wouldn’t even know how many times he would have died.”
“And…”
…
Tuberculosis Rabbit’s dreamscape.
At the edge of a cliff.
Tuberculosis Rabbit was sitting cross-legged at the top of the cliff, with the oppressive sight of thick clouds stretching beyond vision overhead, and the ceaseless howling winds that made his clothes flutter.
Midway up the mountain.
Countless figures sat cross-legged in the shadows, looking eerily like a cult preaching.
Looking closely, the faces of those seated on the mountainside bore an exact resemblance to Tuberculosis Rabbit, as if they were carved from the same mold.
While the normally incessant Tuberculosis Rabbit suddenly stopped talking, stood up emotionlessly, and walked to the edge of the cliff, looking down at the canyon crevice behind him.
Beneath the stormy sky, the canyon crevice before Tuberculosis Rabbit gaped like the maw of a fanged demon, captivating the spirit.
The whooshing sounds made by the fierce winds crossing the crevice were like whispers from a devil, eerie in one’s ear.
Only—
The crevice was filled with bodies.
No one knew how deep the canyon was.
Only that the bodies had piled up to fill the entire crevice, resembling a massive grave.
The manner of death for each corpse was almost unique.
Some had swords through their necks, others had their heads blown apart, some were sliced to pieces, some crushed to pulp, and there were still others who appeared serene in death yet with no clear cause.
There were virtually no identical causes of death.
The clothing on these bodies also differed.
But one thing was the same.
All the corpses had the exact same build, and even their faces were identical.
If Sword Without End and the others were to stand here, they would instantly recognize that all these faces belonged to Yi.
Not similar.
But exactly alike.
As if carved from the same bone, born from the same parents.
“…”
Tuberculosis Rabbit, hands in pockets, stood emotionlessly against the wind at the edge of the cliff, peering down at the crevice filled with Yi’s corpses, silent for a long while, until at last he slowly raised his head to gaze into the distance at a tall mountain some distance away.
He muttered softly.
“Yi, this is our last life.”
“If we fail this time, everything ends.”
“We won’t have another chance to die.”
“Or rather, I only have one more chance to take disaster for you. If we fail this life, next life you will have to start alone, and I won’t be able to accompany you.”
“But this life, it seems there’s more uncertainty, whether it’s a good or bad thing, I can’t tell.”
He thought of Jiaye’s figure in his mind.
This life, Yi had fallen in love.
An unprecedented scenario in numerous past lives, not much related to the Wife-Killing Buff; since the time he and Yi lay on the orphanage wall, Yi fell for Jiaye, the one who would buy him a new punching bag.
Whether it was a good or bad thing, he couldn’t discern.
But at least there was more uncertainty, bringing some new hope—or perhaps different despair.
After a moment.
He fixed his gaze on a man standing at the edge of another cliff not too far from the tall mountain.
In Tuberculosis Rabbit’s dreamscape, besides himself, there was another man.
That man also seemed familiar.
Who else could it be but Sword Without End?
Tuberculosis Rabbit, with calm demeanor and hands in pockets, looked towards the man standing at the edge of the other cliff, speaking softly.
“This is also your last life.”
“If you survive this one, you too should meet your end.”
Sword Without End was of the same kind as them; this life was also Sword Without End’s last.
Every life.
Sword Without End would experience a series of extremely tragic events in the human world, as losing all his beloved ones in this life was just usual business, gradually destroying what was left of his sanity.
Perhaps Sword Without End should feel guilty; if he hadn’t fallen for that girl in high school, she probably would never have died in an accident. That girl’s true cause of death wasn’t the so-called Paraquat.
But Sword Without End’s affection.
He shouldn’t have liked anyone. Anyone he liked wouldn’t live for long.
Sometimes Sword Without End survived it.

Chapter 391: Chapter 319: Void Clan (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)_2
Sometimes, they didn’t make it and ended up collapsing into suicide.
But counting the times, if Sword Without End can survive this ordeal, then Sword Without End can be considered to have achieved success and fame.
However, for some unknown reason, Sword Without End, standing on the edge of the opposite cliff, was motionless, resembling a rock. If observed closely, it would be evident that his eyes were devoid of life, not like those of a living person.
More like a statue.
On that mountain, there were also countless dead bodies, including old people, women, and young people.
It was as if it were a messy graveyard.
...
Yet, strangely, the bodies were neither rotting nor emitting foul odors.
Tonight.
The Tuberculosis Rabbit, for some reason, wasn’t chatting with the people sitting halfway up the mountain as usual, but was silently standing at the edge of the cliff, looking around. After a long while, it turned to face those sitting on the mountainside behind it.
And these people—
All bore terrible wounds, with many having their intestines spilling out.
The Tuberculosis Rabbit swept its gaze over each face and, after a moment, suddenly laughed.
“Ladies and gentlemen, dawn has broken,”
“We shall meet again tomorrow,”
As these words fell,
Those seated in the shadows halfway up the mountain responded almost in unison, saying, “Stay safe.”
“Alright, alright,”
The Tuberculosis Rabbit stretched lazily, speaking nonchalantly, “Save your breath with those pointless words.”
“Take good care of yourselves,”
Then its figure slowly dispersed on the spot.
…
Soon, it was daylight.
All things were revived again.
In the morning light, Chen Yi, groggy, opened his eyes and looked at Jiaye curled up in his arms like a small cat, his eyes showing a touch of long-lost tenderness. He gently stroked behind her earlobe before getting up.
He tiptoed to wash up and get dressed.
Then he went up to the rooftop, sat on a beach chair, and began to carefully check Blue Star’s version updates for the month.
Right after he returned to reality, he had glanced at it, but he had been too busy at the time to take a closer look. He had only looked at the update rules for the month. Now that he had the time, he naturally wanted to go over this month’s update rules in detail.
It was 8:30 in the morning on September 30th.
Tomorrow would be October, and he was only looking at the update rules for September, which was admittedly a bit late. But he had no choice, as he had spent an entire month in the “Rogue Star” map. It was the map he had spent the longest time on.
‘Ding!’
‘Game Update Announcement!’
‘The new version 4.5 of Blue Star will begin a non-stop update at 00:00 on September 1st. The main content and adjustments of this update are as follows.’
‘1. Fixed some bugs with props/skills. The following are the details of the bug fixes:
*Fixed the bug where the feature to summon an adopted father could ignore map effects. This feature was a limited Father’s Day function where a player could adopt up to ten sworn children, and regardless of the sworn child’s location, they could summon their sworn father to their side.
This effect once led to some players adopting hundreds of sworn fathers, allowing them to summon the fathers to their side upon entering certain single-player maps, then those fathers would continue summoning their sworn fathers, resulting in a map designed for one player suddenly accommodating hundreds of players, with each being able to receive a map reward.
Now, players will no longer be able to summon their sworn fathers on any map they are on.
*Fixed the ‘Forest Fantasy’ prop bug, which allowed players to create a shadow with one-tenth of their combat power to fight in their stead.
Some players activated this prop right after completing a single-player map and before claiming their reward, causing both themselves and their shadow to receive a unique single-player map reward.
Some players even collected dozens of ‘Forest Fantasy’ props and activated all of them before claiming the reward, allowing one person to receive dozens of rewards.
This bug has been fixed, and from now on, activating the prop upon map completion will not yield multiple rewards.
Some players used this bug in conjunction with the above-fixed bug, and the system’s backend showed that a D-grade single-player map unexpectedly distributed 110,000 rewards at one point, causing severe errors.
*Fixed the ‘Thousands of Swords Flying Together’ skill bug, this skill…
…*$%##%$#%%#*…’
‘2. Fixed some map bugs; the following are the map bug fixes:
…*Fixed the bug in the ‘Lone Sea’ map where NPCs giving out quests often intentionally issued wrong missions.
…*Fixed the ‘Insect Toilet’ map bug where insects, originally intended to guide the player, were discovered to be exceptionally tasty when fried by a player. Consequently, all insects were captured by players for frying, leading to the map no longer having insects to guide the way.
…*Fixed the ‘Coffee Shop’ map bug, reported by players, where the shop lacked a food business permit and the coffee served was from unlicensed self-production.
…*Fixed the ‘Giant City Ruins’ map bug where switching to a different starting occupation during a momentary blackout upon entering allowed gunners to acquire the sniper-exclusive skill ‘Burst Bullet’…
…Fixed the bug in the ‘One Person Restaurant’ map…
…*$%##%$#%%#*…’
‘3. Added a “Return” feature.
This month, any player trapped in hell who successfully returns to Blue Star before midnight on the 30th will receive a return gift package.
The package includes—
200 Points, a random E-rank Prop Chest *1, and 5 random Skill Fragments.
And any player has the right to invite others to return. If the player you invite enters the hell return map with you and successfully clears it, you will both receive an old player’s gift package.

chapters.content:
Chapter 392: Chapter 319: Void Clan (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)_3
The gift package contains—
1000 Points, a random D-class treasure chest*1, random Skill Fragments*10, Kindness Points*1.
Additionally, there will be a global ranking of points, where the top hundred players who have invited the most will receive exclusive rewards, and the top three will earn a limited-time exclusive title.”
“4: A new ‘Fried Golden Flower’ gameplay has been added for September; players will have three chances to re-randomize rewards on any map during that month.
There is a 10% chance to re-randomize to a higher-level reward.
There is a 50% chance to re-randomize to a reward one level lower.
...
There is a 39% chance to re-randomize to a different reward of the same level.”
There is a 1% chance to re-randomize to a reward two levels higher.
“5: A new rule for September has been added, ‘Prohibition of xp’.
“Prohibition of xp”: This forbids any messy xp, such as heavy punch to the ox’s mouth, same-sex xp, Russian Roulette, Green Forest Hero, Swinging Hammer, etc.
All messy xp are prohibited this month.
A true gentleman should not possess these strange xp, at least suppress it for this month; hopefully, you all can improve.
This rule will last for a month and expire on October 1st at midnight.”
“The Snow Sea Project Team wishes all players a pleasant gaming experience in version 4.4.”
“PS: Upcoming update preview, the project team has decided to introduce a monthly rule about ‘absurd’ elements, so please stay tuned.”
–
This is the update rule for Blue Star’s September version.
It has to be said.
After reading through the entire update announcement, Chen Yi had only one thought in his mind.
Why did he only find out about these bugs after they were fixed?
Not to mention anything else, but that exploit of sweeping away more than 110,000 rewards in a single-player map at once was something even he couldn’t help but be tempted by.
Even though it’s just a D-class map and the rewards wouldn’t be too much, the quantity is overwhelming.
He could imagine that scenario.
A single-player map, as usual, casually allowing a player to enter, ready to let this player experience the difficulty and dangers of a D-class solo map.
But who knew that this player, upon entering the map, would start summoning his foster father without a second word.
This foster father then summons his own foster father.
The summoned foster father continues to summon his own foster father.
The once again summoned foster father, carries on summoning his own foster father.
Within a few short minutes, the player who initially entered the map had summoned the entire family tree.
If we were to talk about seniority, the last foster father summoned would probably be the great (to the nth degree) foster father of the player who first entered the map.
Just a few minutes.
An enhanced team surged into this single-player map.
Before the single-player map could react, it was instantly cleared using swarm tactics, and just before claiming the reward, the enhanced team’s foster fathers simultaneously activated their ‘Forest Fantasy’ props.
Almost instantly—
Along with the player and shadows, a total of more than 110,000 people crowded into the map, claiming 110,000 rewards all at once.
Achieving success and fame, they exited perfectly.
He believed that the number of over 110,000 people was definitely not these players’ limit, but that the single-player map simply could not accommodate more.
However, obviously, this action was too brazen, directly causing the system backend to flash red alert and report an emergency. If not for such brazenness, if they had just exploited bit by bit, it might have gone unnoticed for the time being.
But such a thing was obviously uncontrollable.
You want to exploit slowly, but others might not feel the same.
If you see others power-farming, you can’t just keep on exploiting slowly, right?
However, this return mechanism was evidently well-thought-out by the Blue Star Snow Sea Project Team, who also knew that Blue Star had just survived a disaster and that many players were currently in hell.
This significantly impacted not only the strength of the entire Blue Star but also the well-maintained environment of the players.
But the Blue Star Snow Sea Project Team was unable to directly rescue the players from hell, so they implemented this method: a way to help Blue Star players return within the boundaries of the rules.
This feature was evidently targeting those players who did not have the ability to clear the return map, where the game itself is offering rewards to incentivize stronger players to help these weaker players return.
It’s sort of like cheating.
It’s akin to hiring leveling services, but officially sponsored.
Although it is not explicitly stated, that is essentially what it amounts to.
This feature likely allowed many players to successfully return from hell this month, reviving the once bustling Blue Star; although the number of players could not return to previous levels, certainly many were lost, but it was already a significant improvement.
At least it no longer felt as desolate as it had been briefly.
Furthermore, many players who went down found it quite comfortable and didn’t feel like coming back up.
It was rather comfortable down there.
Even without descending into maps, one could survive. Moreover, in the city, there were enforcement officers from the game to maintain order. If you didn’t contemplate crimes or seek power, the environment was more comfortable than staying in Blue Star.
As for that last September rule, Chen Yi didn’t have much of a reaction; that rule didn’t make much difference to him, as he had no special xp to speak of.
Or rather, his desire for Jiaye stemmed from love.
Love before desire.
If it wasn’t for Jiaye, even if other women stood naked before him, he wouldn’t be moved.
After all, with his current status, if he genuinely just wanted women, what kind of woman couldn’t he find? Even the most beautiful woman would only be able to line up and wait for his selection.

chapters.title: Chapter 393: 319: Void Clan (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)_4
chapters.content:
Chapter 393: Chapter 319: Void Clan (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)_4
I won’t go into detail about other things.
At Li Yi’s place, didn’t he have a chief financial officer of a planet directly offering his mother to him?
This is the power of status.
In the history of Blue Star, without exception, such treatment was enjoyed by the dominant leaders.
Interestingly, a lot of Blue Star students learned during their nine-year compulsory education about some great hero who made so many sacrifices to fight the Barbarians that they were moved to tears, wishing they could go back to ancient times to decapitate Barbarian heads and drink their blood along with their ancestors.
And when they grew up, they found that the Barbarians mentioned in the history books were actually themselves.
...
Their ancestors were the Barbarians.
Suddenly, they didn’t know quite what to think.
…
Lighting a cigarette, Chen Yi, sitting on the balcony of the rooftop, casually flicked the ash into the ashtray on the table next to him, basking in the somewhat warm sunrise. He was enjoying the comfort of the moment in a lazy manner, continuing to look at the system notifications he hadn’t had time to check over the past few days.
And the unexamined system rewards.
The Gold Miner’s hook was still set up by the riverbank.
He cast several hooks before going to bed last night, but didn’t hook anything worthwhile, just some random trash, leading him to feel somewhat disappointed in the profession, even though it had no Occupational Restriction and no limit on the number of daily casts.
Those Sixfold Planet players who still choose this profession despite Occupational Restrictions must have water in their brains.
Moreover, only he could control it; aside from him, no one else could activate that hook, and it wouldn’t operate on its own, effectively dashing his hope of hiring someone to help him cast for 24 hours.
The emerald-colored fishing rod in his hand, however, was quite nice, looking very pretty to the eyes.
It was the most beautiful Prop he’d ever gotten and could even be seen more as a piece of art than an A-level Prop.
‘Prop Name’: Power of Faith.
‘Prop Level’: A-level Prop.
‘Prop Effect’: While holding this Prop, you will be extremely Calm and Composed, with no emotional fluctuations inside, and you can control your microexpressions. In addition, it activates the ‘Air Force’ buff.
After sitting in place and holding this Prop for more than 10 minutes, when you stand up again, the first title/Skill/Prop you use will not consume a use, and its power will be increased by 50%.
‘Prop Restrictions’: The buff effect of this Prop can only be used once before entering a 24h cooldown.
‘Prop Description’: “A person who claims the Air Force every day and stays Calm and Cool without going to the fish market to buy fish on the way home must be a trustworthy vegetable b*tch worth dealing with.”
The effect of this Prop is somewhat ordinary.
For others, it might be tremendously useful, as it can bypass the use count for a Prop or title once, which, for some consumable items or titles, would make this A-level Prop the best supporting item.
But it’s of no use to him.
After all, he holds a title that allows him to reset the count of a named Prop or Skill after killing five million Alien Race players.
He still has 218 resets available.
Which means he can completely reset a Prop up to 218 times.
He’ll never run out, simply can’t use them all up.
If it weren’t for the fact that during the second Upgrade Monument event, the players who looked at him and died triggering the monthly rule Calm and Cool weren’t actually counted against him, he’d have far more than 218 resets, and at least one more zero would be added to that number.
But 218 is still plenty, and the most important thing about this Prop to him is likely the amplification effect.
An increase of 50% would allow his Wife-Killing Buff to last an extra half-hour.
As well as serve as a fashion accessory on regular days.
It really is beautiful, and it feels good in the hand like jade.
Glancing at his Points Balance, he saw he still had over 52 million Points, which he once thought was quite a lot—until he learned that Li Yi had earned 1 billion Points during the Newbie Protection Period and used them to get the Upgrade Monument.
Any pride that had briefly welled up in his heart vanished in an instant.
1 billion Points.
How on earth did you make that much?
It’s just outrageous.
The bulk of his 52 million Points had come from securing the Upgrade Monument in the game and, before the Extinction Sun Star mission, being tricked onto a planet where he killed tens of millions of Cave Demons, earning nearly 40 million Points.
A few minutes ago, he had been rewarded several million more Points through the Rogue Star map.
Adding on the usual expenses, his balance now only amounted to 52 million Points. For a regular player, it wasn’t a small sum, but it wasn’t enough for squandering, not even close to a hundred million. If it weren’t for him being the recipient of the Annihilation Starfield Monument, Li Yi might not even bother to speak with him.
Although he wasn’t sure about Li Yi’s exact wealth,
judging from the other players’ chats in the group, he figured that a wealth of several hundred billion Points was at least guaranteed.
Or maybe even more.
But he hadn’t forgotten about the 900 million Points bounty waiting for him to claim once he left the Newbie Protection Period.
The only thing that irked him was,
he clearly remembered that several races had bounties out for him alone, and by rights, his own suicide trip to the depths of hell to become a janitor should have satisfied that race bounty, so why didn’t he get the reward?
Just because he had crawled back out from the depths of hell?
Not dead enough?
But what does it matter if I’m not totally dead? Isn’t the rule that you get the Race bounty reward as long as you’re sent to the depths of hell?

chapters.title: Chapter 394: 319: Void Clan (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)_5
chapters.content:
Chapter 394: Chapter 319: Void Clan (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)_5
Why make a promise only to break it?
Chen Yi glanced aside with some dissatisfaction, not dwelling on the matter. After all, he didn’t have a pressing need for Points lately, and fifty million Points were enough for now. Blue Star’s Newbie Protection Period would also end soon.
The Newbie Protection Period lasts 12 months.
It started on April 1st.
Now, October 1st is almost here.
Five months are about to pass, and in another seven months, Blue Star’s Newbie Protection Period will be over.
...
Then, Chen Yi lit another cigarette and brought it to his lips as he looked at the exclusive title he received for perfectly passing his first debut map, based on his actions within the map—”God.”
「Title Name」: God.
「Title Level」: Black.
「Title Effect」: When you activate this title effect, anyone with fewer Points than you will feel an extremely oppressive aura when they look at you and won’t be able to look you in the eye. Moreover, their voice will carry an awe-inspiring magnetism, as if they were speaking to a deity.
However, if the other party has the same number of Points or more than you, there will be no effect.
「Title Source」: Exclusively awarded based on player Chen Yi’s actions on the S-Level map Rogue Star.
「Title Introduction」: “Man cannot look directly at God.”
“A black title.”
Chen Yi nodded thoughtfully. Black level was not as high as Starry Level, but it was the highest level title a normal newbie player could obtain. He quite liked it, especially since it was his first black level title.
It also satisfied a small collecting hobby of his.
But what he was curious about was this.
The effect of this title allows those who have less money than him to be unable to look directly at him.
And he also has a Starry Level title called ‘Attention of Millions,’ which, when activated, forces everyone nearby to fix their gaze upon him. What would happen if he used these two titles at the same time?
Would the other players around him look at him or not?
This was a question worth pondering.
But he now had more important things to do.
He casually chose a D-Level solo map and dived in; he wanted to experiment with what kind of creatures could stack with his S-Level Prop, ‘Longevity as the Southern Mountains’.
…
Half an hour later.
A flash of white light passed, and Chen Yi reappeared on the rooftop.
The temperature in the air gradually rose with the rising sun.
Chen Yi casually waved to activate the air conditioning system built into the beach area before sitting back in the beach chair with a sigh of regret.
He had already conducted the experiment.
Killing microorganisms did not activate the S-Level Prop ‘Longevity as the Southern Mountains’.
Although he had guessed this would be the case, the disappointment was unavoidable upon realizing there were no shortcuts. Through his experiments, only two types of beings could add to the stack of the S-Level Prop.
Players, NPCs.
Beyond those, nothing else.
Because he tried killing some chickens and ducks on Blue Star, as well as fish in the sea.
None had any effect.
Only other players in the game and NPCs in the maps, including monsters and bosses, could add to the stack of ‘Longevity as the Southern Mountains’; nothing else could.
In that case, he would have to choose his maps carefully.
Chen Yi glanced at his personal panel.
A new line for Life Value had been added.
「Life Value」: 121.
The initial value was 100, and the extra 20 came from the map he had just entered, which didn’t have many monster-spawning stages. The other 1 point was from a small creature that Gold Miner had caught for him while sea fishing yesterday.
Every 100 points of Life Value added was like gaining an extra life.
He tried to cut his skin with a knife; as expected, he felt no pain and experienced no inconvenience in his actions, just saw his Life Value display -6.
There was also a recovery rate.
(Recovers 0.001 Life Value per second.)
By his calculations, it would take about 6000 minutes to fully recover this amount of Life Value, roughly 100 hours, or about three to four days, which was almost equivalent to the recovery rate of a normal person.
Of course, he naturally wouldn’t wait to recover naturally.
‘Snap!’
A medical prop was slapped on.
The recovery speed immediately began to surge.
(Recovers 100 Life Value per minute.)
In the blink of an eye, the injury was healed.
Looking at it this way, without activating any Prop, Title, or Skill, his physical condition was indeed quite ordinary, and that’s even with him continuously activating the passive Skill ‘Calm and Composed,’ which doubled his physical attributes.
But it still couldn’t withstand very severe injuries.
What he needed to do now was to stack up his Life Value to ensure that even without using any props, his defense would be extremely strong. ‘Today’s goal, let’s stack a thousand layers first.’
Chen Yi muttered to himself as he began looking for maps that had a large number of monsters.
But just then.
Tie Chui suddenly ran up from the rooftop’s security door looking exhausted and excited, racing up to Chen Yi: “Yi, I… I have a major invention!”
“An invention?”
As he lay on the beach chair deciding which map to enter next, Chen Yi looked up at Tie Chui with some confusion and asked, “What have you invented?”
He was indeed curious about what Tie Chui could have come up with.
But Tie Chui seemed to struggle to explain, simply saying follow me, Yi, before turning and running downstairs, seemingly leading the way.
Without overthinking it, Chen Yi got up and followed Tie Chui’s steps, after all, Tie Chui was his uncle by marriage.

chapters.title: Chapter 395: 319: Void Clan (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)_6
chapters.content:
Chapter 395: Chapter 319: Void Clan (10,000-Word Mega Chapter)_6
Chen Yi’s brother-in-law spoke, and there was naturally no reason to ignore him.
Although Chen Yi’s brother-in-law was a bit dim-witted, a prop for treating this kind of disease should be found soon, and then he could return to a normal person.
…
Very soon—
Chen Yi followed Tie Chui to the security room of the residential complex, standing in front of a console that was covered with screens.
Tie Chui, with an excited expression, pointed at one of the screens and exclaimed excitedly, “Yi, look… look… this is my invention!”
...
Chen Yi looked puzzled as he leaned in to see, only to notice on the screen,
Two creatures, roughly the size of an adult fist, were hatching from their shells, appearing to struggle as their heads had already poked out, striving to pull their bodies from the shells.
It looked rather frightening.
Fist-sized larvae, wouldn’t they be terrifying?
What normal person has ever seen such large larvae?
Such a large amount of protein, if Blue Star had these creatures, they would have been eaten to extinction long ago.
“Eh.”
A strange glint suddenly passed through Chen Yi’s eyes: “These two eggshells look a bit familiar.”
These two creatures’ eggshells somehow looked so much like the two small stones he had retrieved with Gold Miner last night.
“Just… just the two that you hooked back yesterday, Yi.”
Tie Chui said excitedly, “I… I saw them moving, so I took these two stones away…”
“But I found that, I… look… they move.”
“I don’t look… they move.”
“So… I brought them under surveillance… ran to the security room… then…”
Tie Chui spoke with a stutter.
But it wasn’t like a normal person stuttering; it was because his mind couldn’t process his next words quickly enough, often resulting in a freeze and unable to articulate his thoughts as fast as a normal person.
If his mind was back to normal, naturally, he wouldn’t stutter anymore.
“Understood.”
Chen Yi narrowed his eyes and pondered for a moment before nodding, “Where are they, take me to see them.”
“Okay.”
Who could have thought these two stones that were caught would turn out to be insect eggs?
Could this lead to a species invasion on Blue Star?
He planned to live on Blue Star for a long time and didn’t want something he caught inadvertently to wipe it out.
“Okay.”
Tie Chui nodded his head excitedly, confirming.
“Another thing—”
Chen Yi paused before continuing, “This is a discovery, not an invention.”
“Understood… understood!”
…
Within a few steps,
Chen Yi had arrived in front of the two struggling larvae.
When in doubt, activate ‘Requesting the Mandate of Heaven’!
After spending 100,000 Points, he identified the two creatures.
“Void Starfield’s Void Clan player larvae.”
They possessed extremely terrifying reproductive and plundering abilities. Don’t be fooled by their harmless larval appearance; just leave them be to develop for one day, and the next day, they would have grown into horrifyingly gigantic larvae.
The Void Clan players had no age restrictions.
Their bodies did not grow with age.
As long as they had enough nutrients, growing from a larva to an adult in a day was a very simple task.
Hence, for players of this race, only two things needed to be done.
Plunder and reproduce.
As long as these two were carried out to the extreme, the race would develop at a terrifyingly rapid pace, and there was never a need to worry about the influx of new combatants or logistics.
If it were just that, it wouldn’t be terrifying.
After all, even with such high-speed reproduction, as long as they had a normal mindset, they would fear death; and if they feared death, no matter how fast they reproduced, they wouldn’t fully exploit this ability.
But the most critical point was,
The players of this race generally had low intelligence, adhered to the purest feudal system, and can be said to fill the seas with their lives without hesitation if their Matriarch demanded it.
Therefore,
The combination of high-speed reproduction, ageless growth ability, tremendously terrifying execution ability, and courage that did not fear death,
Made the Void Clan one of the few races on the Starfield Continent that occupied an entire Starfield.
“…”
Chen Yi narrowed his eyes, staring at the two creatures in front of him in silence, thinking.
The Void Clan players were extremely vengeful; once provoked, it was a feud to the death, and he was somewhat concerned that bringing this plague to Blue Star would be problematic.
Another issue he considered was,
The number of Void Clan players was exceedingly large, incredibly large…
If he could exterminate the Void Clan, then his Life Value would be measured in the tens of billions.
